product_title: TEKTON 28301 Everybit Tech Rescue (TM) Kit for Electronics, Phones and Precision Devices, 46-Piece
review_headline: Nice set with a couple of issues.
review_body:
Awesome little kit. I've been tinkering with computers and electronics for as long as I can remember but have always used the tools that were just lying around or buying stuff as I needed it. Finally decided to buy myself a toolkit but didn't want to spend too much money. This kit checked off all the right boxes (good selection of bits, magnetized bit holder, tweezers, spudger and various other opening tools). When I opened it up, I was very happy to see that everything was very neatly organized as many of the other reviewers have stated. All the bits seemed well made with no imperfections on first inspection. The tweezers were also very nice. They came to a very sharp point and the tips met perfectly when closed. The metal opening tool was very nice and the plastic ones seem like they'll get the job done. The suction cup seemed to hold very well when I tested it and the magnetized mat did it's job holding small screws.

However, when I did a memory upgrade on my notebook, I found a small problem. One screw I needed to use was a Torx 7 security, but the hole on the bit was slightly off center, thus preventing me from using the bit. I was able to get it done using a T6 security without any problems though. One other thing I noticed was that the shorter T6 and the longer T6 were slightly different sizes (the longer one fit more snugly than the shorter one). Not sure if this was intentional or not, but it seems strange to label two bits as the same only to have them be different sizes.

On the positive side, none of the bits I used bent or snapped as a few others have mentioned and other than that one snag, everything else went perfectly. As I haven't used all the other bits yet so I can't comment on them, but as of right now the issue with the T7 and the different sized T6 bits are the only thing holding this kit back from a perfect score in my book.

As for things that would be nice to have, both the triangle opener and thespudger are made of relatively soft plastic and won't damage your equipment. Because of that it seems they'll get chewed up after a bit of prying so it would have been nice if the kit came with a couple of spares, but that's really nitpicking.

product_title: Capri Tools 40208 Aviation Tin Snips, 7", Straight, Yellow/Black
review_headline: Well built, sharp and handy set of small snips
review_body:
This product was furnished so that I could try it out and then write a review. I use a lot of tool and own a lot of tools...been messing with them for over seven decades now - not an expert by any means, but then again, I did not just fall off the turnip wagon when it comes to tools and the evaluation of such.

I own and have collected quite a number of tin snips throughout the years and after loaning them to several relatives who never return things, I still (shock) have eight of them stashed in various locations in my home, sheds, workshop and barns.

The snips being reviewed here are quite good and they do the job they were made for; which if you think about it is the most important thing. They are a bit over seven inches long and the cutting blades (the surface that actually comes into contact with the metal or what ever it is you are cutting, are just a bit less than one inch. This makes it the smallest of the snips I own and I have thus far found them to be extremely useful. Most of the snips I use are big honkers and when attempting to do precision cutting on smaller objects, they are all rather difficult to handle. This little thing gets the job done!

The blades are extremely sharp. The spring action is very strong and spritely, and the action while cutting is very smooth. I find the handles, which are made of a silicone type substance and due to their design (see photos on product page), they are very, very comfortable. There is absolutely NO play or wiggle in the action of these snips...they are solid as a rock.

It is easy to get this thing into very tight places and since I do a lot of `creative' work with tin and aluminum cans and plastic milk jugs (bird feeders and hokey art), I find these to be ideal.

These snips, while being light weight, have a nice heft to them and feel quite solid and business like...I like the feel of them as I use them.

These do have a locking mechanism that can be set or unset with a flick of the thumb but is firm enough so that the likelihood of an accidental opening is quite slim. This lock is made of durable plastic which may or may not be a problem over time...we shall see. I have a feeling that if I do not use the tool has a hammer or such that the lock will last...you just never know about such things.

All in all I am quite satisfied with these snips. Like any metal tool, it is a good idea to keep this well oiled to prevent rusting and it should be stored in a dry location. Rust can absolutely make these things worthless in a very, very short length of time.

Don Blankenship

My only concern is what material fabricate it from. I continue to think MDF is the perfect substrate to make this bed. I decided to go with plywood.
1/12/16 Addendum: Building one bed is a lot of work but, making two is an enormous amount of labor. Anyone wanting to fabricate this bed had better have knowledge in mass production. Without that expertise, it will take about three months to build one bed, especially the mag rims. It took me six weeks to make both beds working 18 hours a day. Be prepared to do a tremendous amount of sanding. My hands are still raw.
When constructing this bed, take your time if you want it to look like the photograph shown. There are many redundant parts to make. It's easy to make mistakes if your not paying attention. When you are finished, your children or grandchildren will love them.
David F.

product_title: Blaklader Workwear Two Fisted Three Layer Fleece Jacket Black
review_body: This is a good jacket but has a few confusing features:  The first thing you notice is the sleeves especially the forearms. They're narrow for a jacket. I wouldn't say tight or even form fitting. They sorta lean towards snug. By that I mean there's not a lot of air between your arm and the inside material. Tight fitting clothing means there's less internal volume to try and heat up making it ideal if working outdoors or wearing it under something else (say heavy weather gear). You certainly notice the arms when wearing short sleeve shirts and I'd wager it'd be much more noticeable in long sleeves.  The other thing about the sleeves is the length. Initially I was a bit mystified as to why they were so long. Surely Americans couldn't be so long in the arms I wondered. Eventually I worked it out. There is a loop in the sleeve end for your thumb. Blaklader state this is for when putting on other clothing on top so your sleeve doesn't ride up. I suspect that in fact the end of the sleeve is intended to be some form of pseudo glove. When sticking your thumb through the loop, the sleeve covers most of the hand up to the knuckles leaving the palm and digits free for work requiring dexterity... Although I could be wrong of course.  Also a bit confusing is the large rear pocket located in the lumbar of your back. It seems strangely placed and I'm not exactly sure what you would store in there. I would have preferred a small/large internal chest pocket instead of that. I would have also have liked to have seen the pen pocket moved from the right chest to the left arm. As it stands, its too small and in the way wrong place.  The storm flap on the front zip is a welcome addition although it seems to open in the opposite direction to my other (non-Blaklader) jackets. I can't tell if this is an error, an American thing or a northern hemisphere thing. Certainly down under, storm flaps open right-to-left whereas this opens left-to-right . If you believe such things, this would designate it as an article of womens clothing.  The advertising blurb makes a big thing of it being made of triple layer polarfleece. It is probably triple layer most places but I'd suspect there are spots that are only double layer.  Having said all of that... I did like it... a lot in fact. It's thick, warm and cosy, Just the thing you want to be wearing on a cold and blustery day. It's only water resistant to the degree that Polarfleece is but you'd have to consider heavy weather gear for anything more substantial. All in all, a good thick jacket which I'd have no problem recommending to others.  A word of warning: Just like all other varieties of Polarfleece, it is made of plastic (usually from drink containers). Plastic of course melts when exposed to flame. Whats worse, molten plastic sticks to skin. Under no circumstances should you allow it to get close to an open flame as it will melt, stick to your skin and then you would require surgery and probably skin grafts. This is especially important given the industrial environment this item is expected to be used in.

product_title: Columbia River Knife and Tool K700KXP Ken Onion Skinner Fixed Razor Edge Knife
review_headline: has a wonderfully comfortable rubberized grip
review_body: I was looking for a field knife for winter deer season. I needed something small that I could dress a deer with, however was looking for a round bellied blade so that I could keep the point of the knife up after making the initial incision, making sure to stay away from the internal organs of the animal. The design of this knife is very unique. The shape of the blade allows you to make a clean incision, without the increased risk of puncturing any internal organs of the animal while making your cut upwards. It is extremely sharp, very aesthetically pleasing, has a wonderfully comfortable rubberized grip, and the blade is small enough to work within the animal as well, slicing and separating fascia, reaching up into the thorax, and working the knife from different angles to remove difficult tissue. I have yet to see any knife like this, and the value is incredible. The weight of the knife is wonderful in the hand, the finish and shape of the blade are very aesthetically pleasing, and the overall design is very functional and comfortable. Grab some para chord and braid a custom lanyard, and you've got yourself a very unique, very functional, very storable little hunting knife. The only drawback I ran into was the size of the sheath. A little large in my opinion, with stiff belt loops. I actually do not wear this knife on my belt, but keep it in a pocket in my hunting jacket. The knife itself is wonderful, and I almost wished the sheath had a better design. Perhaps something that just covered the blade, and not the handle. Although I do dislike the sheath, the knife was absolutely worth the purchase, and it is a pleasure to carry into the woods.

product_title: WASING NEW Product Promotiom Tactical LED Flashlight 400 Lumens 3 Mode Zoomable rechargeable Torch + 18650 Charger + 18650 Battery + Car Charger(L3),Black
review_headline: Most practical light for my car
review_body:
Pro: * Very usable beam pattern
* Evidently a high quality lithium cell
*Decent, but not superior construction
* You can select a mode, then always have the light turn on in that mode (high, low or strobe).
Cons: Barrel cannot be completely disassembled

This would generally substitute well for a large 3-D cell LED light, despite its size. It will likely need recharging before D cells in a similar light would need to be replaced.
Explanation: Wasing's D cell lights, like most, do not have a barrel that disassembles at both ends. For alkaline cells, this is important, since they will swell and then you cannot pull them out of the barrel, ruining the flashlight. I don't know this for a certainty, but rechargeable lithium cells, if not overcharged, do not seem to swell, so a barrel that completely disassembles is not vital. You can pay more and get a model that has zoom focus. However, I found that this model has a bright, small center that picks things out well, and widely dispersed light otherwise. Compared to several similar lights that have a zoom focus, I found this beam generally superior. The ma/hr rating on this cell is not as high as on some others. However, makers are infamous for exaggerating their cells' capacity. Since the model number of the cell is the same, and this cell is actually heavier, I believe that its capacity is greater. The reflector is relatively large, providing a good beam. Unlike any of my other lights, once I select the mode, I don't have to cycle through all the modes to get to the mode I want-- it stays in mode until you give it 2 quick clicks. Since a car charger is included, I would prefer this small light to a large 3 D cell light for my car. There is a Feit 3-C cell light that I really like, but it is more expensive, and eventually the batteries will swell, ruining the light.

I can't complain really because the flash light cost under $8 and I believe the batteries were included to test out the flashlight.  I bought mine from NEON MART and the quality of the product was solid. You can adjust the focus by sliding the head piece, which wasn't overly loose or stiff.  It's rated at 150LM but it isn't quite there.  I have a 200LM headlamp ($65) that is twice the brightness of this 150LM flashlight, but at under $8, this is a great value buy. This LE flashlight is significant bringer than other 200LM and 300LM at the same price.  Buy this flashlight over the plastic incandescent emergency flashlights that are of disposable qualities. You know the ones I'm talking about. The pictures included are taken from my bedroom with the blinds closed around 6pm.  Both are taken 5 feet away, the first with wide angle beam and the second with full focus.  At full focus you can see the shape of the LED, which is difficult to tell from the picture.

For only three dollars more at the time of this review, the Kniper is well worth the extra expense compared to the H.K. Porter model. I do find the release latch somewhat easier to use on the H.K. Porter than on the Kniper.  But the opening spring on the H.K. Porter is weak and I have to push the device open manually with the handles to get the jaws wide enough to do anything.  This would quite irritating if you were using the H.K. Porter model for more than a few quick cuts per use.  The Kniper model claims to be made in Germany while the H.K. Porter model is made in China.  German quality is generally superior to Chinese quality for comparable products.  Also, the Kniper product comes with a lifetime guarantee so that shows some confidence by the manufacturer in the quality of their products, which are highly regarded in any event.

product_title: Jet - JJ-8HH; 8-inch Helical Head Jointer
review_headline: This is a buy, but there are things to know.
review_body:
This jointer is quiet as a mouse. My dust collection system is much louder than running a board across it. And, if you use a proper feed rate, you get glassy smooth results with minimal tear out.

Some points that made me give it 4 stars instead of 5:

Setup: I had a lot of difficulty installing the drive belts. The motor is bolted to a stage that can move up and down, but it is extremely difficult to reach the bolts that control the movement, and the assembly is very heavy. The instruction manual was fairly useless in this endeavor. I had to remove the entire motor, move the stage into place and THEN attach the belts. Quite a bit of work.

The Fence: I find the fence on this jointer a bit short (actual height off the table, not length). I've used several Delta jointers and a Grizzly jointer and I found their fences to be taller, and hence more stable. Not a deal breaker, but it's something I've noticed. Setting the fence takes a bit of work, but this is true of most jointers.

Dust Collection: Despite a short run to my dust collector, I still find a fair spray of chips onto the infeed table. Not a major complaint, but I would like less clean-up than that.

Infeed adjustment: I wish they had a bit more useful scale below 1/8th of a inch on the infeed side. Not a deal breaker, but would be helpful.

OVERALL: This jointer is a buy. The beds could be longer, but in my limited shop space, this is a plus, not a minus.

review_headline: Works better than the cheaper ones!
review_body:
I ordered other flashlights that advertised 2000 lumen but obviously did not produce that! These may not be the full 2000 lumen but they are very bright and definitely worth the money. They will light up the house next door to mine on a dark night unlike the other cheaper ones. I know you tend to get what you pay for but these really do have a good bulb in them and are far superior to the others in this class. One tell tale sign is when you focus the light into the smallest beam on both, the cheaper ones show one wire inside the bulb (I'm guessing that has something to do with light production in the chip) while this one has five or six lines and you can see its a better LED chip! I use it with the three AAA batteries option and its super bright. Others may advertise 2000 lumen but you have to buy an extra battery case or some special battery. Not this one, it works great right out of the box.

So if you need a flashlight that will light up a big area or reach out across a few neighborhood yards this one will do it!

product_title: Howard Leight by Honeywell Quiet Corded Reusable Shooting Earplugs, 2-Pairs (R-01522)
review_body:
I got these earplugs and they are BY FAR the best sleeping earplugs I have ever used.
No other reusable earplug even comes close! These are plugs are so easy to insert and remove. You just pull back one ear, slide it in and it just slides in! If you have tried "Moldex Rockets Reusable Corded Earplugs", you know how much time and effort it takes to insert them. These on the other hand take no struggle, you just slide them in, taking almost no time at all, and you're ready to go. These are as comfortable if not more so than the foam non-reusable earplugs that cost a fortune to use in the long term.

However, there is one caveat (mostly to those who use earplugs to sleep), they wear out, after a few to several months of use you'll need to replace them due to the earplugs shrinking and no longer fitting as they once did. They shrink because of the oils in one's ear that these reusable (but foam) earplugs absorb overtime. At a certain point they just wont stay in your ear, but this still does not change my opinion of these being the best earplugs I have ever used.

Short Version:
- Very Comfortable
- Easily inserted in almost no time at all
- Caveat: after a few months the earplugs will stop working from absorbing oil from one's ear

product_title: DEWALT DC012 7.2-Volt-18-Volt Heavy-Duty Worksite Radio Charger
review_headline: OK unit - BUT once it dies it is trash
review_body:
This item belongs to my son. He's used it for a few years, he says mainly for charging his DeWalt batteries. It stopped working - stone cold dead. I checked several different sources to see if there were any internal fuses. I was sure there had to be! I discovered the factory parts diagram and parts list makes no mention of fuses. I already had most of the screws out so I got the rest out. I read a few reviews here and discovered it was likely there were a couple of screws I had missed since the radio didn't come apart. I read in a couple of places the case was glued shut - Not so on this radio. You just have to look for four round holes at the seam (after getting out all the screws). They're on the bottom center. Use something round (A scratch awl works great), stick it into one of the holes and pry gently. The case should start to split and you can then get a larger screwdriver or whatever in there. As for the fuses - I did find two glass fuses like the ones cars used to use (glass cylinder with a metal cap on each end). Unfortunately in this case both fuses were good, so that obviously wasn't the problem. I took out a few more components to see if I could find evidence of excessive heat or burning or something obvious. The only areas that appeared to have gotten hot were the connections to the small PC board holding the contacts for the battery charger. Before putting everything back together I checked the input voltage, which was OK. The unit still doesn't work, so all it is good for now is a large 3-outlet extension cord. (the receptacles on the end still work).

Bottom line - unless you are an expert electronics repair person or want to spend considerable $ on parts the unit is useless once it dies.

I gave this 3 stars because it DID work fine for my son for quite a while. Maybe I should drop a star since other reviewers say you can't get these units repaired by DeWalt, plus there seems to be a lot of unnecessary confusion over the existence of internal fuses.nce of internal fuses.

product_title: Rechargeable LED Flashlight, MAXTOMARS LED 3 White Lighting Levels Lamp, 7 Colors Flash Light, USB Charging, Eye Protection (White)
review_body:
I got this because my teen was intrigued with the light-changing mechanism. I thought she and her Robotics Club buddies could use it at some of their demonstrations and conventions. And that function works well and it's cool. You push the top (of two) button and the light is red. Push again and it turns to flashing red. Another push gets it to solid green. Then it goes on to flashing green, blue, flashing blue, and finally to a "spectrum" sequence where it starts at red and goes through the rainbow colors and ends in white. It will keep doing that until you hold down the button and turn it off. This is SERIOUSLY cool and I think I can say without fear of contradiction that all kids and a lot of adults would be happy to have this to play with.

What I did not anticipate (and I think this should be stressed more heavily on the product page) is that this is a very handy emergency light. It's sturdy and you can hold it by the handle as a flashlight OR stand it upright to use as ambient lighting. There's a nice 36" charging cord that fits into a small hole on the light and into a USB outlet. Mine came partly charged and worked right out of the box, but you will need to plug it in to fully charge it (at which time the tiny red light next to the plug hole will go off.) Pushing the bottom of the two button produces a really, REALLY bright white light. Shine in in your eyes and you'll be blind for a while. A second push moves it down to a softer light and a third down to a setting that is dim but that provides an amazing amount of ambient light. A fourth push turns the light off.

Fully charged and used at the lowest setting, it's supposed to last 20 hours. That's a VERY good emergency light in my book. If you had some charged up power banks kicking around, you could re-charge it and keep going. The only quibble that I have is that the two buttons are very small and (to me) a bit hard to push. I would prefer larger buttons. But for this price and for what it delivers, I'll suck it up.

review_headline: Great monitor, horrible customer service in Canada

I will be up front and say that we did not purchase this system from Amazon. We purchased it directly from the website.

We have had two calls in now to customer service, the first one went "OK". Finally I had had enough and made a comment about the customer service, she informed me that she was "getting of the phone now" and hung up.

Bottom line, if you can figure out their "very simple system" on your own, it's a great monitor. If you have to call customer service for anything run far far away.

TEKTON 24335 1/2-Inch Drive Click Torque Wrench, 10-150-Foot/Pound
review_body: If your goal is to do the job RIGHT the first time, then this is NOT your tool!  The setting lock nut does not hold your selected torque, loosening each time the wrench clicks.  This I learned after bolt nine (9) of seventeen (17) on the first of a three (3) phase tightening sequence; the value had changed by three pounds.  This means you must babysit the tool by resetting your value (after each bolt click) and trying to hold the knurled handle stationary while you pull in the torque.  I even tried not holding the black knurled handle which did not improve tool accuracy and of course your leverage diminishes.  The locking nut has a through hole apparently intended for tightening, rather like a 'C' clamp, but the manufacturer did not provide that apparatus; should not need one anyway.  Not suitable for engine work and definitely not for cylinder heads.  Spend your money on a Matco or SnapOn or pay someone to perform this critical operation!

product_title: SOG SwitchPlier 2.0 Multi-Tool SWP1001-CP - 12 Tools, Automatic Opening Pliers, Stainless Steel, 2.6" Blade
review_body:
I can’t count how many multi-tools I’ve owned throughout the years; from expensive Leathermans to cheaper ones like Guidesman from Menards. All of them have their pluses and minuses, but so far the SOG stands out as the best -- if only because it has a switchblade-like opener. There are times when I am holding something and only have one hand free, which makes pulling out the SOG and clicking the button with my thumb really handy. The pliers pops out and is instantly accessible. I also really like that there is no case to sit awkwardly on my belt. Instead, the SOG has a pocket clip. I can slip it to the inside of my pocket without the tool feeling like an annoying lump at the bottom of my pocket. This makes it easier to access while keeping it tucked out of the way.

The SOG is heavy and bulky when compared to a standard pocket knife, but it is surprisingly compact in comparison to other Multi-tools I’ve owned. The build quality is really good too; sturdy and tough. The spring on the pliers is responsive and the grip when squeezing doesn’t cut into my fingers.

The selection of tools are useful; no crazy scissors or toothpicks. Just straightforward tools you’d actually use on a normal project, like screwdrivers and a ruler. The only negative I found with the SOG is that the knife (while super sharp and effective) is inaccessible one-handed; I need two hands to pull the knife out, which means there are times where a pocket knife would work better. But overall, I’m impressed with the SOG and would recommend it to other handymen.

product_title: Fluke 324 40/400A AC, 600V AC/DC True-RMS Clamp Meter with Temperature, & Capacitance Measurements
review_body:
Good quality meter, solid sturdy construction. I'm not a professional electrician or HVAC tech, but I wanted a good quality meter that had, in one unit, the typical measurements that I'm in need of: voltage, current, resistance/continuity, capacitance, and temperature. Previously I had a box of various and assorted meters, none of which had all that I wanted, but in combination did. All were of standard (read: dubious) quality, and never quite seemed to agree in scale. I junked them all and went w/ the 324.

It has performed to and exceeded my expectations. The quality and construction seems substantial for contractor/tech work, but I can't comment on field durability, this will be a 'garage queen' for my occasional use. The price point is high for my general needs, but I feel that I'd probably spent more than that on the bevy of meters that I discarded, not to mention the implicit costs associated with poorly calibrated devices and not having any sense of confidence. I'm happy with my decision, and very pleased with my purchase.

I've attached some additional pictures of the product (taken from the Fluke site) -- these should be included in the main product pictures above, but aren't for some reason. Product includes: meter, case, manual, probes (red & black with pointed tips and caps), thermocouple. Manual available for download at: http://media.fluke.com/documents/32x_____umeng0000.pdf

review_headline: can illuminate a room with the high light setting
review_body:
The SecurityIng 4200 Lumens LED Flashlight arrived exactly like the open box on my photo. It has the flashlight inside and a brown string which can be used as a wrist strap. It didn't come with any instructions or safety instruction manual but I figured out how to install the batteries since we have several flashlights at home already.

The SecurityIng 4200 Lumens Waterproof LED Flashlight works on 4 x 18650 3.7V rechargeable batteries which is not included in the box. I had to buy this separately before I got to try the SecurityIng 4200 Lumens Flashlight. The batteries can be installed by twisting the cover (part where the bulbs are).

The SecurityIng 4200 Lumens Waterproof LED Flashlight has a single button which is used to turn the flashlight on as well change through the light modes. There are 3 modes: high, low and strobe. To change through the light modes, I have to press the button for about 3 seconds.

The SecurityIng 4200 Lumens Waterproof LED Flashlight has 7 Cree XM-L T6LED lights. I love how bright this flashlight can be and can illuminate a room with the high setting. Of course it's not as bright as a light bulb but with this, even with no other lights on, I can see throughout the room with no problems.

I like how durable this flashlight looks because of the aluminum alloy case. The glass lens on the flashlight head is super clear so there are no interference with the brightness of the LED lights. The body of this flashlight is a bit thicker but I can still hold it in my hand with no problems. It is also a bit heavier, specially with the batteries in, but I'd prefer this because it's super bright.

With prolonged use, the flashlight gets a bit hot with the high setting maybe because the flashlight's entire exterior is made out of metal. Other than that, this is a very nice, useful and bright flashlight which I would recommend to others. This is also perfect to use for outdoor activities like camping and hiking because it's super bright.

product_title: 350 Lumen
review_headline: This thing is great, I'm an EMT and work mostly nights in ...
review_body: This thing is great, I'm an EMT and work mostly nights in a mixed urban/suburban environment with everything from project buildings to forested estates, and right off the bat you can tell that the paramedic and firefighter who started bright medic took their experiences on the job into account when designing this light.  The light itself is super bright and on wide focus it does a great job of lighting up dark hallways, entire rooms, and vehicles, and narrow focus throws bright light far enough to read house numbers on homes that are set way back from the road with no issue.  The clip is rigid enough that it stays on my belt no matter how I move and keeps it firmly in place even though I spend a lot of time with 30+ pound medical bags slung over my shoulder that hit or rub against where the light is placed on my hip.  The construction is very solid and I haven't noticed any dimming yet despite over a month of almost nightly use with no battery changes.  It fits comfortably in your hand and is not so big that it gets in the way and not so small that you might lose it.  My only complaint is that with the three setting cycle (high-low-strobe)  when you completely turn the light off it cycles to the next setting when it is turned on again it starts at the next setting in the cycle (so if you turn it off after using it on low the next time you turn it off it will start on strobe), but this is a very minor issue as I almost exclusively use it on high and it only takes a fraction of a second to cycle through all the settings.  Definitely a great light that outperforms significantly more expensive ones I've used.

product_title: 1byone Wireless Home Security Driveway Alarm, DIY Receiver
review_body: I needed something to alert me to the arrival of customers when our receptionist is not sitting in the front of the office.  This definitely works for that purpose.  It was easy to install and set up (establish a link between motion detector and receiver).  The range seems fair.  The alert itself is a little obnoxious.  It has an ear piercing siren if you want to use it as a burglar alarm.  It has a "chime" with two volume settings if you need to be alerted to a customer or car pulling into the driveway, etc.  The low volume setting is pretty loud and the chime is four successive ding-dongs.  I would be happy with an option to make that one ding-dong.  If someone comes in the door and someone else leaves 2 seconds later I get 8 successive ding-dongs.  The motion sensor seems to be pretty reliable so far but I would also like to have an option of a door sensor.  I can't complain about the price and I feel like there is a lot of value in this product for such a low price.  I'll keep using it unless or until co-workers or customers complain about the obnoxious factor.

product_title: SE FS374 All-Weather Emergency 2-IN-1 Fire Starter & Magnesium Fuel Bar (Everything you need to start a fire!)
review_body: This is my second pair (SE FS374) and have ordered other magnesium fire starters and I'm a big fan of this particular kind. It should come with a green metal-ish razor but I would honestly just ditch it and use a knife instead (although it does work if you use it right). In a survival situation you need to be able to create fire and without fire you're simply dead meat. You can't purify water without fire (unless you're lucky enough to be next to a natural spring), you can't keep yourself warm without fire, and you can't cook raw meat without fire and so on... You can always make fire without a magnesium fire starter but it's much more time consuming and costs a lot of energy to do. In a short-term survival situation, a magnesium starter is hands down the most important tool to master besides your knife. There is no reason why anyone should be without this, disaster can strike at any time (earthquake, tornado, etc...) and having a reliable tool for fire is essential. The SE FS374 is one of a few magnesium fire starters that I would recommend for survival.  New to Magnesium fires? Buy a few! You can easily run through them when you're starting new, and without practice you'll end up wasting this purchase in a real survival situation.

review_headline: Great Gloves - Color Scheme has Changed to Full Coyote
review_body:
Recently ordered this product. I've used Mechanix original gloves for quite a few years, so I knew what I would be receiving. Mechanix gloves are characterized by their dexterity - having as little material in the finger tip as possible. They are breathable, lightweight, relatively durable for their thickness, and the price is right. For the price, sliding this glove onto your hand feels good. It feels secure, well fitting (though they do seem to have changed the fitment for the thumb, it is now quite loose, but I imagine this suits most users), and it feels like a premium glove. These gloves, to my knowledge, are not insulated, but do provide minor warmth in the cold. They make a great driving glove, if you're into that, or just a great glove to wear out in the elements. They wont provide much protection, obviously. I found that out when an angle grinder bucked against my thumb, but that is expected.

However, Mechanix has changed their color scheme on this product. When I placed this order, the image shown was Coyote and Black. Strangely, that is the image that is shown to my left as I write this review, but on the main product page, the image is different. This glove is now a full coyote, which was not what I had ordered. I received the full coyote glove, but did not bother to return it since it's just a glove, and a $20 one at that. This is the reason for my 4-star review.

product_title: Festool 497514 Kapex UG Portable Miter Station Set
review_headline: Use these extensions and you'll never need a purpose-built chop-saw station.
review_body:
These extensions fit directly on the Kapex saw, clamping to the saw exactly the same way the 494369 Miter Saw Crown Stop Base Extensions do. The base extensions must first be removed. Extensions will work with the 497351 UG-Kapex Wheeled stand and the MFT/3-Kapex Multifunction Table. If you're considering using with the Wheeled stand, buy the stand and extensions in a single package.

If you plan on using these extensions with the MFT/3 table the area between the saw and the table provides rather limited room to tighten the clamp screws. Consider boring a hole in the table top and extending the clamping screw with some threaded rod - so the knob can be tightened from below the table surface.

I find the MFT/3 table and extensions provides cuts with extreme smoothness and accuracy.
If your shop is like mine, real-estate is precious. you find yourself temporarily moving things to meet the needs of projects as you do them. Trading a permanently located chop-saw station for the Kapex table and extensions gives added flexibility with no sacrifice in accuracy or cut quality.

product_title: EnZo Knives 2017 Trapper 95 Fixed Blade Knife with Green Canvas Micarta Handles
review_headline: Great all around, every day carry knife!
review_body:
I bought this in the n690co blade and couldn't be happier. It has sliced through boxes, carved wood, accidentally cut into copper reinforcement in plastic hosing with no dire effects to the blade. It's also very sharp like the other reviewer noted. I say this because as I type this I can't use my left index finger - it's been bandaged since I sliced the tip of it off accidentally while using this knife doing some wiring work on our submersible pump. I chalk it up to my own inattention and it makes me have a definite respect for the edge of this knife!
I carry and use this tool on a daily basis and have to say it is very comfortable in my medium-large sized hands. I did have to sand down the pommel end of the micarta scales as they were a tad sharp-cornered out of the box. That said, this is an extremely comfortable knife in hand even after extended use cutting and slicing.
I bought this to replace a Fällkniven F1 that just didn't feel "right" to me. This is the perfect combo of heft, dexterity and useable blade length for my uses - great for chopping and also detailed work. Though I don't use it on a regular basis, the spine has a sharp 90 degree edge that easily throws a shower of sparks from my ferro rod. The scandi edged blade is perfectly finished and ground as well.
Also, in closing, I'd like to add that mine came with a bushcraft type sheath (more rectangular than blade shaped) with the option of using a dangler loop or traditional sheath loop. It's of nice quality and looks and retains the knife very well - it also doesn't draw much attention like some of the tactical kydex sorts of sheaths. I'm hopeful that I'll be processing a few deer and other critters later on in the year with this great little knife. I'll update this review at the end of the hunting season!

product_title: Gerber Curve Multi-Tool
review_headline: Great little tool... take the clip off and use a quick detach clip around the end instead.
review_body: I love this little multi-tool.  I have multiple Leatherman, SOG, Swiss Army Knives, etc.  However, I don't always carry one of them (and if I know I will have tool needs I bring real tools).  This thing is always on a carabiner attached to my jeans belt loop, draped into my pocket with other small items (see attached pic).  However, be realistic in your expectations.  Even a $170 Leatherman sucks for hours of use compared to a $5 screwdriver, saw, etc.  I find this more durable than my Swiss Army Knife (SAK) Classic SD (I have 3).  The shape fits well for using the blade to slice the tape on boxes and has enough grip for me to cut through those plastic containers items come in.  The lock gives me more security when poking through plastic, and I don't feel like I'm going to break the screwdrivers when I need a little more torque like I do on my SAK Classic SD's.  I do get poked fun at by friends for carrying such a small multi-tool... until they need to use the bottle opener because they weren't carrying or left their's in the car.  It is nowhere near as capable as a larger multitool, so don't expect it to be... If you ALWAYS want to carry a larger multi-tool, that's great.  However, I stopped carrying them regularly because I found when I'm not actually at a work site where I bring my normal tools, this Gerber Curve handles 99% of the things I need to do on my free time.  Even when wearing my other multi-tools I still bring this with.  The main downside is that the spring clip can fall off (deducted 1 star).  Mine did... I actually took it off of my second Curve (use needle nose pliers).  I emphasize that this is a light-duty multi-tool for occasional use.  I don't understand how some reviewers will deduct stars from it for not doing things a tool 5 times it size should do.

I can now buy 2 blades for what I used to spend on one. These types of blades don't last a long time anyway but they will last longer if you keep slow and steady feed rates and don't try to take on too many layers at a time if cutting flat stock. It's easy to chip a tooth on the edges of the steel both starting and finishing a cut. These chips mean that the next tooth in line will be forced to do more work and soon it will fail, and so on.
Remember, slow and steady.

review_body: Got this TEKTON hammer just in time to use it on some wood deck work in back of the house.  Also needed to do some repairs to a wood tree house I built for the kids years ago, damaged by a recent storm.  Never used a TEKTON hammer before and never used a fiberglass handle hammer.  I was pleasantly surprised.  Took me a minute to get used to the handle, mainly because it curves at the end.  You can see the curve in the product pictures.  All my previous hammers for over 50 years have had straight wood handles with no curves so at first the handle of this new TEKTON hammer felt strange to me.  This particular design does absorb some of the impact shock from my old wood handle hammers and I like that a lot.  The magnet for starting nails is fantastic.  I really, really like that.  After I got the feel of this hammer I was able to keep a very good grip on it.  Product appears well made in addition to being well designed and I expect it to last for life.  I find this to be a great hammer for the price, a good value.  Never heard of "TEKTON" before this, most of my tools are Craftsman, Snap On and Stanley.  TEKTON is a new brand for me.  But I can and do recommend this hammer.

review_headline: Perfect for lighter-duty rotary work. Easy and fast to set up and use.

Just use it for things within its capability - I wouldn't cut metals with it or do heavier work like that - it may perform but that's not what I bought it for.

It takes all the chucks, tools, and attachments my corded unit takes, so there was no expense there. Typical use - do you have a 3-way lamp that flickers on high setting? product_title: Stanley 85-610 10-Inch Long MaxGrip Locking Adjustable Wrench
review_headline: Wrench is NOT meant to lock with nothing in its jaws!!!
review_body:
This wrench is made to put in place, tighten with the thumb wheel, and then lock to clamp it down. In other words, it's a vice-grip without the guess work. For that purpose it works extremely well. However, I mistakenly bought it thinking it could be adjusted to a particular size, locked, and then taken on and off of nuts/bolts without the jaw wandering out of adjustment (the problem with normal adjustable wrenches). IT DOESN'T WORK THAT WAY. The thumb wheel is only a conduit for the clamping force, and if there is no force on the jaws the wheel can rattle around. So alright - if I use it the way it is intended to be used, it works very nicely, albeit with plenty of play due to a lack of precision in the manufacture. However, it would have been very easy to make the wheel lock, too, and I believe it was deliberately designed to not replace a set of fixed-size wrenches. For that, -3 stars. For poor manufacturing, -1 star. For fulfilling its only useful function fairly well, +2 stars.d spring is a dinky little thing, just two quick wraps of extremely fine-gauge wire. If I loosen the set screw and let the beefy spring push the plate down and thus push down on the dinky spring, pushing the thumb wheel against the lock lever, I lose the beefy spring's pressure and the handle wants to flop around (the pliers still lock to a nut just as hard because the travel isn't determined by the springs).

Either I have a slightly stiffened lock to use the pliers like a regular adjustable wrench with an EXTREMELY LOOSE THUMB WHEEL, or I have a pair of pliers with the lock handle flopping around and a very, very slightly tighter thumb wheel, which still won't hold its position very well. There is no middle ground, and neither extreme is worth much.

review_body:
This tripod to support a TV satellite dish - I actually have two (one for Dish Network and one for DirecTV) - a very rugged, stable, portable platform - I add a dog spiral tieout stake under the center with a ladder lock strap to provide an anchor - this combo provides a rock solid base for mounting and aiming a satellite antenna -

Additional details

Photo 1 shows the dog tie out stake and LadderLock strap to stabilize the tripod - I used a 1 inch wide, 60 inch long LadderLock strap - it also shows chains for the tripod legs - they help constrain the legs while setting up the tripod -

Leg chain details - I used an eye loop on each side of the immovable part of the leg - fastened about a 16 inch length of chain to one side - fastened two links to the other side and fastened the free end to the end of the 2nd link in the leg chain did this for all three sides - and then hooked the chains together in the center - this keeps the legs from going to far stray as you are setting up the tripod - the chains are independent of the dog tie out stake and the LadderLock stabilizing strap - I used Koch Industries A17721 No. 12 Single Jack Electro Galvanized Steel, 10-Feet, Zinc Plated -

Photo 2 shows the underside of the mounting to the tripod table - the centering plate and the bars that support the mounting bolt can be seen - the phenolic four arm knob is used to tighten the antenna support - even with the knob tighten, the dish and mount can usually be rotated for adjustment -

Photo 3 shows the bolt under the mast that goes through the tripod table and is tightened with the phenolic four arm knob

Photo 4 shows from the top of the table the hole in the center and the two bars under the table that the antenna mast is fastened too

Centering plate details - this is prolly the worst part of the project - it is basically a large washer - There is a 2-1/2 inch 'hole' in the top of the tripod base - underneath the base are two bars with clearance for a 1/2 inch bolt - in order to keep the bolt in the center, a plate is placed inside the hole on top of the bars - dimensions are about 1/8 thick X 2-3/8 outside diameter with a clearance hole in the center for a 1/2 inch bolt - I don't know of any place that such a piece can be purchased - I did some scrounging to find the ones I use -

product_title: Vermont American High Speed Steel Countersink
review_headline: Mine didn't need to be perfect and I was able to make a relatively good ...
review_body:
I usually try to buy American-made products when they are available.

I felt a little duped on this one. The company is called "Vermont American," yet the product was made in China. This company has been around for decades, so I assume that they used to make them in the USA then moved their manufacturing to China to cut costs.

If the name of the company implies that it's an American product, then they need to clearly state in the product description that it is made in China. I know this doesn't matter to a lot of people because they are just looking for the lowest price, but it's important to some of us to know where our products came from and to try to support American manufacturing.

As for the product itself: I only had to make a few countersinks into aluminum with it. I used a hand drill because I do not have a press. If you need a very clean / round countersink you will need to use a drill press (this goes for any countersink). Mine didn't need to be perfect and I was able to make a relatively good round countersink with this with a slightly wavy perimeter using my cordless drill.

One thing I did not like about it is that the shaft is round instead of hex-shaped. This required me to stop and re-tighten the chuck several times because the countersink would slip and not turn. I think there is too much counter-torque for this application to have a smooth shaft. It really needs to be hex-shaped.

review_body: I used the 1/4" and the 3/8" bits with my hand drill to finish off a number of holes I had previously drilled using high speed steel brad point bits.  I used these Forstner bits to provide a little better bottom to the holes.  Used in this fashion they did fine. These are not carbide nor HSS steel bits ... they are carbon steel bits. These low RPM requirements may explain why many are having problems with their bits.  I won't be able to, for instance, use them with my "Total Shop" (like a Shop Smith) because the minimum Total Shop speed is 850 rpm.  So I can only use them with a hand drill. 3.  The bits didn't come in a protected WOODEN case.  They did come in a protected plastic case as shown in the product information on Amazon.  However I'm  happy with the plastic case. 4.  I paid $11.45 for these bits.

product_title: Soldering Iron Tip Cleaner Wire and Holder
review_headline: Confusion by some over the purpose of this product.
review_body:
Okay, let’s clear up some confusion about cleaning soldering iron tips. For the record, I was an instructor in the US Navy, and one of the courses I piloted and taught at Trident Training Facility was Soldering skills.

First, this product is a good product for what it was designed for: removing excess solder from the tip. I have noticed some comments about the sponge. And this is where the confusion about soldering tip care comes in.

When you install a new tip on your iron, you need to wrap it in solder before you heat it up the first time. The solder protects the tip and prevents oxides and impurities from being burned into the tip.

When you go to use the iron, you first use an item like this product to clean the excess solder from the tip.
THEN, you shock the tip by wiping it on the wet sponge. This shocks the impurities from flux other contaminants from the tip. Does it drop the temp of the tip? Momentarily, yes. But the tip will return to it’s original temp almost instantaneously. You are only shocking the tip, not the heater.

Once you have soldered your work, melt some solder on the tip again before putting it into the iron holder. Again, this is to coat the tip. Yes, it will turn brown, and black. But that is the solder, not the tip. The tip will stay free of contaminants, and last much longer.

As for this product, again, it is sufficient for what it was designed for, removing the excess solder from the tip.

product_title: Craftsman Socket Organizer Set
review_body:
I’ve had these organizers for several years. I use them in my Craftsman brand tool boxes to hold Craftsman brand tools/sockets for home use. The organizers were reasonably priced, quick to set up, stable and easy to use/see sockets. The lettering/numbering is raised above the surface and easily read in low light. The letters/numbers are also pretty large and easy to see without my glasses. Photos show I have a reasonably comprehensive set of Craftsman sockets.

My tool boxes have moved five times since I bought these organizers. Twice across country, twice over a thousand miles and the last time about 300 miles. The moving companies are never gentle on my tool boxes. Not once was any single socket lost or misplaced because of these trays.

Per the instructions, the “riser pins” are for use with deep sockets. I didn’t think this was the right type of tray for organizing deep sockets so I only used it for standard depth sockets. I can’t comment on installing the “riser pins” because I didn’t use them. I have all of the smallest size Craftsman sockets. Not one of them is loose or hard to get at. I suspect that installing/using the “riser pins” has caused the problems mentioned in other reviews. Note that the packaging and instructions do say riser pins are for deep sockets…not standard sized.

My sockets fit well into each space. Some are a little looser and some are a little snug. Most of my sockets are 15-25 years old Craftsman. These had the sizes stamped into the side of the socket. I also have a few of the newer Craftsman brand sockets with the etched markings for the sizes. I vaguely recall that for one of those, I decided to scrape the inside edge of the hole for that one socket because it was a little snugger than I liked. I used a utility knife or pocket knife (I wouldn’t sand it) to quickly scrape the inside edge of the hole and the socket then fit perfectly. At this price, scraping a hole or two for a perfect fit is okay for my use.

I have these organizers in the top two shallow drawers of my normal sized Craftsman brand rolling cabinet base. They may fit in a narrower top box but they are perfect for me in my lower base cabinet. I’ve had zero problems with the overall size fitting into my Craftsman brand rolling base cabinet.

These trays were stored/used in non-climate controlled garages with outside temperatures ranging from -50F to 115F. The plastic has held up well for many years. No issues with the quality of the plastic or injection molding.

I could take the time to cut a shadowed tool box tray but that’s really not necessary for my home use tools. I also didn’t like the generic trays that you insert pegs or holders into. I like to see if a tool is missing and these organizers can work for that.

Now for some cons:
I haven’t done an inventory in a few years but I used to have at least one of pretty much every ¼”, 3/8” and ½” socket that Craftsman sold. You’ll note (in my photos) that there are still some open holes for sockets in sizes that Craftsman doesn't even sell. If you don't own or intend to own every 6point and 12 point socket from Craftsman then you will end up with many open holes.

You can also see that there are a couple of sets of the universal joints and drive adapters. I came out of the jet aviation sector so open spaces tend to bother me. I bought the extra universals and adapters just to fill some of those extra holes. Not the most practical solution to buy duplicates since I rarely use those items but I really don't want the open holes.

Use of space isn’t the most efficient but these organizers are just fine for my home use. For me, if I needed more space I’d just buy a bigger box but that’s not practical for everyone.

Overall, I’m very satisfied with these organizers. Wouldn’t (in fact I haven’t) replaced these because they work great for my use and are reasonably priced for what you get. And yes they're Craftsman so you could buy and try them and if they don't work then you can take them back.e reasonably priced for what you get. review_headline: Great updated model - brightest light I own
review_body:
This seems to be an updated model of the other popular Refun light. I like this one much better as it is built much sturdier. With the older light, it would rattle so much while biking that it would switch between zoom levels. This light doesn't rattle at all and holds the level very tightly. I don't have to worry about making constant adjustments while riding.

I was confused at first about how to cycle through the modes, but quickly figured it out. Once you have the light turned on, you gently press the on/off button again, like, super gently, barely a touch. Each gentle touch allows you to cycle through the various modes. To turn the light off you just fully press the on/off button.

The mount attaches easily to your bicycle handlebars and allows the light to be installed and removed quickly. The mount is equipped with a plastic wingnut, so no tools are required to install it. When the light is mounted, you can easily turn it on/off and cycle through the modes via the push button on the back. An added bonus to this light is that you can "zoom" the light in and out depending on how much space you want illuminated. This is great to use when biking on trails in the dark, because you can condense the light into a small patch and see perfectly in front of you.

The light itself is a little bigger than I am used to, but it still seems so small when attached to my handlebars. In addition to a bike light, you can easily slide the light out of the mount and use it as a handheld flashlight, making it a perfect accessory for bike camping.

review_body:

The package arrived with no damage, so all broken parts where placed there at the plant. I opened the lamp sub box first. The base cover had a 2 1/2 inch crack and was not seated on the base. I returned this item and will look for a Aoyue or maybe Weller unit. If these obvious defects were included, there's no telling what was wrong with the main unit.

This it the worse delivered product I have ever received. It is negligent to ship a product with this many broken parts. I suppose xtronic had a surplus of broken parts which they needed to get rid of and figured they'd stick a broken piece in a package here and there. Unfortunately I got more than my share of broken parts. I'd give this zero stars, if was possible.

product_title: Byrd Tool Shelix cutterhead for Dewalt planer DW735
review_body:
It's here! My DeWalt planer is complete! A few months ago I began reading about the Shelix cutter heads and was very intrigued. Finally I took the plunge and ordered a cutter head for my 20+ year old Jet jointer. Upon receiving the cutter head I found it easy to install and was blown away by the smooth cut and seemingly increased power of my jointer. This experience led me to purchase a new DeWalt 13" planer and a matching Shelix cutter head. I waited patiently for the cutter head to arrive, and continued to read articles and reviews about it. I began to get a bit worried after reading several less than glowing reviews that said the cutter head left scallops and lines on the wood. Well, the cutter head arrived yesterday and I went to work installing it after work today.

First, watch the utube videos by Chris Wong and he will walk you through the entire process. It took right at 90 minutes to change out the cutter heads. Upon completion I hooked everything up and ran my first piece of hardwood through the planer. Amazing! The DeWalt planer is somewhat loud due to the type motor it uses, and when you use the OEM steel knives it is excessively loud (my wife who wears hearing aids could hear me planing a piece of pine almost 100 feet away with the shop doors closed). When I fired up the planer and ran hardwood through it I couldn't tell at first if it was even cutting. I took twice the depth of cut as what I did in the pine and the machine didn't sound any louder nor did is bog down. The wood came out. So smooth you wouldn't need to sand it. I looked everywhere for the scallops and lines and they weren't there.

The only thing I could wish for is that DeWalt just got off the dime and offered the Shelix as a factory installed option. If you are considering a Shelix for your machine just get one, you will be amazed.

Update. As of July 22, 2015 I have planned several hundred linear feet of maple using this cutterhead and still have not encountered the complaints listed in some of the other reviews. The head cuts so smooth that some of the planed stock actually tends to stick together when to pieces are stacked one on top another. I still don't get the issue with the Shelix cutterhead being marginally smaller in diameter than the OEM cutterhead. I have yet to encounter a feeding problem on the DeWalt planer due to the cutterhead diameter. product_title: Amber Pattern Glasses Frame, Marrywindix uv glasses Computer Glasses Anti-reflective Anti-glare Plain glasses
review_body:
Personally, I feel like these look a bit weird on me–some people have commented that they look a bit small, and I have to agree. And it’s not like I have an oversized head or anything! At least I don’t think so. Aside from the slightly small size & the large-ish lens, they do a good job in reducing eye strain when looking at electronic screens for a long time.

It gives a slightly yellowish tint to everything, but that’s something you get used to pretty fast. The only thing that’s slightly distracting is when you look at a bright light with these on. The polarizing filter causes you to see double, giving it a funky effect. For computer screens and phones though, it doesn’t alter vision in any way, which is great. After using this for a month, I’ve experienced significantly less strained eyes after looking at a computer screen for an extended period of time.

Overall, aside from the fit being a bit on the small size, I like these glasses. They do what they advertise, and it even comes with a nice case. I can’t take off points for its fit & looks, since that’s a subjective matter (everyone has different size heads after all), and it does what it claims to do–at a reasonable price to boast.

5/5

product_title: Dewalt Tough System Drawer Unit
review_headline: A great design concept but it could be so much better
review_body:
I bought the cart and the three boxes, x-large, large and small. I didn't get a box with drawers so I can't comment on those. I can tell you that the people who are saying that this system isn't tough enough are absolutely right.

I'll start with the locking system. There is a bracket on the back of each box that allows the user to connect the boxes to the cart to prevent them from tumbling off of the cart in the event of going over a curb or some other similar situation. A great idea but here's where it goes wrong; I had the boxes heavily loaded and I forgot that I had them all "locked in" and connected to the cart and when I reached down and proceeded to lift the XL box off of it's mounts I felt a slight tug and then remembered that it had been attached to the cart via the bracket on the back of the box - but it wasn't attached any more because the screws that attached the bracket to the box had pulled out of the plastic that the box is made out of. As I see it there are two possibilities, either I'm superman or the bracket was mounted in a weak fashion. You can decide for yourself which is more apt to be the case.
These two screws have sheet metal threads and without much effort at all on my part they were surprisingly easy to rip right out of their sockets. I'll figure out a way to reattach the brackets but my method will be far more secure that the original. I'll have bolts that go completely through the back wall of the box and I'll make sure that there are either large washers or some sort of a backing plate on the inside to insure that the bracket will hold any time I forget that the boxes are locked to the cart.

The hardware should be much heavier duty than it is. The latches are big enough but they aren't as sturdy and heavy gauge as they should be. I can picture them being bent.
The side handles don't in any way inspire any confidence at all and obviously should be much stronger. I'm so afraid that I'll break them off that I've already installed a pair of auxiliary four inch wide trunk handles which I mounted below the originals and I use them instead in order to avoid breaking the original handles.

I hope somebody at Dewalt is paying attention. If you are I want to tell you that the basic design is pretty good (although it could be better) BUT you need to find a better quality plastic for the boxes. I see plastic all the time that would be more suitable, I'm sure we all do. The plastic I would look at first is the stuff that bulk cargo shipping containers are made out of. If you made half inch thick boxe out of that stuff that would truly be impressive. Surely there are people at DeWalt that know a lot more about plastic than I do but for some strange reason they made a poor choice. If a better, stronger plastic were used I would think that the support ribbing could be done away with which would free up more usable interior space. A 300 pound guy should be able to stand on a box like that and have confidence in it. And please, for crying out loud, beef up the hardware!ady installed a pair of auxiliary four inch wide trunk handles which I mounted below the originals and I use them instead in order to avoid breaking the original handles. He has used other brands in the past and the Tacwise is much nicer than others that he has used. It seems to just be higher quality and built better in construction.

It works great for any type of paper, plastic, or felt tacking that you need to do.

product_title: FSL Gunblock Earmuffs - 29dB Shooting Ear Protection
review_headline: Help Prevent Ear Damage from Noise.
review_body:
At first I did not understand how these were supposed to work. After some research I now grasp the concept behind these. They are not to get rid of noise from the environment but only to reduce. At first I was expecting these to block out all noise. I first put them on and could actually hear what people next to me talking with out any problems at all. Their voices were only slightly reduced in volume. So I had to do some research on why they were not blocking out the noise. Here is what I found out:

How does NRR change decibels of exposure?
When hearing protection is worn, your level of exposure to noise is based on the NRR rating of the protection device being used. Keep in mind, however, that while the NRR is measured in decibels, the hearing protector being used does not reduce the surrounding decibel level by the exact number of decibels associated with that protector’s NRR. For example, if you are at a rock concert where the level of noise exposure is 100 dB and you are wearing earplugs with an NRR 33dB, your level of exposure would not be reduced to 67 dB. Instead, to determine the actual amount of decibel deduction applied (when decibels are measured dBA which is the most common), you take the NRR number (in dB), subtract seven, and then divide by two. Given the previous example, your noise reduction equation would look like the following: (33-7)/2 = 13. This means that if you are at a rock concert with a level of noise exposure at 100 dB and you are wearing a hearing protector with an NRR 33 dB, your new level of noise exposure is 87 dB. If you are wearing a product with an NRR of 27 it would deduct 10 decibels (27-7/2=10).

So with that in mind 29-7/2 = 11 decibles of reduction from these ear muffs. These do perform well at reducing the incoming noise without doubt. They offer a decent level of protection to your ears if you are in a loud environment. For instance, a machine shop, firing ranges, or even a concert. I recommend these for sure if you are in a loud environment for your own protection. They are your ears and you should make sure to take care of them.

The design of the ear muffs are exceptional. They fold up and to a fairly small package to make them easy to transport. They adjust to just about anyones head. product_title: The Mud Glove 737a24
review_body:
I have extremely thin fingers that are still relatively long. I wear a ring size of 4; a standard size 7 ring can only fit comfortably on my thumb. As such, it's pretty hard to find gloves that will fit my hands, since glove sizes (as with other clothes) tend to scale up in all dimensions at the same time, so gloves with longer fingers feel like balloons on my hands and it's really hard to do any kind of more detailed work (I can hold gardening tools just fine, but transplanting cactus seedlings is nearly impossible).

I found a message board post somewhere asking about gardening gloves for people with thin but long fingers, and one poster mentioned that she has a ring size of 4 and found the size Small of these gloves to fit very well (and mentioned that the fingers on the extra small were too short). I couldn't find the slightest bit of information about what the sizes mean on these gloves (I even went to the Mud Gloves website, where the Sizes section had an asterisk next to it, but nowhere could I get measurements or any idea what that asterisk meant) but I figured that if someone else with the same problem liked these, I'd probably be okay with them too.

These are the best fitting gardening gloves I've found so far. The fingers could stand to be a little narrower, but it's much nicer than others I've tried. The only problem is that the sizing assumes a different proportion of finger lengths than I have. I've got perhaps a quarter inch of extra glove space ballooning around my ring finger, but my thumbnail is pushing up against the material pretty uncomfortably. I'd probably be okay if I keep my thumbnails short, but I definitely couldn't go down to the X-Small without my thumb being very uncomfortable.

For some general idea of measurements, my hand is about 6 3/4 inches from the crease at my wrist to the tip of my middle finger (not including the nail), and a little less than 3 inches across the palm.

I wish I knew of a company that would make custom gardening gloves perfectly aligned with my actual hand measurements, but for now, these are great.

UPDATE 09/16: The thumbnail pressing up against the end of the glove finally broke through, almost a year and a half after buying them. They've served me well otherwise, so I'm definitely buying another pair.ng gloves perfectly aligned with my actual hand measurements, but for now, these are great. product_title: Schrade SCHF3N Extreme Survival Full Tang Clip Point Fixed Blade Micarta Handle
review_body:
My first knife was a Schrade and I was baffled at how well it stood up to my neverending barrage of abuse.... With that in mind, I tried my best not to biased when searching for a good survival knife -- and I researched for hours on end to find a good one (overlapping into days, actually). Schrades SCHF3N fit the bill. Not only is it ridiculously cheap but it is very well made. It is .25 in thick (great for batoning), and is made of 440 Stainless Steel. Those two reasons alone are the reason why I bought this knife.

Now don't get me wrong. There are great Carbon blades out there (too many to list; ie; KaBar Becker BK2 [1095 cro-van carbon steel]). While they retain a great edge and are easier to sharpen, they are much more prone to rust. I wanted something that would stand the test of time. Sharpening might be a little hard, but so is life. This knife has a rust resistant metal, is thick enough to baton small logs and can take on whatever challenges lay wait. After much abuse, little wear and no signs of rust, it's easy to say that I love it and couldn't recomment it more.

(I would, however, recommend having a combination of knives. A Stainless Steel, A Carbon, and a good "bushcraft" knife, like a Morakniv Companion).

product_title: Howard Leight 1030110 Sync Noise-Blocking Stereo Earmuff
review_headline: Terrible quality, poor fit and inferior noise-blocking.
review_body: I would never buy these again, nor would I recommend them to anyone looking for noise-blocking or good quality sound reproduction. They are made of cheap plastic which easily scratches and thin metal wires. They are too small for my rather average-sized head and extremely uncomfortable to wear. It is unfortunate that they are advertised as "one-size fits all." They cut off the circulation to my ears and put pressure on my skull which renders them pretty much useless for periods of longer than 5 minutes or so. In the time that I have worn them, they inadequately block outside noise, especially low-pitched sounds such as human voices and some types of heavy machinery. They also inadequately block high-pitched noises such as beeping. This is likely due to a combination of poor fit (regardless of head size), flimsy construction, and a lack of acoustical engineering.

product_title: RIDGID 18-Volt X4 Hyper Lithium-Ion Cordless Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kit (3-Tool) with Radio
review_headline: Quality tools you'll want to use
review_body:
It's always been annoying to me that these manufacturers seem to make it impossible to buy just the drill and a battery. Everything is a package deal so they can relieve you of more of your cash. While researching, I kept saying "I don't need a darn impact driver!" When I spied this set in the low $200's range, I decided to give in and take the package deal. These Rigid guns look almost like they were made by Milwaukee. They seem to be very rugged and after a couple month's use, I can say they are excellent on the job. I prefer the LED to be placed up by the drive area, but the lower mount actually throws light just where you need it. Plus I have to admit, the impact driver has already been used quite a few times working on the bikes and cars. The radio seemed like a throwaway part of the package, but with the cell phone strap and AUX cable built in, it's also been put to use quite a bit.

Here's what I would change in this set: Make the radio double as a charge station. The other would be to substitute a work light for the radio.

Excellent buy and no regrets. I'm hoping the batteries last more than a year.

product_title: Heavy Duty Bench Vise , Forged - 360 Swivel Base with Lock, Anvil Top
review_headline: Customer Service (Scott)  is great. Wilton clone import, Poorly cast and weak.
review_body:
Big, heavy weight vise. I assume it's from China or maybe India. It is steel, not iron, so that's good. The casting is rough, and poorly finished, but it is a utility vise. It screws open and closed smoothly, and the jaws meet squarely every time. It has a nice big 4"anvil that will be useful. Wide mounting base. I expect it to last and it likely will if it doesn't crack in the first few uses. I'm the first reviewer, so I'll keep updating as I use it. This is a Wilton ws8 clone.

UPDATE: On the very first use, to grip some all thread to cut with a hacksaw, the base split as soon as I swiveled and tightened it down. I've never seen such poorly cast parts. The base ring just snapped in two pieces. There is no way this is cast steel, as advertised. Only low grade iron cracks like this. Turns out this vise is total junk. I am requesting a refund for this defective product. Let's see how the seller manages a refund. This is a heavy thing to mail.
Refund was completed for this item quickly and with no fuss. I sent three photos of the broken vise and the seller issued a full refund. I did not have to ship the broken item back. This seller has excellent customer service, and I would buy other products from them without reservation.

The seller agreed to a full refund for the broken vise after I sent photos of the damage/defective part. They were very nice and did not make a fuss about it. Overall I'm disaapointed in the product, but the customer service was very good. Thank you, Scott.

product_title: Milton 1/4" MNPT V Style High Flow Plug - Pack of 2
review_headline: You order brass, you get steel...
review_body:
I purchased a product clearly labeled "Milton Industries Inc. S-760 HI-Flo V-Style 1/4-Inch MNPT Brass Plug" and received a product called S-760-1 Steel Plug. Steel plugs are significantly cheaper to purchase than brass and they corrode. I returned the first shipment hoping it was a fluke and received the same steel plugs as an exchange item. Amazon needs to get this corrected. You are likely not going to receive brass plugs, but steel instead.

The V-style fittings are fantastic and the improvement over M and T fittings is very noticeable with high-consumption tools like impacts and grinders. You won't regret swapping for the V fittings, just don't count on getting brass fittings by purchasing this item. If you don't mind steel and paying more than you have to, order away. Hopefully Amazon will fix this issue and some brave soul who ordered these will be able to let us all know when they start shipping what they say they are again. Good luck!

product_title: Powernail Power Palm Pneumatic Palm Nailer
review_body:
The description of this tool is very lacking. This is less of a nail gun and more of a pneumatic hammer. You don't pull a trigger and boom, the nail is in, but rather it pounds it in. It actually sounds a bit like a miniature jack hammer. The results are similar to a hammer and nail without the risk of smacking your finger or the wood (or the wall). However, if you bend a cleat, they are much harder to pull out than a finish nail. In my brief experience with this tool, 18 gauge cleats will bend VERY easily, regardless of the wood you're using (I was installing Hevea). You will also need to set just about every cleat you drive, which means you'll still be using a hammer.

After using this more I've discovered that there are some tricks to make it more effective. First, to reduce bent cleats you have to not be tentative when driving the nail. If you try to drive it slowly, you'll probably bend it. Second, you can actually set the cleat pretty well with this tool, but you have to push it in and move it around on top of the cleat after the tool stops. This will pound it a few more times if you position it just right. Third, bent cleats are actually not that big of a deal if you don't try to pull them. If you have a pair of pliers you can grab the sides with the ridges and bend it back and forth towards the ridges. In my experience, the cleat will break off beneath the surface of the wood. You just need to pick a new spot for the next cleat then.
