product_title: Oshlun SBNF-054050 5-3/8-Inch 50 Tooth TCG Saw Blade with 20mm Arbor (5/8-Inch and 10mm Bushings) for Aluminum and Non Ferrous Metals
review_headline: Works great on table saw for cutting sheet aluminum
review_body:
Some reviews here have complained that the adapter supplied to reduce the 20mm hole to 5/8" did not fit well. I found it to be a snug fit (the way you would want it to be, to stay put), and it went on without any filing. With the blade on the original cardboard container, I placed the adapter ring over the hole, then tapped it into place using a small hammer. With the adapter in place, it fits perfectly on the 5/8" shaft of my Delta Contractor Saw, and there is no wobbling.

I bought this blade for one purpose: to cut thin sheets of aluminum (less than 1/8" thick) into precise rectangles. With a good fence (I have an Incra TS-LS3) and a properly aligned saw, it was very easy to get cuts to within 1/1000 of an inch, straight, and clean. The blade cuts cleanly and effortlessly, without applying any force that could destabilize the operation. A light touch-up with a very fine file is good for removing the few tiny burrs to achieve perfection.

My table saw can support 10" blades, and you may wonder why I got a blade with such a small diameter, when this aluminum-cutting blade is available in larger diameters. My reasoning is that smaller blades have significantly reduced speed of contact with the aluminum, by comparing the circumference of a 10" blade to this one. Cutting metal is best done with a slower saw. Since I cannot change the speed of the motor, a smaller blade has the same effect as reducing the speed to about 54%. It has to be raised to near the top of its range, but I do not expect to need to cut aluminum thicker than this blade can manage. If you have any comments about why this might not be a good idea, please let me know, but it seems right to me.

It is important to wear ear and eye protection when using this blade, although for what I am doing it is no louder than cutting wood with a wood blade.

product_title: HEAVY DUTY ROUTER TABLE STAND By Peachtree Woodworking - PW3372
review_body:
Just like gas station sushi, there are certain things you shouldn’t buy! This “Heavy Duty” router table isn’t heavy duty. I returned the product after receiving it without the leveling hardware, at my expense. After seeing the quality of the product, I would have returned it anyway. The construction of the square frame material is extremely thin (paper thin) aluminum. As the instructions show, the screws holding the whole thing together go through the sides of the THIN box tubing. When you tighten the screws, you quickly find the screws over-power the thin aluminum and they begin to compress the material, so you can’t tighten the screws very much or you’ll end up squishing the box into a bow-tie shaped pinch (see pictures). The screws and the ultra-thin aluminum are the only things holding the whole table leg system square. I think you’d find a problem with any lateral force causing the construction to warp or collapse. There’s no cross-bracing to help protect against this problem.

I wouldn’t buy another product from Peachtree again. The customer service in dealing with the return didn’t seem too concerned with my dissatisfaction. It cost half as much as the product to ship it back. Poor product value, poor customer service = Gas Station Sushi! Don’t do it. Get some real product and spend a little more with Rockler to get a REAL heavy duty router table (that’s what I did). Just the weight difference alone for the Rockler stand was about 30 pounds.

product_title: Stack-On Storage Cabinet
review_headline: Overpriced junk.... think twice before purchasing
review_body:
The LAST time I buy Stack-on product! I feel ripped off: $28 for this cheap, poorly designed cabinet makes me angry. The plastic outer cabinet has only two keyhole slots at the top corners, with no way to attach the bottom of the cabinet to the wall. So when the drawers stick, the cabinet wants to pull off the wall since it is just hanging from the top corners. The drawers are thin and flimsy, and resemble soft milk-jug plastic... several of mine came warped/twisted.

review_headline: The one I ordered looks just like this one back lit and all but it is ...
review_body: The one I ordered looks just like this one back lit and all but it is a Dr. Meter.  It came with the calibration powders and was easy enough to do but that was only good for one time.  So Ive been using mine about a month now and they say you should re calibrate every couple of weeks at least which I have not done.  I just happen to have some generic pool test strips which show the different colors on the bottle and ph numbers.  So I used some distilled water.  That test showed solid orange which relates to 6.8 PH. then I used the meter in the same water which also fluctuated between 6.8-6.95 so I feel like Im good. All Im doing is cloning anyway the system will be shut down in anothe 4-5 weeks most likely.  But for those new people of interest in hydroponics I advise you to just go ahead and get the meter.  Most everyone who gets the general hydroponics kit where you add a few drops and try to match up colors are not satisfied with that.  You will have a close color range but nothing definite. You want to know exactly where you are ,, thats what I did and wish I had just went straight for the meter. Just be sure you get one that is back lit like this one. I read up a good bit on this before getting the meter and it pays off.  Certain steps will help in the long run to keep it calibrated as evidently Ive been lucky enough to do. Follow directions but directions do not tell you to put the meter in the water first before you turn it on and read it,  then turn it off before you remove from the water do this every time it will keep you acurate.

product_title: BPA Free Disposable Poly PE Gloves
review_headline: Good For Handling Most Foods, A Bit on The Big Side For Me
review_body:
My husband and I both used these gloves for handling foods while cooking, especially when someone is a little under the weather and cooking (that would be me, since I am the main cook for my husband, son, and I. I washed my hands a billion times, but still didn't want to risk getting them sick.)
We both find that these gloves work rather well when handling breads, veggies, cheeses, deli meats, and mostly dry foods. When handling sticky or really wet foods, these gloves tend to slip a bit and don't work too well. In fact, I wouldn't really recommend these gloves for overly sticky or really moist foods.
I like to use these especially when I'm handling jalapenos, habanero peppers, and other hot peppers, onions, certain fruits, and more. They create a good barrier between those peppers and my fingers. Also great when handling chicken or fish (I'm a vegetarian, but I do make these sorts of foods for my family and I hate touching raw meats/poultry.)
They are single use/disposable.

These are good for cafeterias, catering, parties, fundraisers, bake offs, etc. They come with a great amount of gloves in one box too.

I received a box for reviewing purposes. All of the opinions stated here are solely based off of my own experience, as well as my husband's, with the product. No other compensation was received.

product_title: DEWALT DCS355B 20V XR Oscillating Multi-Tool | Battery Pack
review_headline: It took Dewalt sometime to get into the cordless oscillating market but it was worth the wait!
review_body:
This thing is awesome, it took Dewalt sometime to get into the cordless oscillating tool market and now I will never used my corded oscillating tool again! A couple things I noticed, in addition to the front LED it would be nice to have an additional LED or two on the sides of the tool when cutting with the blade set to the side. Also it would be nice to have tool free blade changed with ALL types of blades, I would guess this is a engineering issue since some blade attachments are VERY different, this tool requires an opening in the attachment point on the blade itself where some blades do not have this opening and will not allow for tool free installation. All Dewalt blades as well as some others brands allow for use of the tool free feature but some will require the included adapter and Allen wrench that said seems most brands are now moving to the 'tool free' style blades. I have read some users don't care for the variable speed trigger that this has over the variable speed dial other tools use, for me I prefer this type of trigger as it makes slowing and speeding up the blade MUCH easier and faster vs adjusting a dial.

Overall great little machine!

product_title: Quick Change Chuck for Porter Cable Router Models: 630, 690, 691, 693, 7518, 7519, 7536, 7537,
review_headline: This is a GREAT product! Will buy more of them. Worth every penny!
review_body: I bought two of these in separate occasions off ebay. I was interested in the ease of changing bits, having grown up in my Dads cabinet shop. There was a constant struggle with two wrenches and busted knuckles. After purchasing the chucks I began reading a few reviews that claimed they had wasted their money on thus tool. I shelved them for about a year and continued using factory collets and nuts and a Jacobs Power collet ( which I dearly love ) until recently. I think the success you gave with these chucks depends on the care your take initially when installing it on your router. My first effort was a PC 7539. I had some vibration initially and followed the mfrs recommendations on reducing or eliminating vibration. I moved the chuck in smaller increments than suggested by mfr. the manufacturer, figuring that if I took my time I would have better results. I was a little concerned by the comments of some that they had wasted their money by purchasing this item. I will say that it was more time consuming than I expected. I installed the first one on my PC 7539 and in just about 30 min or so, with a large profile bit in the router, I had it running smooth as butter. I was extremely pleased. About a week later I tackled my PC 890. I will note that it took me longer to smooth this one out as the PC 890 seemed more sensitive to moving the collet. There was a very narrow "window" of adjustment and with a little time and effort I was able to find the "Sweet Spot" and lock in on that point. There were some You Tube videos that were helpful also. I will GLADLY accept one of these chucks from any one who feels they are not a great product! If you put forth a little effort, you will have a great tool in your shop that makes bit changes a breeze.

review_body:
The end result was great using this. However, this mini kit does NOT have everything you need.

I recommend getting the Kreg screws to make it work as designed. They need to be self tapping wood screws, different lengths for different wood thickness, course threads for soft woods, fine thread for hard woods, and the head has to fit in the predrilled hole.

You will need a long, number 2 square head driver bit. A 3 1/2 inch Dewalt one from the local store worked, but a longer one would be a bit more safety margin against marring the surface of the wood.

The plugs to fill these oblong holes can be handy if they will be visible.

Use a screw clamp to hold the jig down while you drill. A spring clamp isn't strong enough.

Keep the directions with the kit because they give all the positioning measurements for various wood thickness.

product_title: iGaging AccuMarking Digital Wheel Marking Gauge + Depth Gauge + Height Gauge 3 in 1 Tool
review_headline: WHY??  WHY NOT!!  Great deal for the money.
review_body: The gauge is heavy and has a feel of quality.  It seems to be very accurate (down to half a thou it matches my other precision instruments).  If you want to scribe a line EXACTLY 0.25 inches from an edge, this is the tool to do it.  That being said, it's a little fussy to nail the adjustment (there is no micro-adjust like on a Glen-Drake TiteMark) but I found by tapping the end of the gauge with my finger, I can fairly reliably move it in thousandths,  Since this is a tool mainly for hand-tool woodworking (power tool users don't really need to scribe knife lines) it begs the question - WHY?  Again, it's a question of accuracy.  In one scenario - you might want to set a mortise, but you don' t have your fancy, double knife mortise gauge handy.  You can set one wall of the mortise, zero the readout there and move 3/8 (or whatever) over and scribe the other wall.  OR In the case where you are gauging off the thickness of another piece of wood, as you might for marking out dovetails, you might care less about the exact, down-to-a-thou measurement - UNLESS you need to repeat that measurement somewhere else and have already reset your gauge - THEN that digital readout might just be your best friend.  You can set the gauge right back to a known measurement and be certain that it's within .0005" - which is certainly close enough for even the finest woodworking.  In addition, if the battery dies (mine came with a battery, PLUS 2 spares) it still works just like a classic wheel marking gauge.  For the price, it's a very good deal.

review_body: I use this connected to my DWS520 track saw, DWS780 miter saw, & DWS745 table saw.  It's not perfect, but does a good job of catching most of the saw dust at the source. It also has 2 filters & every 45 seconds or so it switches from one to the other to blow the other out so the filters don't get clogged.  It's a bit of an investment, but I think it's worth it.  I wish the hose had a better storage system, but it does have an elastic strap to hold it to the vac after you wrap it around a few times.  Comes with a quick connect end that snaps onto the adapters or saws with a twist.

product_title: Klein Tools 55421BP-14 Tradesman Pro Organizer Backpack
review_body:
I purchased this pack about nine months ago . . . it looked like the best combo of a tool and laptop bag that I could find. I'm the phone and now network guy for a ski resort, so I needed to be able to carry my laptop securely, along with my tools, whether in the truck or on foot in the summer, or on skis in the winter when making service calls.
Pros:
-Sturdy Pack
-Laptop is well protected.
-Zippers work well.
-Hard case provided for glasses/goggles.
-Intimidates my coworkers when they heft it and realize what a beast it is to ski around with.
Cons:
-Heavy (the half-a-tire that is mounted on the bottom is great for protection but you pay with the extra weight)
-Tool Organization Options (I've gotten used to it's not very many/logical tools/screwdriver holders, but the main pocket would benefit from having more front-to-back space in it, as well as some other slots for additional tools).

With these cons, I couldn't give it five stars, but one of the guys on my team wants one just like it, so I'll be purchasing another one shortly.

product_title: Uvex S1933X-3 Skyper Blue Light Blocking Computer Glasses with SCT-Orange Lens
review_headline: Sleep better and get healthier with these goggles.
review_body:
These orange tinted glasses work amazingly to block out almost all blue light.

Backstory: My eyes would hurt the next day for some reason, and I did some research to find out it was because of lack of sleep.
But there was a good reason for this. It turns out that humans become more alert when exposed to blue light. During my night browsing on my phone, I was exposed to adequate amounts of blue light to tell my brain to slow down melatonin production. It became harder to sleep and I got more tired the next day. After buying these, I realized I could sleep much better and feel better the next day.

Also, I noticed that teenagers now a days have more chances of getting gray hair early.
Back then, there was not as much blue lights present to keep you from sleeping.
Now a days, we all like a little time to browse hour phones before we sleep, this is a bad habit because we are exposed to lights that tell us to be awake.

With these blu-blockers, you can effectively block out most of the blue light.

I HIGHLY recommend downloading a program called f.lux. It basically does what these glasses do. It turns the hue of your screen to a orange--ish tint and reduces amounts of blue light.
I believe this program is also available for Android phones, but not iOS phones because changing the screen color is a system level change and the unix system prevents that.

product_title: Zircon Leak Alert Electronic Water Detector
review_headline: What I most liked about these as compared to others is that they ...
review_body:
Bought these after doing due diligence. We'd been having backups on occasion when doing laundry and wanted to prevent overflow into lower level family room. Today it earned its keep. It went off with a loud alarm which we could hear on the floor above, even though there was only a small amount of water on the floor. I could turn off the washer in time to prevent a flood.
What I most liked about these as compared to others is that they lie flat (not upright as usually pictured), with the wire sensors in direct contact with the floor. No chance of knocking them over (by foot or animal). Since they are in direct contact with the ground, they sound immediately; no need to wait for the water to reach a certain depth. I understand that they float (no personal experience here) so the alarm will not be covered with water and thus muted. What these may not be good for is those situations where you want to set off the alarm before the water overflows a vessel such as a sump pump or a sink. Those situations may require an alarm with sensors tethered by cord to the alarm, so the sensor can be lowered into the opening. That said, it may also be possible to attach this one somehow, but that is for other reviewers to determine.
Some reviews have indicated that these alarms did not function at all. My unit is a month old and worked beautifully. That's all I can say for the moment.

Purchased with Amazon prime from ePathDirect and I received it with the head unscrewed and was not able to screw it back together. review_headline: Wouldnt it be so easy to tape a heavier item to make stay surounded ...

Where to start, had high hopes for this, thus far its a disapointment.
Open the package. Per usual the item was to one side with the bubble plastic to other sides. Wouldnt it be so easy to tape a heavier item to make stay surounded and protected, free tip to amazon.
The cap iron was off as well as the iron. Instant red flag since you know its been tossed around during shipping. Open the plastic bag to remove the contents and paints chips are everywhere from the iron scraping the inside of the plane. The iron is design funny too, as in the middle of the blade is cut out then going towards the bad its notch to accomdate the blade advancing. Inspecting the iron its damaged and dinged along the bevel.
Keep in mind there was no packing inside the product box, none. Didnt bother checking the iron to see how flat it was. Just for giggels decided to check the sole, a valley in the middle. Rather comicaly unhappy at this point since its not a cheap purchase. Decided to roll the dice and request a replacment. I dont have good expectations. Ill update and maybe take some pics. As a side note i dont expect veritas quality but for 80ish...i do expect better packaging and a little less work to make the items right. The iron is suspect and i bet would flex from the cap being tighten
**** update 2/22/2015
Received the replacement the box looked like it went through some rough shipping. So where to start at least everything was together the cap and iron all snug. The bad bits, the valley is there again, gap was more than I wanted to deal and really what sealed the return was the right wing also would need work. So I went ahead a ordered a Stanley Sweat heart line low angle block plan, was on sale (not sure about now) so with free shipping it was about 20 more than this block plane. I wait to post my update till after I received that item. The fit and finish is excellent there is a small valley in the middle .0015 from the middle point it extends along thelength of the sole for about .75inch. I don't mind working that out. The iron is A2 and the plane has a Norris adjuster. Was able to get very light shavings out of the box. Will be really excellent once its dialed in properly. Some thoughts: I didn't order the wood river L.A. plane due to complaints of the cap falling off and the irons are no longer A2. So for the money I'd say not to deal with iffy tool steel and random milling issue with that valley being large and the wing possibly being off. So pay abit more and get the quality you'd want for still a good price point.

product_title: 60" Hardwood Workbench with 4 Drawers
review_body: The quality of the wood and hardware are excellent. Everything fits well and assembles smoothly. The lower shelf has a protective laminate, as do the sides of the drawers. A couple of construction tips:    There is a tab on the sliding rails on the side of the drawers. Be sure to choose the sides so that this tab is at the front of the drawer.    Inserting the drawers is not all that easy. Be sure that the sliding elements are pushed to the front edge of the rails. Place the drawer in place and push it in as far as it will go, which will not be all the way. Pull the drawer out and push it back in a couple of times. To get the drawer all the way in, pull it out and slam it sharply closed. It will go all the way in and move smoothly and freely after doing this. Had to cut through walls consisting of 5/8 inch  sheet rock with outer layer coated with razor sharp wire mesh and 1/2 inch plaster. The corners reinforced with metal beading and nails. The BDCR20B cut through everything including 2x4 studs, large nails and etc. with relative ease. I used heavy duty demolition blades and the wire mesh dulled them pretty fast. But the saw itself worked more like a  more expensive and powerful corded model. The size and weight of this tool made the project less of a hassle. The batteries lasted a very long time in spite of the lengthier times required to cut through the mesh. Charging the batteries immediately after 1/2 to 1 hour use showed very little drain with exception of draining one completely during a four hour and near constant course of use. I have six batteries ready to go at all times!

product_title: Tuff Stuff Xtreme Portable Air Compressor 150psi High Volume- 35" and Larger Tires
review_body:
I had a couple of problems with the compressor out of the box. As soon as I took it out of its bag i noticed some broken black plastic in the bag. I looked at the cheap gauge on the hose and it was broken but still functional. I was not immediately impressed but I didn't want to hassle with returning it. Then I connected it for a test run. I'm glad that I did this before I got on trail. I flipped the switch and I got nothing. I could hear the tone of my car's engine change like something was drawing power, but the compressor did nothing. I flipped it off and adjusted the clamps and tried again, still nothing. I called Amazon to return it, Amazon was great but I had to wait to hear from the seller. After this I though that I would take a risk and see if the manufacturer miscolored the positive and negative. I crossed the polarities and it still didn't work but it tried to kick over.

After seeing this, I tried one more time with the original set up. This time it worked! I aired down my 33x12.5 15" tire to 5 psi and the compressor filled it to 35psi in 3 minutes. The gauge is inaccurate but I always carry a gauge that I can trust and will probably replace the hose in the future. The compressor itself is a little larger than I expected but I am happy with its size for the speed that it filled my tire. It also stayed relatively cool in that short period of time. I am confident that I can fill all of my tires in one cycle. I did not expect it to be perfect for the price.

Next we'll see how long it lasts.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Floral Knife, Red
review_headline: Great everyday pocket knife, despite specialized function
review_body: Overall excellent knife, with long handle that suits my large hands. I use it as an everyday pocket knife even though it is a purpose built floral and pruning tool. Love blade shape and the single-bevel edge, as it is only 15 degrees, meaning the overall cutting angle is very fine, as the opposing edge is flat. This contrasts to a standard double-bevel pocket knife, which equates to a "fat" 30 to 40 degree total angle, meaning more rugged, but makes slicing more difficult. Occasional honing is a snap using my extra-fine (green) DMT sharpener for reshaping the bevel side and assuring opposing side is flat, then finishing with a small ceramic rod to remove any feather edges. The blade has a very strong back spring and a positive stop, which means it is unlikely to fold back on your hand in use - a real safety feature. Materials are typical lifetime Swiss quality, stainless cutlery blade with aluminum liners and brass rivets. The only downside of a single bevel is they are slightly more prone to chipped edges if abused, vs double bevel, but after years of use, the knife is aging well!

product_title: California Air Tools CAT-4620A Ultra Quiet and Oil-Free 2.0 Hp 4.6-Gallon Aluminum Twin Tank Air Compressor
review_body:
Liked: Quiet, compact, 2.0 HP, large double aluminum tank
Disliked: Poor build quality!

The manufacturer appears they have zero quality control based on the unit i received.
IMO the Box arrived in decent shape and I don't blame anything on shipping. During unboxing I found a small broken plastic piece that I determined was from the power box lid. I found the unit was assembled poorly. The welds are horrible. You do get the recognizable odor of cheap Chinese tools from HF (I dont know what that smell actually is but people know what I'm talking about). The tank support and handle pipe was not welded vertically causing motor and air fitting contact, vibrations, and noise. The power supply box, motor and all the air lines are positioned and/or router poorly. It's so bad! See my photos which do NOT match California Air Tools photos. The power box is actually smashed through the motor (power box lid and side of motor broken)
No excuse for such poor quality control.

I want one that is built correctly! Maybe California Tools can step up and send one that matches the quality in their pictures. I believe it could be a nice machine.

I purchased the item based on specifications/features. I also like the way it looks .
Specs and Notes:

Ultra Quiet only 70 Decibels-I wouldn't say "ultra quiet" but noise level seems very low for what it is.

4.6 Gallon (Rust Free) Aluminum Tank -64 lbs-"Rust Free" sounds awesome. I like the silver paint scheme. The whole assembly is hefty @ 64 lbs. Its awkward when lifting from the handle. Naturally people will lift the unit with the heavy motor side closest to their body but this makes the air filters vulnerable to leg impacts. Another reviewer said they broke one, so be careful. Some may want the model with wheels.

NEW! (2014) Easy Start Valve. Allows for a no load start, for a low start up amp draw. Only 14-amps-
I hadthe newer model. After it filled the tanks it blew off air pressure between the tanks and pump.
Good idea but didn't work perfect. My garage has 15 amp breakers and this unit tripped the breaker twice with nothing else on the circuit. The Breaker tripped the second and third time the compressor kicked on but then ran 10 more times without any problem before I repackaged the item. Who knows if this will work with most 15 amp breakers. Some may need the lower HP model.
I'm considering a reorder hoping to get better build quality but I'm scared I can't get away with 14 amps on a 15 amp circuit.

Powerful 2.0 HP (Rated / Running) Motor on 2.0 HP- More Power! Tim "The Toolman" Grunt

product_title: SOG SOGfari 10" Machete MC04-N - Hardcased Black Tanto Blade w/ Saw Back, Rubber Handle, Nylon Sheath
review_headline: A must have for any outdoorsman.
review_body:
I own MANY machetes, tactical and survival knives, tomahawks, hatchets, and other blades -- but this is my favorite. I bought this machete on a whim and am SO glad I did. Like it's big brother, it is a true machete, but the size and tanto blade make it more usable than most.

It's like the perfect blend of a survival knife and a machete.

Unlike full size machete's, this is a functional blade on your belt. Full size machete's are just too large and heavy to wear on your belt. This has replaced my Gerber survival knife on my belt while on hikes and treks.

review_headline: these are nice casters and you'll be pleased if they're what you ...
review_body:
First off, these are nice casters and you'll be pleased if they're what you need.
However, in retrospect, I have some thoughts on that. If you're buying these for a tool stand, like a bench grinder or a router table like I was, then you may want one pair of casters to swivel and to lock, but the second pair to be fixed. So even if the other pair you ordered, locks, this pair still allows it's end of the stand to move around which I find to be a nuisance.
Notice the ones that came on your table-saw. One pair swivels and locks, the other pair is fixed and doesn't swivel. But maybe that's my bad, for taking Amazon's recommendation on "customers who bought this also bought this."
Another, maybe bigger consideration, be aware that the stud on these is not only metric, but the diameter is larger than the pre-drilled holes in most tool stands.
Again, unfortunately, Amazon, listed them under the "customers who bought this, also bought this", and unfortunately, I didn't double-check the size (which wasn't listed, anyway), and as you might guess they didn't fit the tool stand that I ordered. Maybe that was my bad, too, assuming that whoever had paired the two purchases had done their homework.
One other thing, you'll need a thinner-than-usual wrench to hold the nut at the bottom of the stud tight as you're tightening the nut on top against your tool stand leg. Or, when you finally find the right sized metric nuts, buy an extra as I did, and tighten it down to the existing nut as a spacer. Sorry if that's not clear.
Anyway, they're very nice if you can make them work

product_title: Dewalt D180004 Door Lock Installation Kit,
review_headline: This tool didn't survive the first operation!
review_body: I bought this kit because it's a high quality 'DeWalt' product, and I purchased it at a great price (i.e., good quality at a great price..). However, this is my first negative review, ever! I purchased this for locating and drilling the lockset holes in a solid pine door slab. Per the instructions, I started with the small 1" hole for the latch.  The plastic fixture design didn't allow for centering this hole because my solid wood door was slightly less than 1-3/8" thick. No problem, I just located the center and used my own bit to drill the hole. (So far, the tool is 0 for 1). But I did use the plastic fixture to drill the 2-1/8" hole.  The design allows for 2-3/8 and 2-3/4" centers -- good design. I used the arbor and the 2-1/8" hole --- the assembly almost lasted for the one hole, but not quite.  Anyway, the hole saw threads stripped, and now it's junk -- the arbor threads stripped and now it's junk. The arbor spins and the saw doesn't -- almost funny!  I see at least 5 Amazon reviews complaining about the same issue.  I just called DeWalt Customer Service and the guy said "sorry about that", but he would sent a note to the product manager.  (It's obvious to me the product manager knows all about this tool's performance.)  I know DeWalt makes good quality tools, but I hope I will never buy another tool with their name on it because of the customer service response, and that DeWalt stuck their name on this product.  The product I bought has a simple design defect -- or maybe its a manufacturing defect.  My arbor (there's only 1 in my kit) was not threaded all the way to the backing plate. So when you thread the saw, it stops approx 1/8" short of bottoming out. During the drilling operation (in a solid wood door with a corded drill that doesn't care), as a response to the resistance of the cutting action, the saw tends to cut its own threads on the arbor until the threads become stripped. A simple spacer washer would have prevented this failure. Note that the threaded section of the big hole saw (the saw in this kit that sees much more torque than the smaller saw) is only 1/8" thick -- only several complete threads for that thickness. ((Good saws, including DeWalt, have a much thicker base, or the hole is extruded to allow for many more threads, or they have holes for arbors with locking pins. Also note that the 1" saw (the saw that sees only a fraction of torque than the large saw)  has a much thicker base and many more threads, like a 'normal' good quality saw.)) Anyway, that's why we see all the complaints here. The guys can't get the saw off the arbor because it seized in the process of riding over the existing threads.  One 1/8" thick washer/spacer between the saw and arbor flange would have fixed this issue, but nothing will fix his "sorry, but I'll send a note to the manager..." response. product_title: Kreg KKS-BK Bench Klamp (Clamp Only)
review_headline: Great clamps - and even better customer service
review_body:
Bought a pair of these to use with a 72" Faztek T-slot extrusion which I will use as a heavy duty cutting guide. The clamps lock down very securely, with the handle on the rear of them adjusting the tension or clamping height. The screw on the bottom of the clamps fits the T-slot on my guide quite well, and the clamps come with a plastic shim that sticks to the bottom of them (almost like a washer for the screw) to act as a bearing so that they slide easily in the slot. Also included is a no-mar rubber pad to use with the clamp. All in all, a very well thought out and well built clamp.

As much as I love the clamps, I'm even more impressed with Kreg's customer support. I discovered the no-mar rubber pads were also a perfect fit for some other locking clamps I own (which never came with pads), so I reached out to their customer support to find out where I could buy additional pads for my clamps. Customer support was nice enough to mail me some of them at no charge! I will definitely look at Kreg first anytime I need woodworking clamps, jigs, etc...

product_title: 2017 EVERLAST PowerARC 160STH 160amp HF TIG Stick IGBT Welder 110/220 Dual Voltage
review_headline: The torch this came with was not like the picture
review_body:
The case this came in was damaged but that's not really important, 0 damage to the welder, not even a scratch. The torch this came with was not like the picture, which is a good thing. Its a much smaller, better torch. The arc is liquid smooth. The knobs are smooth and just feel solid as do all the buttons. The ground clamp is solid, never even got hot. The pressure gauge was not silver, kinda disappointed but it works perfectly. The manual was easy to follow. The tig torch cables where wrapped in some dark blue denim sleeve, glad its wrapped, kinda clashes with everything else though. Overall packaging was great, though I don't know how the case got damaged. Had to email the company to find out which foot pedal this uses (47k). Its not to heavy or big, very compact for its capabilities.

When I first opened it i got hit with that new welder smell, so good. Takes 3 different standard wrenches to connect all the gas, even the hose takes two different ones on each end. All the connections fit well, no give at all. From first arc to the last one I did, arc was just so smooth. Plugged in to a normal 110 socket in my wall, no problems what so ever.

This is an excellent first welder for anyone getting in or anyone who wants a portable. They put the key features to keep the price down and still cover the essentials. Its a very flexible and quality welder. I may be a fan now.

review_headline: As long as it doesn't disintegrate in my truck bed tool box over the next few years I'll be happy.
review_body: I was away from home for an extended period (months) and had the need for some \\"truck\\" tools to keep on my vehicle, since I didn't have access to my home tools and needed to do some work on my vehicle.  So, I purchased this set.  I didn't want to spend too much, since these were all duplicates, but I didn't want junk either.  This set is definitely not junk; the tools are of a surprisingly high quality given the price.  They will certainly get the job done.  What really sold me on this set was the selection of tools though; someone really put some thought into it.  Full-size screwdrivers (not just bits) , channel-locks, a crescent wrench, and needle nose pliers?  No other mechanic's socket set near that price range includes all those items, and they all come in handy.  I use tools for a living (electrician) so I appreciate that attention to detail.  These really are the essential tools for basic automotive/mechanical jobs.  Definitely worth the money and deserving of at least four stars.  The case is kind of cheesy, but all of those molded cases are.  As long as it doesn't disintegrate in my truck bed tool box over the next few years I'll be happy.

review_body:
Thus far, this is the best solution I've found for varying angles. Most pros will just use a flat knife, but using an angled trowel gives you the advantage of a nice, clean line. Also, using a straight knife doesn't force the compound into the corner as tightly, creating a much greater risk for pockets, which will dramatically weaken your joint.

The only problem with this trowel is that it is plastic and flexible. When you tighten up the angle, it forces the plane to skew slightly, and round the leading edge, leaving you with somewhat of a rounded corner.

I have a 1907 1-3/4 story house, so I have 45's EVERYWHERE, and being that it's an old house, none of the angles are uniform. That's why this makes a nice addition to my toolbox.

product_title: PEN VISE BY PEACHTREE WOODWORKING PW7003
review_headline: Works great, does the job better than anything else
review_body:
I much prefer this self-centering vise used on a drill press over drilling blanks on a lathe. It's far, far faster and easier, plus the fact that few of the small wood lathe tailstocks out there have enough quill travel to drill through a single barrel pen blank (much less anything longer) in one shot. In short, if you need a hole or center divot drilled precisely on center, this is the easiest and most convenient method you'll find.

Setup is quick and easy. I put a long 1/2" dowel pin in my drill chuck and tighten the vise's V-grooved jaws around it. You can also use a drill bit of sufficient diameter. Then, you clamp the vise to the table. Actually, I drilled a couple of holes in the baseplate so I could use the T-slots in my drill press table, which makes for a more secure setup than using clamps.

Overall, it's a quality tool built to last a lifetime and indeed works well, although I do have a couple of gripes with it.

One, there's enough play in the moving parts that the jaws and mechanism have some slop in them during the drilling operation, which allows the jaws and blank to shake forward and backward a bit. However, it doesn't seem to affect the drilled hole's diameter, roundness or placement accuracy. Where you set it up to drill is where it will drill. So, I can't deduct a star for that, it's just the obsessive-compulsive perfectionist machinist in me that wants everything to be flawlessly precise.

Two, the wood baseplate looks a bit rough after many, many acrylic blanks being drilled using water sprayed on the drill as a coolant/lubricant. The finish is still intact but obviously isn't waterproof, and the wood doesn't appear to have warped despite all the prolonged water contact. So again, I can't deduct a star for that, although I'd have gladly paid more for a cast aluminum base of similar construction to the jaws and spacer blocks. But all in all, I love this tool and highly recommend it for its excellent function, convenience and ease of setup and use, and overall quality construction.unction, convenience and ease of setup and use, and overall quality construction.

product_title: Cut Resistant Gloves by Stark Safe (1 Pair ) Food Grade Level 5 Protection, Safety Kitchen Cut Gloves for Fish Fillet Processing, Oyster Shucking, Mandolin Slicing, Meat Cutting and Wood Carving
review_headline: Husband uses them to work with aluminum and they put my mind at ease!
review_body:
My husband has been taking cans from the soda he drinks, washing them and cutting them down to up-cycle them into things that he is trying to make, I guess sculpture style on a small scale is how I would best describe it. I've actually been worrying that he was going to cut himself because aluminum cans are easy to cut and work with but also very slick, hard to grip and easy to cut yourself on as well. When the opportunity came up to get these gloves free* to review I thought that they would be just what I needed to relieve myself of the worry I have.

I received the XL size to try and they fit both me and my husband well. I have big hands for a woman, and his are only a bit bigger so definitely these fit well on our hands. They were not too snug or loose and the stretch in them was good enough to keep them snug on our fingers without being too tight. Make sure you are checking the sizing and order the right size for your hands and needs.

Since the main purpose of these is for kitchen use after trying them on to see how they fit I took them back off, laid them down and used a kitchen knife to slide against these to see how they did. Now they are resistant so obviously they can be cut if you use too much pressure so I didn't exaggerate the pressure. I used the pressure you would use cutting through soft meat or veggies and they didn't get a mark. So I put them on and very scared I did the same thing and they didn't cut that time either. Now a lot of pressure or a stabbing motion may cut them so I don't recommend purposely testing these out and risking cutting yourself, but just for a basic layer of protection I think they would work just fine. I'm a klutz and do find I easily knick myself while cutting things so I think these would save me from all the small knicks I don't notice until later when I put on lotion or hand sanitizer and woooziers!

Hubby has been using them while cutting apart cans and working on his projects and he said that he likes how they fit well enough that he has full use of all of his fingers on both hands. They don't feel big and lumpy like some gloves do when you wear them making it hard to do things with your fingers. The gloves help him get a better grip on the aluminum as he's working with it and though the aluminum edges have touched his hands he hasn't experienced any cuts or knicks since using these. He was getting some knicks and cuts when he was working with the aluminum barehanded. He said that he is glad I got him these gloves and he will continue to use them while working with the aluminum to keep his hands safe and make me feel better.

product_title: First Alert 2-in-1 Z-Wave Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Alarm
review_headline: Doesn't work with Vera 3 or Home Genie
review_body:
It detects smoke (CRC smoke test) and provides an audible alarm... but a $15 detector can do that.

Z-Wave functionality is sorely lacking. Unable to get Mi Casa Vera 3 UI5 to receive detection alerts (no help from Mi Casa - their response time varies from a week to not at all). Unable to get Home Genie to receive alerts from device: "Alarm.Status" signal would go to 255 during a test then to 0. product_title: Bosch 4100-09 10-Inch Worksite Table Saw with Gravity-Rise Stand
review_body:
I just returned my 4100 (purchased at a big box store) for 2 main reasons:
#1 - the biggest issue is that you are not able to adjust the blade parallel to the miter slot using the adjustment screws. Apparently the design of the saw changed from the 4000 model to the 4100. The 4000 did allow adjustment of the blade, but with the design change, the 4100 does not allow adjustment. The screws are still there, and a description of how to adjust the blade is in the manual, but tightening the screws takes the blade back to the exact same position. Bosch tech support confirmed that no adjustment is allowed with the 4100 and that the adjustment instructions should be removed from the 4100 manual. For a $600 saw I would expect that adjustment would be allowed. From the factory, mine was off 0.035 inches! If I wanted crooked cuts, I'd buy a $150 saw.
#2 - the miter gauge is pretty sloppy in the slot, but apparently that could be fixed with a nice after market miter gauge.
Some nice points of the saw are the gravity rise stand - that's excellent. And the storage areas for the fence and miter are nice. But, the main use for a quality saw is a nice cut, and with this saw you're stuck with the luck of the draw of how it came from the factory. If you happen to get a good saw that's in alignment, if it ever goes out of alignment, you're screwed.

product_title: Fein 72293768090 Top (2013) Kit MultiMaster Oscillating Multi-Tool
review_headline: Tool is solid build but the Fein blades are not :-)
review_body: I bought a FMM250q top set(sn. 2014.03XXXXXX) plus 6 extra Fein blades from toolnut for $200 shipped. Before I ended up with Fein I bought a much cheaper dremel MM20 2.5A tool. That tool is quite but not very powerful and finally returned it due to the saw blade went out extremely quickly. I only cut about 10 feet then the blade ruined on dremel. What I'm doing is to fix my floating bamboo floor that don't have enough expansion space. The floor went underneath the Sheetrock, so I have to use this tool to cut a deep trench and then use chisel to rip the bamboo out. The Fein feels really solid and very powerful.  This is made for construction not for hobby. Fein is louder, in the corner of the room my ears hurt after several minutes of continues use. I'd guess an earplug is needed for daily use. I ruined 2 BIM wood blades for 3 rooms. That's why I rated 4 stars. This might not be fair since underneath my floating bamboo floor it is the concrete. The blade tips will hit the concrete sooner or later, and eventually the whole blade became bald. Anyway, the ruined the blades can still be grind to flat to serve as a scraper or be sharpened to be knife. I found the material on the blades are very good.    The case is very well build and designed. The handle is very cleverly designed. It can be hide by roll to one side. You have 3 position to grab the tool box. Either sides or pull the handle to the middle to lift it. I like this design very much. There is one problem inside the box. They used black foam to hold the tool but the foam on the right side to support the tool is much thinner then the left side. On mine, the foam on the right side broke during the shipment.    Since the blades of Fein is more expansive and behaved not much better for me as dremel blade, so I'd like to rated 4 stars.    My choice of the multitool order was Milwaukee, Bosch, Makita and Fein. Milwaukee doesn't have a corded version. Bosch doesn't have a kit with as many as blades as Fein at this price. For Markita, Homedepot didn't want to honor a 20% discount from a smaller competitor. So I ended up with the original Fein. I think I made a right choice on buying the top set with extra 6 blades. Buying separately will cost a lot more.    The tool less blade exchange works fine for me. You need to have a little bit of strength and do it SLOWLY for the first several blade changes. As a safety rule, wearing a glove is always help especially if you are not a careful person. My 13 years old son did it too fast and no glove, so it hurt him a little. My 8 years son is fine with the blade change since he did it slow ^_^.    I'm a DIY for home improvements. I did many things in my house. I like Milwaukee and Bosch tools. Bosch blades always last a long time for me. Every Bosch saber saw blade can let me cut several hundred feet of bamboo floor. Bosch has an universal saw blade for multitool. So I'd guess their tool should as good as Fein or maybe even better when consider the blades.    I just saw Bosch has a \\"Oscillating Multi Tool Adapter\\". Based on HD reviews, 2 people claim that it works for Fein to use bosch blades. I'm going to get one to open the door for bosch blades. I noticed that some of the Fein blades I own have both Fein and other type of interface(maybe that's OIS). It is interesting to see the competition bring us benefit of both Fein and Bosch.     Wow! We can have either Fein or Bosch and cross use their blades. This might not be good for Fein since Bosch is fairly large to compete with.

product_title: Black & Decker SZ360 3.6-Volt NiCad Cordless Power Scissors
review_headline: ... had these scissors for over two years now and love them. They've breezed thru fabrics from stiff denim ...
review_body:
I've had these scissors for over two years now and love them.They've breezed thru fabrics from stiff denim to silk without problems. Two items to note while cutting: be sure that all layers of fabric are within the blades or only the top layer is cut, and the blades need to face the direction you wish to cut if you want a smooth cut. (I've had bad cuts trying to cut sideways on a collar facing, but if the blades point toward the curve, the cut is smooth.) I've jammed pins in the blades without damage to the scissors & my finger got in the blades once without a cut or bruise.

I'll probably need new blades eventually or a new battery; I'll price it out and decide whether to buy new scissors or the parts. These scissors have a permanent home in my sewing room until they're no longer available.

UPDATE 2/26/15

My original scissors started shredding fabric instead of cutting. I decided to buy a new set rather than replace batteries and blades. PLEASE BE AWARE that newer models have a change in design that is not addressed in the owner's manual. Look at where the blades attach to the scissors; this is gray and has an unlock icon. Initially I thought this unlock icon is for blade changing--nope! I had to press the unlock icon and have the safety lock forward in order to start the scissors. I had charged them for 3 days & the scissors wouldn't start; I thought the scissors shipped with a bad battery, so I went to the Black & Decker site to complain. There I found a PDF flyer that stated if the blades get jammed, the unit won't start until this unlock icon is pushed. Hmmm, I thought: maybe the blades jammed in transit, so I pushed the unlock icon & the scissors started. I don't know if this must be done with each use, or initially. In any case, at least I know the scissors work.

product_title: Gladiator GAWB66BAWG 66.5-Inch Bamboo Modular Workbench
review_headline: This is garage sale material and very substandard for new merchandise
review_body:
Disappointed with the wood surface. Because of that this product is what you would expect to get from a garage sale. As new merchandise it is substandard.

The bench was easy and quick to put together. The metal frame appears to be very sturdy and highly adjustable. But the condition of the wood surface was a total disgrace.

On the bottom large chunks of the wood were gouged out. The wood had a lot of cracks and splinters. I can understand the underside not being perfect. But it was in awful condition.

On the top of the work surface there were similar, but not so severe problems. The most troubling problem was that there were sizable gaps between the laminated strips that make up the surface.

I filled in the cracks and gouges on the top and bottom side of the wood surface with wood filler. Then I sanded it down and resealed it.

However, I bought this thing new and paid a lot of money for it. If I wanted to do all this work I could have bought the parts separately and built the bench myself.

product_title: Powerextra High Capacity 4500mAh for Makita 18v Battery BL1830 BL1815 194205-3 194309-1 LXT400
review_headline: Bring those LXT saws back to life! This pack is a great deal!
review_body:
So, I was skeptical, having never bought an "off brand" battery pack before. My original 3amp Makita packs are 4 years old and are dying. I needed to replace them, and when I saw a 4.5amp pack at this price, I had to give it a try, and the performance blew me away!

The 4.5amp pack last longer, but it also seems to deliver more power to my saws. I have the 6.5" circular saw and I had not used it in some time because my packs couldn't seem to muster enough power to run it at full power, but this got the job done; I had forgotten how that saw was supposed to sound! If you have any of the LXT saws and have been frustrated with anemic performance, grab this pack.

I don't really notice a difference in the power of my drill or impact driver, but my grinder and circular saw definitely seem more peppy with this battery.

Also, the manufacturer says you should run it completely down before the first several charges so that it will charge properly thereafter. You may have a tough time getting that pack to run down though! It holds a charge forever, which makes sense since it is 50% larger capacity than even the 3amp packs which last a good long while themselves.

For this price, are you kidding me? What a deal! I give it 5 stars. I'll come back and update how it's doing in 6 months or so and then again at a year too.

product_title: TEKTON 6725 Punch and Chisel Set, 7-Piece
review_headline: Tekton tools are the best discount tools on the market
review_body:
I have been rebuilding my tool collection as of late. I have always been a Craftsman guy, I grew up with that Made in USA brand. But after about 5 years since my last trip, image my surprise to see Made in China on half there items. I was ready to cry, cursing Wally World the whole time. Well for Christmas I received a $100 gift card for my favorite store, Amazon, I started researching some other tool brands. I came across Tekton and decided on the good reviews, and no long caring about China made (since everything is now), I loaded up my cart with about $150 worth of Tekton tools. A dead blow hammer, chisel set, file set, oil filter wrench, snap ring pliers, digital tire guage, pick set and a few others. The same tools with my favorite brand would have cost maybe a third or so more. I must say, for what they are the quality is amazing and every bit as good as Stanley made or Craftsman's non-professional line (tools in the store). So in conclusion, whenever I need a critical specialty tool I will look to Tekton made tools; they are probably the best for the price you can find...

Sharing this on all the Tekton products I purchased.

product_title: All in One Clamp A-50 50-Inch Grip Clamp Guide w/T-track
review_headline: Great Product, but get to know it before you use it.
review_body:
First off I really like this product. I purchased it to use in ripping more than 20 4' x 8' sheets of various product involved in a large closet organizer project. Prior to this product I would have been forced to use a table saw or clamps and a straight piece of lumber to guide a circular saw.

The main advantage of using the 50-50 Clamp Guide is that it is quick. I've done the clamps and lumber bit before, but it's tedious. Not to mention not always so accurate or stable during a cut. This guide allows one to make your measurements, then place the clamps adjacent to the marks (allowing for your saw's guide plate) and then simply clamp the bar by pressing down on one lever.

Of course with any long cut one needs to make sure there is no movement, and that is what is best about this guide. Once getting the hang of using the clamp, the device stays put. I never had an instance of this clamp / guide moving on me during a cut. I can't say that about lumber and clamps.

There are a couple of tricks that one must understand before getting this thing works at its best.
(1) The first is that one must work both ends of the guide when clamping.
After aligning the clamp bar next to one's marks, the far end of the clamp must be set tight next to the material. This requires sliding the "clamp mechanism" up next to your material, using your fingers to slide it in the Guides underside channel No big deal since you need to be sure the guide is aligned next to your dimension mark anyway. This means one can't operate the guide from the lever end only. I found this to be perfectly acceptable since I had to line up the guide with the dimension mark anyway.
(2) Second. the lever only needs to be tightened one quarter of a rotation. from Vertical (Up) to Horizontal or Horizontal to Vertical (Down). Over tightening doesn't make the clamp more secure, it only stresses the clamp mechanism, which can damage it. I learned this thru experience, and while I marred the clamp mechanism by over tightening, the Guide still produces a solid clamp and secure guide at all times.

Once these points are understood and utilized, the clamp is extremely easy to use and I found myself using it on smaller material which previously I might have put on the table saw.

Oh, one last thing, about getting square cuts. Absolutely no problem, as long as your measurements are good and you utilize a carpenter's square as a guide for placing the "Clamp Guide". I have no problem with this - I can't foresee any situation where I would be ripping a 4' 8' sheet for a finish dimension, without making detailed measurements including a square. As a result, I had no wasted material out of all of the sheets I purchased for this project. To me this means this Clamp Guide was a good investment.

review_headline: I am giving this set 4 stars because it is without a doubt a beautiful set with high quality workmanship
review_body: I just received this item today and imagine my surprise when I opened it up and saw that all the bits were in 5 little plastic bags that were not labeled. The only thing that indicated what bit was what size was the markings on the bit. Remember these are precision bits so the lettering is very tiny. I had to use my glasses and a flashlight for this one. After about 45 minutes of locating each bits individual slot and ensuring they were in proper order, I found that I had received 2 duplicate bits. This was very unfortunate and very disappointing. I purchased this item from Amazon directly in hopes that I wouldn't have any issues. Now I'm faced with the decision of returning it or ignoring the mess up. I use these tools for computers and hobbies. I am retired so I don't use them for work. If I did use them for a job, I would definitely return them. I am giving this set 4 stars because it is without a doubt a beautiful set with high quality workmanship. I labored in choosing several different sets from different manufacturer's before choosing this one. I realize that it is not Amazon's fault and I only hope that Wiha pays closer attention to quality control with their merchandise. If I was the engineer that designed this beautiful set, I would be very angry if I found out that my product wasn't being packaged properly.

product_title: 3M Peltor Optime
review_headline: Does what I got it for
review_body:
I use this for when I have migraines or am otherwise in need of the world just shutting up for a while. It's excellent for reducing the volume of a TV show, film, etc., and it takes the top and bottom off of nearly every sound that actually happens inside my house, but you can still hear sharp or heavy sounds (my sister saying my name, the clackity-clack of my keyboard, etc.) It is a little bit harder to understand conversational speech than when using the 3M OCS1135 Ear Soft Yellow Neons Earplugs; but I only want to use these things when it's just plain too loud to think, so it's a basically an OK tradeoff.

I recommend doubling up with earplugs if you really want peace and quiet, in any case. If there's a thunderstorm half a mile away, you will definitely hear the thunder, and if you have kids screaming in your house, you'll notice. It's not a "seen and not heard" device - the effect is more like what happens when kids actually use their indoor voices for once, or are in a well-insulated basement with you on the second floor.

Oh, and it's very difficult to turn onto your side and read in bed, with these things on. I'm not saying that anyone would buy these thinking that they would want to do this, but it's something I keep surprising myself with. It also makes a tight fit with my prescription glasses, and messes up the fit of my CPAP mask, and there's no hope of wearing nearly any of my cute hats with it even before you account for the eye-popping color problem (you're going to have a heart attack and die of not surprised, right?)

product_title: Uxcell Golden Anti-Slip Handle Steel Blade Oil Feed Glass Cutter Tool
review_headline: Initially cut great but then performance degraded....
review_body: I had never cut glass before and so I purchased this glass cutter based upon price (cheap) and reviews.  I watched several youtube vids to get the gist of how to use this cutter and proceeded to practice on some broken mirror pieces.  From the very first everything went perfectly... I was making straight scores that broke easily and perfectly along the score... every, single time.  So with confidence I started to make the \\"money\\" cuts on larger, more expensive mirror pieces (all were 1/8\\" thick mirror, same glass as the scrap practice pieces).  The first several cuts went okay but then one cut went bad and progressively the successive cuts got worse with more and more breaks deviating from the scoreline... and it just kept getting worse to the point of destroying mirror after mirror.  I was perplexed, frustrated and it was getting expensive.  So when I carefully examined the wheel, it appeared to be a little worn (not really pointed at the tip) and it was apparent that the wheel doesn't turn at all... and never did and never will.  I really don't know if these wheels are suppose to rotate or not but when I look at pictures of more expensive glass cutters, they all appear to have a screw or axle of some sort for the wheel to ride on but all the really cheap ones (these that sell for under $5) don't.  In addition, though I only used oil and never any water to cut, my particular glass cutter showed some rust at the end of it... it must have been there from the start but unfortunately since I didn't inspect it looking specifically for rust when it first arrived so I don't really know if it was already there or not.  Try as I might, I simply can NOT get the wheel to rotate and looking at this cutter I'm not even sure its built to be able to rotate.  This cutter is too darn cheap to even think about bothering to return it so I think I'll do what I should have done in the first place and that is to check down at my local home improvement center for something that doesn't have surface rust and insure that it has a carbide wheel that actually rotates.    Other thoughts:  Did I just get a lemon?  After careful inspection of the photo above, I don't think so... the one in the pix doesn't appear to have an axle either, it looks exactly like the one I received (except without the surface rust in and around the tip).  The \\"carbide\\" tip doesn't have a well defined point (edge).  I've got to believe the cutter I received was what everyone else got too and not defective.  If I had written my review after making the practice cuts and the first two real mirror cuts, I too would have given it 5 stars and praised it for being cheap and yet still getting the job done but... unfortunately after attempting to custom cut 1/8\\" thick mirrors and ruining quite a few with subsequent progressively poorer and poorer cuts my opinion of the value of this tool has been down-graded substantially to the point where I now feel compelled to write this one star review.  I find it hard to believe others who have reviewed this cutter here have cut more than just a few pieces of glass before they wrote their review... but perhaps I did just get a lemon... I don't know.    Update (12/7/14): My suspicions have now been confirmed... the wheel is suppose to freely rotate.  I purchased a glass cutter from my local home improvement center for $4.22 (that includes sales tax) its carbide wheel is larger, sharper and freely rotates. Earlier today I cut up 9 mirrors with this new glass cutter (each mirror requires about a dozen individual cuts to complete and many of those cuts are on a curve) and every single score snapped off perfectly, exactly like what I saw the professionals doing in the youtube videos... it is consistent and soooo easy to do now.  Bottom line... my one star rating is accurate based upon what I received.

product_title: Coast HP1 Focusing 190 Lumen LED Flashlight
review_headline: After testing, I definitely recommend the HP1
review_body:
As a police officer and Commercial helicopter pilot, I play with high end toys.
This is an especially surprising light. If it was handed to me not knowing the brand or price, after using it I would say it's a $39-$49 tool.
I don not have longevity testing to report. Only 1 night of test and evaluation. I bought mine and have not been offer a damn thing to write this review.

The housing in stout with a better than many finish over well cut knurling (diamond texture).
The length & diameter is a perfect balance of small enough for pocket fit, and sizable enough to confidently hold and manipulate.
The Clip is strong and removable with (2) small phillips.
Tail cap switch is excellent in that it has lots of "ON" position travel before clicking. This allows well controlled momentary on/off and signaling.

I feel the light is accurately rated at 220 Lumens and the projection is clean.
The adjustable thrown from Spot to Flood is smooth and easy to use with the right amount of friction.
What stands out in particular with this light is the wide angle flood WITH NO DARK SPOTS.
At a 40' distance on flood it produced a 75'-80' beam that was clean and crisp with no spots.

I will order a handful of these and leave my $100+ lights in my go bag.

product_title: TEKTON 3/8-Inch Drive Extra Long Hex Bit Socket Set, Metric, 3 mm - 10 mm, 7-Sockets | 1363
review_body:
I'll honest and say that I've never been much of a tool guy, but I've bought more tools this past year than I have in the last decade. This Tekton Extra Long Hex Bit kit is the latest purchase I made, and it was for a very specific purpose. I was trying to change out the grip on an AR-15 with an aftermarket one, and you have to go in the bottom of the grip to reach the hex screw at the end. I had a large set of long hex keys in a nice box, but they were just a bit short in getting the hex key tightened after I put on the replacement grip. When I got the screw tightened about halfway, the L-shape end of the hex key was bumping into the bottom of the grip so I couldn't turn it any more. I ordered these, put the size bit I needed on a ratcheting screwdriver and it worked perfectly! I can't say that this is an item that I have needed ever needed before, but now that I'm doing some of my own work on my "toys", I'm sure it'll come in handy in the future. And, there's something to be said about having the perfect tool for the job.

The kit has great quality, it's well organized with the most popular sizes, and I can keep the bits readily available with the handy box. Considering the relatively low price, I think the value of this kit is great especially for those of us just starting out and only needing these specific tools intermittently.

product_title: Silky Professional 177-39 Telescoping Landscaping Pole Saw Hayauchi 390 12-Feet
review_headline: I Should Have Ordered A 21 Footer--Well Worth It For A Small Initial Investment
review_body:
I have owned and used three different Silky pruning saws and have been extremely satisfied with their durable construction and efficient design. Since I'm in my mid-60's, anything that simplifies my trimming chores and reduces the time spent doing them is a great benefit. The combination of light weight, strong and properly designed materials, and sharp and efficient Japanese blades makes hard work quite a bit easier to complete.

I have had three other pole saws prior to the Hayauchi 390. Two of them were your average retail item that weren't properly designed, were not durable, and were heavy to lift and use properly. They both sit outside in my shed. The third one was a power pruner by a notable manufacturer that is essentially a small chainsaw on a pole. While strong and properly engineered, the weight and lack of balance made it a real challenge to use, plus the proper use and maintenance of another chainsaw makes things more complicated and potentially dangerous. That turned out to be a very expensive mistake.

The Silky Hayauchi stays rigid even when the pole is extended to its twelve foot maximum. The pole design has four attachment points which provide rigidity and the hollow aluminum shaft is sturdy enough that very little flex is experienced. The shaft itself is wrapped so that you can maintain a good grip even when wearing gloves. To cap it off, the blade is sharp and well-balanced, easily pulling through anything once the proper angle is selected. You've got to try this thing, it works great!

I do have one regret. I thought that a 12 foot pole saw would probably push the laws of physics far enough that anything longer would not work as well. After using this Hayauchi long enough to have to order a new blade, I realize that the smart design and quality materials would have made a 21 footer even more useful. The increased reach and usefulness is well worth the small extra investment.

product_title: Arrow Fastener T50 Heavy-Duty Staple Gun Tacker
review_body: *** 2015-02-09 Update ***  Works Great After Adjustment    I got curious one day and decided to see what exactly was causing staples to jam in the new T50 I purchased. I disassembled the bottom of the stapler and checked to see if everything fit correctly. All the parts and their placement seemed to be in order. I then decided to slide some staples down the rail used to hold and align the staples. Using a full 'clip' of staples everything seemed to work fine -- I was able to slide the clip back and forth without issue.     I then separated 10 individual staples from the clip and placed them onto the rail. I used the spring-loaded staple pusher to slowly and carefully push the individual staples down the rail as a group. When the group got near the driving end (stapling end) of the rail I noticed a problem. The first couple of staples slid just fine, but the next one hung up and caused a jam. I repeated this test several times reordering the individual staples. Sometimes the first staple would jam, while other times most of the staples would slide through before a jam occurred.     At first I thought it might be a problem with the staples, but they all seemed to be identical, unbent, and undamaged. Upon closer inspection I noticed that the gap between one side of the rail and the center of the rail was narrower than the other side -- this is where the staples were hanging. I used a flat-headed screwdriver to bend out the side of the rail until all the individual staples would slide without hanging. I then reassembled the gun and it worked without jamming.    I loaned the gun to a person who is recovering a living room couch. I warned this person about the jamming issue I had and told her to let me know if she has any problem. The couch is now almost completed and the gun didn't jam a single time. We estimate hundreds of staples have now been run through the gun without issue.    Consequently, I've adjusted my rating on the T-50 from 1 star to three stars. I still think there is a quality control issue with this stapler (hence all the negative reviews) that customers shouldn't have to remedy themselves. Once I resolved the misaligned rail problem, however, the stapler works better than the old T50 I replaced. If you feel up to it, you may want to try to repair your stapler the same way I did.      *** 2014-11-16 Review ***  Another Victim Of Corporate Shortsightedness    I inherited a T-50 from my father that he bought back in the late 1960s or early 1970s. That stapler went through hell and back and always performed great until the last few months. Cleaning and lubricating it has no effect -- it's simply worn out. Thinking what I great stapler it was I purchased a new T-50, but what a disappointment. The new unit jammed after only 5 staples. I had to take it apart to free the jam. I inserted another rail of Arrow staples and it jammed up again after about 10 staples. The nickel plating covering this thing is also flaking off.    Most likely Arrow is using the same tooling in their manufacturing process that they have been using for the last 40 years. Manufacturers do this in order to save the expense of having to upgrade worn out tooling. They then \\"bin\\" each unit produced according to how close it comes to design tolerances. In other words, the units that come the closest to design are given a particular model number -- and higher price -- than those furthest out of tolerance. I suspect the T-50s are the units with the most variation from design tolerances while the model T-50PBN, for example, is closer to design specifications. (Thus it gets better reviews and commands a higher price.)    A former great stapler model is now a piece of junk. I think I can hear the sound of \\"Taps\\" being played in the distance...    ...thanks for reading.

review_body:

This is a very easy to use tool that has practical applications for a variety of uses. The specific use for my model involves traffic collision reconstruction, and diagramming of specific locations to include where items are located, and were specific objects are in relation to fix objects. This measuring wheel is very convenient to transport to and fro, especially as it comes with its own carrying case/backpack.

The measuring wheel collapses so that it does not take up much storage room. Use of the measuring wheel requires very little training. A quick review of the instructions let you know all you need to confront this tool to use. It doesn't measure and feet and inches, which is all I need but may not suit the needs of others. For my purposes, the fact that this wheel can measure distances while transitioning over curbs, sidewalks, and or lawns makes it very handy. Although the brake on the handle enhances the level of precision, you must be aware of the reset button so that you do not confuse the two. This is a well-constructed tool that will come in incredibly handy for people in a variety of professions that require very accurate measurements.

This device comes with a two-year warranty, which is much appreciated. It seems sturdy and even has a cool little kickstand so that you can walk away for a moment if you need to and come back to the exact same spot where you left it. I can drive about 8 nails with it set on 100PSI (driving 3" nails into pressure treated wood) before the compressor comes on. product_title: Niji Roll Multi-purpose Pouch
review_headline: Cheap construction matches the price, but very limited options for a multi-purpose pouch.
review_body:
This Niji branded roll-up pouch is exactly as cheap as you [should] think it is for the price (currently $6), but its real issue is the name -- it should be 'Art Pouch'.
It is a lightweight nylon rectangle with a border single-stitched (ie likely to fail) around the edge. The most worrisome part is the closure is a snap set into a thin fake-leather strap. This is guaranteed to fail sooner rather than later so you'll have to be very careful & deliberate when opening to not rip out the snap (or just resort to closing with rubber bands as I do).
But the real issue with this pouch is not the construction -- as noted, you should be expecting that for this price. The real issue, assuming you just wanted a cheap, basic pouch; is the elastic band has 36 retaining loops of which 35 are all the same size. If you only want to use this for pens, small screwdrivers, penlights, or other similarly sized items; you've got no flexibility (ok, 1 loop of flexibility) for something bigger. I had an art pouch in college exactly like this: 35 pens/pencils and 1 eraser (the large loop).
If you need a multi-purpose pouch with some flexibility -- or if you need something with any durability -- keep looking.

product_title: PointZero Airbrush Air Compressor Regulator with Water-Trap Filter
review_headline: Airbrush Air Compressor Regulator with Waret-Trap
review_body: This product seems to be a very good product for the price. The description of the product was accurate. The two male-to-male reducers (1/8\\" BSP to 1/4\\" BSP), was a disadvantage to me because I needed to connect a 1/4\\" air hose from my compressor to the regulator and another 1/4\\" hose from the regulator to my Paasche H airbrush. I got it to work by replacing the provided reducers with two male-to-male 1/4\\" NPT to 1/4\\" NPT connectors.  My research of  BSP (British Standard Pipe) fittings revealed you should not mate BSP fittings with NPT fittings if the pressure holding capability is at all critical. But, I ignored the warning on mating the two thread types, used some plumbers sealant tape on the threads to eliminate any air leaks, and concluded my pressure holding capability is NOT critical.  Everything is working the way I wanted it to.

review_headline: Very Pleased With The Bench Dog ProLift Router Adjustment System
review_body: The Bench Dog ProLift Router Adjustment System is as advertised. It fit perfectly into the Bench Dog ProTop Contractor Benchtop Router Table. My Porter Cable model 7518 router fit exactly into the lift without having to buy any type of adapters. The only thing I had to do was put very thin washers between the lift and the insert to raise it up flush with the metal plate. I work with thin pieces of wood and the edge of the wood would catch between the metal plate and the insert edges. With the help of the washers, everything is flush. This is my first router/lift system and I am inexperienced in using it. So I am going to my local Rockler store and get some private lessons-well worth it. As I get more experience, I will add to my review. So far, I am happy with the ease of installation, the clear instructions provided, was a little surprised how much it weighs, but happy that it is made very well. I am very glad that I bought the lift because it makes using the router much easier by making adjustments above the table and to change the router bits. I expect to have years of use out of this lift.
