product_title: Forney 95 FI 120V FLUX CORE WELDER
review_body:
This welder is a great beginners unit, or for use around the house for smaller projects. You won't be welding large sized or heavy structures together with this, of course. At the price point, it's a good choice. It requires minimal expertise or experience and is pretty much ready to go straight out of the box. The only assembly required is the mask and the handle on the unit. It comes with an extra tip and an extra lock piece for the wire roll.

You will want to buy a real welding mask and gloves. The mask that is included is very minimal and requires to be held while using, so you will only be able to use one hand while welding. The mask is thin, pliable plastic and comes in two pieces, plus the glass eye shield. You have to assemble it. it is fairly narrow and most likely will not be comfortable or ideal for any length of use. There are no gloves included. It comes with a plastic handled wire brush/tap combo tool, but you will most likely want to buy better quality of those as well, unless you already have some.

This is a solid, compact unit which makes it great for portability. It provides clean welds, is capable of welding all types of carbon steel, and runs on a regular 115v electrical socket.

The hose length is adequate and not so long that it gets in the way while you're working.

Wire reel loads quickly and easily. It feeds wire smoothly and you can adjust the feed speed.

There are only 2 power settings and no adjustments in between. This may not be suitable for someone who likes to tweak the output more. Adjusting the wire speed properly is the most critical though, and you can absolutely find a range with both settings to weld smoothly and efficiently (within the limitations of the metal gauge, of course).

Handles on the clamp are hard plastic. Rubberized grips would be a little more ideal.

Overall, it is a well made unit that is great for small to intermediate-ish jobs, hobby welders, light auto or industrial and \\"around the house\\" work. Don't expect more from it than what it is ... don't expect to weld steel beams, and I think you will be satisfied with it. It is great within its intended purposes and workload.

We haven't had any issues with it malfunctioning or performance-wise. If that changes, I will update my review, but so far all of the small projects we have completed turned out with desirable results. As with any welding, know the limits of the machine, set the feed properly and you will do fine.ers, light auto or industrial and \\"around the house\\" work. product_title: Peltor Sport Tri-Flange Corded Reusable Earplugs, 3-Pair Per Pack
review_headline: Exceptional Value, Good Quality, Solid Performance!
review_body: Three pairs of any reusable, non-foam plugs for this price is a steal, but these happen to be good performers, as well.  Have used one pair at a loud concert and the others at an indoor shooting range.  Ultimately, they did well in both conditions.  The report from loud firearms, including small rifles, were not an issue and these worked as well as any other plugs I have used at that range.  In a concert setting, I would opt for "high fidelity" plugs with a lesser NRR if given the choice, simply for sound clarity, but these were all I had on hand that night and turned out to be a better alternative than the common foam plugs I often use, as these quieted down the volume without completely muffling the guitars and vocals.  Again, I wouldn't buy them with the intention of using them as a "concert" plug, but they made a great backup and at this price, you can't beat the quality and value!  As far as fit, they are a bit on the larger size.  Most medium-sized plugs tend to fit my wife and I easily.  These were a tad snug for both of us, but even during the concert, where I used them for several hours consistently, I did not find them to be particularly uncomfortable and they only required occasional readjustment.  Overall, a great bang-for-the-buck ear plug that gets the job done and comes in a convenient pack of 3 for the same price most other brands charge for just a single pair.  Highly recommended!

product_title: CDI 1/4-Inch Drive Click Torque Wrench 150-Pound Capacity
review_body:
I use this torque wrench almost every day as a helicopter mechanic. The handle is nicely knurled, so oily hands won't slip off the handle while you're trying to torque a fastener. The adjustment lock is very positive, and doesn't drift while you're using it to torque multiple fasteners. My coworkers who have used it have all been impressed as well.

Most wrenches of this size are 30-150in/lbs; this one starts at 20in/lbs, so you get a little more room to work at the bottom end of the range.

My QA dept. was very happy to see the enclosed calibration certificate, so I could start using it immediately.

My only pet peeve is the directional control lever. It's much too easy to move, and it points opposite of every other directional control lever on every other ratchet or torque wrench I've ever used (after 20 years as a helicopter mechanic, and 30+ years of fooling around with cars and tools, I've pretty much used them all at least once). It's a minor annoyance, but not a big enough deal to get upset about, or consider a deal-breaker.

review_headline: Tools Can Last Years; How's DeWalt's Service for Amazon Buyers and Kit's Value?
review_body:
Power Tools can easily last 10 years. Traditionally, power tools are sold at hardware stores, who can rapidly diagnose problems, sometimes fix, usually rapidly exchange, and offer some tips. Who helps Amazon buyers in diagnosis, returns, and service problems? Does one have to pay shipping costs of $25 to $50 to return a tool under warranty or in need of post-warranty repairs?

Well balanced, has features such as automatic LED lighting, feels sturdy, made of a plastic that claims can help reduce electrical shock (if one happens to hit a live wire, power), feels precision-made. As an analogy, using common flashlights, DeWalt's powerful flashlight, at 20 volt, was even useful for me as a small searchlight. DeWalt also manufacturers drill bits and accessories, so it's easy to buy add-ons. For amateur tool users, as I, these features and easy-to-purchase accessories really help my user experience. Using DeWalt magnetic drill tips (sold separately) and the well balanced drill, my amateurish drilling of wood screws nailed these straight on!

Is the kit a true savings? Adding up Amazon prices for the kit's individual components--$510 to $525--so, the kit at $400 (11/2014) is approximately a 25% savings. Good deal, but not a steal. During holiday buying season, I noticed the price dropped dramatically.

My DeWalt arrived DOA. Was the battery, charger, or drill bad? DeWalt does not directly provide weekend telephone tech support, and its website's black coloring is difficult to read and content disorganized. On Monday, instead of helping me diagnose, DeWalt's telephone support sent me to visit their Houston factory service center. I had to drive 60 minutes to learn what malfunctioned, but DeWalt's local staff quickly diagnosed and immediately replaced the charger. The local staff explained they can also repair and even rebuild certain tools. I guess if an Amazon customer went in at not-busy times, they can also offer tips on how to use.

DeWalt online and telephone service communications methods are not quite ready for online customers. DeWalt's confusing website also listed a nearby service center that no longer serviced DeWalts.

Had the battery charger or weekend telephone support worked, DeWalt would have received a 5 star because these tools are professional quality tools at a good price. But, the battery charger was defective, weekend service was lacking, website was confusing, and I had to drive 60 minutes to resolve the defective battery charger. So, a 3 star. product_title: Paslode 902000 16 Gauge Straight Finish Nailer
review_headline: Great when it works...which isn't often.
review_body:
I've had my Paslode for about three years, and it was great for the first 4-5 months. Then it started to have issues with misfiring. It would take 2-3 tries to fire a single nail. After about a year of this, it stopped working completely and I decided to take it apart and see if anything was noticeably wrong. I discovered that the red and black wire inside the case was pinched and the insulation was damaged. This damage happened when the tool was originally manufactured, by the way -- I'd never taken the Paslode apart to that level and that part of the wire is completely inaccessible if you're just cleaning it.

Well, after finding the wire online (NOT an easy thing to find, incidentally) I ordered it for $3 plus $12 for shipping. It took three weeks to get to me. I replaced the wire and fired three nails...and then it stopped. I waited 30 minutes and tried again and it fired two nails and stopped.

I wish this tool worked -- it would be awesome if it did -- but after three years of frustration, I'm DONE with Paslode.

review_headline: I think the meter is well made with nice features. The light is a very nice feature ...
review_body: I bought this for my Dad to use for mechanic work. The meter has two AA batteries and a 9 volt, I changed the batteries out for long lasting ones to hopefully prevent acid decay n the long term future. His last meter (different brand) died because of battery leakage and corrosion of a wire inside. I think the meter is well made with nice features. The light is a very nice feature as well the audible continuity.  There is no off switch or selection on the meter to turn it off, just set it on a voltage reading selection as there is a small current to test for resistance.  I have  no idea for the long term durability or accuracy of the meter. However it seems well made for it's price and the outside case should protect from drops and knocks to a moderate degree. Doubt you can get away with dropping it into the water for very long but if you fish it out quickly and open it up and dry before usage it may survive. Gave it 4 stars because I don't know it's long term durability.

product_title: ThruNite Archer Series 1A 2A V3 CREE XP-L Tactical LED Flashlight
review_headline: This may be THE light for you...
review_body:
This is really a 3.5 star rating, due to a functional issue that is causing me to return the light in favor of a NiteCore MT2C ( http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00937VTJM/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1 ), but the build of this flashlight is so nice, that led me to rounding up, even though I'm not keeping it.
Pros: as mentioned, very nice build. The knurling is very functionally aggressive without being too rough, and it has it in the right places, including the head' which is important considering the UI of mode switching, which involves loosening by a 1/4 turn (or less, in practice) and tightening to change levels/modes. The anodizing is clearly well done, and the IPX-8 rating is a clear plus, even if never needed. There are light crenellations on the stainless steel head bezel, not clearly evident in photos. Very nice fit and finish, great clip design. Square/trapezoidal threads (for those that care) turn smoothly, and are greased out of the sturdy box. Takes readily available AA batteries, a big plus, and gets a LOT of very useful light out of them, with a nice neutral tint and very consistent spot/flood combo pattern. Firm large forward clicky tail cap button felt good to me, and is operable with light gloves.
Cons: the big one for me, and the reason for return, is that "firefly" mode never worked for me on this unit- it was the same perceived brightness as low setting, though advertised as much lower, so I effectively had to go thru two of the same levels. Which leads to the next *for me* con: the UI, though I knew its method on purchase, to me a "tactical" light should only require one hand during use, while this one needs both for mode switching if required, and since it does have a strobe mode, one shouldn't have to fumble to activate it. Also, *for me* I found it just too long and skinny to comfortably carry and handle! despite the welcome included holster. I have larger hands, and wear and use this as a work tool in private security, and often need something a little less obvious on my belt. Again, I knew dimensions going in, but in practice it just didn't work for me.

In the box- the Archer 2A comes well-equipped, with a great clip design that a screw-down ring retains firmly- zero chance of it popping off if installed properly, but easily removed if not needed. The aforementioned holster is of good quality, sturdy nylon with elastic sides that run long enough to avid it coming out of the sides. Also included are spare o-rings, and a clearly written manual.

I thought that the 2 AA batteries, excellent reviews, and ample lumens would make this my new EDC work light, but I ended up deciding that noticeably more light, a shorter, wider body, and easier UI was worth using CR123a batteries instead. The NiteCore MT2C is still not the perfect light for me- I'd prefer the one-handed multi-click UI of my MagLite XL, but is there really any perfect flashlight in this price bracket? I'll keep looking. I'd keep the ThruNite if I thought I'd use it more, and if my toy/tool budget were larger, but I'll be getting some rechargeable batteries for the NiteCore instead.

As I stated above, this may be the perfect light for you, and almost was for me, but not quite. Hope this review helps someone. product_title: QEP 60089Q 120-Volt 3/5 HP Portable Tile Wet Saw with 7-Inch Diamond Blade for Ceramic and Porcelain Tile
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body:
This is a DIY Homeowner Special. The price should clue you in to what you are getting. It is very cheaply made.

It will work for your average DIY small project, with a little TLC. Go rent a saw from the local Home Depot or Lowes if you are doing a large project. This will not survive a commercial environment.

On setting it up (as with any new table saw) you must first align the blade to the table. The screw locations on this are a bit tricky, but most folks will figure it out. The instructions could use some clarity. Once that is done, the saw will cut true.

The Saw only operates with a toothless blade. As such, if you buy another blade - make sure it is flat, and doesn't have the little vents around the edge. The saw will cut ceramic tile just fine - I don't know if it will cut marble or glass. For a bathroom project or kitchen backsplash, it should handle the cuts with no problem. Don't rush the cut - let it cut at it's own pace, and you will be happy with the result.

product_title: Magnetic Screen Door - High Quality Walk Through Mesh Curtain, Instant DIY Install, Screen Size 35.5"x 82.5", Fits 34”x 82” Openings
review_headline: Glad we came across this as I didn't even know something like this existed.
review_body:
I wish I knew of this product years ago, but couldn't be happier to have this now. This is such a fantastic product, I don't even know where to begin with everything I want to say, so I will start with the setup.

I am a mom of 4 little kids, I have next to zero time to even blow my nose let alone try to put something up on my walls. Not to mention my technical ability to do any handy work around the house. (Ask me what I did to my sons bassinet one day...lol) Regardless, somehow I was granted 5 minutes of reprieve and so I took the screen door, glanced at the picture and went to town. (You read that correctly, I didn't read the directions. I know, I should have but I didn't.) This thing was so easy to put together, I was literally done in probably 7 minutes flat. The picture really gave me exactly what I needed to know. I aligned the individual Velcro pieces to its counterpart on the screen door, then one by one took the adhesive cover off the Velcro and starting in the middle of the screen worked my way down and around. Ta Da! And well since I have 4 kids, I decided to work my way around and reinforce it with a few thumbtacks that are provided. I did my scan around the door to make sure all the sides are flush and the center is aligned so it closes, and wa la! I was done!

Now why is this such an amazing product to have? Well for me at least, there are three reasons.

First, I don't even know if they make true screen doors for the type of back door I have. I would love to leave it open during nice weather, but pretty much our back door stays closed all the time. I would like a nice breeze to flow through the house now and again.

Second, I am so sick and tired of asking my kids to close the door behind them, I could puke. (Is it just my kids who refuse to close outside doors?) During times where I don't want to leave the door open, at least if the kids do leave the door open it will keep those pesky littlefly thingies from entering the house in mass numbers. MASS NUMBERS.

Thirdly, and this is the bonus for my very kind, very hard working husband who slaves the BBQ grill to bring us nice hot meals. He BBQs. Profusely. What a great product to have when you don't want to open and close the door 100x in such a small period of time. Just leave the door open, and the screen door will shut itself after each exit and entry.

So is the product easy to use? Does it really magnetictize (my word, not a legit word) itself shut behind you? Yes and Yes! If you walk out, you simply put your hand in front of you sideways to undo the first magnet (single handedly)and continue walking and the rest come undone very easy. As you exit the screen door, the weight that is in the edge of the screen door flap\panel falls back into place by gravity and re-magnetictizes itself.

The door is made really well, very sturdy to endure all the exit and entering, the weather...the kids. :/ Absolutely this is a must have product. Glad we came across this as I didn't even know something like this existed.

review_headline: Excellent Grinder With One Major Flaw
review_body: This is an excellent grinder with one major flaw. The design of the grinding wheel shaft and support flanges allows the shaft to stick out too far when you are using flap discs. I use this tool for grinding weld surfaces smooth. When you get the grinder close to parallel to the work the shaft end digs into the surface making marks. This only happens with flap discs. If you use thicker grinding wheels the shaft does not stick out as much. To solve this problem, I machined a special adapter that is used with flap discs. The adapter uses up more of the grinding wheel shaft, moving the flap disc further away from the head of the tool. The adapter works perfectly and the grinder shaft no longer digs into the work making this a virtually perfect tool. It is a bit heavy but using the side handle helps immensely. The tool vibration is very minimal and it maintains speed under a load. Sometimes it takes a few tries to remove the grinding wheel nut but it's nice not to have to use tools to remove it.

product_title: Linear Z-Wave Garage Door Remote Controller, Nexia Certified
review_headline: Simple way to control your garage door wirelessly
review_body:
I've heard about Nexia for a few years and have been curious to try their system and supported products. I'm already a huge fan of home automation as I have a [[ASIN:B00DGEGJ02 Belkin WeMo Light Switch, Control Your Lights From Anywhere with the Home Automation App for Smartphones and Tablets, Wi-Fi Enabled]] that I absolutely love and that regularly gets controlled wirelessly. I also own a [[ASIN:B00KJJW36G Denon HEOS 3 Wireless Speaker]] that I very much enjoy operating from my SmartPhone. Based on my experience with WeMo and HEOS the thought of controlling my garage door with my SmartPhone sounded very appealing.

So far, this [[ASIN:B00N75ZPZ0 Nexia Home Intelligence Z-Wave Garage Door Opener Remote Controller]] is delivering on my expectations. I found it very, very easy to install. No special technical knowledge or advanced DIY skills are necessary. I'm an average DIY'er and I found that to get this up and running it took less than an hour with only basic tools and a ladder. Connecting it with the Nexia system is also very easy and I found it to be on par with HEOS and WeMo in terms of simplicity.

In terms of operation, this has also gone as expected. I like the range of functionality and how easy the Nexia interface is to use. To date the biggest benefit has been piece of mind for those situations where I'm unsure if I have shut the garage door, which can result in wasted time if I have to turn my car around and head home, or lost sleep if I have to get up in the middle of the night. But I feel like I've only scratched the surface and that once I get more used to it and have more time I'll find even more ways it's convenient, much as I do with my WeMo.

I also like that you can streamline your home automation by controlling a range of things from lighting to thermostats to locks to security cameras to a water sensor to help detect leaks. It makes me think that the potential is in not just buying a single product, butinto a system for your home. I see the appeal in this because if I like the simplicity of having a single app for home automation. I also think it is interesting that Nexia isn't a closed system that limits you to products by a single manufacturer which makes me hope it will offer continued flexibility and breadth in the future.

product_title: Huntsman® - W20 490P Fiber Shell Welding Helmets 4W20 490P Fiber Shell Welding Helmets - Sold as 1 Each
review_headline: Still the best conventional helmet I think.
review_body: I have been using these for 35 yr.s and still rely on them today.  I don't know why they say it's not suitable for overhead, I certainly use it in every concievable possition.  It does seem that the quality has slipped some in recent years but it's still the best non-auto darkening I know of, reasonably lite wt., 'sleek' and compact in that it doesn't have a protruding flip up lens (always loathed those) the slider works very nice and easy tho the last two I have purchased quickly broke where the spring steel has a 90 deg. bend to hold the sliding part, fortunately a couple pair of pliars and a few seconds was all it took to put new 90 tab on the end and being that it was less sharp of a corner they never re-failed.  I have gone thru maybe a dozen auto darkening units of many kinds and they just don't quite do it for me with the exception of when one is doing a lot of tacking of smaller parts or very frequent stop and starts are needed.  Even the 4 sensor auto darkening units sometimes fail to activate when reaching in a hole, (all sensors get shaded from arc at same time) two sensor type often get shaded such  that they don't activate, on a machine say, but the main problem is that they don't go completely to clear when I want to used it as a face shield which I do constantly plus you usually need to remove the helmet and switch it to light (number 3 say, never 'zero') where as this helmet one only need to swipe the lever on top and you convert from dark welding lens to clear face shield for wire wheel, grinding, etc.  Also it seems that Huntsman set the standard for quality suspensions and that is absolutely crucial.   Eventually the detent cams that hold the helmet up or down nicely wear out and you need to either replace the parts or the entire helmet as it's exasperating when the helmet falls over your face unintentionally all the time, it takes some effort and time to replace the cams so may not be worth the trouble.  Other then that and blatant abuse it should last a decade of daily use.  For some reason I favor the fiber shell even tho it will not tolerate much water and isn't significantly lighter then the plastic shell version, either are fine.  (It seems like it's lighter I guess  and you can't do much welding in the rain anyway.)  Also you might be able to find a good auto darkening insert to fit this helmet and have it all but that adds weight and reduced viewing area plus significant cost.  Auto darkening CAN be crucial IF you are doing a lot of small part fit up and tacking, for heavy continuous welding they can be more of a cost and nuance than they are worth.

product_title: Stanley 20-047 20-Inch Blade Length x 12 Points Per Inch FatMax Saw with Blade Armor Coating
review_headline: one serious problem with this saw
review_body:
I have one serious problem with this saw. The blade is not firmly affixed to the handle and rattles around / moves from side to side slightly. This is not a big deal if you are cutting dimensional lumber for framing or construction, but it makes the saw a very poor choice if you are trying to make precision cuts for projects that require very tight tolerances. You may note from the photo that the saw blade goes through a metal piece just before the plastic handle and that the metal piece contains three screws. Unfortunately, the gap in that metal piece is wider than the saw blade, allowing it to rattle back and forth slightly. Even when the screws are tightened as tight as they can be without stripping them, the gap in that solid piece of metal cannot be closed onto the blade so as to prevent it from rattling back and forth.

I have an older 15 inch Stanley FatMax saw that I have been very happy with and had hoped the 20 inch Stanley FatMax saw was simply a longer version of the same with an improved blade. It is not. The new blade is superior in that the low friction black finish is indeed low friction and is helpful when cutting. The quality of the blade is very good and the plastic / rubber handle is comfortable, as is true with my older 15 inch Stanley FatMax saw. The major problem is that the 20 inch saw blade rattles and moves slightly in the handle. This limit's the saw's utility and makes the tool feel cheap, flimsy, or less reliable when using it. A second minor complaint is that my older Stanley FatMax saw came with a plastic blade guard that snapped onto the blade and handle, but the Stanley 20 inch FatMax saw does not come with such a blade guard.

The Stanley 20 inch FatMax saw is also advertised as having a slightly thicker blade that is more stiff. I can't say I notice this compared to my older FatMax saw, but it could be.

Overall, the saw is perfectly functional and will likely last a very long time, howeverthe fact that the saw blade rattles and moves from side to side slightly is a serious design flaw that limits the saw's utility and is a disappointment.

product_title: Gerber Bear Grylls Sliding Saw [31-001058]
review_headline: Definitely not impressed with anything in the Grylls model line - and this is no exception
review_body:
Not what you want to bet your life on, should it come to it. I've bought several 'sliding saws' over the years, after first finding a very nice Fiskar 10" sliding saw that was actually made in Finland (I think it is model 3625, but they don't make it anymore). Since then, I've based my experience with sliding saws against that single saw - and few have ever measured up to it. I still have that saw, and often pick up various new products and compare them to it, and even highly used, it out-performs everything I've bought lately.

I picked up the 6" Grylls-Gerber sliding saw here a few months ago, and tested one out. First off, I'm NOT a fan of a 6" sliding saw, it is too short for everything but the smallest kindling. I carry a small camp hatchet and a sliding saw unless going Elk hunting, when I also take my 21" inch bowsaw, so my sliding saw I depend on for most firewood cutting in regular hiking-camping season. The difference between a 6" and 10" blade are like night and day in most instances.

As soon as you take it out of the pack, there are a few things that really jump out at you. The blade is relatively rigid for a small saw, but worse than that, it is thin - and I mean thin. The teeth are cut unusually deep and narrow, more akin to bristles than saw teeth, and this really showed up significantly compared to the Fiskars unit. In cutting, keep in mind, almost any saw seems razor sharp when you cut with it new, but saw on some wet oak for a while, then go to sappy pine, now back to dry aged oak, and come back to that pine again. Not so sharp now? Yeah, you just wore the new off of a cheap blade. Gerber being the manufacturer, I didn't expect real 'cheapness' in a blade, but after 20-minutes of real hacking on some cured oak, I found that the SK steel they used to be too brittle for sawing. It broke in half on me. So much for a 'well-made slide-saw'.

From what I've seen, and for the price, you are paying for a name - not actual quality, and sadly, this has shown through other 'Grylls-authorized' products from Gerber. From knives and hatchets that have been sold that were not full-tang, to this sliding saw, the comments from 'actual hard-core users' are pretty much the same, find another product.

There are a couple of good products out there still (though Fiskars sent their sliding saw manufacturing to China, with roughly the same catastrophe that I saw in the Grylls-Gerber sliding saw). Take a look at Bahco, their saws are still really saws. Gerber apparently does still make the EAB Saw (exchange-a-blade) which, though still only 6.5" blade length, is Finnish made, also. Sadly, they killed the 'Sportsman' model for sake of the Grylls model.

Where once upon a time, you could count on a piece of equipment, you really will want to back up your saw if this is what you are relying on. Either a bowsaw or a hatchet should definitely back up the slide-saws you see nowdays. product_title: Woodstock D4151 110/220-Volt Paddle Switch
review_body:
Update 2 - Jan 2017: I bought and installed the same switch despite the reliability issues because I couldn't find a better one. After I installed the new one, I opened the old one and looked inside. The photo is the inside of the back cover. You can see the lower 2 terminals are completely burned. I wired the switch 120V and these were the hot terminals. After this, I'm changing the rating again to 4 stars because even though it failed at a load far under 35 amps (claimed ampacity), the box was at least heavy duty and secure enough not to burn. Not even a hint of a sniff of smoke outside the box. So even though it's going to burn at underrated loads, at least it will burn safely.

Another thing I noticed while reading reviews was that some people claimed the installation screw holes (not terminal holes) were in the wrong position and they had to drill new holes. This is not true. They are positioned for a finish plate (same as a plastic decora switch plate). The switch needs to be installed in a surface mounted box with a steel finish face plate, which will provide grounding to the box (you did ground the box, didn't you?) and the holes are lined up to fit. I grounded by wire the box and attached the box directly to the steel chassis of my table saw. 100% grounding - chassis, box, switch...

Update 1 - Jan 2017: switch died after about 18 months. Changing review to 3 stars. Big knock for reliability. There are no signs of overload on the outside of the switch (burn marks, smell). Nice functionality but poor reliability.

Original review:
This is a great switch. My 20+ year old delta tablesaw switch was upgraded with this. It works great. The buttons are a little hard to push but I think they'll ease up over time.

Pros: works great. Big stop paddle. Can kill it with your knee or whatever may be handy. Nice and safe.

Cons (not worth detracting from 5 stars):

No documentation. Not that big of a deal since the switch itself is marked with line/load sides. However, there are a couple of other screws in the back that may or may not be ground terminals. I wasn't sure so I left the switch itself ungrounded.

The terminal blocks are small. I had a few ring terminals that fit but not enough and ended up recycling 1 from a different wire. It would have been better if the terminals were large enough to wrap 12 awg stranded around. Not really possible. Those screws are small. You need removal rings to make it work properly.

It is deeper than a standard 2 gang box. I used a 3/4" extension cover (the kind for double layer drywall) and it fit fine in the box.

I hung the box under the tablesaw fence rail in the same location as the original switch. The electric box didn't fit so I used a few inches of steel angle I had laying around and bolted everything together. Bonus! Now the chassis and motor are grounded together. review_headline: The only reason I am giving this a 4 start rating instead of a 5 star is because the instructions are useless. There are no word
review_body:
I owned two Zircon stud sensors, one was really old and the other one was newer and purchased when I finished my basement. They both finally went to that big stud sensor paradise in the sky and quit working so I went off in search of a new one. I originally looked at replacing it with another Zircon but the only model that had decent ratings was one that cost $50. I am not a professional and do not need to lay out that much cash in order to find a stud.

I was looking at the second cheapest model in the store and that was even $5.00 more than I paid for this unit. Stanley is owned by Black and Decker and both brands are known more for their home tools rather than something professionals would use. I decided to bite the bullet and go cheap at the same time and ended up spending about $15.

The only reason I am giving this a 4 start rating instead of a 5 star is because the instructions are useless. There are no words, the company is apparently catering to the illiterate or the Ikea crowd. Since I do not have an advanced degree in hieroglyphics I did not understand any of the instructions and I had to go online and watch a video. On the upside it is only a stud finder and I was able to figure out how to work it pretty much on my own.

The unit is great. It finds studs like a champ and I love the "V" channel in the front of the unit where you can mark the stud. This is extremely helpful when trying to mark the location from an odd angle and you are guaranteed to mark the wall in the correct place. It also has a function that finds live electrical wires buried in the walls and that too seems to work as designed. I hope to get a long life out of this unit and am very happy I made this purchase.

review_body: So far I have been very happy with the usability of this tool. I purchased this to monitor solar panels, and found it a fun tool to go around testing all of my USB chargers and other external batteries. I cannot speak on the accuracy of this product because I have nothing to compare it to, however, I can tell you that it is consistent. I have done multiple tests with my phone plugging this into a wall outlet and allowing enough time to get a solid reading, then go outside and plug in my phone to my solar panel, and would end up with the same results. I was weary at first wondering why my most prized samsung wall chargers would only put out half of their rated power, but you have to remember that a charger will only output what the device takes from it. So my phone may only draw 570 mA on a good charger with a good cable, but if I plug in my tablet to that same outlet, it may draw 1.2+ A . Keep that in mind when using this device. Overall I am happy with this product and I would recommend it for anyone looking to monitor their USB chargers or to monitor their solar panels.

review_body: There is only one word that can describe the quality, price, and customer service of this Stanley Mechanics Tool Set, SUPERB. Every aspect of this set has met and exceeded my expectations and probably will yours. It comes with mostly every tool that could be used around a car or the home. There are 1/4, 3/8, and 1/2 inch drive ratchets with short and deep sockets to pair with that are both SAE and Metric. Along with an assortment of combination wrenches and a large selection of bits and bit drivers; it is everything that you could ask for in a ridiculously low price that no one can afford to pass up. They are all highly polished and easy to remove dirt and grime. The steel is forged in the same factory where Husky, MAC, Blackhawk, Proto, and Bostitich are made. They also use to make Craftsman and Kobalt; so their quality is not in question and somewhat above in certain tools. The customer service is also where they shine, it is an American call center and all that is needed for a replacement is your name, address, and part number, no questions asked, this can be done for the lifetime of the tool. Then they will ship you a new one free of charge in 3-5 business day; I prefer this over Craftsman where you have to take it in store, which can be an inconvenience to you if they are not near by. This can also cost you gas money, when with Stanley all you have to do is sit back, relax, and marvel at your new and shiny tool when it arrives. The ratchet in this set is a 52 tooth gear with an 8 tooth paw that grabs the main gear, it is a middle ground between fine and coarse tooth. The case is sturdy with secure snaps and tool clips, it is not covered by the warranty, but should have no problems lasting. Overall this set is one that should not be passed up and is the hidden gem in the vast sea of tool sets, get this tool set, you will not regret if for the rest of your life.

product_title: Safety Siren Pro Series3 Radon Gas Detector - HS71512 by Family Safety Products, Inc.
review_headline: More sensitive than the charcoal canisters by a factor of 2.5
review_body: This detector is sensitive.  We had the house inspected before purchase and the inspector left two charcoal canisters in the basement.  The test results were 3.1.  After moving in, we bought and ran this digital meter over a month time period.  In the same area in the basement (at the same height and under the same conditions) we averaged 7.7.  So we had a radon mitigation company install the PVC pipe and fan system.  We allowed the radon vent system to run a week.  Then reset this digital meter and deployed a new set of charcoal canisters right next to it, for the 48 hour period.  This meter shows (and has normalized over a four day time frame) a level of 1.8.  The canister test result was 0.8.  Both pre and post mitigation differentials were a factor of 2.5x higher with this meter.  Hard to say which is more accurate since everyone uses the charcoal canisters.  We think this device is more sensitive and gives a better picture of the actual levels over a longer period of time.

product_title: DELTA 36-T30 T2 30-Inch Fence and Rail System
review_body:
I installed this fence system on a Delta 9" Contractor Table Saw and Jointer Combination manufactured around 1985. I bought it new but the stock fence and rails were never quite right. I was having to fudge from the rail scale after getting out to a certain point. So I was looking to improve accuracy and speed of setup.
I inquired with Delta and got the brush-off first and after insisting I was rudely and arrogantly answered by their "tech help". But after reading some of the other reviewers putting this on their non-spec saws, I decided to bite the bullet.
It can be modified but I wouldn't advise it or brag of success. If the table of your saw is not 27" long, which is what this fence was designed for, you'll be taking chances with your abilities to accurately drill for the length (front to back) of your saw table. The problem is that the rear "clamp" is cheaply designed. The handle clamps the fence to the rails but it could also activate the rear clamp with a mechanism, drawing it tight to the rails. This essentially is what is done but by hand with the stock fence that came with the 9" Contractor saw. Instead this is static and so any modification of the fence rear clamp for the length of the table saw becomes highly critical if both front and rear are to be firmly clamped to the rails.
Also the "T" formed by the bar of the fence and the angle are not square and adjustments to make the bar parallel to the blade and miter gauge slots make the angle of the fence look off from the front rail. Another issue is I had to use Loktite on the nylon screws that adjust the level of the fence. Otherwise they would turn with moving the fence.
If I could I would give this 2.5 stars but to say it's "OK" is giving it too much credit. I would not recommend purchasing this if you are a professional or if you love quality tools or especially if you would have to modify it to fit on your saw if it's not 27".After spending over $200 on this it's really a better idea to buy a new or quality used saw if you want to have a quality, accurate, and speedy fence.

review_body: UPDATE 8/25/2016.....Tried Porter-Cable bag 78121 ($10 for 3)  and it works PERFECT!  Its a 10 gallon size for 7812 vacuum but no problem. Start using home central vacuum system bags at 3-4 dollars per bag instead of PC bags at 7 dollars per bag.  I use a 10 gallon home generic bag (2 layers synthetic with serrated cardboard opening) and it takes an extra 30 seconds to fit it up on the vacuum internal connection due to the physics / geometry of the bags opening(They were not meant to connect at the high point of the vacuum) The 7810 is about a 5 gallon volume but the my bag just nests into the space easily.  You might be able to find a smaller home bag but not necessary.  Hope this helps.  You sheet rockers may want to try this.  To hell with Porter Cable and their OUTRAGEOUSinflated price. product_title: Kaito KA339W Multi-functional 4-way Powered LED Camping Lantern & Flashlight with AM/FM NOAA Weather Radio & Cell Phone Charger, Color Green
review_headline: Cheap china knock-off, poor quality, not good for camping...
review_body:
I don't post comments unless the product rating is far off from my opinion. I took this device out for a 3 night camping trip and hit refund as soon as I got back.

This is a low quality, cheap plastic device that no camper would want to purchase. There are many issues other than the cheap construction and "one drop" lifespan.

- The radio does not have a digital tuner so finding a station can be difficult to lock in a station. The antenna is thin and would be easy to bend.

- The WORST FEATURE is the USB "charging port". Many of these devices charge your phone off the internal batteries. Not this one. In order to use it you have to CRANK for the entire time you are charging the phone, and even then it is a lower charge than other products. I estimated I would have to charge over an hour (and the unit states you can't do that continuously) to get about 1/2 a charge. You can't charge and use the phone at the same time. Great if you have two people?

And my personal favorite....

- The Siren button is less than an inch from the light button. How would you like to set that off at 5am when fumbling for the light? The slide switch is so easy to move that the manufacture TAPES IT IN THE OFF POSITION so it does not go off in shipment. Nice!

product_title: Gerber Crucial Multi-Tool , Gray [30-000016]
review_body:
I like the feel of this tool. I don't need a multi-tool with a saw, a fishing rig, a magnifying glass, etc... this hits all the points, pliers, screwdrivers, knife blade, bottle opener.

I use this as part of my EDC. Part of the knife is a plastic material, (the darker part). The colored part (shown green here) is aluminum. The pliers grip well, but they are not vice grips. The hold on, pull things out, and do the job at hand. I do wish they were spring loaded, but lets face it, none of my "real" pliers are spring loaded, so whatever. Deal with it as they say. Some folks are talking about the awkward curve for the handle, its fine.. again.. Im not pulling teeth with this... the wire cutter works ok, zip ties, etc.. all ok.

I feel like sometimes people are trying to claim or use this tool to replace $30,000 worth of Snap-On tools. Its not for that, its for tasks at hand, not day long work fixing an F1 race car.

The blade is strong, holds and edge, can be resharpened, and LOCKS. Its a blunt tip used for a stiff tug rather than a stabbing action. Think pulling and carving. The rearward is serrated for rope cuts.

The screwdrivers work fine, giving enough clearance with the tool closed, they also LOCK. I hate trying to apply pressure as the bit flops over smashing my hand against the work.

The bottle opener works, as a bottle opener. As a carabiner, its ok, but I prefer the pocket clip when it comes to mounting. I leave the carabiner up in my tool pouch so its easier to grab, its inline with the pocket clip - all flows for a fast grab when needed.

I picked it up for $18 from a vender here. I think its a factory second. Slight marks on the blade sides, and body - new in a box, with paperwork - but whatever, its not like Im going to keep it clean and happy on a shelf.

All items open easy, I like that I can get to them without opening the tool up, HUGE plus on that point.

If you need a real tool that gets the job done, try it, if you can get it under $25 its worth it.

goes for $30 at most local hardware box stores.

review_headline: let me just say that I bought a "certain" brand of concrete board that is very difficult to cut and get nice consistent edges on
review_body:
I'm currently remodeling our bathroom, which will include some tilework. I was looking for a diamond disc in addition to diamond hole saws in preparation for the tile, so I decided to buy this disc. Well, let me just say that I bought a "certain" brand of concrete board that is very difficult to cut and get nice consistent edges on. So after a scores and cuts that I wasn't happy with, I decided to give this disc a try. I should have used it from the start. I realize it's only concrete board, and not as hard as stone/tile/rock, but it cut through (as others have said) like a hot knife through butter. As long as you keep yourself steady, and make sure you don't have anything below the material you're cutting (don't want to cut into your slab or anything), this thing works great.

I still need to try it out on the tile when I get to that point, but to me, this disc is worth the price even for just concrete board! Just keep in mind, if you do use it on concrete board, use only outdoors and take all proper precautions due to the silica dust in the board.

Just a side note: I took another reviewer's advice (thanks Dave E.) on the backing flange for my grinder and it worked great. Gave me just the perfect offset for the disc and guard!

product_title: SE PFT-58 Timer Pill Holder Alarm Pillbox Capsule Medicine Case
review_body:
I've had a number of these over many years, and I'm grateful to them. I admit that most of the criticisms are true. 1st, sometimes the battery doesn't work, and good luck changing it; 2nd, it's true that learning to set the buttons takes some practice; 3rd, it is an awkward size and shape.
But in its defense, let me point out the positives. It's an affordable hours-&-minutes (vs minutes-and-seconds) timer, something that's not easy to find. (There is one other cheap one, but it's more fragile, more prone to getting its buttons turned off and even more awkward to carry around.) It's cheap enuf that you can just toss the ones that die, or finally run down, and still come out ahead. And I have a work-around for the awkwardness: with each new one I take an awl, put its tip in the dimple at one end, and give it a small whack; then I insert a paper clip and twist--providing a jump-ring for some string.
I realize this isn't for everyone, but consider how little competition this one has in its price range.
The next best one I've found is the Polder timer on a rope, which has some advantages--especially a lock, so that you can't jostle the buttons off--but that costs quite a bit more, and doesn't have a pill compartment.

review_headline: First I'd like to say that Inova got almost everything right I ...
review_body:
First I'd like to say that Inova got almost everything right I liked about this light. A dim setting of 6 lumens and a high setting somewhere around 56 lumens. A push button tail click for temporary use. Than there is a screw on tail cap for a more permanent 'on' mode. I also like the rigid body design which is plain and ok looking. I also like the grooves in the tail end. I wish there was a pocket clip but the S-Biner(Nite-ize owns Inova, go fig.) and lanyard seem to work well in combination, although at times annoying. It also runs the common AAA battery. So than why the 2 stars? I had this light for about a month now and have not had any issues with it until recently. First, you can cycle through modes by pushing the tail cap twice in a row. Same thing by twisting the cap 'on' twice in a row. I have no clue what has happened but now I am having issues with the light turning on and off. When I push the tail cap, it now stays in high mode only. Than after a while it doesn't work. This is the same with the twist on tail cap. From what I can tell the failure is in the tail cap design. It looks like an issue with the twist method design and the click button tail cap. It's not depressing correctly. From what I've read it's an on going issue with the Inova lights that share this tail light cap. I wonder if it's because when it's in my pocket I am pressing the cap when I sit down. I'll see if I can find a replacement cap and see if it helps. Until than this gets a 2 star from a light that should be a 4 star. It's built durable and has all the right features but hit or miss quality is not good.

Update: 2/ 2015. So finally got around to getting a new tail cap and replaced the battery. I haven't had an issue since. It's pretty tough and usable. It's a plus that you can clip it to your pant pocket and have it dangle in your pocket. At the same time it becomes a PITA to take off when I am wearing my nylon hiking pants. It's not bad on my jeans but anything the S-biner can really bite into like nylon pants or sweats, it doesn't want to let go. product_title: Pro-Series MMIG125 125 Amp Fluxcore Welder Kit, Black
review_headline: For a modest priced wire welder - it works well.
review_body:
For a modest priced wire welder - it works well. Once I used up the small spool of wire that came with it I switched to Blue Devil .035 flux-core. Like all such welding wires you need to deal with the splatter. Carefully clean what your going to weld to bright, shiny metal and this unit will do the job. Just getting what you pay for these days is a bit of a challenge. This unit, without a doubt, delivers for the price you pay. Wire feeds smoothly and the arc is big, fat and hot. Give yourself plenty of test runs to get the hang of it. If you're an experienced welder, you'll quickly recognize what it is capable of and have no problems. 1/4 inch plate and square tubing can be done easily if you work it at the right speed. Since you only have high and low temperature settings, you don't have the flexibility of more expensive welders that have 4 settings or better yet are completely variable.

I have some doubts about recommending this as a first welding tool unless you're willing to spend time learning how to use it properly. Check out YouTube - there are lots of great videos to get you started on flux-core MIG welding. This is my first welder and I worked very carefully with it until I could do things right. Now I have moved up to a higher-powered unit that supports gas.

One thing for sure - it's a heck of a lot better than the cheap stick welders most people pickup to learn to weld with. Those I can't recommend for beginners.

product_title: Jakemy 54 Bit Screw Driver Repair Kit for Computers and Mobile Devices
review_headline: Poor quality bits - stripped screw head
review_body:
I've replaced about 20 IPhone screens and consider myself a seasoned technician. I've been a certified electronics technician since 1992. The bits in this set are obviously forged with a low budget manufacturer. The pentalobe bit in particular had dull edges that I could not see upon initial inspection and it stripped out the first screw head on the first iPhone I used it on. I was very disappointed but then realized, I was the idiot trying to save a buck - not following my own advice that I give to others, which is - don't buy the bottom dollar item because you ALWAYS get what you pay for. I'm re-considering the iFixit branded 54 bit set that is in my opinion over priced, but the highest quality set that I can find right now. Their web site doted on their high precision forging processes which uses a US based company, high quality metals, good quality inspection blah blah blah...

I might just purchase a pentalobe set by itself and keep this one for the larger bits where a little dullness in the bit won't matter.

Buy at your own risk, but I feel this set is a dud and the company should find a better forging process for their smaller bits, then raise the price a little ... Better to put out a decent quality product at a competitive price than to give people a product that will leave a bad taste in their mouth.

product_title: Dremel 8050-N/18 Micro Rotary Tool Kit with Accessories (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Tiny, lightweight, cordless, a great Dremel in a tiny body
review_body:
The new 8050-N/18 is a mini version of the 8100-N/21 cordless. The bundle includes a few more bits, in a sturdy plastic case.
Unfortunately, unlike the cheaper 8100, the 8050's battery is built-in and non-removable.
The package contains a charging cradle and a power adapter (110V only, output is 12V DC @500mA)
A full charge gives you about an hour of work, which should be more than plenty.
The speed can be adjusted by steps using +/- keys at the bottom of the handle.
The work area is well lit by white LEDs included in the tip of the tool.

I really like the convenience of the cordless operation as well as the very small size of the handle, but it's a shame Dremel couldn't figure out a way to make the battery interchangeable like on the 8100. product_title: Columbia River Knife and Tool Ikoma Fossil Razor Knife
review_body:
The CRKT Fossil 5470 has a way of seeming small for a fairly large knife, certainly when you consider the substantial blade it it produces. This knife was purchased to be my EDC and also the "nicest" knife I have bought for myself. With respect of my review cred, consider my previous EDC's over the past decade in order have been CRKT M-16, Spyderco Tenacious, and Kershaw Leek. I'm not a high-end knife guy, but my knives are used and well maintained for EDC, backpacking, farming tasks, defensive mode, and of course opening retail packaging.

Somehow the stout blade of the Fossil has a way of feeling smaller and less obtrusive in my pocket than my Kershaw Leek. Obviously the Leek is much smaller, but the Fossil just has a way of disappearing from my mind when carried yet is always ready to be deployed when needed. I give this knife a high rating for allowing me to tote such a large piece of razor sharp steel and hardly even notice its weight or volume in my pants.

Aesthetically the knife is sexy. Everyone can see that and everyone that sees it in person has said the same. If you prefer a more discreet knife presentation, then the large blade can be a bit of a shocker for some. The satin polish on the business end does have classy contours that doesn't scream "tacky-zombie-skull-rape" implement. My opinion is that it bridges a gap between gentleman's knife and tactical folder.

The knife is very sharp and seems to hold an edge well. I haven't had the time to put it through its paces, but I haven't needed to sharpen it yet, as naturally I use my new knife every chance I get. The opening is butter smooth and addictive to flick open as other reviewers have commented. The lock up is very sturdy when deployed. It was actually a little tough to disengage the liner lock at first, nearly causing a chipped thumbnail, but it seems to have smoothed out now.

My only complaint at this time would be that the pocket clip is a little loose for retention in the pocket. I was working under my Jeep and found that the knife had slid out of my pocket when i was wiggling around on my back for a while. So I'll need to remove the clip, bend the clip towards the knife body and then it should create an adequate pinch and not fall out again.t clip is a little loose for retention in the pocket. product_title: Monoprice 10796 Z-Wave Motion Detector With Temperature Sensor
review_body: This is a rebranded Ecolink motion sensor and as such it performs well.  Check out some of the reviews of the Ecolink to get a better idea about it's performance.  This costs just a little less than the Ecolink, but you also are not provided with the rather nice and handy wall mountable holster that Ecolink includes with their unit.  I've given this four stars rather than the five I would give the Ecolink for not only the omission of the holster, but the instruction manual included with this is both inaccurate and incomplete.  It is only because of my prior knowledge and experience with the Ecolinks that I didn't have any difficulties, but if someone didn't have that experience they could find themselves scratching their head.  The manual instructs you to push the program button to enter into inclusion mode.  Well there is no button.  You just put the battery in.  And there is no explanation at all regarding the included jumper and it's four possible settings.  Even though there is no indication anywhere as to who exactly makes this device, the jumper labels PET, PET2, and TEST are identical to those found on the Ecolink.  Indeed, the entire PCB is identical.  I guess if you were in the market for a dozen or so of these and you didn't plan on placing any of them in a corner where two walls meet, you could save a little money, but for me just the additional mounting hassle will have me spending the couple extra bucks for the real deal.

I used them one at a time, instead of together.  First turn the switch do it's just barely not buzzing.  Then start your pattern on your wall. If it buzzes constantly, turn it down a smidge at a time,  until it only registers on studs.  You know you're getting studs when it beeps for a short time,  every 12 to 16 inches,  deepening on your house construction.  At this point you will be able to go back to the stud (I forgot to mention to slide it lightly against the wall) and mark both edges of it  Mark the next one and then test again by going further up or down the wall. product_title: Terralux TLE-110S MiniStar110S LED Upgrade Kit for Streamlight SL20X/20X
review_headline: Check the part number! the heading is incorrect!
review_body:
Be careful buying this LED conversion kit, the one being sold by firefly buys is a TLE-110S-MM which is different from the TLE-110S sold by amazon. The product descriptions match, but if you don't read the tiny print at the bottom of the page which lists the model number you might make my same mistake.

The kit worked but the MM led has a multi-mode selection of 600 lumen, 300 lumen, and low which is not in the product description either. My old SL 20X on/off button does not really work that great for the multi-mode bulb so I returned this and got the TLE-110S which is sold by amazon. If you have an SL 20X I would avoid purchasing the TLE-110S-MM but if you have a different model flashlight with more than one on/off switch it might work correctly.

When I would lightly depress the button it would be on high output, but once I completely pressed the button and it clicked on, only the 300 lumen mode would work. Cycling the brightness only works when you lightly depress the button and not clicking it on. This is problematic for my purposes, I just want the light to be bright with one click, so I returned this for the other LED kit.

Make sure you check the fine print under part number to make sure you are getting the right LED kit since its not mentioned anywhere else in the description or title.

review_headline: Nice lantern for night dives and day dives as well.
review_body:
I was looking for a lantern for night dives and sometimes use it during day dives (you know, when you are trying to find that small fish under a rock or inside a reef...). This lantern is good enough for that.

I also have the Intova Torch Light. I would definitely recommend this one over the Torch. This one is brighter and is about the same size as the Torch.

It gives you two options of zoom: wide or narrow. They it works is that you actually slide the front part of the lantern between wide and narrow, so you can actually control how much wide or narrow you want the focus beam to be. Very nice.

It is bright clear, bright enough so it can be used during day and the wide zoom allows you to have a nice lantern for a night dive. Do not expect to use this in caverns. I have not tried but it seems that there are some other lanterns which are better suited for cavern diving.

They use CR123A batteries and are very small (they fit in the palm of my hand, going from the base up to the tip of my index finger - I assume they would fit like that in any regular sized adult male hand). They are made of a metal alloy that feels sturdy and at the same time they are light weighted.

product_title: Delta 36-5052 10-Inch Left Tilt Contractor Saw with 52-Inch RH Rip (Steel Wings)
review_headline: For the price I would have expected better, in the end this gets the job done.
review_body:
For the price I would have expected better, in the end this gets the job done.

I ordered this saw from Amazon and 2 days later it was delivered by ABF Freight Company. The saw wasn't supposed to be here for another 4 days but it showed up early, good you would think. Unfortunatly where I live it's been off an on rain, the ABF Driver called me to let me know he left the saw in my driveway, with no one home.... Not pleased with the delivery, I would have expected they would call to set up a delivery window with me but worse of all it was left in my driveway on a day of lots of rain. That's more a review on the delivery however I think it is important you know that part.

Ok, the saw. It ships in 3 large, heavy boxes. I actually wasn't aware of how big this thing was going to be. It's massive.

There was a little damage on this saw when I was unpacking it. The brackets that are used to secure the wheels on the left side were completely bent. I don't think this was shipping damage as the box and foam was in tact, I had to use a pair of pliers to forcefully bend the bracket back in place so I could attach the wheel.

The saw assembly is one of the worst things I have assembled in a very long time. The reason is simple. The legs on the saw have to manually put together, on mine they had put tabs over the holes then looks like they powder coated it so the tabs were left on and they were hard to get off. It also left exposed metal where the tab was stuck on.

The bags of screws was the worst. A lot of items I've assembled either have a page in the manual so you can lay the screws on it to identify what they are or they are packaged very well and each type labeled. Not so with these.. They were packaged in a number of bags but no labels or anything making it very hard to identify what screws go where. I spent more time sorting the hardware then I should have had to.

During assembly of the saw and \\"wings\\" that is pretty easy, but I really dislike the fact the extension table is made out of wood and part of the directions require you to find out where the holes go in the wood and drill them yourself... It seems like for the price Delta is charging you these holes should be pre-drilled and even have a screw-nut on it, instead I had to get the drill out, the leveling tool and start putting holes in my new saw table.

In the end assembly was completed in about an hour, had they labelled the screws and pre-drilled the holes in the wood table it should have taken 15 minutes or less.

So hows it work? The saw works very well. It has a nice rail system to ensure straight cuts, however in my testing the rail actually moved a tiny bit throwing the cuts a bit off.

I like the on/off switch which helps to make sure you are safe, and the fact that this uses standard blades, can use stacked dados, etc makes it a very versatile tool.

The only problem I have with it is this thing DOES have wheels and they work well, however when you add the extension table it is just not practical to attempt to move this much. I'm tempted to remove the wood extension table, cut the rail system down and use it as a smaller style saw.

All in all this is an ok saw, I really dislike the assembly process, the saw does work well once assembled but it is still hard to move. I do have a compact dewalt table saw with a stand and the only difference between this and that is this is a more permanent saw which also takes stacked blades to cut dados. product_title: Gerber 30-000315 Crucial F.A.S.T. Tool
review_headline: 15 month review: Not bad, but also not great.
review_body:
After using this tool for a little over a year, I figured that it would be a good time to review it.

Pros:
-Compact with only the "essentials". It's my Every-Day-Carry (EDC) and I like that the Phillips and Flat drivers are roughly full sized.
-The F.A.S.T system works well and is holding up admirably, although I really only need the knife maybe 5-10 times per week.

Cons:
-Recently, the "screw" portion of the torx Chicago screw that acts as the pivot for the blade and phillips driver fell off and was lost. Rather than go through the warranty process with Gerber, I just replaced it with a 2mm machine screw from the hardware store. Not a huge deal, but you'd think that Gerber would use lock-tite or something similar to keep that from happening.
-The plier jaws have developed a tiny bit of a wiggle. Not terrible, but probably more than should be apparent after maybe 4 dozen uses.
-Initially the locking mechanism for the knife was EXTREMELY difficult to use. I used a little powered graphite to help get it going and it's worked fine ever since.

All in all, it's not bad for the price, but you probably shouldn't expect it to last forever.

We were able to hang a headboard onto the wall and feel confident the thing wasn't coming down. Now, I am getting ready to add shelves to a wooden bead board closet and it easily went through thick, old wooden bead board to find the studs (the nails in the studs).

It does take a bit of getting used to as you have to move it back and forth on the wall to eventually isolate the exact spot but, once you get the hang of it, it works very well and you get it done in a minute or so.

It's a little pricey, but so worth it. The guesswork is eliminated. I highly recommend this metal detector. It's worked every time for me on plaster/lath and wooden bead board. It's lightweight and easy to read the output.

product_title: UltraFire® E17 1000 Lumen Flashlight Led Cree T6 XM-L Camping Torch Flash Light The Lamp With Mount Holder Set + 2pcs 18650 Li-ion Battery Ultrafire 3.7v Batteries + 18650 Dual Charger
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo3APYKXG3XF9KV]]***UPDATE 8/9/2014***
See customer images

*bat and lux test*

Decided to get some raw data for the flashlight.

Some info will be repeated further in the review

High Mode:
*2.2~2.3 amp draw
*Initial lux 4800~4900
*Run time @ 35%> light output 25~35 minutes

Med Mode:
*180~210 mA draw
*Initial lux 2600~2750
*Run time @ 35%> light output 55~60 minutes

Low Mode:
*18~22 mA draw
*initial lux 680~720
*Run time @ 35%> light output 3hr+

Notes:
***Lux meter measurements @ approximately 1 foot with focus at max spread \\"X2000\\". Which produces a lit area of about 1.5 feet dia. 4200mA UltraFire batteries where fresh out of the supplied charger and light was in 73 degree F room with still air.
***Strobe and S.O.S. not tested
***Output is not regulated, the light levels do slowly fall in accordance with the bat drain.
***AAA Alkaline, Ni-Cad, Ni-MH and Li-Ion negligible performance/too expensive compared to 18650 Li-Ion bat (best use AAA if you just plan to use it intermittently).

modes: High/Med/Low/Strobe/S.O.S Button can be pressed half way to cycle the modes. Just like for a digi cam when auto-focusing.

Pro:
The construction and performance of it seems to be on par with any other light out there for it's given features and attributes (but way less expensive). The \\"zoom\\" is awesome. It's like having a noticeably brighter Mag light that fits in the palm of your hand.

Con:
The quality however is lacking in certain areas. For one the rather soft plastic lens. While very clear, would scratch and gouge easily. The circuitry is basic and allows what seems to be unregulated flow of current to the emitter on high. The amp hour rating of the bats are totally off as well. I should have been able to get a solid 2.5~3 hours of effective run-time on med out of a 200 mA draw from a4200mAH bat. The bats are more realistically around 1800~2000mAH.

This is a nice little light (for the price). In the video you see me shine the light at a house across the street (about 150 feet away). This is on the high setting. Even on the low setting when focused out to a point I could still clearly make out the features of the house. On the high setting I can clearly make out objects out to approximately 400~500 feet. The light looks dim as the video quality has been reduced and my phone does not record low light levels with realistic contrast and brightness.

I would Highly recommend ***NOT*** using the high setting unless you really need it. Not that the light gets excessively hot but the amp draw is a little over half the rated amp hour of the 4.2AH 3.7V Li-ion bats you get with it. Not sure if that's good for the emitter long term ether. More immediately, is not good for bat life. The med setting seems to draw around 150mA and was still plenty bright enough for general use. The other settings would not realistically effect bat life. The're likely not going to be used often or they don't draw enough current to be worried about it (low only drew about 15mA).

The 3 AAA provides the appropriate voltage but take note that the bats are in series to get that. This reduces the nominal max available current draw to the weakest battery of the 3 (and no more than 700mA in my case as you're about to read). I even used my 700mAH rechargeable energizes but it didn't seem to want to let it run above low for any real length of time. Plus the AAA just don't produce that pure power output that separates this from the $3 single LED ones you get at the hardware store.

The charger you get with it seems to be the appropriate constant voltage type. With a dead bat/s in the charger and plugged in, the light will be a reddish-orange and will slowly fade to all green as it charges. It's not the most sophisticated charger but it works likes it's supposed to. One dead Ultrafire 4.2AH bat took about 4~5 hours or so to charge with the supplied charger (assume 10 or more hours for two bats).

All the tech stuff aside, I will certainly be telling people about this little light and encouraging them to check it out before deciding what to buy in regards to expensive lights.

product_title: Ergodyne Chill-Its Cooling Towel
review_body:
Great product, works like it's supposed to. I use this to cool down when I have a migraine or sinus headache and it works! I don't like to use a cold pack for my headaches because they seem to make them worse. I wet the towel with cold tap water, wring and fold it in half then lay the towel over my forehead, eyes and sinuses. I also use this when I feel hot after work or traveling in the car. Instant relief!

I bought 3 different brands of cooling towels (Chill-its, Frogg Togg and Mission EnduraCool) to try and I like the Chill-Its the most: lightweight, doesn't feel like a wet towel or too spongy in texture, was the 2nd coldest towel among the 3 brands and stayed cool for a couple hours at least in upper 80s degrees heat & heavy humidity (I live in Hawaii) before needing to be recharged/wet again. It doesn't have a strong odor like some reviewers stated at least not IME, does have a chamois-like cloth texture whether wet or dry (almost like the chamois cloths for cars but they don't keep you cool like Chill-Its, I tried one out of curiosity) and is easy to care for - just wash with mild detergent (preferably fragrance-free) and hang to dry then store in case or store in its' case moist in the refrigerator as recommended by manufacturer to make it colder longer. Reasonably priced and cheapest of the 3 at less than $9.

Frogg Toggs was a very close 2nd in my opinion: it was the coldest of the 3 brands I tried and also stayed cold the longest. It was the heaviest of the 3 towels though, bled blue dye when I first washed it (I got one in varsity blue); has this slightly spongy texture and a latex smell initially. Frogg Togg was reasonably priced at $10+. My brother immediately snapped it up and used it during a recent pistol competition where it kept him nice and cool and comfortable throughout.

Mission EnduraCool towel I liked the least, I bought it at a local sports store where it was the only available cooling towel. I wasn't impressed, it just felt like a regular wet towel after following the instructions, even tried cold water and snapping it several more times with no appreciable difference in coldness (only got cold with use of cold water, but warmed up quick within half an hour). It was 2nd heaviest in weight when wet/damp among the 3 towels I tried, it felt wet even when wrung well and had a slight chemical smell. It does have a nice silky-like fabric feel and looks the least like a car finishing cloth among the 3 brands, was ready to use/wet right out of the case (the other 2 brands need to be washed first before use) but that's all it had going for it. It was the most expensive at more than $20 + sales tax but I needed some cooling towels last minute to send with my parents who were going out of the country at the time.

I would definitely buy the Chill-Its towel again when I need another cooling towel.

product_title: Vktech Temperature Sensor Probe for B5 B6 Li-Po Balance Charger 35cm
review_headline: Cheap add-on to more safely charge batteries
review_body:
I bought this to use with my [[ASIN:B00466L0BW Tenergy TB6-B 50W Balancing Charger for NiMH/NiCD/Li-PO/Li-Fe/SLA Battery Packs]] I believe it will work with the Tenergy TB6AC as well as the IMAX B6 and other smart chargers with a temperature sensor port.

Setup & use
===========
It is plug compatible, fits right into the combo USB/Temperature probe socket - it is keyed so it can only be inserted one way. Just plug it in, set your battery on the sensor or sensor on the battery, then start your charger as normal. If the probe senses an unsafe temperature the charger should stop charging.
On the TB6-B charger you can configure the temperature cutoff level. I set mine to 50C.

Minor Issues
============
- The probe does not come with any instructions, no specifications, or any documentation. After some trial and error I figured out how to change the cutoff temperature on my charger.
- I tested it by lowering the cutoff temperature and first heating it with a hairdryer and then a match. Unfortunately I initially received a bad sensor. I reported this to Vktech and they were great, no hassle at all, a couple of quick emails and they sent me a new sensor. I tested the replacement and it works perfectly.

Recommendation
==============
I would buy this product again. It is easy to use, just set you battery on top. This seems like a better idea than a li-po charging bag that will only contain a fire, not prevent one.

review_headline: These muffs do NOT attenuate impulse or continuous sounds above 82 decibels!
review_body: I bought these muffs to attenuate the gunfire decibels from my AR-15. I have over 20 years of military experience firing M-16s and M-4s, and know what good sound attenuation should be. These muffs have excellent powered sound amplification for hearing distant noises, but the attenuation provided by these muffs to gun shots is no better than non-powered ear muffs. Shooting with the volume turned up amplified the shot and just about blew out my ear drums. Two Army officers shooting with me tried the muffs and both literally ripped the muffs off their heads in pain after firing their first shots. The 82 decibel threshold was definitely exceeded but not attenuated. Buy these muffs if you want sound amplification, but DO NOT buy them if you expect to reduce sounds above 82 decibels caused by impulse sounds such as gunfire or continuous noise such as lawnmowers. For those purposes, you're just as well off buying non-powered muffs or foam ear plugs at the hardware store for less money.

review_body:
I remember my first Maglite, what a beauty. Such a sleek hardbody, with just a touch of curves, those were the days. With her big, bright eye and willingness to be turned on, it only took a couple of AA's to keep her happy, sigh. Back in the summer of '79 we traveled together, worked together and really bonded, telling each other we'd be together forever.

I've been with many other since, up to and including Big Bertha, the 5 D cell model and they're always there for me.

This is the new version of that first love and I've got to say, it's a spunky little trollop. It's much the same, except that her eye is even brighter and she doesn't ask for those AA's as often. One night when we were all alone together, she showed me a couple of new tricks.

She screamed \\"Turn me on twice, quickly\\" and the sensual look in her eye let me know she had reduced power and could go on like this almost forever. Then she said, \\"I want you to do it three times in a row\\" and what a shock that was. She started an energetic blinking that had me quivering right down to my toes!

Needless to say, I do love this young one even more than the original, nothing sags and no crows feet. But all of my Maglite's have always been there for me and some guys are always looking for one that's younger or will stay turned on longer.
