product_title: SOG Flash II Knife
review_body:
I was planing to ravage this knife in the review here, as it was really beginning to piss me off.
So I put up against a Ken Onion Blur and it was looking really 2-3 star (keeping in mind that 3 is average, and the Ken is a really solid 5).
The clip was wrong, the release was wrong, ergo was terrible, the safety.. well you can go argue knife safeties with the people who argue gun safeties. It was just all wrong.

I hated this knife so I decided to be a jerk. This thing was going to go up against an H1 knife in a dry shaving competition. What is more, since I was building a dislike for the knife, the Spiderco warrior was going to get the benefit of being the right hand knife, as I am right handed.

That is when I figured out that this was a lefty's knife. In the left hand everything is amazing. The AUS-8 somehow beat the H1 in edge retention (by a small amount), it cleaned its wookie arm nicer that the Warrior and with 1 less nick, while being run left handed by someone who is not a lefty. Both need sharpening/stropping now.. remember I said "wookie arm" not "10 year old boy arm" the hair that both of these went through would intimidate a chainsaw.

Yes, I could have been a complete jerk and run them against the Feather straight razor.. But when you think you are already fixing the race, who needs a ringer.

In the end as a 37$ knife (Amazon sale) for lefties, I'm not sure you can beat this, ever.
If you are a right hander I'd take the Ken Onion Blur every tad of the week due to the 45 degree thumb stud alone, not to mention the knife's more beefy feel.

Also, as a side note: While Tanto blades are great for cleaning your teeth, cleaning your fingernails is more risky/ouchy/crappy. So when you are bored, with a knife, figure out which you are more likely to do and pick your EDC appropriately.

It's only maybe drawback, is its very elegant (dare I say "feminine"?) form and weight. If you love a light, slim, fast, knife, this is for you. If you need something that simply has beastly/comforting weight, you will never be comfortable with this knife.

product_title: HUSQVARNA OUTDOOR POWER EQUIPMENT CRT900 Counter Rotat
review_headline: A real brute of a machine
review_body:
Overall this tiller is a brute. The 4 cycle engine provides a lot of power to the counter rotating tines that tear into the ground. This is not a tiller I'd recommend for someone who has a small area to till or who does not have the upper body strength to control it. The engine starts easily but you have to remember that it has an on/off switch on the side so pulling the starter rope with the switch in the off position is only going to lead to frustration. I've been tilling up an acre of ground where we've taken down pine trees and pulled the stumps. The ground still has some tree roots in it but this machine has been tearing them up. Some of the larger roots have been a problem but the tiller has at least let me know where they are so I can back off and pull them out.
Issues:
1. The single bar controller down to the main body is a design mistake. The older dual bar controller is so much easier better when it comes to directing and controlling this machine.
2. The cotter pin connecting the shift lever to the shift indicator is poorly designed. There is little space to work in and the cotter pin is very stiff (which it should be). The pin's straight edge should be an 1/8 to 1/4 inch shorter as it rubs against the housing making shifting very difficult at first though after a while it rubs a groove into the side and becomes easier to shift. Why didn't I pull the pin and cut off a piece? Again the space in the connection area is VERY limited combined with the stiffness of the pin. I got tired of tearing up my hands.
3. The bottom front of the tiller has a shiny black plastic cover that was broken when I received it. The pieces weren't in the shipping crate so I have to assume that it was broken at some point prior to being put in the crate.

review_body:

The tips on all of the blades are ground hard very precisely. Much better made than the cheapo stuff from the local big box and even better than the pricier stuff from the local DIY hardware stores. The fit of the #2 Phillips screwdriver is tight and you won't be slipping out or stripping any screw heads. The gripper spring works really well. almost too well, you'll need to learn a lift and twist motion to separate your driver from the screw head. I like the shape of the handle, seems to fit my extra large hands quite well. There is a hole thru the handle so you can use another screwdriver for leverage on a really tight screw.

It is kind of pricey, but when you need to start a screw in tight quarters, then using a good tool is much better than losing screws deep inside a PC case or auto body console.

Can't speak for durability since I've only had these a short while.

Thank You Amazon for carrying such quality products.

product_title: Makita EK7651H 14-Inch MM4 4 Stroke Power Cutter
review_body:
I will update this review in time. I just got this saw, and wanted to furnish what I know. For now, I would just like to say:

This saw is great. It has all the power of the two stroke Stihls and Husqvarnas, but its so much quieter and cleaner. I've used Stihls and Husqvarnas my whole career, until these Mini 4 Strokes were invented. The manual states that it is 4.1 horsepower. It seems comparable to the others in power. It's cleaner, though! Unlike other saws, when you leave this saw running nearby in between cuts, the exhaust doesn't choke you nearly as bad. Also, it sounds and smells like a go cart, which is kind of cool. At idle, it runs smooth, and is pretty quiet. The quieter 4 stroke may deceive you when cutting, because you don't realize it's more powerful than it sounds. It cuts fast, looks to be made very well, and seems like it will hold up on the job. The five-stage air cleaning system seems to be superbly thought out, as well, which should also keep the saw reliable. I love how easy it is to just put regular fuel in it too, instead of mixing gas. The manual doesn't state that you have to use premium fuel; just unleaded gas.
(I got on a website to find gas stations in my area that have non-ethanol gas though. I know from experience, and from experts that ethanol in gas eats away at rubber small engine components, and causes condensation in them, leading to all kinds of engine trouble.)
Mine saw is made in Japan, which I like. I don't care for China.
The only bone I have to pick, is that it took me probably over twenty or thirty pulls to get it started out of the box, after priming and choking properly. I can usually start most saws in about three pulls. When warm, it has taken me at least five pulls to start, but it's not broken in yet. My local Makita rep has been AWOL for a year or so, so I've given up on him for help. Usually, Makita stands behind their products, so I'll have to contact the national office directly with any questions.directly with any questions.

This is a very small little knife that would be good for a backup, or something to have for that "worst case scenario". Basically, if it comes down to do or die, this little gem will hold up. It's an inexpensive knife, but built very well. 2 fingers go into the holes, the rest of your fingers gripping on the underside of the blade and on the notched side of the blade iteslf. It might seem awkward, but you will be able to figure out a comfortable and useable way to hold and handle it very quickly. The blade is strong and thick, sharp right out of the box too. A light sharpening and you are MORE than set. The thing I really like is that the sheath it comes with can be placed horizontally on a belt, meaning that this can be carried in a very concealed manner without bulging, sagging down on your rump or dangling around your kneck (unless you prefer that--it does come with a lanyard). The sheath is solid, holds the knife well, and you can deploy this knife easily. I'd say this is a very user-friendly knife that could be handy in a tricky situation. I had been looking for a small tough knife that can be hidden easily and used for unforeseen personal protection while travelling abroad. This knife meets all those requirements. product_title: California Air Tools CAT-6310 Ultra Quiet and Oil-Free 1.0 Hp 6.3-Gallon Steel Tank Air Compressor
review_body:
The CAT-6310 is amazingly quiet for any compressor. It's even quieter than my 12v compressor I carry in my trunk.

I have painted 3 cars using this compressor and the Tool Force A-C1 50 PSI 2-in-1 HVLP Spray Gun which consumes about 4 cfm at 30 psi. This is right at the rating of the CAT-6310. If I just hold the trigger on the spray gun continuously the CAT-6310 can't keep up, but for normal spraying operation it does keep up, even though just barely.

All of the air connections are either pipe, copper, or steel braided. I like the safety 120v solenoid check valve, the adjustable pressure switch, the 90 degree ball valve to empty the tank, the extra handle for lifting and the included regulator with filter and moisture trap. Most don't come with a filter/trap included. I did have to change the quick disconnect to match the automotive style that I use and I added a couple lock washers for the wheels. But otherwise this quality compressor exceeded my expectations. Especially at the $169 price. I wouldn't hesitate to buy it again, even over a larger oil type compressor which would be much louder. We even use it in the house for my wife's air brush painting. Even though the CAT-6319 is very quiet my wife likes near total silence when painting so we have the compressor in the hall and use a 25' 3/8\\" hose in addition to a 10' flexible air brush hose.

I expect the CAT-6310 to last many years, especially if it actually lasts the rated 3000 hours.

product_title: Grizzly G9849 Magnetic Base/Dial Indicator Combo - President's Special
review_body:
I got this dial indicator for woodworking. Woodworking? Yes, there are several uses for a dial indicator in woodworking, including aligning table saws and band saws, setting planer knives, and micro-adjusting fences. That said, I cannot think of anything in woodworking where I'd really get nervous not having a $200 Starrett or Mitutoyo dial indicator. I won't buy a completely unknown Chinese brand either, but if Grizzly imports them and does spot checks and says they're good enough, that's good enough for me.

The whole thing comes in a very nice plastic molded carrying case, which is a good idea for a measurement tool that shouldn't get knocked around when not in use. You do have to take everything apart to get it in the case, but without that the case would get rather large. And when I say "very nice" I don't mean "Festool nice", but I do mean much nicer than I'd expected: this is not just a throwaway for shipping, they really intend for you to store the tool in it.

Complaints:

* The finger nut holding the indicator on is not slotted, as the manual suggests. Not that I care, but it confused me, since the manual has you insert a screwdriver to tighten it.
* There was a small washer missing. Just a little 5¢ steel washer, nothing special, but the manual tells you to use it in assembly, and it's not there.
* The manual was a little torn up from being shipped in the same plastic carrying case as some rather pointy parts.

product_title: Extech Mini Multimeter
review_body:
Very disappointed. Setting it on the AC or DC scale it never read zero but jumped around at reading above zero. I called the company and the jumping around for voltages above zero not measuring a power source was normal. The higher ohm reading might be the contacts are covered in a non rust material at the factory. I sanded the leads to remove any coating and the reading were still above zero ohms. Talking to the company again I asked if reading above ac or dc volts should be added to any reading and they said no.
They were correct since when I measured voltages with my $20 meter and this they were within 1/2 a volt of each other.
I also use the temperature readings for air conditioner units. I use the 2 meters and a shop thermometer in the same outlet vent on a car. the shop thermometer read 40.5 f the $20 meter 42f and the ex330 54f. At room temperature they are all about even 77-78 f.
I am not saying you will get incorrect reading with this meter but for me zero should be zero. I will stick to my lower coast meter and throw this one in a draw. The only useful function this has is flashing red when it senses a live circuit which the $20 meter doesn't do. For 2 1/2 times the cost I expect better. I do not feel like this is a precision instrument.

product_title: DBPOWER 80Meter/263Feet Digital Laser Distance Meter Handheld Range Finder
review_headline: 3x cheaper than brand name 80m measuring kits!
review_body:
As an engineer, measuring objects, rooms, or small buildings just can't be done with a measuring tape. Sometimes you have to use what today's technology has to offer. And with measuring kits costing upwards of $200. you do want to speed you money wisely. So sit tight while I provide a detailed and thorough review & overview.

Design:
Holding the device, it feels clearly well made. Cased with hard rubberised plastic with nice 'jimping' along the edges of the face. It also has bubble level measuring. The design gives off an attractive, yet robust look. Orange accents make it easy for you to spot. On the back of the device, there is a mounting socket for grubs screws such as mounting it onto a tripod. The LCD display is made of high quality and is backlit, which gives it a premium look (you do have the option of turning the back lighting off) and can be seen outdoors clearly if desired. To top it off, it comes with a nylon pouch with a belt strap as well as a lanyard strap. Interesting enough, the device is supposed to come with AAA batteries but my shipment didn't come with it.

Features:
It has length, area, volume measurements as well as a continuous measuring function. The graphical user interface is easy to use. It also has a Pythagorean proposition indirect measuring function as well which I find pretty handy when measuring the height of a small building. With a simple press of the button the measurements can be measured at the nose or the tail of the device. Boot up and shut down response is very quick and will shut off after 150 seconds to conserve battery power.

Specifications:
I guess the most important specification is the precision. The manufacturer's specifications states that the precision is within 2mm. Compared to a branded measuring kit such as the Bosch DLR130K's ~1.6mm. Pretty close and I would say identical precision. Starting off with the units, it is shipped using the metric system (meters) but can be converted to English measurements (in & feet). Measurements can also be displayed in different refinements. 0.000m, 0.00m, 0.0in, 00in, 0'00\\", and 0.00ft. The laser is a Class 2 635nm that runs <1mW, which is a common safe laser that are found on many laser pointer these days. Battery life is manufacture claimed at 40000 times for single measurements.

Conclusion:
I believe this device competes well with many of the Bosch measuring kits. It's cheaper, offers very similar features, accuracy, and specifications compared to many branded measuring kits out there. The only caveat I see that that since it isn't branded by measuring kits from Bosch or Stanley there isn't a manufacturer's warranty.e converted to English measurements (in & feet). I attached a couple of boards across the top of 2 ceiling joists and installed the racks to the cross boards, even with the top of the ceiling joists instead of the bottom of the ceiling joists.  This allows the bikes to be raised tight against the ceiling joists so there is now about 6’ 4” clearance between the floor and the lowest wheels, and I don’t bump my head.  With ceiling joists 2’ on center, I was able to install both racks between a single pair of ceiling joists.  The second rack is installed reversed from the first rack so the front wheel of one bike is next to the back wheel of the other bike.  I will certainly recommend this bike rack to my friends.

I found a repeated up and down motion helps soften the metal and coax it back the way it was. Patience is the watchword. As you make progress on the dent, steadily work your way toward the middle.  Also, buy some superglue and be ready to glue the metal and rubber parts back together (I found it helpful to stack cans around and on top of the dent remover to make sure the glued parts remain in contact). I've glued the dent removers together about five times now, lol. After about six hours of work using the removers (plus about six night hours of waiting for the glue to dry, the three dents on my car are 90% better, and I have bought another set after wearing out the suction part of the rubber. The original car body shop quote on fully repairing the dents (due to vandalism) was $2200. I would have given this dent remover five stars if the rubber did not keep breaking off and separating from the metal lever...that's the fundamental flaw in the design.

product_title: Coast FX414 Frame Lock Folding Knife 4-Inch Blade
review_headline: A Good Knife in Need of a Clip
review_body:
I had the chance to finally try out my Coast FX414 knife on a spring weekend camping trip and I'm happy to say the knife performed perfectly. The major detraction from this little 4" blade, as my title indicates, is the lack of a belt clip.

---------------------
DESCRIPTION:

The first thing I noticed about this knife is that it's heavy. The 7.2oz weight as indicated on the product description is really deceptive as the knife feels significantly heavier. I don't mean that as a detraction either. The knife feels really well made and has a a good balance. Construction is from 7Cr17 stainless steel which is the same steel used in a Gerber knife I own that was considerably more than the Coast knife. I expect that like my Gerber, this knife will age well and generally rust free.

The checkered aluminium handle is another feature I like. It makes the knife look good and again feels really good in hand. Unlike some of the other reviews here I didn't have any issue with my knife not locking open and closed straight out of the box.

The blade itself is 4" and features a fully edged surface except for the last inch or so which is serrated.

---------------------
USE:

As I said I had the chance to use this blade on a weekend camping trip to a local state park and the knife performed great. I used the serrated cutting surface to slice through some 550-cord without any problems. I didn't have a chance to try out the blade on any fish but I imagine the knife would do very well as it's extremely sharp.

In fact the only thing I consistently thought the knife was missing was a belt clip. It's a hassle to have to throw this knife in my pocket or pack.

Other than a relatively minor gripe about the belt clip this is an easy knife to recommend!

product_title: Empire Level EM81.10 10-Inch Magnetic Torpedo Level
review_body:
Empire offers superior quality products and as far as I'm concerned they are under-priced. Made in the the US. I am happy to see that this level uses embedded rare earth magnets instead of those weak magnetic strips that I hate. And, if the magnets pull out as I've seen in other reviews, then I'll just epoxy them back in instead of whining about it as others have. Or, I could replace them with a slightly less strong rare earth magnet, either way it's a simple fix. That's the nature of these very strong magnets, they hold so strong that they weaken the material used to bond them to the level. That also happens with other high end brands too, it's not exclusive to Empire.

You can't hurt yourself buying Empire, they're solid and reasonably priced. It's the best value out there.

review_headline: This Black & Decker drill / driver is very nice with the autosense feature. The battery is interchangeable with my B&D weedeater
review_body:
This Black & Decker drill / driver is very nice and I liked the autosense technology that stops when a screw is flush with the surface. I tested this B&D drill driver on a number of 1 5/8 inch screws for a wood fence and it drove them in quite well and stopped when they were flush. I used the phillips bit attached to the bottom of the drill and I didn't have any problems with the bit jumping off the screw heads. I used the flat bit on some larger wood screws where I had drilled a small hole and the B&D drilled them in flush also. The flat bit jumped off the screw head sometimes, which may mean that I should have used a larger bit. Switching the B&D over to the drill mode, I drilled some 13/32 inch holes in 2x4's and it performed quite well. That was the largest drill bit that I could get into the 3/8's inch chuck. The drill is a 0 to 800 rpm variable speed.

The only issue that I had with this B&D drill & driver is that the forward / reverse switch is right above the trigger, and sometimes when I gripped the drill with work gloves on, my finger would bump the switch into the center (off) or into reverse.

It's nice that the 20V lithium battery is also usable in my Black & Decker weedeater, the LST420. (However the 20V battery for this drill is 1.5 amp hours and the 20V batteries for the weedeater are 2 amp hours.)

product_title: Acoustimeter RF Meter Model AM-10 Radio Frequency Microwave Detection Meter EMF Protection. The Best RF Detector! Protect Yourself from EMF
review_headline: Great all-around Meter for detecting wireless hazards
review_body:
I didn't want to spend too much time with a detailed review on this but after seeing the bogus negative reviews on here, I had to chip in.

First off this is about as good as it gets as far as detecting just about every conceivable wireless device that is commonly around us these days. If there is one negative I can find about this meter is that it doesn't pick up really fast spikes from devices such as smart meters very well. You can clearly hear every spike but it will only register 25-50% of the time on the display readout. This is not a big deal though unless you want really scientific data on every spike. You will still get a good idea of what average power the Smart Gas/Water/Electric Meter puts out.

What this does better than most any other meter is that it's very sensitive and covers a much larger Microwave frequency range than most others. Some meters are better for Smart Meters but only cover up to 3 Ghz frequency. So they will not detect the 5.8 Ghz phones or Routers that are increasing in popularity. The LED lights also make using this device so simple and if you want more technical info, the display will give you near exact measurements of what it's reading.

Are there meters out there that are better and give better info? Defintely but it will cost you... to the tune of thousands of dollars in most cases. I bought this simply because it's very educational as well as great at showing you what you can't see or hear. Always use it check out areas I haven't been to before to locate Cell Towers and the like. Very Pleased with it having owned it for the past 6 months or so now.

Pros:

Very sensitive and picks up weak microwave signals from very far away
Picks up a very broad range of microwave signals ranging from 200 Mhz to 8 Ghz and beyond
Informative LCD display that shows exact up-to-date readings
Simple LED displays that show peak of signal strength and average
Very Helpful Audio function that allows to hear what type of signal is being emitted
Battery life is great around 15-20 hours with two rechargeable AA NiMh batteries

Cons:

Does not always detect really fast microwave emissions from devices such as Smart Meters
Not a Tri-Axis Meternction that allows to hear what type of signal is being emitted

review_body:

The project was to make a frame for a sailboat line bag. I had chosen a heavy wall (0.0863) stainless steel tube (also purchased from Amazon.com http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004XNAKKK/ref=oh_details_o01_s00_i00?ie=UTF8&psc=1), that is perfect for tapping with a 3/8" fine thread tap (ID is almost identical to the recommended "O" size drill bit for this tap).

product_title: Stanley STMT71654 201-Piece Drive Mechanics Tool Set
review_body:
Stanley mechanic tools are the most underrated tools of our time. Forget the Craftsman brand, Stanley tools meet the "lifetime warranty" standard of tools and do it cheapest. The 201 toolset everyday price at walmart is cheaper than the best craftsman sale price. I have time and again ran into bolts that have broken the ratchets of other brands, only to have my Stanley ratchets succeed where others have failed.

The other secret about the 201-piece set is that the ratchets that come with the set are the 89-818/819 line versus the 91-929/930 line that you buy individually at walmart. The ratchets that come in the set are 54 teeth with an 8 teeth pawl design whereas the 91-929/930 line are 45 teeth with a 3 teeth pawl. While the 91-929/930 line are strong ratchets (I have also used them for years), the ones that come with the set are even stronger and thus sell for almost twice as much.

With manufacturing moving to china, quality control has probably slipped. Some of the ratchets will feel very rough to turn, just like the craftsman of today. That's because they don't come greased anymore. The first thing you should do before using your ratchets is grease them. Think about it, you have gears grinding on each other thousands of times, there will be wear and worn ratchets will never pull as much torque as new ratchets. You wouldn't leave your transmission un-oiled would you? Snap-On tools come greased. Professional mechanics open and re-grease their ratchets at least every year. It is best to use a light grease as a thick grease would create a thicker barrier between the teeth, thus increasing the odds of one day slipping and stripping the teeth. If it is too difficult to open the ratchets, you can also just dip the heads in 1-2 inches of motor oil; oil will seep out while using it and it needs more frequent oil dippings, but it really is the easiest oil change you can do.

review_body: I'd initially bought a real cheap soldering iron ($20) for some hobby work. I'd only used nice soldering irons through work or school labs in the past, but figured, hey, it just gets hot, how bad can it be?    Well, it can be pretty bad. The cheap one took FOREVER to heat up (5+ min), couldn't maintain heat with a large solder connection, and although it had an adjustment knob, I pretty much had it at the max anytime I used it. Except then you'd set it down for a minute, and it would be too hot! It required constant adjustment and frustration.    This addresses all those issues. It gets to temperature in <30 seconds, maintains it while doing both big and small solder joints, and in my opinion is just as capable as the much more expensive Weller units I recall using in lab. The variety of tips it comes with is an added bonus. We'll see how it holds up.    Update: coming up on 1 year of moderate use, and it is holding up just fine.

Cons: Depth adjustment is useless for angled stapling; comfort grip started to pull away; didn't come with a case, just a cardboard box; really have to work to get the angled adapter head in the right place when stapling.

Notes: It took a little bit to get it adjusted, and I discovered that I had to back off the depth adjustment all the way, otherwise the head wouldn't press all the way against your flooring, and would rock side to side. Had to set the compressor at about 100 psi. At the low end of the compressor range, right before it kicked in and brought the pressure back up, the staples wouldn't set all the way, so I averaged having to set probably one staple per board. I definitely recommend the staple setting tool if you're going to staple flooring, it was a life saver. I found I HAD to make sure the adapter was pressed flat on the floor or the staples wouldn't completely set.

All-in-all, this is a good little stapler which will get the job done. Take the time to adjust it and expect to hand set a bunch of staples while you get used to the pressure, angle of the head, and the like. It will be frustrating, but after a while you'll be humming along.

review_headline: Be careful with your connector size
review_body:
I purchased this tool for crimping RCA connectors. As another reviewer pointed out, the connectors are too long to work in this "universal" tool.

The directions that come with the tool are not helpful at all. The reference several different model numbers, but the packaging gives no clue as to which model number this tool is.

I DID get it to work with the RCA compression connectors I have. My fix involved pulling out the piece where the connector would usually rest. This idea came from the instructions which stated to remove the piece (on certain model numbers). Unfortunately, my model was not designed for this piece to be removed as it cannot be put back in. So while this will now work on the longer RCA connectors, it will not work on other shorter connectors.

For the price, I guess it worked out. It is, however, poorly documented and the description does not make it clear what size connectors it will work with and what sizes will not work.

product_title: Wenger 16999 Swiss Army Knife Giant
review_body:
First off, I was given this knife as a gift from an uncle that I've never been very fond of. He's a nice fellow, but he's a bit "from the other side of the family" if you get my drift. Anyway he delivered it in person and therefore was exhausted from climbing six flights of stairs, so I offered him a seat and a glass of water (tap, not bottled) and we made polite, albeit small, conversation. He gestured at the box and told me that the Wenger 16999 Swiss Army Knife Giant was inside and that he wanted me to have it. I was touched but still somewhat confused by an seasonal expression of familial affection. I offered him a cup of coffee or tea, which he declined (I admit I was a bit relieved). Moments late he raised himself from the chair and made motion towards the door.
"By the way, that damned brother of mine isn't really your father" he said, in the same tone as you might address a mailman. "I am" he said with just a hint of flourish and I think if I recall correctly, a wink. Then he left before I could think of a reply. A subsequent telephone call to my mother confirmed his claim.

I'm curious what the return policy is on such an item.

product_title: Freud Premier Adjustable Rail & Stile Bit with 1/2" Shank - Round Over Bead Profile (99-763)
review_body:
I bought this set when the wife asked me to make some cabinets for her laundry room. Because the ceilings are 9 foot in that room, the hanging wall cabinets are 42" high. I was a little concerned about the strength of normal stub tenons given the weight of 40" solid hard maple raised panel doors. Used this set to make doors with extended tenons set into mortises buried within the slots of the stiles and the result is door frames that are crazy strong. Great design of the two-piece rail bit made making the extended tenons very easy. I also like that the slot cutter on the stile bit is adjustable to accommodate either solid wood panels or undersized plywood. Very sharp right out of the box creating a finish-ready profile that needs no sanding.

To be fair though, using this set to it's fullest requires very fine adjustment of the router bit height inside the table. Luckily, I have a router lift that supports that kind of very fine adjustment but it might be frustrating if you don't have easy fine adjustment. Also, while it's very easy to make extended tenons with this set, the mortises were possible only because I have a hollow chisel mortiser. Without that, making 1/4" mortises inside the stile slots would have been a challenge in itself.

review_body:

I have owned this machete for approximately six months and have used it semi-frequently. It is built solidly and the most damage I have seen it receive is a small dent in the blade from accidentally hitting a rock.

I typically use this machete while out hiking in the woods. Most of the trails I hike on are not the best kept and are prone to having the trunks of dead ponderosa pine trees laid across them. I have not used this machete to cut through the trees themselves as cutting through a tree trunk a couple feet wide would take alot of time and effort, but to rather cut off the branches that are sticking out from the fallen trunks as to make climbing over them easier. I must point out that these branches can have a diameter as small as a half inch; more commonly they are closer to a diameter of 3.5-4 inches, with some branches up to 5 or more inches. The blade does need occasional sharpening, but it has not broken on me yet and I do not expect that it will anytime soon.

The saw attachment is not very useful in my experience as it is faster and easier to swing the blade against the branches a few times. I have cut down a few trees in this manner. I removed the lanyard that comes attached to the handle as that wasn't very useful either. The sheath that it comes with seems well suited to the machete and has not received any damage as of yet.

A small, unimportant note to those that may not already know: this machete is the one used by Rick in the third season of the walking dead. From my experience with this machete I am confident that it would prove to be more than a match for zombies/walkers in melee combat if such a thing were to happen in reality.

product_title: Coast FX412 Frame Lock Folding Knife 4-Inch Blade
review_headline: OK, but the frame lock was poorly done
review_body:
This an OK knife, sold for a very low price, but there was a problem with the frame lock on the knife that I received that makes it imperative that you only use the knife with great care. The knife uses a frame lock – a piece of metal that prevents the blade from closing. However, while the lock did engage on my knife, only about half of the thickness of the locking piece did so. When engaged it did lock the knife blade, but I worry about it slipping, enabling the blade to close on my fingers. I was able to open the knife one handed, but the lock only engaged when the blade is opened with some force, making it imperative to make sure that the lock is engaged before using the knife.

I am a fan of coast flashlights and they are my go-to lights that I use in preference to all the others that I own. I was therefore surprised to see a coast product that was not assembled with the care that I have come to expect from their products. Ordinarily, a possibly defective safety feature would be enough for a one-star rating, however, many pocket knives do not even have any sort of lock, and that while I fear that the lock might slip it has not yet so, so I am giving the knife 3-stars, with the very strong caveat that one use it only with very great care. The lock on other knives may be OK and if it were, in view of the price, I would have given the knife four stars. All that would have been required for the lock to fully engage was a little grinding on locking piece, and this may be the case for other knives, but not mine. This looks like a case of poor quality control, which is not surprising for a knife sold at this price, but is for one bearing the Coast name.

The finish of the knife was OK, but as others have remarked, one of the screws holding the wooden inserts was raised a bit instead of being recessed along with the others, which is another example of poor quality control. The blade was reasonably sharp, but not overly so. The knife lacks a belt clip, but has a lanyard hole on the frame.a belt clip, but has a lanyard hole on the frame.

product_title: Milwaukee 2420-20 12-Volt Hackzall Saw Kit
review_headline: Not worthy of the m12 line
review_body:
I'm a big milwaukee fan, and have most every tool in the m12 and m18 lineup. This little guy may have its place for a few odd jobs where a full size recip or even the 18v hackzall won't quite fit. It has been handy to get into a few tight spots with a short blade, like cutting a pvc pipe inside a cramped cabinet under a sink for example. Power tends to drain quickly with the standard m12 battery, but the worst issue is the blade holder and the mechanism for changing blades. It is a spring loaded twist knob that wears out very quickly, meaning it is extremely hard to change. It's tight to get open, and once it is in the open position it's equally impossible to get it locked down again. Imagine trying to do this with wet or dirty hands trying to grip the little recessed collar while holding the saw and the blade in place. It's just a recipe to slice yourself. The collar is similar to the one on the m18 version, but that one is larger and easier to access, though still not ideal. I usually find myself having to grip the blade change collar with a wide jaw channel lock and then twisting the saw body to make it move how I need it to.

You're better off getting a full size sawzall and for anything job that is too big for use the m12 multitool instead.

product_title: Knipex 8701150 6-Inch Cobra Pliers
review_headline: Perfect for so many jobs, a must have for anyone that uses a pliers on a daily bases.
review_body:
I have been using this 6 inch Knipex Cobra Pliers since receiving it from Amazon back in Sept. 2013.
This pliers is a perfect companion to the multitool that I also cary daily at work. After having it for a few days and seeing just how handy it was I started searching for a sheath for it. At first I was excited to find on Amazon the Knipex 00 19 72 LE Sheath.

[[ASIN:B00DEMWH4I Knipex Tools 00 19 72 LE Tool Roll Empty, Black]]

Even though the Knipex sheath seemed a bit expense the description made it sound like it would be a custom fit for the 6 inch Knipex pliers.

After receiving the Knipex sheath I discovered that it was to bulky and to large for my Knipex 6 inch pliers. The Knipex sheath was so large that my Knipex Pliers would slip out the holes that where in the bottom sides of the sheath.

After much trial and error with a number of different sheath I was able to find one that fit the 6 inch Knipex Cobra Pliers perfectly, the Ripoffs CO-02.

The Ripoffs CO-02 has a belt clips that works perfectly for me, but if you prefer a belt loop on your sheath Ripoffs makes the same size one with a belt loop instead of a belt clip. Not only does the Ripoffs CO-02 sheath fit the 6 inch Knipex Cobra Pliers perfectly, they are also dirt cheap compared to the Knipex factory sheath.

My Knipex Cobra Pliers gets used and abused on a daily bases. Has a great finish that seems to hold up very well to fighting off rust as my pliers gets wet a lot. The grips are also perfect as they provide just the right amount of grip and as of now have not pulled loose from the metal handles.

I have worked with larger Knipex Cobra pliers in the past and have been very happy with the quality of them. This smaller 6 inch model seems to have the exact same build of quality and I'm 110% satisfied with them.

I will be adding photos of my Knipex 6 inch Cobra pliers along with the Ripoffs sheath to the amazon product page. I hope you find this review and photos helpful.

product_title: Gerber GDC Money Clip [31-002521]
review_body:
So, I'm a huge fan of Gerber most times. I've had the multitool, and I have 2-3 fixed gerber blades and an innumerable quantity of folders.

So, I thought when I saw this product, that it would be in line with what I've come to expect from Gerber. WRONG.

The G10 part of the clip feels cheap, the ring on the blade is obviously meant for girls, or effeminate men with small hands/fingers. I didn't have a huge number of expectations when I bought this, but I bought two and I'm reconsidering giving the idea I had to give it as a gift.

The biggest problem I have with the whole thing, is that the knife doesn't lock in the damn case. The body of the money clip is a bent piece of spring steel, with an anodized aluminium spacer, and a plastic outer layer, screwed together with four screws. Even if it didn't feel cheap, the biggest problem I have, is that the blade doesn't fit in the clip. Oh, you can slide it in, but it doesn't go down far enough for the clip to engage, so if you ever carried it around, you'd end up with holes in your pocket from when the blade falls out of the money clip and cuts your clothing.

The knife and blade edge itself are nice enough, if a bit hard to use with the tiny ring hole. But seriously, I can't use it because the blade won't lock into the money clip portion.

review_body:

I use my cabinet saw for the majority of my finish cuts. My only recomendations on the saw would be to cut a zero-clearance plate to replace the yellow plate and add a backboard. Secure everything without running the blade through your new fence and plate. After it is secure, make a cut and you'll have a zero-clearance bottom and fence helping reduce tear out.

Ease of changing the blade is also great. It includes a wrench that snaps in place so you don't lose it. If you're just cutting 2x material where cut quality doesn't really matter, the stock blade is fine. If you're doing any furniture making you should upgrade the blade to a 60-80 crosscut blade.

product_title: Stanley Sweetheart 750 Series Socket Chisel
review_headline: Decent for the Price, but not worth the "SweetHeart" name
review_body:
I have fallen into the hobby of restoring and actually using 100+ year old Planes, saws, drills and other woodworking Hand tools. I am by no means an expert at hand working with these tools, as I stated, I am an amature woodworker. I do however have a few years background in hand carving and woodturning, both of which require really good tools and knowing how to make them surgical steel sharp.
I purchased this set of 8 SW wood chisels because "Socket" (non shanked) Chisels are the best for detail wood working. These were also supposed to the equivalent of the 1920's era of the Sweetheart series.....without going into the History of the series, I will just say the old Stanley tools made by either Stanley Rule and Level co. or SW are very prized tools to have because of the quality of the making of these tools.
I have spent the last few weeks getting some old planes up and running, and finally had the time to start getting these chisels honed, and this is where the issue begins. The tools have a bit of machining or milling marks still on them and they needed to be removed before honeing. A Sharp chisel of this type REQUIRES a flat back/bottom of the chisel as these are used as "Parring" chisels for doing precise cuts and cleaning out of tennons, shoulders, rabbets, dadoes, and groves. In order to be able to do this the flat of the chisel must be like the bottom of a smoothing plane.....absolutely flat. This is the part of the chisel that "guides" the cut.
Anyway, upon starting to remove the machining marks, I found the largest chisel with huge cups in the bottom.....it has taken me 4 hours to get enough flat edge to keep this poor milling from controlling my cut.........I saved a couple bucks and wanted the nastalga of owning a set of SW chisels to go with my real SW Planes and other tools...........unfortunately Stanley had the opportunity to take the poor quiality tools they have been know for the last 50 years, and start making what made them their name to begin with....it is a real shame that Stanley used to be considered the best......and bringing back this line was supposed to compete with Lie Nielsen, Lee Vally (Vertias)?.......Really......Groz the Chinese manufacturer makes a higher quality tool.......look at the reviews from people that use the tools that took the chance on this name to by the brand again.......everyone has been sorely disappointed......

I am stubborn, and I will make these work, they are A1 steel, and will take an edge, and I will eventually polish both sides, but fortunatly for me, I am not a pro, and therefore am not relying on these tools for a living.....so I have the time to fix them....

Do yourself a favor and save weeks worth of flattening and go buy a good chisel from Lie Nielsen......of course your going to pay twice as much for them......but they are higher quality.....they will still require about 10 minutes of prep time to get them polished and Honed......10 minutes vs 4 hours ("good enough to use, but not polished").......its your choice.

I for one, I will stick with the 100-120 year old Tools from When Stanley was a name to be proud of, the rest of my tools will be from the "higher end" makers......you really do get what you pay for, and when it comes to tools: "better to cry once, because of the price, then cry every time you try to use them".........ing what made them their name to begin with....it is a real shame that Stanley used to be considered the best......and bringing back this line was supposed to compete with Lie Nielsen, Lee Vally (Vertias)?.......Really......Groz the Chinese manufacturer makes a higher quality tool.......look at the reviews from people that use the tools that took the chance on this name to by the brand again.......everyone has been sorely disappointed......

product_title: Bosch GLL 2-45 Self-leveling Long-range Cross-line Laser
review_body:
First of all I'm impressed with the overall value of this laser level. In the box: 1) the unit 2) Cushioned carrying case with Velcro belt loop 3) Two very well designed attachments 4) Some sort of a target and 5) Three AA batteries.

Attachments: The photo of the attachments on the front of the box (lower left corner) shows the two attachments connected together (magnetically). The picture of the back of the box shows them separate.
The two attachments are very well designed. The first attachment screws into the bottom of the laser unit. The unit can slide forward 1 1/2 inches in the attachment. The attachment has two, 1 1/2\\" support pegs that slide out to provide a steady base if setting the unit (in the attachment) right onto a surface like a table or floor. The back side of the attachment sports two very strong 1 1/8\\" donut magnets (probably neodymium). The magnets are very strong and \\"lock\\" on a metal surface like a refrigerator. I had mixed luck on corner braces in our walls. In the older part of the house (plaster), it didn't stick too well - on our recent addition (drywall), it stuck well. At the top there is a tear-drop shaped hole so you can hang it on a screw like a picture.

The second attachment is a strong spring loaded clip. It attaches back-to-back to the first attachment via the magnets and has a small gear that matches the notches on the back of the first attachment. That allows a fine tune adjust of the clipped unit up or down 4\\" when it is clipped to something.

Without the attachments, the unit attaches to any standard 1/4\\" tripod mount. It fit all three of my camera tripods.

The operation of this unit covers all the bases. In the unlocked mode (\\"leveling mode\\"): 1) It can project a horizontal line only. 2) It can project a vertical line only. 3) It can project both horizontal and vertical at the same time.
In the locked mode (allows you to project an \\"out-of-level\\" line any where you want), it can only project the horizontal only or vertical only line.

The beams project not just straight ahead but wrap around to left, right, up, and down surfaces as well. My first task with the unit was to hang two floating shelves on opposite walls of a room. Worked perfectly. Look forward to using it to tile our bathroom and hang kitchen cabinets.

The beam was bright in a bright room with the late afternoon sun shining through the window. It bean itself was a little thicker and not as crisp or solid red as I expected but still not a problem or complaint from me. If I had to describe the beam, I'd say the field part of the beam was more \\"pixilated\\" or \\"snowy\\" than solid red. This could be true for all units as I have nothing to compare it with.

According to the manual it also has a pulse mode \\"...that allows the unit to be used in situations in which the lines cannot be seen.\\" ...it does not work with other laser receivers. ...the laser lines flash at a very high frequency (invisible to naked eye) and thus become detectable for the laser receiver.\\" I don't suppose I'll ever use this mode.

The leveling mechanism locks in place when you turn the unit off. This was a big selling point for me after reading all the reviews of other units that don't sport this feature. It apparently renders the units useless when it gets knocked out of wack. With another unit, I was concerned this would happen in shipping or in use.

On the down side, the carrying case only holds the unit itself. I wish it had room for the accessories too. Not a big problem - the box is small enough - I'll just keep everything in there.

Before purchasing I checked the Bosch website to learn more about the laser level but couldn't find the GLL 2-45 listed. I contacted Bosch who told me it's one of their newer units and has not been posted to their website yet.

This unit runs $200 at Home Depot but I got the last one from the Amazon seller, xcorpusa, for $125.98. It arrived in three working days via USPS priority mail and was in perfect shape. For that price it was an easy decision to opt for a unit with more features for just a few dollars more.

My wife and I have 4.5 acres of wooded property around our house and there is a small forest of trees scattered throughout. After storms and windy days large branches fall to the ground and I like to cut these up for our fire pit. We also lose a couple trees a year due to disease

I just insert one end of the log or branch into the teeth and let me tell you it is snug and won't budge. Then I go to work with my chainsaw.

product_title: Dremel 4486 MultiPro Keyless Chuck
review_body:
Do not put it in a vice and try to open or close the jaws. It does not work this way.
As you screw down the chuck on the dremel shaft, the end of the shaft pushes up the jaws to close around the bit.
In my opinion, the only 1 star reviews that hold any credence are where the tool gets stuck in the chuck and I have only seen 2 of these.
If the tool bit does get stuck in the jaws, try this. I have had similar problems on a different tool and chuck.
Release the chuck, even take it of the dremel, and tap the jaws or tool bit down in order to force the jaws downwards.
Then give it a good clean.

The light pattern is good (with no holes or shadows) although at the \\"zero\\" setting the beam pattern is a square, very unusual. The \\"zoom feature\\" allows a tight beam or a wide beam. However the zoom feature compromises the water resistance of the light.

The quality of the light is good. It appears to be good quality aluminum and the lens is glass, not plastic.

Overall it is not as high quality as an LED Mini maglight but it also costs 1/2 the price as a Mini maglight.

Update:

After using the light for a while I have come to like the output but it does have one feature that I find annoying. It is a personal preference and clearly stated in the description so no points off. It has a 6 way switch hi, med, lo, strobe,sos and no momentary position. So if you use it like i do by turning on and then off. The next time you turn it on the light out is med. Do this again and it is on lo, then strobe then sos. You have to remember to cycle the switch 5 times to get it turn on hi if that is your preferred setting.

It's not what I "wanted"..as I wanted the much more expensive and made from aircraft aluminum woodchuck quad, however I needed something today, so I bought this at Tractor Supply and was not disapointed once I started moving some heavy oak logs around.

I was in the woods with brush everywhere from where a logging company came through and made a mess, So I was literally tossing/throwing this out of my way when I didn't need it, and lifting some big/long logs up using the jack fuction. I did not have wrenches with me to tighten the bolts, so they were very loose, but I was still lifting big stuff and moving large sections around with no troubles.

There was a pile of BIG logs laying every which way,(which I wanted) so I took off the base, and rolled those suckers off of eachother, and out of there so I could cut them into semi managable pieces. I could not have done gotten the large pieces moved without this, and the jack function kept my chain out of the dirt.

While not my first choice, I was pleased that I bought it. Use common sense when lifting or using it...and it probably will last.

product_title: Minosharp 3 Sharpener Black/Red
review_body:
I recently bought a pair of Globals. The directions said that because the steel they are made from was higher quality than regular knives, NOT to sharpen these like regular knives. Globals have a different bevel(angle of sharpness) and are thinner. So I got this. I didnt need the course wheel but got it anyway(you never know). Globals I notice stay sharper longer than regular knives.
I used the medium and fine wheels and they came very sharp. One thing I wonder is when you run them through the wheels do you need to run them through the opposing direction? It looks as if it only sharpens one side of the blade. If someone knows please make a comment.
I also sharpened a non-global knive (A henckel). This was in bad shape so I used the course wheel on it. I gave this the thumbs down. The results werent great so I didnt want to waste the sharpener on it.

review_body: I got these gloves for an endurance event (goruck challenge) & the gloves kept my hands warm, free from splinters and getting torn up and they were a snug fit so I could easily grasp objects. Great buy

product_title: Bosch 5312 12-Inch Dual Bevel Slide Compound Miter Saw
review_body: This saw is awesome! I have used other brands and they all were good but the Bosch engineers did their homework on this one. The big fence and etched in scale is nice an visible. The slide, movement and locking mechanisms work perfect. I got right to work with this machine after a quick familiarization. It has a lot of power and its cuts are precise and perfect. I added the Laserkerf and I can't be happier. I am not a fan of the blade mount lasers. If you want a product that is engineered well, well built (cast) you won't go wrong with this machine. It will last a lifetime. I am an avid Dewalt fan but my 3 or 4 Bosch tools have yet to let me down!

product_title: NEBO Redline Bikelight 220 Lumens 4X Ajustable Quick Release
review_headline: The light works well (I've bought two)
review_body: Not too happy with the mount system. The plastic tab that holds the light onto the mount (the tab is on the rail which is attached to the light, not the bike bracket) broke very soon after purchase. The light still mounts in the holder but because the tab is snapped off the light will not stay in -- it just slides out, rendering it useless without some other way to hold the light in place (I'm using a hair tie). I contacted the company for a replacement rail (a simple piece of plastic that screws onto the light body) but was told I would have to ship it back to them to determine if it was a manufacturers defect. I offered to buy a replacement piece but was told they do not sell them. It seems silly to ship it back and forth for a tiny piece of plastic so I will continue to use it with the hair tie. As I said, the light is good - I have one for my bike and one for my every day carry bag, i'm just disappointed in the mounting system (and a little with the support).

product_title: BAFX Products® - Decibel Meter / Sound Level Reader - W/ Battery!
review_body:
First, understand that this is a basic, low-cost, minimum-feature meter. It does not have memory or graphing or do any complex measurements. It has basically two features -- current sound level, and peak sound level. And, it does one or the other, not both at the same time. If you can live with those limitations, this meter works well.

It reads the sound level twice per second, so it may not get a totally accurate reading on a gun-shot or a drum beat. But, for average sound levels produced by a band, a stereo, or machinery, it works great.

One user complained that it seems "completely uncalibrated" out of the box. The instructions state that it comes calibrated from the factory. The 40db she mentioned in a nearly quiet room is about right. 40db is a really quiet room. A spoken voice at 90db? If spoken right into the microphone, that is pretty believable. And, readings do move all over the place even though the human ear doesn't notice noise levels changing. That is true with any decent spl meter. The human ear isn't nearly as sensitive as an spl meter. If you are measuring a sound that you think is constant, but you see the meter jumping between 82 and 88 db, you need not be alarmed -- the human ear usually cannot distinguish jumps of less than 10db or so.

If you aren't familiar with the physics of sound, you should know that sound pressure, which is what this device measures, and volume, which is what your ear and brain perceive as an interpretation of sound pressure against the ear drum, are not the same thing. For example, if I walk into a room with a sound pressure level of 95db, I will hear loud noise, and I will feel the sound physically pounding me. If a totally deaf person walks into the room with me, they will hear nothing at all, but they will still feel pressure of the sound.

I do wish that it had the ability to show peak and current levels at the same time, but I could have had that feature if I had been willing to pay for it. The backlight is really nice in a dark room, the size is handy, and the tri-pod mount is a nice feature. Overall, this is a winner.

review_headline: Very bright flashlight, doesn't age well.
review_body:
My first experience with this flashlight came when I found it abandoned in a ceiling. I replaced the batteries and was really surprised at how bright it was. It made a home on my tool belt for several months before the light would intermittently turn on and off. I decided I wouldn't judge it based on that, since I didn't know how worn it was when I found it. I bought another one, it worked great, then the same thing started happening.

This time I put a little more effort into figuring out what was wrong, and what I found was the contact points on the batteries were actually being dented by the flashlight, causing bad contact with the prongs. Rotating the batteries around like you would tires on your car prolongs their usage, or you can just replace them and the problem is solved. I don't know if it's because I walk too much, climb too many stairs, take off my tool belt too hard, or if the flashlight just crunches the batteries but that's why I gave it 4 stars.

Also, cosmetically the rubber on the head of the flashlight will eventually peel off with hard use but does not affect the function.

product_title: MagLite Mini PRO LED 2-Cell AA Flashlight
review_body: Maglight seems to still be lagging behind the current level of LED flashlight technology. Don't get me wrong, their low lumen outputs provide for good run times and their lights are much brighter, and for longer distances, than you would think, just going by their lumen ratings. Their excellent reflector design and spot-to-flood focusing makes the Maglights much more useful than they might seem if you just go by the rated lumen output. And this focusing ability, or lack of, is why I only give the Mini Maglite PRO 4 stars instead of 5. I have a Maglight 3D cell LED flashlight that gives as much illumination (at spot focus) at 500 feet as my Fenix TK41, yet the Fenix cost about 5x as much, and has about a 5x higher lumen rating. It is the 3D Maglight's ability to focus that does this, and this is where the Mini Maglite PRO falls down. It's focusing ability (my flashlight, at least) goes from Flood with a large brighter spot (can't call it a hot spot) to slightly less flood with a slightly smaller and brighter bright spot. It will not even come close to the tightly focused beam of the bigger Maglights, or even my (non-PRO) 2AA Mini Maglite LED flashlights. It is a good floody light, but if it had the ability to tightly focus like my other Maglights do, it would be a terrific light. Especially at this price point. I don't regret buying it, but it is somewhat of a niche flashlight due to it's lack of ability to tightly focus, whereas my other Maglights are good all use flashlights.

review_body:
These are nice workshop gloves for dirty jobs.  The material is tough enough to withstand all the pinching and friction put on them working in the small awkward spaces of my motorcycles, but retains enough feel that you can get a bolt started blind without cross-threading it.  The material slides easily when they first go on, but the moment your skin is wet or sweaty they get really sticky.  They don't breath at all so you WILL get sweaty in them.  The wrist gusset feels a bit tight and doesn't have much stretch, which is good new/bad news because it will keep gunk out but makes them a real bugger to get off if they're slippery.

A nice box of nitrile gloves well suited for extremely messy work, but a bit of a pain for lighter work where you just expect some smudges on your hands.

review_body: I installed this yesterday. Not difficult, but the instructions that come are very hard to interpret.  Once done, it works perfectly for what I purchased it for. I wanted a door monitor/intercom system so I would know who is at or was at my door so I can choose whether to open the door, or just speak to them. Picture and audio is very clear. For the price, it is an exceptional wireless door video-audio intercom system.

product_title: Dustless Technologies Cheetah II Ash Vacuum
review_body: I bought this after reading the reviews about how loud it is.  The reviews understate how bad it is--sounds like a 747 on the tarmac.  Those that said it wasn't any louder than an ordinary vacuum must have a pos.  That said, it works well if you keep in mind that is designed to suck ash and not large coals--which clog the intake.  It is important to follow the directions and press the nozzle down in such a way that only ash gets picked up.  That being said, if you use it properly it will do the job--it has cut down the ash/dust in my house tremendously vs using an ash bucket.  If I had it to do over again I would have spent more money on a slightly quieter unit.

Corey

product_title: DELTA 36-T30 T2 30-Inch Fence and Rail System
review_body:
I had almost convinced myself I needed a Biesemeyer but finances eventually won out and I'm glad it did. The Delta T2 fence is a really nice fence. I've been a serious woodworker for over 30 years and this fence does everything I ask of it. I understand the extra mass in the Biesemeyer compared to this fence, but unless you are doing production cutting it just is not necessary. If you slow down a bit and relax, this fence is more than adequate.

The fence came in one box and was well packaged. Setup on my old Unisaw took an afternoon but I was careful to make sure everything was square and plumb. The fence slides with just finger pressure and locks solidly. Adjustments are easy and the tape is easy to read and dead accurate. It also allows you to adjust the tape gauge readout slightly over so cuts are always within spec. This is not necessary so much with sheet goods but if you cut as much solid wood as I do, it's nice to have an extra 1/64 to 1/32" over to compensate for board tension, etc.

Dishing up hot food directly from a heavy cast-iron frying pan is a challenge. A hanging tab would have been nice (deduct one star) - I added a split ring to the cuff of each glove so I can hang them in my kitchen. Although they aren't perfect I'm finding these gloves useful and am happy with my purchase, although I don't think a person with small hands would be quite as satisfied.

product_title: Racor PBS-2R Two-Bike Floor Bike Stand
review_headline: not so obvious to assemble and pretty light but still holding my bike upright
review_body:
My bike doesn't have a leg so I was tired of dropping it on the floor or resting it against the wall. I searched for something not to big and that didn't required making holes in the walls. I found this rack and for the price I decided to buy it. Reviews were not excellent, but I bought it anyway.
When I got the packaged and opened it took me a little while to figure out how to assemble it, because the instructions were not that clear. I may sound like a useless girl, but I have built all the furniture in my room faster that this little bugger!! The tubes seemed to fit in any combination possible, specially when they actually DO NOT fit into each other. The screws and bolts were needed perfectly shaped so difficulty was added on top. I tried different options, unscrew, screw, unscrew, screw...4 times at least!! In the end, I lost my patient (after over an hour), gave up, decided that the shape the pamphlet was showing me was impossible to achieve and did it my own way!
Then, once it was assembled I realized that the whole rack itself is pretty light, so when I was placing my bike and then remove it, i was lifting the rack along with the bike. I tried to put some weight on the base but it hasn't been so successful. I don't think it can be attached to the floor either. My bike fits perfect though, and I kind of like it as it's doing the job I needed...though, I had to get used to step on the rack with one foot when pulling back my bike!!
So, despite those problems, it's kind of okay because it does stand my bike upright that it's what I wanted it for.

product_title: Platinum Tools 100054C Clamshell EZ-RJPRO HD Crimp Tool
review_headline: Excellent tool but the cutting blade should be made out of carbide!
review_body:
I have a whole bunch of different crimpers but this tool looked interesting along with the Platinum Tools RJ45 plugs and Strain Reliefs. It really makes making 100% reliable crimps (no need to even test it) that work every time! You put the wires through, double check the color coding once more, and crimp. The crimp action cuts the tip of the wires and crimps the strain reliefs in one action. I did about 5 cables but then I noticed that the wires were not cutting off clean anymore. I checked the blade and to my horror the blade had all sort of damage (which caused it to not cut off the wires properly). A quick email to PT and they immediately offered to send me new blades and warned me that I might be using counterfeit cable that had steel in it. So I got out my magnet ... and oh my god, one batch of my beautiful Australian Made CAT 6 certified cable was actually magnetic. The orange pair and green pair were not magnetic but the brown and blue pairs sure were. A quick check online and it turned out my batch was a counterfeit Systimax Cat6 cable! Fortunately only one of the rolls I used so far turned out to be bad, but I have to go back and change all those cables!!! So keep a magnet ready and always check your cables to make sure they are copper before crimping with this crimper!

I have since changed my mind on this crimper. Have to admit that Platinum Tools were really good about shipping me new blades, but now I noticed I have a problem with crimping pin #8 and sometimes pin #1 on many cables I have done. Somehow the tolerance on the RJ45 die is not a good fit. To be fair Platinum Tools offered to replace the crimper, but I would have to ship it from overseas and the cost of me shipping it back would be more than buying a new one. I have since removed the RJ45 pass through cutting blade and am having much better success crimping all points, but I still carry another cheap crimper just to make sure the job is done properly. The only reason I still use this crimper is because I like how they crimp the Platinum tools strain relief boots. I also did a check on cables I did with a DSX 5000 cable analyzer and it seems that the pass through connectors cause a much higher impedance with the cables made with those connectors. I now use the Cable Matters Cat 6 RJ45 plugs (give excellent results up to 24 gauge wires) with the Platinum Tools Cat 6 clear strain reliefs and am quite happy with results. I did buy the Platinum Tools Cat 6a termination kit and will see if it can actually make certifiable Cat 6a terminations that passes Fluke DSX5000 certification.

It's sturdy 250 lb weight limit per leg is far better than the DeWalt portable stand that has a maximum total weight limit of 200 lbs.  Also, I know the DeWalt is more compact; allowing you to get through most interior doorways with it, but to be honest, the price you pay by using a smaller, flimsier DeWalt stand is far too great. Bosch claims this will fit Makita because up until 2014 or so, it did.  I will just bolt the saw to plywood, cut out the middle for a sawdust pass-through, then bolt it onto the table.  I did not compare the Makita portable stand because the price was not comparable, plus I've never used it. The 90° angle allows me to reach into smaller openings but at the same time in makes in hard to use it near large flat surfaces since my cordless impact and drill need more clearance. product_title: Crescent CC12PVAD 12-Inch Connect Hand Clamp, Set of 2
review_body:
I think that the manufacturer's video does a fair and accurate job in describing these clamps. I really like them and give them 5-stars. For those who cannot play the video let me tell you why I like the design of these clamps.

I find the design of these clamps has been very well thought out (especially with regards to items number 5 and 6), as follows:
1. The clamps open to 12 inches, with a manufactures claimed gripping force of 500 pounds (which I have not verified).

2. You can reverse the clamp to make it a spreader.

3. There is a quick release trigger that unclamps the pieces and also allows one to quickly position the pieces before squeezing the clamping trigger.

4. The clamps and rubber face pieces have a few degrees of play in them so they will grip and clamp faces that are not perfectly parallel, but will tighten up be parallel if the pieces being clamped are parallel.

5. The rubber face pieces can be very easily removed revealing angled seriated teeth for pipe clamping. About a one-inch diameter pipe can be accommodated with only the rubber face piece covering the seriated teeth removed. If both rubber pieces are removed the jaws should be able to accommodate about a two-inch diameter pipe and possibly a bit larger.

6. The clamps have a slot at their end that enables one clamp to attach to other clamp. This slot piece, which has a lever on their top to lock it in place, is red and easily identified in the picture of the clamps. This slot piece enables you to clamp to a workbench and then clamp to a work piece, or to clamp two pieces together at different angles because this slot rotates a full 360 degrees. The slot rotates, but then easily locks in place by just pushing down on the lever portion of the clamp piece.

My only reservation is that while the extension rod is metal, otherwise the clamps are high impact plastic. While I do not see this as a problem for clamping flat pieces together, it could be when clamping to a metal pipe. The plastic serrations will not damage the pipe, but might not be able to impart sufficient force on a round pipe where the gripping contact point is very small. So far, however, this has not been a problem, and I do not feel that it detracts from my five-star rating.flat pieces together, it could be when clamping to a metal pipe. review_headline: My Favorite Self Defense Carry Knife
review_body:
This is my favorite James Williams knife. It is a large knife--not an EDC utility knife. According to Williams it has one purpose--self defense. Or if you're in the military or law enforcement--it's a great tactical knife.

It's not an assisted opener and that is great for this knife. With little to no wrist action you can deploy this blade about as fast as any assisted opener. I like it that it is NOT and automatic safety lock. You have move the safety to on. If you want a stealth opening--you can quietly open the blade with a little thumb pressure.

I normally do not like a thumb disk but on this BIG blade it is a help. This knife is a lot thiner than the Hissatsu if you're comparing the two. When deployed this is a nasty looking knife commanding some authority. However, you NEVER want to pull out a knife for 'show' --especially this one. Amazon has one of James Williams knife self defense videos that is well worth getting if you do purchase this knife with self defense in mind. Williams also has a YouTube comparing the Heiho, Hissatsu and the Otanashi Noh Ken Samurai blade knives.

Lastly, this is the kind of knife that may not be permitted as a carry knife in your state or local area. Remember, if you ever use this knife for self defense you may have to explain to law enforcement why you have this kind of lethal killing knife in your possession. If you know the risks and use this knife with caution--it'll be one of your favorites.

review_body:
I was worried at first that this wouldn't be very good, considering how cheap it is. My previous multi-tool was a Leatherman Surge, which is about a $100 item. This is easily better, and has caused the old Leatherman to get relegated to the bottom of my toolbox. I've had this for over two years now, taking it everywhere I go (including a field expedition to Central Africa for three months) using it almost every day, only cleaning it every few months and sharpening the blade even less often. It's still as good as it was when I first got it, in every respect – totally unfazed by all the use and abuse. This past Christmas (2013) I bought another one for my sister's boyfriend, and he likes it just as much as I do.

The handles are very comfortable (rounded edges, nice curves, and rubber inserts at the bottom) and I like that they are spring-loaded. The pliers and wire cutters definitely get the job done. I really like that the tools are all on the outside of the handles, so that one doesn't have to open the handles to get at them. The scissors (often a weak point on multi-tools) are excellent, if inevitably small. The main knife is solid, holds a decent edge, and sharpens up easily. It always seems to have the tool I need, and while I could do without the saw and the serrated knife (I'd prefer a file instead of a saw, ideally) all the other tools get used regularly so it's not burdened by a bunch of superfluous, rarely-used tools. It's light for a full-sized multi-tool. Also, all of the tools are locking, which I appreciate.

I'd say that I will definitely be buying this again, but unless I need another Christmas gift I don't think I'll need to – the one I have seems like it's going to last a very long time.

product_title: Black Bull MBS45 4-1/2-Inch Metal Cutting Band Saw
review_body:
If you decide to buy this, you can make it work and may feel that it's worth the price. I am included in that scenario and feel eventually it will be a decent saw. With that said, this is made in China.... The manual is almost less-than-worthless, a mere paragraph describing building the fragile base that "forgets" to tell you about essential parts. I am a mechanic with 40 years so I thought it would be a snap to build. The only guides to build is the small exploded diagram, the picture on the box and a few vague sentences. Following their instructions, when I placed the "very heavy" top on the base, it promptly collapsed into a pile of useless junk metal on the floor. I eventually hoisted the top portion and re-installed the base using my own skills while hanging from a chain hoist. I straightened the bent base parts and reinforced it with angle iron and it seems to hold.. Now comes the final installation, the pulley cover has two holes to mount it. No matter how you look at it, additional holes are simply missing and they have to be located and drilled for the cover to fit properly. Obviously, the engineer/s never put on e of these together or they would have immediately found their mistakes (I hope). I had to make a template for the hole placement, buy additional screws and
finally after about a day's worth of struggling, it's working. The top portion (most important) seems to be well made cast and I believe with a new American made blade, it will be dependable enough. Typical Chinese quality, just barely good enough to get by. You would NEVER find this lack of quality and poor design from any American made good. Unfortunately, I thought since the company Black Bull is located in Buffalo, NY that it was made in America! Not so, this saw is found under many other name brands as well. Should have done my homework, I would have paid more for a quality American made product but I guess I will make the best of it and hope my troubles are behind me.

The spring spreader is a well made forged tool with comfortable handles.  The spring wires are very strong but easily spread with the tool. product_title: Central Machinery 1 HP, 12 Gallon Mini Dust Collector - Filters Down to 35 Microns
review_headline: Not too noisy, and does what I want it to do
review_body:
First thing, I'm not using this as a dust collector, I'm using it to evacuate dust out of my shop. I'm not an expert by any means, but from what I've read 35 microns is not small enough to be protective of human health. However, since I'm venting outside instead of filtering the air, that really doesn't matter to me.

The motor does "tick" a bit as it spins; the tick goes away when I remove the brushes and spin the motor by hand. Therefore I suspect that the reason the motor has a tendency to eat brushes is that the rotor is not as smooth as it should be. However, for the price I can deal with buying a few extra brushes.

Regarding noise, I took some water pipe insulation foam for 1-inch pipe and put it around the base in place of the casters. This made the unit quite a bit quieter. That, and the unit is fairly light so I'm not sure how useful the casters would be anyway. If I had to move it, I'd just pick it up, rather than ruin my back bending over to push the thing on the casters.

The other HUGE positive for me is that the switch is wired in using standard spade connectors. I'm installing the blower in a fixed location which is not easily accessible: the spade connectors allowed me to wire in a 10-foot section of extension cord to bring the switch to a more accessible location. I cut a replacement cover for the switch box out of plywood and then installed the switch on an an electrical outlet box (I did have to make a custom cover for the switch). Overall, MUCH easier than wiring an outlet up to a switch.

The suction is about what you'd expect from a 1 HP motor. You'd definitely get more with a bigger motor & impeller, but this works for my purposes. You get what you pay for and all that.
