review_body:
I bought this knife after watching a video review just because of the opening system. I thought it unique so I thought I'd give it a try.
I'm a longtime fan of Ken Onion's designs, specifically the Kershaw Leek.
This was my everyday carry knife and I own 3 variants with different blade steels and handle material.
I've got to say though, from the first time I opened my Enticer...I was in love!
First off at 2.5 oz. it just disappears in your pocket it's so light.
Opening is blisteringly fast, have had several people mistake it for a switchblade...it's just that fast. Does it take a little getting used to compared to a conventional flipper? Sure. But the effort is well worth it.
The knife is also very thin, 2/3 the thickness of my thinnest Leek.
Here is another salient point, when the knife is closed, it's locked!!!
It absolutely can not open in your pocket, and a good thing too! Because straight from the factory it's wickedly sharp! And it holds it's edge well.
I've had mine and used it daily for six months and I'm just starting to notice it not being quite as sharp as it was. If I'm being knit picky I'd have to say my only complaint, and it's not much of one is that the handle material isn't very \\"grippy\\". Now for carrying in your pocket everyday that's just fine, however if you were using it for small game hunting or fishing or any activity where your hands may be wet...I'd like a little more aggressive pattern on the handle. So, I highly recommend this knife...buy one, you'll love it!

review_headline: Decent saw blade but be careful!
review_body:
I recently bought one of these to give it a try based on other reviews that I have read. The product works pretty well even when cutting into a piece of poplar. It seems to do a reasonable job cutting fiberglass as well. Having been suitably impressed, I ordered four more as spares as I tend to wear out Dremel accessories with regular frequency.

There are a few things that I noticed that I noticed about these:

- Remove the washer!
The washer that comes with it is sloppy on the screw and if left in will cause the blade to be unbalanced and vibrate violently

- One of the mandrels that I received was ever so slightly bent. This caused considerable vibration.
Testing the blade on another mandrel indicated that the blade was fine.
The other four were not a problem.

Aside from the above items, the cutters worked quite well even at 35,000 rpm.

I would definitely recommend trying each and every one that you buy as soon as you can after receiving them to check for defects. If they are not balanced when you try them, send them back as they are an injury waiting to happen.

Please be careful with these as they can cause serious injury before you can even react.

review_body:
I've had this saw for about a year now and I absolutely love it. Granted this saw is NOT CHEAP AT ALL but if you are a professional carpenter who needs to saw rough lumber on a daily basis, this is definitely for you. I've broken down the features into a easy-to-read list.

PROS
- This thing is a absolute beast. It WILL saw through anything made of wood that you throw at it. I've tried other brands and none stack up to it's strength. (Milwaukee's might be on par or above but since it sucks on pretty much every other aspect, I don't count it.)

- Versus the MD model (plug in your own extension cord), this corded version is a lot better and here's why. No contractor I've ever met dedicates one cord to one tool. We all use splitters (my crew runs 3 off of one cord) as it's much more efficient and cost saving. We use 10/3 cords with our crew. They won't fit with the MD model, it's too big. Now you can try to run a 12/3 or higher on this saw but trust me, you're gonna need all the amperage you can get. Lastly, the cord in the MD DOES pop out. I've had people tell me it won't, but every time I've tried it, it manages to loosen during the cut and it's annoying as hell. Stick with the old school and get a fixed cord.

- Did I mention this thing is BUILT like a beast? Yes it is. Now I'd say that most other worm-drives are but I've only used this one long enough to share my experience with it. After I make a cut, I don't set the saw \\"gently\\" on the ground or spend the time to hook it back on the horse, I just drop it and go. It saves time and frustration. I've thrown it onto grass, dirt, sand, mud, and subfloor. With this thing, I'm actually scared I'll break the plywood!

- The weight is balanced perfectly. One of the aspects that pros look at to determine if a tool is good is whether or not it feels \\"good\\" in their hands. This thing does. When you make a cut without a sawhorse (lumber resting on foot) you want the weight to be focused towards the ground. When you are making a flat cut, you don't want it to be hard as hell to push. This tool is balanced so that cuts are smooth and easy.

NEUTRAL
- Bosch markets their lower guard as \\"anti-snag.\\" During miter cuts, I always pin the guard back so I don't have to worry about it, but I hear from coworkers that this \\"new design\\" isn't very helpful at all. Personally it doesn't bother me.

- The vari-torque clutch. Again, Bosch comes up with some weird feature that doesn't seem to accomplish anything. The clutch is designed to activate when the saw jams up. But carpenters know that when you jam, you back out of the cut and go again, a clutch just messes with the whole thing. I've heard people say that it does help them, which is why I put in as a neutral feature.

- Made in China. Yes, I know, it's made in china. But hey it works right? I'm a die-hard American and I'd do as much as I can to support my country but American saws of this version run you up 100 bucks more. The chinese version works just fine so why gripe about it?

CONS
- It torques up like crazy. This thing will jump out of your hand when you start it cold. It makes lining up a plunge cut THAT much more difficult. You can lessen it by revving up the motor and then starting your cut, but it's definitely a drawback in the saw.

Other than that one complaint, nothing really bothers me. This saw is built tough and designed for professionals. If you work as a rough carpenter, PICK THIS UP. You will not regret it!

The directions indicate that the operator should repeat the "pull" stroke on the CERAMIC side 8 to 10 times for a blade that is "reasonably" sharp, which I did. As a result, the blades seem sharper, but were not yet "razor" sharp (I usually keep my knives very sharp). I suspect that the better knives are made of harder steel and may require more work than the 8 - 10 pulls. I have not yet used the SERRATIONS AND GUT HOOK sharpener but suspect that that process will require much more care and time (as you must match the angle of the grind).
I have been looking for a sharpener of this type for awhile as I am prone to overworking a blade while sharpening and probably remove too much "knife" in the process. So far, so good! I would recommend this product to others.

review_body:
I got these pliers at a great price from Amazon 2013.07.30, but they are a newer model, like the picture, and do not match the description. They do no have the 12AWG wire stripper recess in the cutters. This may be the first item I return, because I really wanted the stripper in the pliers to make it one super versatile tool. Returning is a pain though already bought a different pair from another vendor hoping to get the right pliers this time. [UPDATE: despite a clear picture showing stripper, the other Vendor shipped the wrong item, and what a pain to return. I emailed a few Vendors that had pictures showing the stripper on the big auction site, but they reported back they also had the wrong pictures... looks like the design has been changed, and this product is just not the super tool it could have been, I suspect patent dispute caused the change).

Aside from the missing feature, these do seem to be a great plier. They work great for grabbing and and have a lot of leverage as advertised. They are designed though like some other Lineman pliers not to close completely at the plier end (cutters close complete), and on this model with the tape-puller this design is probably the best. Given the leverage It might also help not crushing wires especially for people not paying attention.

I give it 4 stars because the wire-stripper feature is a valuable time saver that I was really looking forward to, I would not have bought it had I known it was not included. However; for the $25 I paid it's an amazing value, and that made me buy it over the more expensive options. It didn't quite work out for me, but if you don't need that feature, these pliers will do the job for a very long time.

review_body:

I know you can buy a product to do this and if you install professionally you probably would want to. But for me it was the perfect solution. product_title: Keter Folding Compact Workbench Work Table with Clamps, 21.7 x 33.5 x 29.75-Inches, Black
review_headline: Everything I'd hoped for and more!
review_body:
This is a masterpiece of engineering, in my opinion.

In its folded state, it is compact and lightweight enough to easily carry with one hand by the handle.

To open, you hold by the side handles with the top facing up and pop open the tab on each side with your thumbs. In one swift motion, the legs swing down. You then pop the three braces in place underneath the table top. That's it. It takes literally about 15 seconds to fully set up.

I've used the included clamps a couple of times already. They fit easily inside the table when folded and fit neatly into slots on the table top when needed.

Folding the table up is almost as easy as opening it. Just unlock the plastic braces under the table top, pull the table up by the handles on the lower level, and pull upward until the plastic tabs lock into place. Easy.

If I could give extra stars, I would. I have used this table already for projects around the house like laying a concrete pad for a shed outside (used the table to cut wood for the frame) and fixing some cabinet drawers in my kitchen island. It is so light and easy to use, it will be a constant companion on all my projects, even if its only use is to hold a hammer, screwdriver, or my iPhone's portable speaker. If you are thinking of buying this table, don't hesitate. You will not be disappointed.

At the end of the dive you can remove the pouches for easy rinsing and drying, but keep your weights together for the next day's diving, rather than having to fiddle with the individual bags of shot that you have in the pouch.

There is one significant feature of these pouches that is not mentioned in any of the descriptions of the product on any web site I have seen: These pouches have a Velcro type baffle in them that lets you isolate your weight to either the forward or rear part of the pouch for even more precise control of weight distribution and to prevent weights from shifting in the large pocket.

product_title: Stanley 060864R Folding Sawhorse (2-Pack)
review_headline: THEY ARE WHAT THEY ARE AND ARE PERFECT FOR WHAT I USE THEM FOR.
review_body:
First of all, I did not purchase these via Amazon but I wish I had as I would have saved about twenty dollars...and it must be noted I bought mine on sale here locally.

Anyway...

These sawhorses are what they are which are relatively inexpensive sawhorses which are ideal for occasional home use. They fold down quite nicely and take up little storage room. These sawhorses ARE NOT built for industrial or professional use, not by a long shot! If you took them to a construction job site I would imagine they would last only a very short time. If that is the purpose you plan to use them for then you had either better fork out a lot more money, or better yet, build your own...something that is not all that difficult to accomplished, especially if you are a trained carpenter.

I use mine around the home and may use them four or five times a year. Most of the chores I use them for are rather light weight with the heaviest being throwing some planks across them to act as makeshift and low to the ground scaffolding. They hold my weight just fine...190 pounds). I also use them for minor and brief woodworking projects accomplished outside my shop. They also work quite well in slapping together lightweight tables when we have a yard sale.

These things only weight a little over 12 pounds and since I move them from place to place this becomes a very big deal...particularly at my age and physical condition. I have several homemade wooden sawhorses out in the barn and let me tell you those are heavy suckers and wear me out hauling them around...something I have to do when I have very heavy and lengthy projects going....arrrgh! Having these little things around has been good for my back and knees.

For the price and for what I use them for I could not ask for more.

Don Blankenship
The Ozarks

1) At home you can cut overhanging branches with ease.
2) It's ready to go right out of the pouch.
3) It has the potential to saw through much larger wood.
4) Extreme Portability
5) Its Great for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Fishing.
6) Super light and it cuts through wood with ease.

I am going to address each of these claims one by one.

1) At home you can cut overhanging branches with ease.
I found cutting branches either above or bellow me to go very fast and the pocket chainsaw was able to get into tighter locations then both my chainsaw and handsaw. I give it 5/5 stars for pruning trees!

2) It's ready to go right out of the pouch.
I find this statement to be mostly accurate. As all you have to do is untangle it and wrap it around what you want to saw. The untangling can be a bit of a chore if the saw pieces stick. So I give readiness a 4/5 as I like it but can be annoyed by the saw sticking.

3) It has the potential to saw through much larger wood.
While defiantly never going to be my first choice when camping anywhere near a road for cutting wood I did manage to cut down a pretty big tree in my back yards after about 30 minutes of work on it. Which all things considered is not bad. 4/5 Stars

4) Extreme Portability
With the comfortable case that clips close and its relatively small size. (the one I received weighed only 5 5/8 oz's in the case) I find this comment to be the best part of this item. 5/5 stars

5) Its Great for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Fishing.
Try as I might I could not come up with a way to use this chainsaw for fishing but it defiantly can be used for camping hiking and hunting. 4/5 stars

6) Super light weight and cuts through wood with ease.
It is defiantly super lightweight at under a half pound The closest alternative I have is a ultra light camp ax at 3 pounds.
It does cut through wood really easily especially if you can stand above or bellow the wood so you get a straight cut. Angled cuts tend to get caught in the wood of larger branches or in my case the tree I cut down.

My overall thoughts.
While by no means the fastest saw I have used it is the most maneuverable and by far the lightest weight saw / ax I have in my collection. Would I personally use it at a camp site I could drive up to? No but as a piece of equipment in my hiking pack for longer lightweight hikes as a just in case I cant find some wood? Oh yes. It will definitely be joining me for some hikes in the next few months. Great product 4.85 stars rounded up to 5.

product_title: Leatherman - Style CS Multitool, Stainless Steel
review_headline: Perfect keychain tool for a desk jockey
review_body:
I'm not a handyman. I don't do any sort of day-to-day work where I really find myself needing pliers or a screwdriver. For me, the most important tools are scissors and a knife (for opening packages or otherwise cutting open things too tough for my hands) and a bottle opener. I also want something small that I can keep on my keychain without it unnecessarily bulging out my pocket (\\"Is that a Leatherman in your pocket, or...\\"). So, that rules out almost any large multitool that unfolds to reveal a pair of pliers, which is probably the majority of Leatherman's offerings.

That leaves stuff like the [[ASIN:B000FNFXQS Swiss Army Rambler]] or the [[ASIN:B000JCN0FG Leatherman Micra]]. The Micra is pretty close to what I was looking for, but having to unfold the whole thing to get at the tools is pretty inconvenient. Plus, mine has a habit of opening up just slightly in my pocket, which has actually led to me reaching into my pocket and stabbing my finger on the revealed scissor tips. The Rambler is almost all the way there, but the bottle opener is still too thin to effectively open a bottle--you really have to work at the cap along a few different points before it's loose enough for the opener to pop off.

The Style CS comes with a nice, big pair of scissors like the Micra, but the tools are still accessible from the outside. The carabiner has a little metal protrusion on the spring clip part, making it super easy to take off of your keychain, and the bottle opener is thick enough to pry off a bottle cap in one go. And the tweezers are springier, have an angled tip (good for getting at finer things like splinters), and are removable; trying to use the Micra's tweezers can be frustrating when you've got your fingers wrapped around the unfolded tool and are awkwardly trying to get your index finger and thumb in the right position to work the tweezers with some semblance of manual dexterity, all while you've got the rest of your keychain dangling off the end.

Size-wise: the Rambler wins, no question there. But the Style CS is still small enough that it doesn't really add any appreciable bulk. It does look a bit longer than the Micra, but it's just about the same length as the Micra when it's actually hanging on your keychain, since the Micra's got the mini-keyring as added length. The only real complaint I have is that the little groove on the Style CS's knife is a little too close to the pivot point, making it harder to flip the knife out than it needs to be. But otherwise, for a guy like me who spends most of every day at a desk in front of a computer, the Style CS is a solid addition to my keychain.end.

product_title: MSA Safety Works 10061646 Bifocal Safety Glasses, 2.0 Diopeter
review_body:
Let me start buy saying I love this concept! In theory these specs solve a problem that's been an issue for me the past few years. The first time I noticed my vision was not as crisp as usual, (about the time I turned 50), is one of those watershed mortality moments. Fine joinery has been a passion for most of my life, and the loss of good near vision had a major impact on previously fine tolerances. Reading glasses are ok, but they don't provide any eye protection. Adding safety goggles negates the value of the glasses, but introduces the concept exploited by MSA...to marry the two.
These glasses are excellent for working at a bench on a relatively stationary task, such as a drill press, grinder, router table, bandsaw etc. Where they fall down is where you have to walk around. Anything at floor level is out of focus (cos that's where the lens is) and that makes them a bit hazardous for obvious reasons.
With the above qualification, I would recommend these glasses, certainly worth a try at the price.

product_title: Grizzly H8133 8-Inch Digita Length Scale
review_headline: Be Warned: Counts the wrong way for fixed cutter head planer.
review_body:
If someone has a better understanding of this product then please respond. I bought this for a planer. It seems the most obvious use for a product like this. I had to construct a way to get it mounted but I have it solidly mounted now and I planed a board down to 7/8\\". I then calibrated the scale to read .875. My first gripe is that this scale doesn't have inches just the decimal equivalent. My next gripe however is the biggie. When I cranked my planer up to shave another 1/32 off, the scale counted up instead of down. Planer bed goes up and the board get's thinner not thicker. So this scale is useless. I can't imagine what other purpose this scale would have. So be warned. It doesn't count in the right direction for a fixed cutter head planer. Go with the igauge 12\\" ([[ASIN:B003JUII2A B003JUII2A]] It is cheaper and far more versatile. Also the brackets that come with the grizzly guage have very small nets and bolts to hold the small black brackets to the ruler. One was very crooked. The igauge has a bolt but threaded metal backs. Far better quality. The igauge has MM, Decimal Inches and Fractional inches. Wow I really love the igauge. Did I mention it is less expensive?

Oh finally, the grizzly came with a dead battery, I had to replace it myself. The igauge takes two to operate it. They sent me four in the package not installed so they are all still working. Imagine that?

product_title: Coast HL8R 800 lm Rechargeable Focusing LED Headlamp
review_headline: Forge Ahead into the Caverns of your Basement and Attic Crawl Spaces
review_body:
At up to 309 Lumens my model of the Coast HL27 headlamp (designed in the US, made in China) gives good illumination whether used in tight spaces or in the open outdoors. The bright LED is adjustable from focused to diffused white light. The beam angle stays put where focused. Better overall designed headlight sets are available and more expensive, but at this price point, you get a workable headlight gear. Just be sure to put replacement batteries in your pocket before you begin your search so you don't get left in the dark. There is no audible alarm or battery saving feature when power is low.

CONS:

The outside ring adjusts the beam and angle. It is hard to adjust with one hand and even two hands in tight or difficult spaces. I had to roll over on my back, take off the headband adjust the light and angle to where I thought I would need them refocused, put the headband back on and roll back over to continue my crawl space crawl--a real inconvenience, but doable with some assisting language.

The fully elastic headband is tight and uncomfortable and I need an Aspirin after wearing it for more than 30 minutes.

PROS:
I classify the HL27 as good for light to medium duty tasks, for someone who either uses a headlamp occasionally or is constrained by price. It is very useful for my unpleasant household tasks of needing a focused light in a tight area when I well may need 2 hands free to get the job done on a single try.

review_headline: Heck of lot cheaper than a new planer...
review_body:
POWERTEC HSS Planer Blades for Delta 12\\" Planer 22-540

It had been several years since installing new blades on my Delta 22-540 and both blade edges had seen better days.

- don't cut yourself on the Powertec blades - they are nearly sharp enough to shave with. Shipped in a tough plastic case to protect you and the blades.

- perfect replacement for Delta 22-540 blades. If you receive the wrong blades, use Amazon's return process and reorder.

- relatively easy to install - refer to the tool's manual for instructions.

- the planer's performance with these Powertec blades versus those dull blades is like having gas in your car versus being on empty. I planed 50 board feet of white oak with the new blades, which is darn hard wood. No issues - and reasonably smooth surfaces.

- you'll absolutely need the knife-gage that came with the 22-540 in order to properly set blade height. If you don't have a gage, you can get one from Delta.

- While the new high-quality planers are better than any 23-year old planer, they cost in the $500 range. With these blades, the old Delta is restored to like new performance. That means (on oak at least) the surface is pretty smooth, but with faint lines every 1/16\\" or so where the blades hit, plus it snipes the last couple of inches on every board.

Highly recommended.

product_title: LTM830160 - LEATHERMAN 830160 Surge Multi-Tool
review_headline: A heavy, expertly made tool...great for survival outdoors
review_body:
I purchased a SOG PowerLock a number of yrs. back from Wal-Mart...

I hadn't bought another, because I didn't think I'd ever want to do so. The SPL is a heavy-duty long lasting tool, but I wore down it's file too quick for my liking, so I decided to go the Leatherman Surge route.

Glad I did so...the LS is a little heavier than the SPL, but has a 25 yr. warranty.

The knives and saws are HQ razor sharp out of the box compared to my SPL, whose blade was as dull as watching grass grow when I bought it!! SOG makes great knives, so...whats up w/ that??

Scissors are more durable, and major cutting tools can be accessed w/o opening to reveal pliers head.

I bought the LS for its outstanding exchange-ability w/ saw/fiile, and universal after-market screwdriver magnet bit features, when you buy add on adapters of course.

Cons: Ordered the nylon sheath model, got leather, w/ no bottom hole for plier open holstering.

Tool was TIGHT...HARD to open/close before I EEZOXed the hell out of it, much, much better now. ALL tools need OTB lubing.

EDIT: This isn't the 2013 model either, since the LS2013 uses the same pliers head as the ST300! If I played my cards right, I could save a few bux by sending the tool back to Leatherman for updating, but all this swap off may end up costing me more than just buying a ST300.

I wish all multi-tool making companies would realize the difference between the words \\"tool\\" and \\"function\\".

Example: Pliers are a \\"tool\\". If I were to make a pliers head w/ 8 different un-removable features/functions, it doesn't mean I have made a \\"tool\\" that has the same constant use durability as eight purpose built PAIRS of pliers, and I wouldn't consider those 8 functions as tools, rather a features list. MHO, YMMV.

You cannot fit the whole 40 piece bit/head kit, the extended/removable bit driver shafts, and a full compliment of extra file/saw blades in this sheath I was sent. The leather is dry and stiff, it will need love as all leather does.

So, at the end of the day, Like Sheriff Brody said in Jaws \\"You're gonna need a bigger boat!\\"

The features, as well as larger, more day to day, all in one though somewhat limited capabilities of multi-tools vs Swiss Army style knives are what have made them such a viable purchase option.

Leatherman started that. I wish I had.

product_title: DEWALT DW618B3 12 Amp 2-1/4 Horsepower Plunge Base and Fixed Base
review_body:
I've owned and used the DW 616 1-3/4 hp router for the last for two years and have always yearned for a Plunge base and a D handle sub base for mortice and dado cutting respectively . Finally decided to acquire the extra bases and In my searches came across this DW618b3 kit with an larger 2-1/4 hp motor priced at around $242

When I crunched the numbers I realized that having already committed to shelling out $200+ on the two bases individually , I could basically pick up an extra 2-1/4hp Router motor and a carry case for an extra $30-$40.

Off the bat i was concerned that a number of users posed negative feedback about the magnetic speed control switch failing, but since most of these are pre 2009 i figured Dewalt has sorted this problem out and besides if the motor failed I could still use my Dw616 in all the sub bases and have a carry case for every thing. so I went ahead and pulled the trigger (pun intended)...

Item Delivered fast, arrived in great shape and complete with all accessories as described.

First off ...was very impressed with the case. Its solidly constructed looks like it can take a beating and is probably worth $50- $60 on its own, its internally moulded to securely hold and store all sub bases so they don't bang together during transport and I was surprised to find there was even a cutout in the case to hold the DW 6913 router edge guide that I bought as an add-on accessory (by the way this guide also fits the smaller base on the DW616 an added unlooked for bonus). I can store both routers mounted in the bases In this case along with a selection of bits ( all in their individual protective cases of course). Just be aware of its size 24" x 20" x 8"

Instructions were clear concise and accurate making for easy set up. Bases have a quality feel and are very solid , well finished with comfortable handles that provide a firm non slip grip. Clear sub-bases for viewingof bits and workpiece were flat and true and all were properly centered.

Plunge base , plunges and returns very smoothly , turret ( 5 steps one adjustable) has a quality feel with indexed points for sure positioning, depth setter took a little working out but works perfectly and accurately. Easy access handle mounted Plunge lock to hold tool in deployed position allowing for flat bottom mortices and dadoes. Shopvac hoses fit snuggly and dust/chip extraction works about 90% with some minor dust leakage.

D handle base is a joy ( for me) to use with a built in trigger lock so you can lock the tool on and then concentrate on guiding and routing. My one nit pick here is the lock release, you have to pull the trigger to disengage the lock and it has been a bit fiddly on one or two occasions but this may just be me working out the correct trigger technique.

Tool is surprisingly quiet, when compared to the smaller dw616, love the soft start and adjustable speeds, plenty power , super smooth in operation . Ran a series of plunge cuts for 1/2" wide by 2" deep mortices with a (freud) 1/2" upcut spiral bit with very clean results. Switched to the d handle with 3/4" double flute bit and ran test dadoes of varying depth without a hitch. Bit change out is a snap with the built in spindle lock and changing motor in between bases took all of 1-1/2 minutes including, changing the bit, reinstalling the fine depth setting ring on the motor ( ring not used with the plunge base ) and resetting the speed.

Some one took their time designing this tool thinking through a lot of the finer details . All in all im very pleased. Great value for me!!!!!!!!!

review_headline: This is excellen flood water leak "insurance" for the homeowner ...
review_body:
Every home owner I've ever met has relayed to me a catastrophe story about a flood in their home. It's those \\"I remember when\\" stories that got me thinking about my own and how invaluable this little wireless sensor can be. I'll never forget the time when it was actually \\"raining\\" in my kitchen when a second floor water heater began to leak and then let loose a torrent of water. Now that's an attention-getting catastrophe, but this sensor is perfect for those subtle leaks that are hiding. Under the sink, in the basement, and even in odd spots where water can sometimes sneak in from the outside.

What is very interesting about this sensor is that it can be set to emit a variety of tones. This would be ideal if you plan on installing more than one of these HomeSafe water flood alert system. For example, sometimes it's rather difficult to figure out where a certain sound is coming from if the tones are the same. If I've got water coming into my attic or coming down through my chimney, I don't want to waste time trying to figure out where I need to go. I've got one quirky little problem when rain comes down through a chimney when there are torrential rains outside and it's a need to know situation. Perhaps this little device will let me know where the leak starts.

For the price, which is quite reasonable, it's great insurance for any home owner. Small leaks can really be quite costly. I know because I've replaced an entire ceiling. This alarm can let you know immediately (and insistently) that you've got water problems. There are four screws with toggle bolts included if you want to have a more permanent installation. One interesting cautionary note was that if you have it too close to a heat source it could go off randomly. With the decent warranty, this nifty little item is probably worth investing in.

I recently loaned the wrench to a friend for use on his bike and he told me that it wasn't clicking at all. He over-torqued one bolt and stripped another. When he brought it back, I mated the torque wrench to a ratchet to see how much force it would take to click when set at 20 inch-pounds. It doesn't work, no matter how hard you push.

This appears to be some rebranded generic made-in-China product. I have a larger torque wrench of the exact same style that's branded \\"Mountain\\" - it's even in an identical-looking blow-molded case. That wrench works fine, so I guess these are just a game of roulette in terms of quality control. Save your money, especially if you're working on something expensive like an engine or high-end bike, and buy something better.

product_title: Kintrex IRT0421 Non-Contact Infrared Thermometer with Laser Targeting
review_body:
This is the best infrared thermometer I have ever used. It accurately measures a wider range of temps than most, has a tighter focus ratio (12:1 rather than 8:1 or 10:1), and a clearer, backlit display than most. The grip is ergonomic and thereby comfortable. I've never burned through a set of batteries on it, despite using it for hours on end for various projects.

Uses with which I have experience:
-Automotive paint / enamel finishing (make sure your paint is at the intended drying / curing temp)
-Beer-making (stir your wirt, then scan across the surface)
-HVAC leak-checking (door and window seals from inside and outside the home)
-Water for coffee / tea (check that water is at desired temp by stirring and scanning the surface)
-Breadstone heating (pre-heat, then check stone, then give 20 minutes after the surface reads the desired temp)
-Health / Illness (hold trigger down while swiping it across under your tongue, from the closest distance you can, then look at the highest temp recorded. Alternatively, check inside the ears in the same manner)

I love this. Irreplaceable in my life.

product_title: CLC Custom LeatherCraft 5-Pocket Cell Phone/Tool Holder - 1105
review_headline: Yes its a bit large, but only as large as it needs to be
review_body:
This thing is great. Is is a tad on the bulky side but no larger than it needs to be in order to hold a few usefully sized tools. An excellent balance of size and functionality I think.

The sides of the cell phone pocket are elastic, and the pocket is deeper than most modern phones are thick, so the pocket nicely conformed to snugly fit my phone despite it being wider than the CLC spec of that pocket. CLC site says approx 2.5\\"W, my phone case is 2.875\\"W, and it looks like the pocket would still expand to slightly higher than 3\\"W. My phone is a HTC EVO 4G LTE w/ 4.7\\"diag screen which was big before the Note showed up. The pocket would hold my phone with a bulkier case, but maybe not a Note. The height of the pocket is such that the edge of my phone sticks out just enough to not muffle the speaker. My phone is 5.375\\"H. With the flap closed there is still room for a slightly taller phone. It is also enough room for a headphone cable to easily fit with a right angle plug. A straight plug fits too because of the way the flap is cut narrower at the top but it is marginal on my phone as the flap puts pressure on the plug in a bad way but other phones may fit better. The inside front and back of the pocket have a little padding with a nice soft fabric to go against the screen.

The front pocket does not have any elastic, but it is just wide enough to hold side-by-side both a multitool and a 8-pc folding hex key set (with metal frame only, plastic frames were all too bulky to fit). The front pocket is deep enough that I put a stubby bit holder on the bottom of it and the multitool and hex keys fit on top. Total dimensions of what I fit in the front pocket are 2.25\\"W x 5.5\\"H x 0.625\\"D. Either my Leatherman Wave or original SwissTool fit well.

In the middle pockets fit a small screw driver, 0.625dia handle 5\\" total length, could fit up to a 6\\" length. The other middle pocket I fit a sharpie and a pen, you can fit a third writing utensil in that pocket if you really try but its tight. There is a gap between the two middle pockets, that while not an actual pocket, can also fit a pen or pencil.

With my phone and all the tools in there the flap closes to halfway between the minimum and maximum that the Velcro allows, so there is nice adjustability for longer or shorter tools while still keeping the flap snug.

The flashlight loop is pretty self-explanatory and tight at the 0.75\\"dia of my flashlight. Anything wider wouldn't fit. The keyring clip is plastic and probably will break eventually but the fabric loop it attaches at seems solid so that could be easily replaced by a metal keyring clip.

The initial reaction from those who have commented on it has been something like \\"is that an 80s vintage cell phone?\\" but they are nonetheless impressed when they see inside. I am told it also looks great next to my CLC impact driver holster, I just wish that holster had the belt clip too.

A nice product that I am very happy with. If you think it is too big or small there are certainly other options for different phones and more or less tools. For my needs it turned out perfect. Goldilocks likes it too

Summary of my kit, loaded pouch is 1 lb 13 oz

Phone (HTC EVO 4G LTE)
Multitool (Leatherman Wave or SwissTool)
8pc folding hex key set (1\\"W x 4\\"H x 0.875\\"D)
Stubby bit holder (1\\"dia x 1.5\\"L, in bottom of front pocket)
Screwdriver (0.625dia handle 5\\" total length)
Sharpie
Pen
Pencil
Flashlight (0.75\\"dia)

I hope this helps you make a well informed decision on the product either way. Enjoy. Or not.

review_headline: What can you say about "the standard"! - LOTS!!!
review_body:
As a cabinetmaker you seem to have to either love pocket hole joinery, or hate it! However, as a woodworker making a few cabinets I had mixed feelings. Anyway I decided to take the plunge in a small way, and bought a "Kreg Mini Jig Kit [[ASIN:B009MS5QSW MINI JIG KIT]]" just to try it out!

The kit has not been used yet. The screws however are another matter entirely!!!

Do yourself a favor and try the Kreg screws, you will get rid of those drywall screws pronto, or at least relegate them to their proper second place role.

These screws cut their own pilot hole and have a reduced shank, so if you select the correct length, they allow the top board to pull down tight without your having to drill a clearance hole. Plus the washer head means no splitting of your wood.

BTW - the pilot drill from the kit, though it has never been used to drill a pocket hole to make a joint, has had lots of use as a countersink, it has a wonderful depth guide and is of course perfectly sized for the screws.

Warning, this pilot drill gives new meaning to the term "razor sharp" - even the flutes will slice the unwary, please don't ask me how I know this!!!

product_title: Wilton 11127 675 5-1/2-Inch Jaw Width by 5-Inch Opening Utility Workshop Vise
review_body: This vise is worthless as is. Once mounted you will discover that the vise has about 3/8" wobble (yes, I know, you must be kidding) at the handle! So if you need to hold anything in one stable position, this is NOT the vise for you. After you un-mount and dis-assemble it you will discover that the center swivel shoulder bolt is about a 1/8" smaller than the cast (not drilled) hole it is in. The shoulder is also to long so that makes for a 3/32" gap between the base and vise when you tighten the swival clamp. The cast hole will need to be filed round. Then you will need to make a precision sleeve to fit over the shoulder on the bolt so it will fit the new round hole you made. Next you will need to make a shim/washer for the shoulder bolt to make up for the shoulder that is too long. This washer needs a 5/8" center hole and you will need to make it the perfect diameter and thickness. To make a two hour long story short, if I had not already drilled the holes and mounted the tee-nuts on my nice new workbench then I would have returned this pile of junk as defective. I bought this vise because I thought it looked like my 5.5" wilton vise that I have had for years. And as it turns out they really do not look all that much alike side by side, the new one is about 2/3 the amount of material. The insides workings of this vise (namly the mount that the main screw goes into) is about 1/4 of what my old wilton vise is. If you hammer on this vise to tighten it, then this skimpy little castin will snap fast. This vise (after two hours of re-building, re-designing. repairing, re-mounting) is a medium duty vise at BEST! Don't even think about hammering on any part of this vise or anything mounted in it or you WILL be using it as a boat anchor. This is one of the only products that I have ever seen that even the chinese are NOT willing to put their mark on it, not even a sticker, and I don't blame them. My advise to wilton is to remove their name from it and save what is left of your reputation. My advise to you is to do what I should have done, hit the flea markets and find a real vise for half the price. As for me, I learned to be nice to my old wilton vise since by todays so called standards it must be worth about at least $300.00 if this pile of nice junk cost me $100.00. product_title: INCRA MiterV120 Miter Gauge
review_headline: Incra V120 'Grabs' Table Saw Table Edge
review_body: Once I made a fairly dramatic adjustment, the Incra Miter V120 worked fine on my new Bosch 4100 table saw. The underside of the  device has a hard rubber pad that meets the metal front of the angle crescent and, you would assume, should be in perfect alignment with that metal edge in order to ride smoothly onto the table. But the hard rubber pad was more than 1/32nd higher than the metal and, so, its sharp horizontal edge \\"caught\\" and stopped dead at the table saw table edge. It had to be forced forward. Ultimately, I had to use an electric sander to work the hard rubber down so that it was even with the metal edge across the whole front of the  Incra. Once I did this, the thing worked great. The expansion discs worked perfectly and solved the initial problem I bought the Incra to solve -- the Borsch 4100's loosely-goosey T-slot channels. I also liked that it had two screw holes that allowed me to quickly attach a longer horizontal push fence on the Incra.  In the last year, I've purchased the table saw, band saw, router table and radial sander, all of which have T-slots in them and all of them from different manufacturers had incredibly \\"loose\\" T-slots for the miter gauge provided with the product. I can't help wonder why this is such a universal problem.  And, at the same time, it's difficult to imagine why Incra hasn't paid closer attention to this out-of-alignment problem which is the FIRST thing a new customer notices about the product INSTEAD of the fact that once it's working properly, this V120 miter guage solves the maddening sloppy T-slot issue that plagues today's workshop tool sales.

product_title: My Weigh SCGEMPRO250 250 GemPro 250 50g x 0.001g Scale
review_body:
I've been using the GemPro 250 scale for over 3 years and the best points are:

1. Very low drift. I can use it within a few seconds of turning it on, unlike my more expensive Sartorius milligram scale which requires about 20 minutes' warmup before it holds a zero reading over prolonged periods of time. This feature alone saves a lot of time so I am using the GemPro more often than the Sartorius.

2. Very accurate. Once it's been running a minute or so, it consistently produces accurate readings as good as my more expensive Sartorius milligram scale.

3. Easy to cover. I use a plastic punch bowl inverted over the scale to keep the exterior clean and I store the scale upside down to protect the weighing cell.

4. It's very light, easy to transport, and the digital readout is easy to read. The backlight can be turned off, on continuously, or on only while weighing. It's easy to calibrate but hasn't needed a calibration in 3 years. I check that daily and it's stayed calibrated for much longer than my other scales.

Worst points:

1. The weighing platform is relatively small, and requires an attentive, delicate touch to avoid crunching the cell below the platform by accident.

2. The entire scale is small, which for some is an advantage, but for weighing lighter bulk chemicals, it can be a disadvantage. I found a larger weight pan that fits with the cover open.

3. After reading other reviews, I add that the scale is entirely plastic except for the weighing platform, and as with most plastic products from China, it doesn't have the solid feel you expect from a milligram scale, but it is small so the scale is relatively unaffected by being made of plastic - it works well and is rigid enough for reliable readings.

I mentioned my Sartorius milligram balance drifting continuously during a 20 minute warmup.
I finally discovered why.
I usually turn off the wallwart (outlet strip switch) after use. Recently, I accidentally left the wall wart turned on all night, but the scale turned off, but when I turned the Sartorius scale on, it had zero drift and could be used immediately - my Sartorius was rock-solid steady - no drift at all.

The wall wart was the whole problem with Sartorius drift. So if drift happens, it could be the wall wart power supply, not the scale that needs attention, either leave the wall wart plugged in or get a better power supply.

The Gempro 250 still is drift-free after power-off and with about 10 seconds warmup, and is worth the money. I still use it daily and love it, but I wish it was a little larger. I can't say how long it will last, but it's still working for me.

The DC390B has a large and precise angle deck that stays where you set it even when you bump it on the wood. Motor does not bog-down when cutting 2X lumber. The design of the rotating blade guard opens smoothly when contacting the lumber so you don't get that jam-up at that point which can cause your cut to go astray. It's relatively light, has a truss/joist hanger and, my favorite feature, the safe button is designed to move with your thumb without torqueing the saw or making you contort your hand to disengage it.

I could not be more pleased. It works very well, and is very easy to use. It is a bit heavy, but I never felt tired when using it, although when I temporarily hung it on my pants while setting the wood in place I certainly felt it pulling. But it was so nice not to have to set up a compressor or lug hoses around, and very nice when I just had a few nails to drive in since there was no set up at all.

The only downside is that I can't find most of the smaller size packets of nails (700 count size) without paying quite bit in shipping; my local lumberyard only stocks the 3000 count size. Since I am not a contractor, I don't need the large boxes, but what I would like to have is the all the sizes but in smaller amounts.

product_title: Powermatic PM1500 1791500 BandSaw
review_body: First rate finish on every piece.  The saw came packed in a crate (503 pounds) and everything was tied down nicely with NO shipping damage, scratches, etc. The fence alone is a strong selling point.  There are other fences on the market similar to this one and I can imagine this type becoming an industry standard. It does what a tall (and low, when on its side) fence should do and is simple to adjust and set up.  The blade tensioning system and foot brake are added features, that, once you begin using, you can't live without.  I've seen complaints on some forums regarding a very short power cord, mine is over 6' and has a NEMA 6-15 plug so that's clearly not an issue.  Dust ports (2 -4\\") are designed by someone who has actually used a band saw and had to clean up after one.  Absolutely no dust in the lower wheel cabinet and the velocity at the top port is high enough to keep the lower bearing (below the table) set clean as well.  Blade guides can be adjusted by hand in seconds and the bearings are big enough to take some abuse.  I'll be replacing the blade with a Lennox (carbide tipped) since they seem to out-cut and out-last anything I've ever tried.  This is a serious saw,  I'd like to wax it and just enjoy looking at it but we have work to do!

product_title: DEWALT DW293 7.5-Amp 1/2-Inch Impact Wrench with Hog Ring Anvil
review_body:
Son and I were really excited about finally getting an impact wrench for tire rotations that would not require a large air compressor. He is my little helper around the garage.

The impact wrench looks good. Certainly on the large and heavy side compared to an air impact wrench. That happens because the energy conversion system on the electric model is fully on-board while that for the air model is split between the electrical system on the compressor and a smaller on-board turbine motor.

The impact wrench had some difficulty removing service shop fastened lug nuts, but had no problems removing lug nuts I had hand torqued to factory specifications. The immediate observations were that the electric motor got really hot very quickly, and after working on just 10 lug nuts, the internal grease pack around the anvil started liquifying and leaking out making a mess of my garage floor.

Stay away from the Hog Ring Anvil. Gets hard to fit and remove sockets.

Dewalt needs to focus on better cooling for their electric impact wrench models. Overall, don't buy. Stick with the air impact version if you have a high CFM air compressor. Else, get a 1/2 inch drive extra long breaker bar for lug nut service.

product_title: My Weigh SCPS8300 Palmscale 8 300 Digital Scale
review_headline: Very accurate, comes with useful accessories
review_body:
The Palmscale 8 300 is different from the Palmscale 8 800. As of this writing, there are many sellers offering the Palmscale 8 800, but only one (AZ Discounters) offering the Palmscale 8 300. Also, they offer the lowest price I've seen for this scale anywhere on the internet.

The Palmscale 8 300 (versus the Palmscale 8 800) weighs up to 300g (versus 800g), is accurate to 0.01g (versus 0.1g), and the units include grains rather than troy ounces. I wanted the more accurate scale to measure doses of a powdered supplement. The Palmscale 8 300 is perfect for this because of its flat weighing surface and high accuracy. It comes with two trays - small and large. I use the small one with 3\\" weighing paper to weigh the powdered supplement. (This is the weighing paper I use, if anyone is interested: [[ASIN:B007I7P0N0 Dyn-A-Med Glassine Weighing Paper]]) It also comes with a leather carrying pouch and a 200g weight for calibration, but I found the scale to already be perfectly calibrated so I didn't need to calibrate it.

The scale is very sensitive, and the instructions say not to use it too close to cell phones or open windows (drafts), and to make sure it's on a solid surface. I put a mousepad under it to reduce vibration. If you take care and follow the instructions, it's very accurate and reliable.

review_body:
I bought this for myself a year ago as a house warming gift. The sawzall alone has helped me tear down a ton of small trees and huge vines in the backyard. Having two batteries is incredible, I can exhaust two batteries doing that yard work (I am still working on the backyard), and myself in one evenings worth of work and come out feeling satisfied. I also have a 12v DeWalt drill and that has it's purposes too, as a matter of fact it is so much lighter than the 18v drill it is my go to unless I have a bigger project or need the light on the end of the 18v drill. I haven't had much use for the light, but it's always nice to have another flash light laying around. Used the saw only a few times but it was more powerful than a friends equivalent name brand battery pack saw and felt better when cutting. Batteries are still running strong after a year of weekend or week day after work projects, they hold a charge and last a pretty long time. Overall I would suggest this kit for anyone who doesn't have any buy into another name brand companies tools already, especially if you bought your first house and it needs some work!

Aside: I just purchased the [[ASIN:B000HCVN48 DEWALT DW4892 12-Piece Reciprocating Saw Blade Set with Case]] because I needed new wood blades from Home Depot, the case is fantastic for holding multiple blades, it fits in this kit's case, and they were about the same price as here on Amazon.

review_body:
Originally I was going to buy a Dremel, but a friend suggested this because it can handle more heavy-duty work. He was right. If you actually want to cut tile or metal, or grind down just about anything, you need the power that comes with this product. I used it to file down some plastic bumps that were blocking a fitting, then used the saw to cut and trim metal gutters. Easy to configure and use, and I'm very pleased with the results.

One possible downside was that the kit was delivered without two of the bits that were supposed to be included. No problem - I called during regular business hours, they asked me what bits were missing, took my address, and three days later I received 'em in the mail. No proof of purchase or receipt or any other hassle required.

Finally, they asked me to fill out a survey form, which I don't usually do...except they included a pre-addressed envelope with the postage paid, something I haven't seen in forever. I can therefore highly recommend both the product and the service behind it.

product_title: SE MJ362520LV 20x Power Jeweler's Loupe with LED and UV Light
review_body:
These are really pretty low quality, all things considered. The optics are cheap and provide a lot of distortion, making viewing difficult and reducing the usable viewing area significantly.

The LED lighting is nice as a concept - and fairly necessary given the magnification - but the electronics rig itself is noticably cheap, and the UV LED is low power and low quality as well. This would be easy to forgive if the optics were better quality.

It's also not nearly as portable as you'd think without the plastic box it came in: this unit really belongs on a desk or in the lab, not in the field. If it came with a fabric or leather slipcase, that might change things a little. As it is, I can tell that if it goes in my field bag without being in its case (which feels like it'll pop open, and being thin plastic will wear and crack quickly) it risks damage and will certainly get dirt and bag grime on the optics pretty quickly.

That being said, these do work, are kind of nice looking, and won't break the bank. But when you can get a Carson folding loupe for a couple bucks cheaper that actually has decent optics and can actually be thrown in a bag without worry, you'll never want to look back at a poorly made tool like this one ever again.

product_title: Lufkin CS8525 Control Series Power Tape, 1-3/16-Inch by 25-Feet
review_body:
This product review of the Lufkin CS8525 Control Series Power Tape, 1 3/16-Inch by 25-Feet, Orange/Black, under the category of power and hand tools is part of my obligation to Amazon for accepting to be a member of the Vine program, a club of selected customers that provide opinions about \\"new and pre-released items.\\" We enter this club by accepting free copies of products but we promise in return to submit an opinion.

Lufkin is a recognized brand and while we own several measuring tools we selected this item for review because we wanted to see how something like measuring tape can be improved. Lufkin is one of those rare manufacturers that have been in existence since 1869, providing excellent quality tools for the home and they are famous for the quality of their products and services.

We have one that is metal and if we keep our hand holding it when retrieved it can cause harm, actually cutting the surface of my hand. The new CS8525 Control Series Power Tape is easily handled, providing a perfect amount of grip and we were able to measure the room with great easy and accuracy.

It went beyond our expectations because our old tape reached 14 feet but this tape can go as far as 25 feet with its 1 + 3/16\\" blade. It was easy to stretch the tape to the target walls and the end hook made it easy to capture the measurements with a certain degree of precision.

Now, the thing that really helped us was the \\"innovative drag-strip\\" which made it easy to control the tape using only one finger and the retraction was safer than our old measuring tape.

Highly recommend upgrading your tools by the acquisition of this great tool.

review_headline: reviewing twice because i bought two now
review_body:
I install direct tv, and have installed dish in the past.

I use impact drivers on a daily basis for putting in 6 inch lag bolts annd screw clips for wiring.

I also regularly drill through walls.

I have used dewalt 18v xrp drivers, rigid drivers and recently a makita lxtd 04 white from the common 200$ set at home depot, and now Ive got two of these lxtd 01s

I ruined the lxdt 04 by leaving it in the rain. the driver and the battery dont work so I replaced it with another one of these ( I had one of these already) and two new full size batteries from the kit here on amazon.

The lxt04 is in itself the lightest driver in its class with the fastest recharge rate, and at this point it costs full retail the same as its inferior competition like rigid or dewalt.

this one improves on that one in a few areas.

it has 3 speeds. not gears it lowers its output hp so it is gentle like a screwdriver. I use this regularly for wall plates or simple things, it becomes a screwdriver or a 12 volt driver.

the light turns on and off. Nothing that good.

the battery light flashes when its low. Competors already have battery gauges on their batteries but this is better than nothing.

It is slightly more powerful. more importantly the impact engages with less push, so this is a more closer to full time impact driver than makitas own lxtd04, the common brushed motor one.

For my job this is great i wish the impact driver was always impact personally, It can be dangerous putting weight on a driver from a lladder.

the newest hitachi impact driver has a full time impact switch makita hasnt released one yet. The closest thing they have is this which is a mostly full time impact driver.

when my lxd04 died I analyzed the price on amazon and with the kit involved this one cost me 30$ more than replacing the lxdt04 and getting two compact batteries instead of full batteries. all things considered that made it less expensive or aabout the same.

this model is actually eol as it was replaced by the llxdt 06 , which is exactly like this but it has a battery guage and 3 gear speeds as opposed to motor speeds ( read, it has semi drill function.)

thats why its so cheap and you can find real discounts. I got the bare tool for 85$ and the complete set for 185$ but both of those deals are already gone as I write this.

its certainly better than the lxtd04 that comes in all makita sets. it weighs 2 ounces more, which still makes it the lightest one out there.
so how you work this into your set is just a dollars and cents thing.

I like buying this tool bare, and then getting the hammer drill and reciip saw set. Those are the best tools makita makes. their non hammer drill ( even the brushless non hammer drill) is sort of gutless.

have the top line driver, a full use pro drill and sawzall. Anything else personally should be corded except for lights and a multi dremel tool might be nice.

product_title: DEWALT DC500 2-Gallon 12-to-18-Volt Cordless/Corded Wet/Dry Vacuum
review_headline: It's ok, not sturdy, and NOT cordless without additional investment.
review_body:
The DC500 is decent, but not extraordinary by any means. At $150 for the unit plus another $90 for a battery and charger which are not included it's not a value. The unit has a \\"wet/dry\\" filter which really isn't designed for such use. Any dust imbeds in the filter and if it gets at all wet with the dust imbedded it becomes clay and impossible to remove. Power cord is ridiculously short, which means a extension cord is needed or buy the battery and charger. The Hose is quite short and if extended too much will come out of the adapter which connects it to the base unit. If you use the strap to carry it with be careful not to bend over as the over-fill protection ball will block the air intake and you will need to shut the unit off to regain suction. The hose will also get blocked with certain pieces of debris as it travels to the base. Unit is good for a car, wish it had available adapters to clean electronics.

Overall I'm ok with the unit, but it has a very limited usefulness and it's not as sturdy as the DeWalt name leads the consumer to believe.

product_title: Grizzly H5695 Cord Reel
review_headline: Poor product and customer service isn't much better...
review_body:
In theory, this is a great product but it fails to deliver. I have owned this item for several years and it finally gave up the ghost. Here are my gripes:

1. First and foremost, this cord reel has always been a problem retracting. It pays out nice and smooth but to get the cord to rewind completely is next to impossible. Since day one I've had to manual feed the last 10 feet of cord by pushing and manipulating it into the housing. Very frustrating and not what I would call a time saver... if anything, I could manually coil up an extension cord of comparable length faster than having to \\"fight\\" this device.

2. As others have mentioned, it appears the leader cord that plugs into the wall is of a smaller gauge wire than the actual extension cord. If this is in fact true, it seems a waste that Grizzly would go to the expense to provide the heavier gauge wire and would have been wiser to invest in a better retracting mechanism.

3. The rewinding mechansism finally gave up the ghost completely after a little over two years of very limited use (it's installed in my garage and gets used a couple of times a week at most). Very poor quality.

Last but not least, when I contacted Grizzly products via there website to see if they could at least send me replacement parts and I would repair/replace the winding mechanism myself, I was informed that the item was out of warranty and I would have to purchase a replacement spring at a cost of $19.25 plus $7.95 shipping. I think I'll seek out another replacement product instead... I will miss having the 40' of heavy duty cord but I can replace the Grizzly unit with a Bayco 30' cord reel for under $30 at Home Cheapo...

The color, comfort and form factor of this head set is awesome. They feel good for long periods of time and are nice and low profile. Some people dismantle them and reassemble them so the thinnest part at the top is at the bottom for even less interference with a rifle stock. The electronics work well if you don't damage them when you install batteries. They aren't affected by cell phone interference like the Howard Leight models are. I guess these are compatible with some type of comm system. I don't know anything about that, but I'd like to know what I could do to integrate that.

product_title: INCRA Miter1000/HD Miter Gauge
review_headline: 1000HD is not a very efficient tool but needs modifications
review_body:
The 1000HD is extremely well made and has that gotta have it, cool factor. But it is pretty much over engineered for most woodworking applications. My V120 is more than adequate, but it doesn't have the same cool factor. So I bought a 1000HD. Here are my observations.

After a weekend of use I am not very impressed with the 1000HD's usability. My old Jessem miter gauge is much more user friendly and efficient. I am a sneak up on it woodworker and the flip shop stop's interlocking rack system makes it difficult to easily sneak up on a cut by simply moving the stop. It tends to jump from rack tooth to rack tooth, making it difficult to move the flip shop stop for super fine adjustments. I suppose that is why Incra engineered in the micro adjuster. But using the micro adjuster requires the use of a tool to loosen the two hex screws before a micro adjustment can be made (using the same tool). After the micro adjustment the hex screws need to be retightened. Another approach I tried was to use the steel rod on the flip stop to sneak up on a cut. But that requires loosening two cumbersome thumb turns, moving a very small rod, and then retightening the two thumb turns. Problem is, moving the steel rod can and will cause at least one thumb turn to fall out of its carrier (what a pain). I don't recommend using the steel rod to sneak up on a cut; it's just not a good approach. Both processes are cumbersome and time consuming.

UPDATE: Modified the Flip Shop Stop. Removed the plastic black interlocking rack device from the Flip Stop and replaced it with a piece of oak. What a difference! Now the Flip Stop slides smooth as silk but still bites in a bit when thumb screws are tightened. Love it!

Finally, on my Jessem I frequently set the stop on the fence extender and then simply slide the extended fence in and out for micro adjustments on longer board cuts. This is extremely fast on the Jessem because it incorporated a large thumb turn to loosen and lock the fence extender. The stop is also loosened and locked with hand friendly thumb turns. Unfortunately, the 1000HD requires a tool to loosen and lock the extended fence. Further, the lock screw is low on the fence and the tool can be difficult to work with if you have large hands.

UPDATE: Replaced the hex screw that holds fence extender with a spring loaded \\"L\\" shaped turn that tightens and loosens in 1/2 turn. Great improvement.

The 1000HD is a nice miter gauge and it will find a place in my shop. But some details were overlooked that can make the 1000HD a pain in the ass to work with if you expect it to be an \\"active\\" miter gauge (easily moved and reset). Rather, the 1000HD is more of a static miter gauge (set it and repeat cuts). It is my opinion that if Incra worked through some of these details they would have a killer miter gauge.

I suppose all you Incra miter gauge fans are going to start slinging stones and arrows. Just keep in mind these are my observations with respect to how I use a miter gauge. It's not personal.

The other parts (thin metal legs aside) are made of the cheapest plastic you've ever seen. I'm a professional carpenter, and take care of my tools, but I'd be shocked if these lasted me a year.

Functionally, there's not much to clamp to, and I have concerns the rest of the plastic top will break up after a few screws are driven into it, but they do fold up and latch together (for now), which is why I got them in the first place.

In summary, nothing about these screams \\"good value\\" or \\"quality\\" ~ I'd be willing to pay more for something like these, designed and built better. I definitely feel like I paid a little too much for them.

Next time, I'll just fork out the dough for the Trojans.

product_title: Mujingfang Chinese-style Rosewood Polishing Plane
review_headline: Great Results At A Nice Price
review_body: As with most planes, especially in this price range, this one requires some work to be at its best. Allow this wood plane to sit in your shop unwrapped for a few days before working on the body so it aclimates to the humidity level. Flattening the sole with sandpaper and glass is quick. Check the front of the mouth - it may need some cleanup to allow chips to pass smoothly. Set the blade and wedge several times and check fit, looking for shiny spots on the wedge. Mine needed a little work to increase the contact surface with the blade and body - it doesn't have to be perfect. The blade is superior! It is thick HSS and holds an edge! It will require honing before use. I also did some trimming on the handle and the body hole for a better fit.  In use, this plane works very well. The mouth is pretty tight - 0.010-0.012" - as it should be for a smoother. With its 63° bed angle, I find it handles the grain and knots that create tearout with a 45° blade very well. Understand this - the higher blade angle requires more force for the same cut depth as a 45° bed angle. It's best to set this for light cuts - from feathery 0.0005" up to 0.003" or 0.004" - it is a SMOOTHER after all. It leaves a very nice finish.  The brass insert at the front of the mouth is good to have - reduces wear. The front & rear of the mouth is shaped straight up for 1/8" , so that occasional reflattening of the sole does not open up the mouth. It's a very nice tool to have!

product_title: Bosch 1250DEVS 6.5 Amp Corded 6 in. Variable Speed Dual-Mode Electronic Random Orbital Sander/Polisher
review_body:
I bought this sander one year ago. Its been in use daily in my cabinet shop,and its a terrific sander, but it has really paid for itself floor finishing. This baby in turbo mode with a 60 grit disk, strips old finish right off without clogging. Mind you, this is a 6\\" sander, so you can imagine the amount of work involved, but I stripped and sanded a 12 ft square beech wood bedroom floor to 150 grit ready for finish in about 1.5 hours. And that included flattening and cleaning up the mess a typical floor edger had made in a closet and room edges. (the most time consuming part). The dust pickup is literally 100% I use a fein vacuum with auto start.
This sander has lots of power- I wouldn't let my girlfriend or even my helper use it in turbo mode. It can really get away from you if you are hogging a lot of material off. It takes a lot of strength and experience to control the machine, but the results are excellent.
As a finish sander, with finer grits, it is a much tamer machine, smooth running and powerful. I still use a 5\\" ROS for 3/4\\" edges and sanding between coats of finish with 320 grit, just because its lighter and easier on my wrist.

product_title: Kreg KHC-RAC Right Angle Clamp
review_body:
I've been using Kreg pocket hole jigs for many years with complete satisfaction. Typical of Kreg, the Pocket Hole System works well and is a great time saver.

As one other reviewer mentioned, these are second versions of the right angle pocket hole clamps, but with softer handles and witho0ut the quick release. I have both, and IMHO these are better than the originals except when the soft handle material gets damaged due. These are easier on the hands and $4 less expensive than the all metal originals. My original clamps seem to have smoother machined threads than my newer models, b.t.w.

These work well when working on free standing cabinet carcasses as they allow the woodworker considerable flexibility. However they have their limits. For smaller face frames, I've found that these clamps have too much bulk and weight for the job. In this case, I use the less expensive Rockler Pock-it Hole Clamp with Quick release which are regularly on sale for around $15-$16. The Kreg clamps work, but are less convenient for me because of their bulk. However, the Rockler clamps are not as well made and are made of plastic, so they really only work well for me for small face frames. For other applications, the Kregs are superior. There are several videos of the Rockler and Kreg clamps online, so see which would work best for you.

I should mention that there are times when you need to hold the adjoining pieces flat to keep the joint lines flush while tightening the pocket hole screw - this is explained on the Kreg Pocket Hole videos. The KHC-RAC holds the pieces together, but won't always prevent them from sliding and ruining the joint line. The KHC-RAC is a \\"holding\\" clamp for lack of a better word. For that reason, I recommend having something like the Kreg KHC-Premium face clamp in reserve as well. The latter is more of an \\"alignment\\" clamp. These two clamps work together to keep the two pieces in proper alignment in both axes. If I could only get two clamps, I'd get one of each of the Kregs, rather than two of the RACs. Of course, more is better when it comes to clamps and woodworking.

product_title: Titan Tools 11205 Offset Micro Bit Driver with Bits
review_body: We use alot of hex driver bits that fit hex socket head fasteners.  For years, we have used T-Handle hex keys for this, but this caused a problem because they do not store well in they pick trays very well in a tool box drawer, and they are all manual, not fast.  For that reason, we switched to Snap On ratcheting T handle screwdrivers and short bit sets.  this worked great, but when it came time to get into tight places, I needed a ratchet to drive the short 1/4\\" hex bits.  I picked up my first Titan micro bit driver at Autozone.  60 tooth fine ratching mechanism, nice action and very small, which I really like.  After that, I loved it so much, I ordered two more for other workstations from amazon and also ordered the 1/4\\" standard ratchet that Titan offers in this offset profile.  They have become a mandatory tool in our tool boxes here for light assembly.  I hightly recommend them.  One thing I will mention is that I always take any ratchet I get apart (carefully) when I get it and lube the ratchet mechanism with 1 or 2 drops of 3-in-1 oil.  These ratchets ship BONE DRY so I would recommend lubing it for years of trouble free use.  Just remove the two torx fasteners in the front of the ratchet head and gently pull the mechanism out.  i would do it over a bucket or confined tray so if you drop the detent ball or small torx fasteners, you can find them and put them back in.  But just a drop or two of oil improves thier action and durability.  Awesome for small stuff and light assembly.  Buy it!

product_title: FastCap MY GRIP-BLACK My Grip, Black
review_body: This is a great idea and a grunt product. However, a few things kept the rating down. First, the product must be submerged in boiling water b apply it. Unfortunately, it floats rather well I and this resulted in it heating unevenly. This was not a large problem, as I simply boiled it longer. Second, when boiling, it had a tendency to float around and stick to the pot, where it would  begin to melt away. Even when using a non-stick surface, this would occur. So, keep it away from the edges of the pot. Third, much like duct tape, it sticks to itself initially much better than it sticks to other things. When removing it from the boiling water, make sure not to let it fold on itself until you are actually placing on as a handle and want to seal the ends together.  Last, you have very little time to remove this from the water and place on your object. Thirty seconds proved to be much to long for the product to retain its stickiness. Even after ten seconds, it starts to stop sticking very well because it cools rather quickly.  All together a great bargain with a great idea. I'm just have someone whose quicker do it if you are a bit older and slower like Me.  Either that or be prepared to try a couple times. At least its reusable.

review_body: From the time the compressor cycles on until the 80 gallon tank is once again fully charged, about one minute passes; at this rate it is going to take quite some time before replacing the break-in oil at the 100 hour mark. The compressor runs at a fairly low RPM and is thus moderately quiet and does not have that annoying sound most cheap compressors produce; in fact, it's kind of a nice rumble. Vibration is minimal, really minimal. Compressors of this type are not rated for a 100% duty cycle i.e. they are not designed to run continuously with no cycling on & off; however, we used it stripping paint at 150 psi for the better part of a day with a large external fan aiding the cooling and only tripped the motor reset once but it did have a few times to catch up while we moved ladders. This is a workhorse of a compressor. Because it is very heavy I mounted it on an industrial equipment dolly which allows for somewhat mobile use around the shop; as mobile as 700 pounds can be. The scfm rating is very high for a 5hp compressor; I don't think there are too many 5hp compressors that can match or exceed it. Champion compressors are another quality American line but I prefer the heavy build quality of the Quincy line of compressors. BTW, Quincy builds another 5hp compressor that is rated at 200psi continuous duty and 500psi intermittent duty but it is very costly and grossly overkill for most commercial/light industrial applications. Mine came with a single belt although the pulleys have another v-groove for twin belt drive from the HD Baldor motor. The compressor was manufactured in Quincy Illinois and has a 50,000 hour service life according to the manual. I installed resettable and non-resettable hour meters to insure maintenance intervals are met but at 58 years of age I'll probably never see the day it finally wears out. I purchased this product before I began buying tools and equipment through Amazon and had to pay an additional amount to have it moved from the store to my shop; therefore, I wouldn't hesitate to order it online and have motor freight deliver it. No set up is required other than hooking up the power cord; it even comes with break-in oil.
