product_title: Rayovac Indestructible 2 AA Flashlight, DIY2AA-B
review_headline: Very bright and tough, good deal for the price.
review_body:
I picked it up at Home Depot for 14. Its brighter than a 2 AA maglite with aftermarket LED upgrade, but not quite as bright as a 3 AA or 2C or 2D with built-in LED. Not quite as bright as any of my tactical lights but those cost many times more. It is much tougher than any other flashlight I've owned, especially the old style maglites. The rubber body does a great job protecting it from impacts. I beat the hell out of the thing just to see how it would survive (wanted this to be my moms daily light for her long walks home in the dark). No issues with it going out, no loose parts, kept its watertight integrity. In fact it can actually be dunked and held underwater, even though the description merely states \\"resistant\\". If you take the end cap off you can see the body is much thicker than most other AA lights. The push-button end works well, easy to work with one hand, never had any issues. The two brightness levels are nice, you still get plenty of light on the low setting and it lasts an extremely long time.
The bulb should not burn out in your lifetime. Its one of the better quality CREE's and while not as bright as the tactical lights, its also less expensive.

This is a great replacement for all those still using their AA maglites and want better light and a tougher body. Its not quite as powerful as the same Rayovac with 3 C's, but its not nearly as large or heavy. This is good for everyday carry in backpack or purse, glove compartment, camping gear, especially good for the tool box, and a nice tough, waterproof emergency light for any room in the house.

Only downside is the apparent lack of accessories and no beam focus, but the beam provides nice coverage and I cant see myself or mom ever needing focus. Its got a white, bright center dot and a bright large ring.

product_title: Coast HP17TAC Focusing 615 Lumen LED Flashlight with Tactical Strobe
review_body:
I've had a thing for flashlights since the big quake of '94 when I discovered I didn't have one handy after the earth stopped rumbling. Ever since, I've been collecting an array of cool flashlights. I recently bought some really neat compact flashlights on a carabiner clip [[ASIN:B008SOJFY2 similar to these.]] And now, on the opposite end of the spectrum, I just got my paws on this herculean, professional grade tactical flashlight by Coast. This is my second Coast flashlight, and for a brand that I've never heard of before, I'm highly impressed with the quality of their flashlights. The cool thing about this one, is it reminds me of the kind military and law enforcement carry, and definitely meets the caliber one would expect from such a flashlight. It measures about 13\\" long, and takes three D-size batteries. It weighs about 12 ounces including batteries, and Coast anticipated a personal pet peeve of mine, and was kind enough to include 3 Duracell batteries with this top-notch flashlight.

This flashlight feels good in the hand, and the weight is evenly distributed, making it easy to handle, and feels secure in the hand. Make no mistake, in a pinch, this flashlight could double as a club and knock out any intruder cold, without even placing a dent on it. The best feature is the ability to easily focus the light beam; just slide the lens housing forward or back to create a concentrated spotlight or a wider range floodlight. You can even hold it overhead, like a torch, and it will easily illuminate a pitch black room. The specs say it can shoot a focused beam around 300 yards, and judging by the intensity, I have no doubt it could reach those distances. The flashlight also has three light settings; High, Low and Strobe. The strobe is actually pretty intense, and more powerful than the crappy Radio Shack strobe light that I had as a kid. The shaft has subtle grooves to help with your grip and a comfortable rubberized multi-switch, that easily changes between the three light modes. The button also has a soft trigger, which allows you to turn on the beam with a half-button press, before it actually locks into the On position. The focusing lens appears to be high quality, and could likely withstand accidental drops or intentional impacts (within reason, I imagine.) There's also a loophole on the rear of the shaft, which I used to attach a wrist strap that I had. I guess it would have been nice if Coast had included that, too, or a carabiner clip. But that's just minor knit-picking. I'd rather have included batteries, than a strap.

Bottom Line -- Make no mistake, this is NOT an economy flashlight, but then, you're definitely getting something of high end quality to justify the steep price point. I'm really happy to add this to my flashlight collection, and it's the type of thing I'm glad to have, but hope I'll rarely ever need it. One world about China/Taiwan/Asia...- vs. American-made tools and instruments: It is American importers that provide foreign suppliers with the cheap specifications that ends with poorly designed equipment (tools, taps & dies, ...). Often foreign manufacturers will balk at American orders because it is below their quality standard and some will even refuse to sell to American importers because it violates their mission statements or their ethics. Asia will sell you the highest quality equipment at par with the best America has to offer; unfortunately, American importers (and the average \\"Joe\\") mostly want the \\"cheap\\" (dollar-wise) stuff. For the importer, it is all about profit, for the average Joe, it is paying a little as possible. Sadly enough, in some areas, American-made equipment is below European or Asian quality standards. product_title: SKIL RAS450 450-Square-Inch Aluminum-Top Benchtop Router Table with Extensions
review_body:
I was shopping for a small bench-top router table that did not require any drilling or preparation prior to use. Before purchasing this product, I contacted Skil customer service, asking if the table would fit my Porter-Cable 690 router.

Their response:

Thank you for writing. The Skil RAS450 router table will accept most manufactures routers. I have attached the owner's manual for your reference. Please write back if there is anything further that I can assist you with.

Liisa
Skil Customer Service

The owner's manual contained no information about the patter of the screw holes in the table or about which models the table would fit. I decided to order it, since the PC 690 is fairly popular, and I thought it would be included in \\"most manufacturers\\". I didn't fit.

The PC 690 LR has three screws forming an arc with 2.32\\" radius. The diameter of the 3-screw pattern on this table is considerably larger.

I returned the table for a full refund (minus shipping costs), but I am disappointed with Skil customer service for being unable to provide me with the specific measurements of the patterns on the table, or with a list of compatible tools by major manufacturers.

Based on what I could assess without using it, the table deserves two stars. Don't imagine you are getting more than a cheap router table. It is compact, sturdy for its price, and reasonably flat; that is worth something. Although I didn't get to use it, I had my doubts about the quality of the fence system provided. The extensions are useless; they do not sit flush with the table. The hole in the table didn't seem to accommodate larger bits (>1.5\\" diameter? I didn't test this).

If you want a cheap usable portable table, make sure your router fits, then consider this table.

The comfort factor is also quite good. No sweating -- a big discomfort factor with over-the-ear protectors. Quite light in weight. Sometimes I forget that I have them on.

They sometimes will rotate a little which decreases the seal with my ears. This lets more sound in but is easily remedied by rotating the protector to re-establish the seal.

product_title: Coast G10 Inspection Pocket Light, Black
review_headline: Coast G10/7830: Small, bright and handy
review_body:
Small flashlights of almost any type can be handy gadgets... unless they fall apart within the first day or so that you buy one. If you've ever purchased one or more of this type of light from some bin sale as an impulse item at your favorite chain hardware store, then you know exactly what I'm saying.

The [[ASIN:B0015VY4SC Coast 7830 LED Flashlight Mini Tac Black]], also known as the Coast G10 from the markings on the housing, doesn't fall into the above category. In the first place, it has a knurled black aluminum housing that emulates some of the larger Coast LED flashlights, but in a much smaller size. Turn on the pushbutton switch on the rear, and you get a diffused beam than has a brighter hot spot towards the center. To simplify this, here are the high and low points about this small light.

Likes:

+ Tight, compact size; just under 3¾ inches in length
+ Sturdy water resistant casing; tested immersed for about an hour
+ Negligible weight; under 1¼ ounces including the battery
+ Bright for its size; has ~24 lumen light output, 2¾ hours runtime
+ Comes with 1-AAA alkaline battery; runs equally well with AAA Ni-MH rechargeable
+ Provision on the base for a ring or lanyard; none included

Dislikes:

- Rear on/off pushbutton can be hard to use with heavy gloves in winter

Overall:

This small LED flashlight comes in a black box with cutouts in its hard foam rubber interior to protect it in transit. product_title: Bosch JS470E 120-Volt 7.0-Amp Top-Handle Jigsaw
review_headline: A very nice, very capable jigsaw
review_body:
After intending to buy the barrel-body version, I found this unit while I was out getting my project supplies, for the same price. So I picked it up. And, after using it for a lot of different cuts in both a flooring project and miscellaneous household woodworking, I love it.

What you have to know: it's a jigsaw. It's a hand-held tool designed for compromise between straight-line cutting and free-hand cutting. Its precision depends a lot on your hands, your working surface, and the blade you use. You'll never get fixed-tool performance (chop-saw, compound miter, or table-saw) on straight or angle cuts. If your cuts are going to show, you have to be very careful with this tool. That said, I was able to make several straight-line finish cuts in flooring that mated together just fine around door jambs. I had to scrap a couple attempts to get there, but I'd have had to do that with a larger tool anyways. With the jigsaw, I was closer to the work, and it was easier to pick up and try again. Good crosscut, rip-cut and detail work.

Features: The variable speed setting dial on the back, combined with the variable-speed trigger, gives excellent fine manual control when going through material of varying hardness (knots, etc.). Used with the plastic overshoe and the clear anti-splintering insert (which combine to give a clean, smooth plastic surface all the way around the blade), I got no marks on the finished surfaces, and had the added benefit of a guide line ahead of the blade to match up to my pencil marks. Between the insert and its guide line, using a stiffer blade, and the support wheel at the back of the blade, my cuts were as precise as my hands and eyes allowed. The blower keeps the line clear, and the variable blade oscillation lets me choose between four settings to trade off between speed (III) and stability (0).

A solid tool all around. Good design compromises between high-end features and overall cost. This tool is as precise as I expect a handheld power tool to be, and very easy to use. Great to pick up, make a cut, and put down again; also great for long sessions making multiple cuts, whether long cuts or complicated series of cuts. product_title: Kobalt 32-piece Double-drive Screwdriver Set
review_body:
Im giving this 5 stars because it's great for what it's able to be used for. I personally wouldn't use this for high-torque applications on a regular basis. This is better suited for times when constant screwdriver twisting becomes tedious - think of this as a middle ground between a standard driver and an electric driver. It operates as a standard ratcheting driver with one hand, then \\"double ratchets\\" with two hands. The larger driver is larger than most ratcheting drivers I've encountered. The \\"storage\\" space inside the handle is gimicky to me; the pieces rattle around annoyingly. The provided case for tips is more than good enough. Many people comment on the cheap feeling, but I believe it's strong enough for my needs as an electrician. The plastic directional switch would be better as metal, but it suffices. That said, there's no \\"neutral\\" or \\"lock\\" position on the switch unlike most regular ratcheting drivers (which effectively would make it a standard manual driver). Also, what looks like an extension bit holder on the end is in fact permanent, making the larger driver almost 9\\" long. The hobby sized driver will be very infrequently used by me, but I can say it's nice and sturdy in my larger hand. It also has the spinning palm rest like most hobby drivers.

Overall, it's more than worth one Jackson - as it is at Kobalt's standard retailer. This is a great gift idea, and perfect for anyone wanting to save wrist muscle stress - carpal tunnel sufferers especially!

product_title: Surebonder 8510 6-32, 8-32, 10-24, 10-32, 1/4-20 Threaded Insert Tool
review_body:
I purchased this tool for use with 8-32 steel Rivnut inserts. I found that the threaded 8-32 tip was very loose when threaded into the insert.

Basically, the thread on the tool tip was severely undersized and only minimally engaged the thread in the insert. When the tool was operated to cinch the insert, the threaded tip stripped out of the insert before the insert had deformed enough to lock into the sheet metal that was receiving the insert.

In fact, when unscrewing the tool, I found a thin \\"curl\\" of metal around the threaded tip...it was the thread metal shaved off of the inside of the insert!!

As I find more and more in these days of cheap tools, I had to \\"remanufacture\\" the product. I am fortunate to have a lathe and a full compliment of metal working tools. I had to cut off the 8-32 tip and drill, tap and thread in a length of 8-32 threaded rod that had the correct thread diameter. A lot of work.
The result was a useable tool...now the thread on the tip fully engages the insert and it does not strip out before the cinching takes place.

To further add insult to injury, I found that the knurled \\"nosepiece\\" corresponding to the 8-32 tip was threaded at an angle relative to the axis of the tip so that it would not seat properly in the tool. So I had to rework that too!

I now have a functioning 8-32 insert tool after a couple of hours of machining. I have not tried the other thread sizes but I expect similar problems.

It is a shame since the basic \\"metal\\" is present in the tool...it is just so poorly manufactured that it does not function.

I may have received a lemon, but I believe what I found can account for another review that I read that indicated that the tool worked for awhile then failed.

This is case where I would seriously recommend spending more money and buying another brand or finding a manual, simple wrench driven tool.

product_title: Factory-Reconditioned Ryobi ZRTC400 11 Amp 4 in. Handheld Wet/Dry Tile Saw
review_headline: Water delivery system designed by bean counters
review_body: I have been using this saw to cut thin sandstone flags, and it is a great little saw with one exception: the entire water deliver system is a JOKE. It's as if real engineers designed the saw, and did a good job, but then turned the water delivery system over to bean counters to design at absolulte minimum cost. Here are the problems I've had: 1) the attachment to water supply has a diverter that allows most of the water to shoot out of the connection (all over your work area) to keep pressure to little saw water line low. It is not possible to set incoming pressure low enough to keep water from spewing out of connection full-time and still have sufficient pressure to cool blade; 2) the water line to saw is a tiny, soft transparent plastic tube that keeps blowing off the connections at both ends. Barbs on connections are not sharp enough to retain line; 3) and this is the WORST! The fitting on saw that contains ON/OFF valve and spray heads around blade is a flimsy little 25 cent (literally) piece of brittle molded plastic that sticks way out the back of saw. It is impossible to pull on this fitting without breaking it. If you tangle the hose on your sawhorses or step on it when picking up the saw, it will break immediately (I have broken 3 of them now). In addition, when the water line blows off the barbs on brass fitting that screws into this piece, you must be very careful not to twist the hose when you push it back on the barbs: the plastic female thread on end of plastic fitting is so thin-walled that you will split it apart when you accidentally screw the barbed brass fitting further into it (just using your fingers). Spend the extra money and buy the Alpha 5 inch wet saw - I did and have been very happy with it.

product_title: Porter-Cable PCB420SA Belt with 8" Disc Bench Sander, 4" x 36"
review_body:
Update as of October 24, 2013:

Buyer beware. Great design, but needs to be used in a cold or air-conditioned environment, I think. The fully-enclosed, unventilated motors will burn-out in a hot environment.

Our 5th Porter-Cable PCB420SA belt/disc sander is still running after a full year under heavy use. The others were bought and used during the summer months. Some may have been in direct sunlight, which may have contributed to the motor burning out and not being able to handle serious use.

Our older, almost-two-year-old PowerTech BD 4800 motor failed today, most likely due to dust igniting in the motor, which, unlike the Porter Cable version, is not fully enclosed. Advantage: better cooling for longer motor life. Disadvantage: dust can get in and ignite for a shorter motor life.

Regarding Parts: It is MUCH faster to get replacement parts from southernwoodtools.com (importer/\\"manufacturer\\") for the PowerTech BD 4800 than to get basic parts for the Porter Cable PCB420SA. The Porter Cable parts I ordered took three month to arrive. Good thing it was just a spare idler drum.

I ordered a replacement PowerTech BD 4800 motor for only $46 from southernwoodtools.com today. They ship the following day via Priority Mail.

Original review from October 13, 2012:

Not suitable for serious use, though better than most \\"consumer\\" models.

We've returned 4 out of 5 that we purchased from Lowe's in a pinch for sanding children's blocks.

On the surface, the machine is well-made, but there are some design flaws that cause the machine to overheat and burn out when used to sand wood, which is all we do. Usually, the dust collection expeller fails first, but, sometimes, the motor goes first. One failed after four days of shop use. One failed after 10 days. One failed after 30 days. One failed after 75 days. The last one is still running though the expeller no longer spins. We hook up shop vacs to these (with Dust Deputy cyclones) to manage dust, so the v-belt driven expeller is not necessary and does not block dust extraction when it fails.

The dust collection path for the belt side is not actually fully enclosed and tends to throw dust into the bearings, v-belt for the expeller, and motor enclosure. The fully enclosed motor isn't quite fully enclosed and is susceptible to dust and, at the same time, overheating due to lack of ventilation.

On the positive side, the idle drum (the free spinning roller for the belt) is very well made and and like the direct drive and overall design concept. The table actually rotates without having to be moved. The base is quite solid.

We've found that the PowerTech BD4800 has performed better (5.5 amp motor still works) even though the idle drum failed after six months and the arrangement of disc and belt is a bit more awkward to use than the Porter-Cable. PowerTech Customer Support provided a free replacement idle drum which was easy to install. After my experience I'd rather spend $12 every six months on a new idle drum that play revolving door with a dozen Porter-Cable's. Currently, I'm shopping for another PowerTech BD 4800 or BETTER tool with a 1/2 to 3/4 horsepower motor.

I hope you find this useful.

All the best,

Pepi Acebo

review_body: I bought one of that together with several pieces of spare blade just over a year, I found that is easy and convenience to use. I stopped and disconnect the electric, I found that the blade can move forward and backward by hand. I tried to unscrew the housing and want to find out the reason, but no screwdriver head can fit into the screw head. I brought to Sears to see which kind of driver heads can open the saw housing. The Sales told me that need special tools, I called the service dept. The gentleman told me they don't repair those small tools, but they have parts, and asked me what was the damaged part. How do I know without remove the housing. No way, I disposed it and ordered another one from Amazon again, because I still got a lot of blades that only fit for this model and this saw is really easy to use to our retired old man. review_body: I really hopped these would help keep my air-tools oiled, but they are just not worth the hassle. review_body: This is he first tire gauge that I've owned that doesn't allow air to leak out of my tires while checking the pressure. In addition, the prior ones end up leaking out more air than I put in. I use my own air compressor, which is only capable of slowly adding air to tires. product_title: Bahco 396-LAP Laplander Folding Saw
review_body: For all motorcyclist who  like an easy campfire after a day of biking this is the tool that will pack away yet provide big results effortlessly. Price, quality, and availabilty makes the Laplander an easy choice.

product_title: Neiko 10071A Torx Bit Socket Set, T8 - T60, S2 Steel | 13-Piece Set
review_body: I have used the Neiko Hex set with no problems so far up to 500 in-lbs, but this Neiko \\"Professional-Grade\\" Torx set failed on the first use at less than 150 in-lbs...I put the T20 Tip on a 1/4\\" ratchet (it is a 1/4\\" drive) to tighten a screw holding a neutral lug in a 200 Amp service disconnect.  The screw was small (about 1/4\\") and as I was tightening the screw I heard a pop and the tip of the T20 bit was embedded in the screw and you could see the shear actually twisted the metal of the T20 attached to the ratchet! How they could call this \\"professional\\" is beyond me!  If I had put this bit in an adapter for a larger ratchet (say a 3/8\\" or 1/2\\" drive with an adapter) I could see it being damaged but this should not have happened. This set would never hold up to a mechanic working on the caliper bolts! Those are torqued to ft-lbs not the in-lbs I use in electrical work! I can only assume that this set did not get properly hardened in the manufacturing process. I am returning tomorrow. As usual, Amazon returns are painless, the return label is already printed!

product_title: Welding Jacket, Leather, Golden Brown, Interior Pocket, Heat Resistant, Small
review_body:
This jacket is excellent in fit, styling and rugged safety performance. It is so well made that you could use it as a motorcycle jacket.
Four star vs five star: I would have given this jacket the perfect 5 star if it was designed with a taller neck collar. The collar is good enough to protect your neck from the UV light and sparks. However, the collar isn't high enough to protect the back of your neck while grinding. The hot sharp sparks sometimes fly over and around your helmet and lands on the back and side of your exposed neck and you get burned. I wear a cotton cap under the helmet to cover the top of my ears and some portions of the back of my neck but the sparks still get underneath and around that cap. High collar would do the trick. Alas, I'm looking for neck covering...

product_title: Streamlight 88030 ProTac 1L 275 Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe w/ 1 x CR123A Batteries
review_body:
this is my trusted sidekick at work. runs on cr123z and it makes them last. has three settings, cycled by multiple pushes of the switch. starts on bright, then strobe (only good for irritating ppl), then lower up close light. it does get a bit hot, but that is expected since it pushes 180 lumens. my only suggestion for improvement would be some sort of replaceable rubber sleeve for the inevitable tooth hold. but this would only put this light up to 6 stars. if you are hemming and hawing over this or a surefire, save your child's college fund and get this one.

update: i have since replaced this on my belt with its big brother, the protac HL. meaner and just as leaner, but with a larger head. the lowly 2L was relagated to the door pocket of the truck, where it has performed flawlessly on more occasions than i will admit. i just threw it in there without so much as a second thought and have had to use it for things such as spare tire changes, and checking the campsite for the truck keys so we could go home at the end of the camping trip. battery conservation is good too, all things considered. still a great light for the money, and unless you own any of the other higher output lights, this will make you happier than a puppy with two peters.

update 4/18/14: this has since made its way into my hunting pack. outside opinion would call that a downgrade. quite the contrary. i trust this light to come on after rain, snow, hail, dusty atv rides, 10 mile hikes, etc. it has not yet failed me. i carry 4sevens lights on my belt now, but this will always have a place somewhere in my flashlight stable. its only fault, as i mentioned above, is that there are brighter lights out there. if you are not a flashlight-o-phile then this light will do everything you need a flashlight to do.

product_title: Racor BR-2R Double Vertical Bike Rack with Center Shelf
review_body:
This works great for most bikes, but be warned that extra wide or deep rims may not work. It holds them in place by the rims between the spokes so that no pressure is placed on the spokes. I use the racks to hold two helmets and the spacing is perfect so that my handlebars are not interfering with each other.

I docked it 1 star for the following reasons:

My mountain bike really has to squeeze into the hook because of its larger tires and rim. The hook should be made slightly larger. If my tires were even 2mm thicker I don't think it would work. My hybrid works perfect, as does my road bike and I believe most bikes would.

It mounts via only 2 screws and they are spaced 24 inches apart. Most garages/walls use 16in spacing so only one will hit a stud. This was easily remedied by screwing a 1x4 across three studs and mounting it to it. It does come with anchors, but I personally wouldn't trust them holding up two bikes.

Conclusion: 4/5, it's still a great value and works even with the limitations mentioned above.

review_body:

The sound attenuation is quite good - even without music being played. I wear them at work when I need to concentrate on something without being disturbed by coworkers around me. Now, add the MP3 player into the mix and I'm off in a world of my own! I also use these in my home wood shop and have replaced my standard muffs for these muffs. They're perfect for work and home. As for the sound, it's not bad at all.
So, considering the price, the fact that the muffs don't require batteries and the decent sound quality, this is a great deal. The only minor gotcha is the audio cable that comes with it to connect MP3 player to muffs is pretty cheap. I replaced it with a decent one within the first hour.

product_title: Makita BHP452HW 18-Volt 1/2-Inch Compact Cordless Percussion-Driver Drill
review_headline: Three Month Review from Major Weekend Warrior.
review_body:
This purchaed replaced my 20 year old Makita.
The \\"only issue\\" with my older Makita was after twenty years I could not find a re-chargeable batteries anymore. Otherwise the old drill still works super!.

Bought new Makita \\"Drill\\" & \\"Impact\\" \\"Package\\" Christmas Dec/2011....
1.) Was worried reading bit-wobbling reviews...my new Makita does not wobble. Its very smooth.
2.) Trigger goes slow to super fast without problems, very smooth trigger.
3.) Battery 18V Lithium-Ion turns out to be very good. Runs down after 2 hours of working small stuff. Probably runs down quicker than my 20 year old Makita. Good news is the very fast 5-10 minute charge time!!!!! My old drill took 30 minutes to charge(Maybe it was a better battery?).
The new Makita Drill & Impact package comes with two 18 volt batteries.
That said I have also purchased the longer lasting 24v Lithium-Ion battery on Amazon! The 24v has a 30 minutes charging time, and it is slightly heavier.

Overall summery: THIS DRILL IS LIGHT, WELL BALANCED IN HAND, SMOOTH TRIGGER, SHORT BATTERY LIFE WHICH IS PROBABLY OK FOR 80% OF DIY JOBS.
The short 18volt battery life is no problem because after 2 hours of working you probably could use a 10 minute coffee break witch is enough time to recharge the 18Volt battery. When the first 18 volt battery runs down you could always use the spare 18volt battery, and you will have another 2 hours of work time.

For me after 2 hours of any project a 10 minute break is good with me. I am glad I purchased the 24 volt battery, although after using it.........
I prefer the 18 volt battery for 99% of DIY work, I like the lighter weight.
If I was a construction guy in the field without \\"electricity\\" there is no doubt I would use the 24 volt all the time.

COME ON MAKITA AND OTHERS! KEEP WORKING HARD ON BATTERY AND WEIGHT ISSUES!

\\"If you can Envision it you can Build it.\\"
Good Luck all Weekend Warriors!

product_title: Waterloo PMX2704 26-1/2-Inch Wide by 18-Inch Deep by 32-Inch High Red Tool Cabinet with 4 Ball Bearing Drawers and Tri Channel Construction
review_headline: Little Red Chest for the Rest of Us
review_body:
Pro: More solid than others in this price range, ball bearing drawers.
Con: Only two castering wheels, marginal drawer edge finishing, bad choice for car tools.

By no stretch of the imagination is this for the professional, but it is fine for the rest of us (and that is what my \\"star\\" rating is based on - as a pro box it would be a \\"2\\").

The sheet metal is thicker than expected. I believe it will hold up well to moderate home use. There was no oil-canning of the drawers or top with placement and removal of even fairly heavy socket sets.

The finish work on the outer edges of the drawers is poor - leaving sharp edges. Some work with a file will fix this.

That only two of the wheels caster is really irritating as the description explicitly states \\"Red 4-drawer ball-bearing tool chest with 4 pivoting wheels.\\"

Having only two castering wheels, it is awkward for the confined space of my garage. I will be going to the hardware store to find replacements, which is irksome, time-consuming, and adds an unanticipated expense.

Described as \\"26-1/2-Inch Wide by 18-Inch Deep by 32-Inch High\\" the actual tool box is only ~ 26\\" high, 32\\" is the height including the wheels. Fair enough I suppose, and, unlike some others, the width is an honest one as it does not include the side-mounted stand off handle.

I bought this box mostly for my mechanic (automotive) tools - but, given the drawer sizes, it is actually better for household and carpentry tools. That was my error, as I did not pay enough attention to the drawer sizes, but was focused on descriptions of durability. Thus will likely be buying the drawer chest which sits on top (increasing the total cost by about 70%)

It arrived well packed and undamaged.

review_body: this is simply a great product and exceptional value that is something that is essential to perform some tasks.  I could not have completed my project without it.  It is a required tool for working in a situation where there is close clearances as under the hood of some of the modern automobiles.

review_body: do not buy it bad idea. It could not work for four different staples. Bought and tried to use it. did not work as suppose to.

review_body:

manafactures use. Both gibs on the vise where extremely rusty and pitted. Making the vise
unuseable until I removed the gibs and reworked them

product_title: 3M Scotchlite Reflective Tape Silver 2-Inch by 36-Inch
review_body: I want to be more visible so I purchased this tape to put on my bicycle/motorcycle helmet. Reflects light nice and strong. Please note that another reviewer mentioned that the light only reflects light back in the same direction it came. So to see the reflecting effect, keep the light source near your eyes and you can see it works great.

product_title: Bosch GCM12SD 12" Dual-Bevel Glide Miter Saw,
review_body:
The Bosch Dual Bevel Compound Hindge Glide Miter Saw is Amazing. Being in the home building industry I find the up-front controls very handy and the fluid motion of the cutting action very smooth. The saw was ready to use right out of the box and everything was plumb and level. The extentions are nice when cutting longer material and with no rails it is a great benchtop saw taking up very limited space. It is a little heavy but I'm hoping its a sign of quality. The only thing that I'd call a con would be with the fences in place you cannot make a sharp miter/w a sharp bevel cut; the hindge device runs into fences.
Overall Bosch has come up with one mighty miter saw!

product_title: Starrett 63168 SM44W Steel Tape Measure with Adhesive Back, 1/2-Inch x 4'
review_body: Bought this to replace the worn tape on my table saw.  I pulled up the old tape, cleaned the surface with denatured alcohol and then put down the Starrett.  It adhered perfectly.  I actually like this tape better than the original.  The numbers and line increments are easier to read than the old one and the bottom of the tape isn't junked up with any of that soul-less, metric crap. Its hard to go wrong with Starrett.

product_title: Smith's PP1 Pocket Pal Multifunction Sharpener, Grey
review_body:
Great price for this easy to use compact blade sharpener.
Two or three light passes on the blade and you get yourself a blade flade that would cut like if your got your blade right out of the box.

product_title: Hot Max 24163 1/16"x45" 1/2-Ounce Lead Free Self Fluxing Soft Silver Solder
review_body: If you look at the back of this package it is NOT LEAD FREE! It says so on the back in big bold print. It was very disappointing.

product_title: Craftsman 9-42717 Regular Left Cut Aviation Compound Leverage Snips
review_body: As always Craftsmans tools are very good. This regular left cut aviation compound leverage snip is excellent. The shipment was quick.

product_title: Pitbull Ultra-Portable 100-Amp Electric Arc Welder - 110V
review_headline: Works Great, Nice, Low Cost AC Arc Welder
review_body: I received my welder yesterday and welded with it today.  I purchased it to build rebar cages for outdoor air conditioning condensing units (nefarious thieves are stealing them all the time in the Atlanta area and I was a victim on one of my rental properties).  I tested it by welding sticks of rebar together with 3/32\\" 6011 rod at approx 70 amps.  This welder only tripped the 20 amp circuit I was plugged into once in two hours of welding and it happened when I stuck the rod to the rebar.  I never had it go into cool down mode and I was burning stick after stick. Today was the first time I have ever used a welder and I was able to run decent beads on rebar and flat steel after about 5 sticks.  I watched a lot of how to videos, read a lot of instructional material, and spoke with friends that weld prior to today, in preparation to start welding.  I recommend this machine to anyone who is looking for a low cost, highly portable stick welder.

product_title: MAGLITE XL100 LED Flashlight
review_body:
When I first received this flashlight, I was quite pleased. Unfortunately that did not last even two months. About a month into ownership, the light lost about 70-80 percent of its brightness and nothing I have been able to do (yet) has corrected the problem. I suspect that the very annoying switch in the base is the culprit as new batteries failed to change anything and changing the setting by the switch fails to do anything other than dim the light further. Overall, before this light broke, I might have gotten 30 minutes of light from it, at the very most. I am hoping that the problem can be solved by bypassing the switch and turning the product into a simple on and off flashlight...

Overall, I think the engineers who designed this light were a little too interested in using new technology rather than simply making a light that works. Even when everything else is perfect, it can be a pain to use the different functions of the light as the switch to change functions is finicky and it requires extreme care to arrive at the proper setting. I enjoy technology more than most, but there is a reason that the standard switch has been around for so long... nothing better has yet been discovered, and gimmicks are something that engineers should leave to the marketing department.

product_title: Ramsond CUT 50DX 50 Amp Digital Inverter Portable Air Plasma Cutter Dual Voltage
review_headline: Beats the crap out of the harbor freight cutter
review_body: I don't normally bother to review anything, but have to say this machine is *really* impressive. I have had mine about 2 months at time of writing. It is only half the size of the Harbor Freight cutter, but is 10 amps stronger and doesn't overheat nearly as easily. Mine was only Four Hundred Dollars too (they have hiked the price since then!!), so the Harbor Freight cutter at Seven Hundred Bucks went right back to the store. PoS in comparison.. weaker, overheated easily and almost twice the price?!  I have cut a bunch of half inch steel plate with the Ramsond thus far.. it does really well with that, especially with a new tip.  It goes thru the steel like a hot knife in butter.. Brilliant stuff!   It will get thru 3/4 inch.. just about anyway. It kinda has to chew through it so the cut isn't very clean.  Tops Tips:  Make sure you have a good strong compressor with lots of air flow! The air keeps the tip cool and pushes the molten steel away from it. No air or weak air will fry the tip in a heart beat.  It will eat the tips fairly quickly, especially with bad air supply and bad technique. I don't know why Amazon doesn't sell replacements.  The cutter will blast a spray of molten steel away from the cut. Be cognisant of where this is going to end up... it will bounce back at you or could damage clothing or anything around it, so pick your location and angle of attack with care. I find a nice 45 degree angle will push the steel away well and keep the tip cooler.  Thats about it. Definitely worth a try. :-)

product_title: Walboard Tool 08-001/AC31 Drywall Circle Cutter
review_headline: A pretty handy little tool for eiather measuring out or cutting drywall openings!
review_body: I've had one of these tools for about four years, now, and it comes in pretty handy when hanging drywall in entire rooms. Once you know where you want your circular cut-out to be, you can use this tool to make a nice, clean mark on the drywall (and cut it out, later using a [[ASIN:B000WP2YAW RotoZip DR01-1100 120V Drywall Router]], or you can use this tool, itself, to cut through the drywall and then knock out the piece with your hand. Either way, the tool is very handy, and it's small size make it easy to carry in your tool belt with your other drywall tools. Defenitely recommended for anyone who is hanging drywall that needs circular cut-outs!

product_title: DMT FWFC  Double Sided Diafold Sharpener
review_body: This thing arrived sooner then expected. It was a heck of a tool, not only can I sharpen my carbon-steel knifes to a razor like sharpness I can also micro serrate the blades too. The only con of this thing is that you have to \\"break it in\\" first before it become very useful. Now if you'll I got to prep my swords to sharpen with this too

product_title: Black and Decker 5106551-01 18 volt dual station battery charger
review_body: Just what I needed for my battery powered weed eater.  I have 4 chargers and this allows me to charge 2 at the same time allowing for me to weed eat more at one time

product_title: DMT W6X  6-Inch Diamond Whetstone Sharpener with Hardwood Box
review_headline: DMT  three stone in wood case.
review_body: I looked at electric/spin sharpeners and decided not to go that way because most professionals use stones.  So I bought the three pack and brought back a wusthof knife my wife said would have to be sent out.  We were both impressed, It's easy, if your on the fence go for it.  I bought the three pack because most of my wifes knives needed more than the extra fine grit, so for the price of two I got three.

product_title: Rockford CAT944 1 Gallon Air Compressor
review_headline: You Get What You Pay For
review_body: I got this compressor last week.  I took it out of the box, plugged it in and...nothing.  As much as I hate doing it; I read the directions.  That didn't help at all.  I ended up using the allen wrench that is supplied with the compressor to take off the plastic cover over the motor.  Guess what? One of the connector wires to the power switch wasn't connected (and another connector was also pretty loose).  I put it back together and plugged it back in and it turned on *YAY*.  I was happy until I realized that no matter how tight I attached the connectors, they weren't air-tight.  I had to go out and buy glue to seal all the threaded parts.  It certainly is much louder than I expected it to be! After all the tweaks and extra effort, it works fine now and meets my needs.

product_title: Milwaukee 6538-21 15.0 Amp Super Sawzall Reciprocating Saw
review_body: So far the Milwaukee sawzall saw model 6538-21 is a great tool. Powerful with 15 amps and a long stroke. It will take down just about anything you throw at it. I own a lot of tools and have used several other sawzall-like products. There is nothing like an original though. No superfulous stuff just the beefy tool you need to deconstruct just about any structure or tree for that matter. Comes with a very nice carring box with good latches. The box will keep your tool from becoming dinged by banging around in your vehicle.

product_title: Bosch DC510 5-Inch Diamond Cup Grinding Wheel for Concrete
review_headline: best tool for concrete with high abrasion resistance
review_body: Incredible aggresive grinding wheel for concrete and hard to sand materials such as Portland brownstone that have a high abrasion resistance. Typically the smaller the segments the more aggresive is a grinding wheel. I tested a lot of grinding wheels and this one keeps performing very well.

product_title: SE MW10085 Illuminated LED Zoom Microscope, 60-100x Magnification
review_body: This is not what i ordered but it suits a purpose. its hard to focus and real touchy, it does however give me a look at the trichs!

product_title: WCI Quality Handheld Pro Non-Contact IR Infrared Thermometer Gun With Laser Targeting And Type K Input - High-Speed Accurate °C Or °F Temperature Measurements From Far - LCD Display - For Electrical, HVAC, Automotive Diagnostics, Or Cooking Etc.
review_body:
Working in heating and cooling/ventilation, I don't want great tools, I REQUIRE them for safety and so I can provide my customers with quality work and satisfaction. I am confident using this for my jobs and at home. It is compact, fast acting, specific, true, easy to read.
Simply point and shoot, keeping you far away from extreme temperatures, which in the end keeps you safe. I think that is the most important factor in any home or business, big or small. I swear by this product for my HVAC crew.

product_title: Body Glove 90407 V-Line+ Dual-Lens High Impact Safety Glasses, Black Frame, Smoke Lens
review_body:
I ruined ten pair of good safety glasses before I finally discovered what was causing the destruction. I spend a lot of time working outdoors on various projects. For some mysterious reason, after wearing them only a few times, the lens on my glasses looked as if they'd had been sprayed with acetone. Even when operating a chain saw and wood chipper, I don't get hit in the face with debris sufficient to cause the damage that my glasses were sustaining.

SUNSCREEN or SUNBLOCK was causing the damage. Even the expensive stuff like Neutrogena ruins the lens.

How can I keep sweat from getting on my glasses?

If you touch the lens with sunblock on your fingertips, kiss your glasses goodbye.

This problem has not yet made it around the Internet enough to find a good solution.

To avoid skin cancer, we're bathing in stuff that destroys plastic.

Some say sunscreen will eat the paint off your car but I can't afford to test that theory.

I hope this information saves somebody a pair of safety glasses.

product_title: GearWrench Tools KDT41740 Magnetic Universal Spark Plug Service Kit, 5/8-Inch, 3 Piece
review_body: This product is awsm. Works great on Trucks with hard to reach spark plugs block off by Coolant bottles, brake boosters, A/C plumbings, etc... Beats trying to find the right length extension and Swivel adapters.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE PC250MTK 2.5-Amp Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit with 36 Accessories
review_body:
I finally had a chance to use this tool heavily over the last three days, doing remodeling trim work. This meant using the tool for everything from special cuts my compound miter saw could not touch, cutting kerfs in a piece of molding to allow it to bend to fit a curved wall, to many cuts in drywall. I used it as a saw, a scraper, and a power rasp, where it works very well. It also cuts through the odd nail when that is needed.

Since then, I keep finding new places to use it. For example, I needed a hacksaw to make a car repair, cutting through a piece of steel. The problem was I had a half inch of free space to work in. No hack saw would easily get in there, and hand work with a free blade would have taken forever. This tool did the job in short time.

Changing blades is fast, and nice that no wrench is needed. Just a squeeze of your hand and the next blade is in place. It was also nice that I could easily rotate the blade into any orientation for a special cut.

If you are worried about the oscillating nature of the tool, I found no problems there. Ok, if you let it do so, the tool will oscillate your workpiece and do nothing. Clamp your work in place and no problems. Noise levels were not remotely objectionable. Yes, when I used it as a power rasp to shape some drywall, it threw up some dust, but can you be surprised? This is why dust masks are made. The cord is plenty long. The plastic clamshell case the multitool comes in is good to carry it around, and holds all the blades, etc.

Did I need a battery powered version? Hardly. When I did use this tool, I used it heavily for a few days. But the next time I pull it out may be some time from now, and I'm fairly handy. I see no reason to want to worry about a battery pack. Is it fully charged? Will it hold a charge when I do need it? An extension cord is a good solution for the few times that the lengthy cord supplied with this tool is insufficient.

All in all, I'd happily buy it again. This is the tool that lets me solve problems I could not easily solve otherwise. I only wonder why I did not spring for one before I did.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE PC13CSL 7-1/4-Inch Circular Saw with Laser-Guide
review_body: The saw works great, and I like the laser feature to help follow your lines.  The only negative I have to say about this is that the instruction manual is really lacking.  The picture that shows where the various features are is not very detailed, but it's not too hard to figure out.

product_title: Columbia River Knife and Tool
review_headline: Excellent work, play, knife and edc knife
review_body:
I first used this knife at Sportsman's Warehouse and was greatly impressed, but decided to buy on Amazon for the price. Anyway, there seems to be some variance in the design, for example mine has a thumb stud on each side of the blade so I can open either left or right handed, but my friends does not. I think the difference is between the M4-02, the M4, and the M4-02W. Sadly Amazon does a poor job specifying this, important, albeit subtle difference. Still I argue it is worth the is.

Now that's out of the way, I am an archaeologist and spend te majority of the work day in the dirt. At first I was worried that bronze or brass bushings and steel spring used in the auto assist would gum up quickly, and it does especially in dirt. But a can of compressed air or your trusty air compressor and a little 40 weight SAE and you are as good as new. Also it is incredibly easy to take apart and reminds me a lot of the mainspring mechanism in a firelock, if you squint. I bought a tool at Harbor Freight for 2$ but I think a 3/32 or 1/16 Allen wrench will do the job. Also on day 3 I used it to open tin cans and clean off a rock face and it was still sharp. It wasn't very sharp after I dropped it open down a boulder field while surveying, but it was one piece and the bone bolsters were a little scratched up; the nicks in the blade came out with a wetstone that night.

In short I recommend it to anyone for a small EDC workhorse. I still carry my 10\\" fixed blade while I am I the field if tat helps.

product_title: Bosch 37769 T25 Torx Power Bit, 6-Inch Length, Extra Hard
review_body: This item is very good and the perfect length for what I needed it for. The picture shows that the star tip sticks out from a flat cylinder. actually it comes as a tapered look. I don't think this makes a difference in function.

product_title: ABC Products - Extra Large ~ All-Purpose Suction Cup Hook - Rated To Hold 25 Lbs (Offer is for 2 Suction Cups - It Works - Made in America)
review_body: I used both of these hooks together to hold a large mesh bag full of tub toys.  This bag is very heavy, maybe 20 lbs when everything is soaking wet and the hooks work beautifully. They haven't moved in the 6 months they have been there. They are heavy duty hooks and well made of sturdy material. Probably one hook would work fine on this bag but since I didn't have use for the other hook I used them together. I highly recommned these!

product_title: Black and Decker 20 volt Lithium Battery and Charger Combo
review_headline: Slow to Charge / Quick to  Drain
review_body: User-friendly, but the battery takes far too long to charge and drains much too quickly. I bought this as an extra back-up for my lawn trimmer.  I have a relatively small yard and go through at least three batteries before I'm finished.  I didn't want to deal with power chords or gasoline. Battery power is a nice \\"concept\\" but not efficient enough to get the job done effectively.

product_title: Festool Kapex KS 120 Sliding Compound Miter Saw
review_headline: Gone Fstool and Leaning Towards A Kapex
review_body: I oversee a university technical theater shop. My Master Carpenter came to me here in the states after 12 years in England where he developed a keen liking for Festool products. We have been changing over our scene shop to Festool hand tools and I have been extremely happy with the results. We have added a number extractors that help keep our spaces clean along with the primary shop. We build in the shop as well as loading into remote theater facilities so the extractors have been an extremely welcome addition. I am getting ready to add a stationary compound miter to replace the old DeWalt in the shop we have an integrated dust collection system that I think will work much better with the Kapex than my old DeWalt. Also the front rails will fit into our table setup better. I too am feeling the initial pain of the price tag mentioned by others in the reviews however I have yet to regret the pain of any of my Festool investments. Even the Domino rig that initially seemed quite steep but has so outclassed any biscuit rig I have ever used that I can't help but be happy with it. Both plunge saws, routers, all the sanders and jig saws that easily attach to the extractors and come and go to the theaters for build time and load ins seem to make everything worth the extra few dollars we have paid so far. I am leaning heavily towards the Kapex and hope that I feel the same when I pull the trigger on that one since I have not tested another slide compound that I prefer.

product_title: Black & Decker 74-671 Mega Mouse Paper Coarse, 80-Grit
review_body: It's a little pricey, but it's got quick-change velcro on the back, and fits perfectly on their Mighty Mouse Cordless Sander.  Likely not for a professional carpenter, but just fine for me!!!

product_title: B.A.G.G. ARCTIC GUARD Cold Weather Hand-Fitting GRIP Glove - X-LARGE
review_body: if you are looking for a winter glove you don't have to be careful with and can throw away later for the price you cant beat these things

product_title: Vornado VH110 Black Whole Room Heater 1500 Watt
review_body: I purchased this Vornado to replace one that I had for 5 years.  As to be expected, this product is simply amazing! It heats up 3 large rooms of my old home (9 ft. ceilings).  Saves loads on my gas heat costs.

product_title: Bon 41-146 Woven Kevlar Gloves, Large, 1-Pair
review_body: I'll be upfront in saying that I did not purchase these gloves for any kind of tool- or industrial-related purpose. I was looking for dependable, heat-resistant gloves to protect my hands while moving hot grill grates and cleaning the grill over high heat and flame. These gloves were inexpensive and, boy, are they effective. These are not designed to handle hot coals, but they are terrific at protecting hands and fingers when they are near them. I have used these gloves for over a year now and they show no signs of breaking down or falling apart. The yellow color is about the only negative with these, but I gotta say that the color makes them very easy to find and nearly impossible to lose. These gloves are a solid value and they perform exactly as I had hoped - far better than the Ove-Gloves they replaced.

product_title: Mastercool 85510 R134a Can Tap Valve-Screw-On Model
review_body:
This is a HIGH quality can tap to use with you're A/C manifold gauge sets; it worked well with my Neiko Pro A/C manifold gauge set. The $7 DV-134 A/C Pro can taps sold at Autozone and O'Reilly's are COMPLETE JUNK compared to this can tap... I initially bought one and when I tried to charge my car opening up the valve the DV-134 A/C Pro can tap also leaked a lot of R134 from it's valve stem, - this didn't happen with this Mastercool can tap, which when opened up didn't have a single leak. I bought two Mastercool can taps and they worked great. They also seem to hold pressure shut / not leak when closed, so if you don't fully use your can of R134 you can probably save it for next year.

Only problem with this can tap is the top will come off if you carry the R134 can + can tap by the top knob. Then you have to pop it back on.

product_title: IIT 92630 D-Ring Carabineer Key Chain, 3-Pack
review_body: I ordered these to put on spare keys. The colors are bright, making it easy to find the key I want, and the carabiner clip allows me to snap them onto a large ring on our wall, so that the keys will never get lost.

product_title: DEWALT DCL0900 Replacement LED Bulb
review_body: this works well with the 36 volt flash light. not as bright and a bit tough on the eyes when used as a work station light. The battery last so long with this bulb, I think its worth the price since it screws on and you can easily switch back and forth.

product_title: Black & Decker CD418C-2 18-Volt 4-Tool Combo Kit
review_body:
I already had several B&D tools that use this battery system, so I was interested in the circular saw and a couple more batteries (which I am sure occurred to B&D already). I already had 2 of the drills so that was irrelevant as far as I was concerned.

The circular saw works well, as long as you dont bind it. It is more susceptible to binding than a corded saw (since it obviously has less power) and as the battery runs down this becomes more evident. The \\"push this while pulling that\\" safety trigger is as annoying, distracting and awkward as all such devices are and will not stop you from cutting off your hand; may even distract you enough that you forget to watch where you are cutting in the first place.

The flashlight is, well, a rechargeable flashlight. Its not super bright but runs forever on a charge. And if you like to prolong your battery life and prevent \\"memory effect\\" in NiCds, then this is a good way to run them down before recharging.

The 'sawzall' saw is more of a 'sawzfew'; doesnt seem to work very well for non-trivial jobs. I may try buying a better blade for it, the ones that came with it seem low-quality.

Ironically, the drill (which I didnt even care about initially) has become my favorite. It has a 2-speed mechanical gear change lever on top which gives you a choice between high speed and high torque. In \\"high-torque\\" setting this is the most powerful cordless drill I have ever used. The only time I could not dive screws all the way were 5\\" long 3/8\\" lag screws that even challenged my pneumatic impact wrench.

And of course it comes with a charger and fairly nice carry bag. All-in-all a good value, especially if you are on the \\"Firestorm\\" battery plan.

I am up to 7 total batteries now, although the oldest ones (5-6 years old) only hold about 20 seconds worth of charge; ie useless, other than for the flashlight. The Firestorm pole saw is still awesome.

product_title: Plastic Picker Pail Bucket 18Qt
review_body: I do wish I could have found a smaller qt size.  18 qt was the smallest I could find in this style.  It's not super heavy, but heavier than I expected for what looks like a normal plastic bucket in the photo.  It's not just a regular plastic bucket, more like fiberglass-resin or something.  Interesting, I ordered two of them and each one was a different type of plastic and one was slightly heavier.  The harness should certainly help with that.  This bucket and harness together are a great idea!  I can't wait for those summer berries!

product_title: Pit Bull CHIDB003 Mini Drill Bit Set Tools Precision Tool Model Car, 21-Piece
review_body:
The bits:

Wow these are tiny! The smallest bit is thinner and shorter than your average needle.
They seem to be durable enough, just don't intentionally try to bend them and they should suit you well. Also, unless only a very small portion of the bit is protruding from the collet (like 1/4 inch) you can't apply too much force or you could bend these bit. I've only used them on balsa and pine and birch toothpicks so far to test them and not surprisingly they did very well. On the balsa the thinnest ones just poke right through (bout as soft a cork). They did alright on the pine and birch, but the going was much slower. One definitely needs patience to get through harder woods, and metal would still be doable but very slow. I'm currently making from scratch about a 1/300 scale model of the Italian training ship the Amerigo Vespucci, and these drill bits are perfect for drilling anchor points.

The pin vice:

This is made of aluminum and brass and is pretty cheap. There were still small metal filings inside the collet and it was at first difficult to clamp down on anything. After some fixing the thing works fine.

Before I did anything with this pin vice, I knew it needed a little work.
First I blew out the metal shavings inside the collet.
Then I used some wd-40 on the threads, this helped a ton.

I can say with certainty that you CAN in fact clamp down on every size drill bit this set has, but you may need to adjust the collet just ever so slightly before bits will start fitting nicely. I've been able to grip the smallest bit (#80) with ease. In fact, I had to bend the collet back just a little wider with a jack-knife for it to accept the largest bit.

The storage casing:
This thing is a pain in the but. I do like the design, but it is pretty poorly made and mine was way to tight. It was impossible to open the way it was designed to do, but a jack-knife did the trick nicely.

EDIT: Okay, I just need to point something out. While the case is very cheaply made, I did just notice that the tab that lets you hang the case also has little things on it that intentionally stop it from opening. It turns out you must push the tab out of the way before you can open the case. After that, well, it's still pretty tight, but much more manageable.

If you are a serious hobbyist who would use these daily, you may want to buy something a little more expensive.
But if you're only occasionally using these, this kit is pretty good for the price. I wouldn't have paid $15 for this or even $10, but I got it for like $6.50 and am very satisfied.DIT: Okay, I just need to point something out. product_title: Black & Decker RTX-1 2 Amp 8,000 to 30,000 RPM Variable Speed Rotary Tool with 55 Accessories
review_headline: Dont' buy if you appreciate a quality tool!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review_body:
I'm surprised to see all of the good reviews. Its not often a tool makes me mad, this one has so I'm writing a review.
#1 - If you tighten to collet nut enough to secure the mandrel then when you go to loosen the collet nut the collet is stuck inside of the collet nut. Literally it takes a pair of pliers or a hammer to knock or pull the collet loose from the collet nut. In the process you have broken your cutting disk. On one job I have broken about five cutting disks because of the poor quality of the collet. You don't even want to use this tool because you know you are going to have to beat out the collet when you are done. This is Black and Decker trashy engeineering at its best.
#2 - I recieved certain mandrel sizes (cutting burs, sanding discs, cutting discs)although they only included one collet size with the rotary tool. So you can't even use the accessories that were provided in the kit unless you buy another $20 worth of Black and Decker junk to get the right collet size.

product_title: WCI Quality Microwave Oven Leakage Meter Detector With Alarm - For Radiation Free Home
review_body:
This is probably not a genuine microwave oven leakage meter. Why do I say this? Here are my reasons:
1. It typically shows a reading of <0.3 within inches of my Panasonic microwave, but http://www.amazon.com/Digital-Microwave-Oven-Leakage-Meter/dp/B0027AIL7A/ shows much higher readings of 1-9. Unfortunately, this data alone is not sufficient to tell which of the two is severely flawed. Only a third authoritative meter of known reliability can tell. Even so, the Gen-El meter has pretty good ratings and so I recommend going with it instead. At least one user mentions testing the Gen-El meter with three microwaves, with variation observed among the three microwave models.
2. It shows positive readings even minutes after turning off the microwave. This doesn't make any sense. The Gen-El meter shows a clear zero, as expected.
3. The included one-page instruction manual is written with little attention to proper use of grammar and punctuation. I can only deduce that they gave the product engineering the same level of expertise and attention. To be clear, the other/Gen-El meter's instruction manual is written only slightly better, and doesn't inspire much confidence either.

I returned it. Perhaps later I'll purchase a good broad-spectrum EMF meter and see if I learn anything of interest. I am not even sure whether one can at all learn anything of the sort from an EMF meter.

product_title: Big Horn 11256 2-1/2-Inch Y-Fitting
review_headline: Does Not Fit Any Hose Or Attachment
review_body:
I have to agree with the one-star reviewer of the same 2-1/2\\" Y fitting from Peachtree Woodworking sold by Amazon. This reviewer could not make the Peachtree Y work; I cannot make Bighorn's Y work, either; perhaps Peachtree's is being sourced identically to Bighorn's. Shockingly poor design!

This Bighorn Y is sized so neither the I.D. or the O.D. can be used with any common 2-1/2\\" vacuum hose or fitting. My only recourse is to buy 3 flex cuffs (rubber tube with integral ring clamps, sold by Woodcraft for $8.39 each) or come up with a substitute sleeve and ring clamps which can either be inside or outside this Y's three junctions.

If a manufacturer is going to sell into a market, they should do their homework to make sure it their product is compatible, one way or another. Simply providing a Y function without a working interface on three junctions into an industry standard is very poor product design.

Since I know of no Y that actually works to connect within a system, at this point I am stuck with a lot of expense and legwork for a (seemingly) simple-enough fitting. Very poor!

product_title: Bosch 4100-09 10-Inch Worksite Table Saw with Gravity-Rise Stand
review_body:
Product arrived in packaging that looked really beat-up, and the box looked like it had been previously opened and re-taped. However, there was no damage to the contents of the box, the factory foam protection worked just fine. I did find something strange in the box - a deluxe low-flow water conservation shower head! Anyway, I finished assembling the entire saw and the gravity rise stand, only to discover that the table saw insert (the elongated oval snap in piece) that closes up the gap around the blade - was missing. I had a major renovation starting in just 4 days - and I needed the insert. I mistakenly called AMAZON - because I believed this saw had been shipped once before, opened and returned, and that I was not getting a \\"new in the box product.\\" Amazon could not send me a replacement insert (even though they sell them on the web-site) and all they were willing to do was send me a replacement saw, upon me sending the old one back. After assembling the gravity-rise stand and mounting the saw - I was not going to return it. I just wanted some satisfaction that I had received a product from their \\"seconds\\" warehouse. After asking for a supervisor, and spending what felt like 20 minutes listening the most obnoxious \\"chime music\\" the original customer service rep came back on the line to say that AMAZON would ship me a new saw (and stand) and that I could disassemble what I had, put it in the new box, and send it back to AMAZON. I didn't really want to do this, but I asked the cust-svc rep if they could get me the replacement within 4 days (the start of my project.) The service rep put me on hold for what seemed like another 20 minutes - with the same obnoxious chime music - until I did what I genuinely believe AMAZON customer service wanted me to do - HANG UP.

It then dawned on me to call BOSCH Customer Service - even though I was convinced that AMAZON had caused this problem. I spoke to very nice rep at Bosch, and briefly told her I feltthat Amazon was the cause of the problem, but that I had a product with a missing part. Without hesitation, putting me on hold, or contacting a supervisor - she began looking up the part number to send me a replacement. She was thrilled when I told her that I had the part number, and said they were sending one out, and gave me a reference number in case I had any problems getting the part. The insert arrived in just 2 days, and I started the remodel job on time.

Now for the saw: Excellent contractor table saw. Many of the dissatisfied reviews on this site are expecting features from a much more expensive, permanent mount type table saw in a woodworkers shop. The motor and spindle were square and aligned right-out of the box. The fence clamps parallel and true to the blade - every time. There is a little \\"chatter\\" as you slide the fence back and forth - but other than the sound it is not a problem. The riving knife and kick-back guard and well engineered, well made, and do not get in the way. The mitre gauge leaves a little to be desired - but is as good as any other CONTRACTOR grade table saw out there. The table extension is extremely sturdy. The built in fence measuring gauge is surprisingly accurate. With a Freud Diablo finishing rip blade, this saw slices through 2X and cabinet ¾\\" plywood like a hot knife through thru butter. The motor has plenty of power. The Gravity Rise Stand is truly amazing and easy to use. I have just finished building a complete set of \\"built in place\\" kitchen cabinets, with lots of rips, dados, and rabbets - and this saw is the best PORTABLE CONTRACTORS table saw that I have ever seen.

product_title: Genesis GMT15A Multi-Purpose Oscillating Tool
review_body:
I must admit that I was a bit skeptical of this product because of its low price. While shopping around, I did quite a bit of searching online but also went to the big national home improvement store chains to see what they had to offer. If you have done the same, you will likely have discovered that the starting price for similar tools tends to be in the $100 range. Online, one can find a few less expensive tools but having seen the much higher price elsewhere, I didn't quite know what to expect.

The Genesis seemed to get some of the more positive reviews and those reviews also seemed more numerous and more consistent than those of other, inexpensive oscillating tools. Thus, I decided to give it a try, thinking in the back of my head that it wouldn't be a large financial loss if this tool turned out to be a dud.

Well, it turned out to be stellar. I've used it to cut laminate flooring (plenty of it), hardened fiberglass, dry wall, etc. and never encountered a problem. The Genesis cut smoothly, quickly, and efficiently.

While I have no way of comparing this particular item to the more expensive versions, I simply cannot think that those expensive tools could do a better job than the Genesis. After all, a smooth cut is a smooth cut - and that's what this tool does really, really well.

review_body: This is, of course, the standard Exacto blade holder and handle, so no surprises there.  Exacto is the best quality knife for many of the projects I do. When the blade is dull, I put it away until I need to clean the crumbs from between the stove and counter, for instance.  The non-cutting side down, I can get out some of those pesky crumbs that I wouldn't be able to reach any other way.  Getting ready to re-paint some of my interior rooms and, in my book, an exacto knife is a necessity for painting.  It's good for removing caulk or bumps that others have painted over before I spackle and repaint and even cutting small holes around those and other kinds of wall blemishes, in preparation to filling, sanding and painting them.  For crafts, I use them to remove rough plastic edges and flashing but where I really love them is in using the edge of the blade to move pieces around precisely before adhering them.  Then, when I decide where I want them, I apply my adhesive tape or dots and use the end of the handle to apply pressure to them to assure that they are stuck tightly.  This knife has literally hundreds of uses and I couldn't live without at least one.  Apparently, someone I know agrees because my old one disappeared.  I'm sure glad to have this one to replace it!

I don't really use the laser but it is effective when dialed in.  Gentle start, easy to change the blade, pretty much ready to go out of the box, I have not been disappointed.  I give it four stars only because it is no longer manufactured in the USA (like Delta), which is a prerequisite for five stars in my book.  Unfortunately, Delta doesn't make miter saws anymore.  After nearly a month in my shop, the Jet is holding up nicely though.  I use it to cut everything from cedar to ipe and it cuts aluminum beautifully.  Would definitely recommend it to a friend.

review_body:
I needed a 4-inch grinder with a 3/8\\" arbor adapter for using flap discs in my welding shop. My ancient Makita had finally died, so I bought this one to replace it. The grinder is well-balanced, reasonably powerful, and smooth running. The angled side grip is a nice touch, and is more ergonomic than the old one. The power cord is reasonably long, and made of actual rubber, not cheap plastic. It coils well, and doesn't hold memory too badly (which is good, because it has to be coiled very tightly to fit in the case: see below).

The case, however, needs some work. It holds the grinder and a few wheels, but the cord has to be coiled just right, or else the case won't close. Come on Makita, there was plenty of room to give me more than 2\\" for the cord. Heck, you could have left the whole top of the case unmolded, and given me room for a pair of gloves, or a short extension cord. Instead, you molded the entire thing full of empty plastic, and the case is annoying to use.

Nonetheless, I bought the grinder, not the case. The grinder works great, and lets me make use of small-diameter arbor flap discs.

product_title: Wall Dog Anchor Screw
review_headline: Great if used for the right kind of jobs
review_body:
I have used dozens of fasteners for over 40 years (I am 60) and have taught classes in the use of wall fasteners as part of a course I designed and taught at three junior colleges in San Diego. The WallDog is an very interesting and unique fastener. It should NOT be used in place of a togggle bolt and it does not have as much holding power as the larger threaded EZ Anchor, however I love it when I need to attach things to drywall for things which do not need the strength of those other anchors but which need a great deal more holding power than just using a drywall screw into drywall only. For example, I just installed a number of 1 x 6 wooden shelves (3 - 4 feet long each) under some of my windows for my cats to sit on. Each shelf was installed on top of two wooden support brackets each of which used 4 screws to attach it to the drywall. With 4 screws in each bracket, the WallDog was more than adequte and a heck of a lot faster than having to use either the EZ anchors and separate screws or toggle bolts, or needing to locate the studs with a stud finder (and they would not have been in the right places anyway). I will be buying another box of 75 of the 1 1/2 inch style that I can only find at Home Depot. Everyone else carries only 1 1/4 inch which is not quite as long as I want to use.
I hope Amazon will bring in the 1 1/2 inch model as the extra 1/4 inch can be3 important. I am nor surprised that they were not adequate for the reviewer who9 use them for curtain racks. I never would have assumed that it would be strong enough for that since the angle of stress on the curtain brackets is quite high and the brackets are not large enough for the WallDog to grip drywall in positions far enough aw3ay from one another to give the required holding power

product_title: Pro-Grip Mortising Hinge Mate By Peachtree Woodworking PW584
review_headline: Good for close, but not perfect work
review_body: The idea of this system is simple, and perhaps that's why it didn't come with instructions?  No problem, the online videos available at Youtube show how it works just fine.  The main complaint I have with this product is that the manufacturing of the aluminum extrusions needs some touch up.  The middle section of the rail is just a bit taller than the edges of the rail, may 1/64\\".  This doesn't seem like much, and it's not, until you find your router base bumping into one of these sections and of course lifting the router bit up.  The resulting hinge mortise ends up with small high and low areas.  To combat this, I bought a larger acrylic router base, the kind you set into a router table, and that worked fine for small hinges.  Big hinges still ended up with me riding over the bumps.  It may be worth surfacing the tops on a mill to get everything just right.  Otherwise, the system is nice, small, easy to set up.

product_title: DEWALT DCK210S2 12-Volt Max Screwdriver/Impact Driver Combo Kit
review_body: I have been a construction worker for many years and have used many tools,and this is the best piece of equipment I have ever used. Period. I install above ground pools and I needed a drill that was smaller and lighter than the 14v DeWalts i was using. I looked at all of the 12v compact drills, I watched videos, read reviews, and went to the store  to feel them in mt hand. I could not decide, because they all had the same grip: fat and uncomfortable. I picked up the DeWalt and knew it was the one. This little drill is beautiful. You can instantly tell the amount of r&d that went into this drill compared to the others, it is perfectly balanced, and extremely comfortable. Due to the angles which I must drive screws, other drill hurt my wrists, but this drill does not. My work speed has increased quite noticeably with this drill as well. My work requires the drill to withstand being thrown in the sand and dirt numerous times a day. and withstand rain and heat as well. The only issue I have had is sand in the clutch adjustment which makes it hard to turn (happens to all drills). This drill is tough. It is quite powerful too, and will snap your wrist back on the drill setting if you are not careful. Add to the design, power, and durability, it charges in 15 to 20 minutes and the batteries last about two hours of full power screwing and drilling. i belive that this is the best drill money can buy, and unless you need an extremely powerful drill and stiffer clutch , can replace your clunky 18v quite well.

review_body: I bought this nailer from Amazon and after shooting about 20 nails it misfired, why? it did not jam at the nose piece, that was fine. I tried opening the magazine cover and I could not. That is where the jam was . Where the spring loaded pusher  pushes the nails, the nail slipped over the pusher, wedging between the magazine cover and the pusher. I eventually got it unwedged, and started using the nailer again, it repeated this mess several times. I called the factory rep. He recommended me to return the nailer, being it was bran new and it probably had a defective magazine cover. I exchanged it for a new one, same problem. I even took it to a service center. Returned it for a refund. I still liked how light and nimble this hitachi nailer was, I went to the local lowes store and talked to them, They said the hitachi's are good nailers and they did not have any issues with them. They were on sale and were selling alot of them. The price was still a little higher than Amazon, but I decided to buy one from lowes. I took it home and it operated flawlessly. Now I am a happy camper. Why did I get two bad ones from Amazon and finally got a good one from another retailer???? The important thing  is, I am well pleased with the nailer I have now, but had to cut through some crap to get there.
