product_title: Sears Brands Management Copr 00937548 "Craftsman" Tool Tote 12"- Black & Grey
review_headline: I'm sick of zippers and latches!  I want instant access!
review_body: The lock on my old tool box was about to break, and since it was necessary to have it shut properly in order to carry everything around, I decided to get a new one before I left a trail of tools across the house.  I found mine at Sears Hardware, in several different side pouch colors.  My experience with the old box (which resembled a suitcase) led me to decide to try something that didn't have to close at all.  I was tired of breaking latches and trying to force zippers closed!  There are net pouches on each narrow side, but only one long side has the outer red (in this photo) canvas pouches.  The other long side has some velcro straps that it says are for holding levels in place. (Or whatever else you want to put there.)  Inside there are elastic strips sewn into each of the long sides, forming loose holding pouches, but nothing on the short interior sides.  The metal frame feels quite sturdy, and all the pockets and elastics appear to be well sewn.  There are four heavy rubbery type feet on the bottom.  There is also a metal . . . thing on the side to hold your tape measure.  My biggest concern was whether it would hold my hammer, since it was only 12\\" long.  As I was fortunate enough to be at the store with this, I was able to try out hammers in the tote to see if they would fit.  The regular size hammers (about 13-14 inches) fit at an angle without causing problems, but for larger hammers, not so much.  When I got home I discovered my hammer was even smaller than the basics, so I lucked out!    What's in it now?  My hammer, my B&D power drill, a set of screwdrivers tucked neatly in the pockets, multiple screwdrivers, several jars of nails and screws and misc bits, a small level, three tape measures (one on the outside), pencils, a scraper, a bottle of glue, a sanding pad, a tube of drywall putty, a drill bit set, a hot glue gun, pliers, a wrench, some tiny screwdrivers, and a few workshop rags.  There is plenty of room for more, just not my DeWalt drill, but that has its own case.  I do not feel this tote will tip over easily, nor that anything will fall out of it accidentally, and it is not too heavy to carry around.  It was exactly what I was looking for.  I only hope it's what I needed and that it will last longer than the previous case.

product_title: Mechanix Wear - Team Issue Knee Pads
review_body: I purchased these knee pads last year as a Christmas present for my then 81 year-old father who has literally spent his entire life on his knees at hard labor on our/his property. Amazingly, he's now 82, does the same hard work capable of any strapping 18 year old, and he ain't slowing down. Thus the purchase; I couldn't stand to watch him continue to pound his poor knees at his age. I have *never* seen this man protect his knees from hard-packed dirt, concrete, lawn, ditches, rocks, black-top or any other surface. He has told me that in his lifetime he's tried many different types of kneepads but I've never seen him in them. So, anyway, I did my research and happened upon these. Turns out, I hit the mother-load. He faithfully wears them for a number of very good reasons: 1. he reports that once on, he doesn't even know they're 'there.' That's good, because, like I said, he acts like a teenager when tackling out-of-doors projects. 2. He reports that they DO NOT SLIP. I can only imagine how important this would be. 3. They WORK. Perfectly designed, they are forgiving, rugged work-horses. They perform better than the Manufacturer's Product Description. Given my experience with my dad's demanding routine and my own expectations for good, comfortable, sturdy protection, these are a grand-slam. Buy them. COULD NOT BE HAPPIER!

product_title: Chicago Pneumatic SS3113D 3/8" Drive 13 Piece Metric Deep Impact Socket Set
review_body: Been using these for 3 to 4 months, great for the price they are, haven't had issues to speak of and been beating the crap out of them, no rusting, no numbers wearing off, no rounding out or breaking. great product and a great price. did a review on the other 2 sets of these as well, the other 2 sets are just as good, no issues and i use them every day on land rovers doing anything from water pumps to oil changes to rear ends to brakes and suspension.

product_title: Vaughan 19710/S2 Split-Head Hammer
review_body: We recently bought a bunch of hammers. This one comes out on top.  We bought a DEWALT DWHT51145 15 Ounce MIG-Weld Framing Hammer, a Vaughan 13050 24 Ounce A/S Rip Hammer, a Stanley 51-946 22 Ounce AntiVibe Framing Hammer, a Stanley FatMax Xtreme AntiVibe Rip Claw with Smooth Face 24 oz. Hammer 51-179, a Stiletto Tools Inc TB15MS Ti-Bone Titanium Hammer With Straight Handle, and a Vaughan 19710/S2 Split-Head Hammer.  The two Vaughan's came out on top. They have no noticeable vibration, even though they are not anti-vibe hammers. I used to love my Stanley antivibe's, but now I have a new favorite, the Vaughan 19710/S2 Split-Head Hammer. Not only is it vibration free, it gets a lot of eyebrows raised because of its odd look. On another note, we have driven landscaping spikes through 2 6X6's with the Stiletto. It will drive more than a 2 lbs mini sledge, which was amazing.

product_title: Ergodyne ProFlex High-Performance Back Support Belt, Black
review_body: Belt worked well, as expected- helped relieve temporary back pain from repetitive motion.  Easy adjustments with velcro straps made this a winner- also good back stiffeners.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE 75182 Variable Speed Router Motor
review_body: I would have given 5 stars, but the runout at the collet was a bit excessive for a router this pricey.  It's only really noticeable with my largest panel raisers, but this was why I invested in this particular router in the first place. It sits in a benchdog tablesaw extension and router lift. This router really complements this particular setup, it makes for a very heavy duty, robust and professional setup. I'm very pleased. Like others have mentioned, I ordered machined collets for it, which cost about 40% of the total price for this router. I wasn't really happy about it, but I did get 1/4 and 1/2 collets in the set, which fit my other PC routers(and many others) as well. Again, only really noticeable with my big raisers, and checking with a dial indicator gauge I use to check slot-to-blade and fence to blade runout. I'd like to report that I noticed a huge reduction in vibration, and vast improvement of bit performance with the machined collets, but honestly I didn't see that much difference. Bottom line: This router HAS to sit some type of router lift, but I doubt you'll find a more versatile router with this much power, that fits as many router lifts. Since I had no plans to try to manhandle this thing as a straight up router, it was nice to save almost 100 not having to buy the fixed/plunge bases.

product_title: Gerber Infinity Ultra Task Light.
review_body: This is the 3rd Gerber flashlight I've bought. they're all wonderful. Best flashlights I've ever owned. If you need a great flashlight I couldn't recommend a better choice.

product_title: Fein Wet/Dry Vacuum with Auto-Start - Variations
review_body:
I bought this unit in February of 2009 with all of the accessories. What I like is its stability and low noise. It has plenty of power and still remains quiet at the highest speed. Achieving the variable speeds consists of repetitive pushes on one of two buttons. LEDs light to indicate the speed range selected. It is not an infinitely variable speed, such as is found on a light dimmer. I use it to clean the fur/dust from my two rabbits and where they have missed the litter box. Their enclosure in the tiled Family Room is about 11 feet in length by 7 feet wide. They also have a ramp to go up to their other house. They are not afraid of it. However, I did get the bright idea of using it on its lowest speed to vacuum the excess fur. When the brush sucked that fur coat up, Erik's eyes got wide and I just knew that this idea was not a good one. While they are a mated pair, the female, Bandit, ran and hid from me after I had stuck the vacuum on Erik. He was not hurt and I use the hand brush. One slight problem was when one of the contractors used the unit to clean the fireplace. The soot went through the paper bag and blackened the snow white cloth filter. Of course none of this I knew until they were gone. It was a real mess to clean up.

This unit is used primarily for the rabbits because they do not like loud noises. I used it once in the garage with a portable stand mounted sliding compound mitre saw. The unit works very well. The vacuum continues to run for about 6 seconds after the saw had stopped to allow the vacuum hose to clear. It's pretty neat. This vacuum is a quality unit and I like it very much.

product_title: Oshlun MMA-0303 1-1/3-Inch Standard HCS Oscillating Tool Blade with Uni-Fit Arbor for Fein Multimaster, Dremel, and Bosch, 3-Pack
review_body: I use these blades on my Corderd Bosch Multi-X and find they work great as a standard wood blade.  There really isn't much to be said, the last as long as Bosch or Fein blades, I haven't had problems with them breaking at welds...you won't be disapointed.

product_title: Pet Blinkies for collar , leash or harness
review_body: This is the best collar light for walking at night. It is lightweight and very bright. I highly recommen it.

product_title: Silverhill Tools ASDY32 Triwing Screwdriver, Size-3.0

review_body: I received the screwdriver shown. It is labeled Silverhill triwing. I has the yellow ball at top and black handle. product_title: Makita MAC2400 Big Bore 2.5 HP Air Compressor
review_headline: Just what the other reviews said it would be.
review_body: I ordered the MAC2400 on Monday and it was here by Wednesday afternoon a day earlier than Amazon had indicated.  Fed Ex delivered it to my door with arrows up!  I am not disappointed.  No damage, the cowling needed to be carved out for the air filter to fit properly (I used my Dremel with a sanding disk), it's quiet, especially compared to my large Porter Cable air compressor (which has given me good service) and as expected, the manual is a little vague but having read a lot of the  MAC2400 reviews I found no problems completing the minor assemble needed and breaking it in.  I ran it over a half hour with the tank drain open to break it in, then realized I had slightly over filled the oil by dumping the entire bottle of oil into the crankcase.  When I drained the excess oil  back down to the red dot I  was interested to see the amount of metal/aluminum particles that came out with the oil.  I dont think this is unusual though but I do plan on changing the oil early on after starting regular use.  I really find these reviews to be very helpful and appreciate everybody that has taken the time to submit one!

product_title: Peltor Junior Earmuff
review_body: Knowing that my daughter only has one set of ears to last her whole life, I bought these so she could attend outdoor music events with us.  At 5mos old she did wonderfully with these and slept through several performances.    I highly recommend them.

product_title: Rayovac Lantern
review_body:
Last week I had the opportunity to shower and get dressed in the dark in the light of my 9 hours emergency candle(s). Right away I understood the shortcomings of my backup lighting system. I did not have candle stands, the slender candles were easily tipped over and thus a fire hazzard and you have to have fire to light them. These holes in emergency preparedness could have been plugged with candle trays and storing matches or a lighter with my candles and if you so choose, this is a perfectly acceptable approach. However, for me I decided to search for an alternative that was safer, energy efficient and that produced better lighting. Enter the Rayovac Sportsman Xtreme Lantern.

I went to Amazon to do my normal research and the Rayovac bubbled to the top because it has an LED lighting system that works well, is very easy on batteries, has two main light settings and has a fairly rugged construction. The lantern takes 3 D-cell batteries and on the low setting will provide 150 hours of lighting (72 hours on high). The low setting still throws a good amount of light and even for an extended power outage (lets say a week long) I can't imagine running the lantern for more than 6 hours a day. That means it will keep me illuminated for 25 days before I need to replace the 3 batteries. That is incredible performance that would take about 17 9-hour candles to duplicate (and throw about 1/4 the light). To match the low output power of the lantern it would probably take about 4 times that number of candles or about 68 candles! By the way it will cost you about $102 to buy 68 candles; for that price you could by 4 of these lanterns with money left over to buy a boat load of batteres. The lantern has a nice handle that neatly folds into the latern body and a hook on the botttom so you can hang it upside down to provide overhead lighting. I have read some reviews where people talk about the difficulty of reattaching the battery lid. It is really very simple, just allign the arrows of the bottom of the lantern with the arrow on the inside of the battery lid and give it a 1/8 turn to secure it in place. I think there is a nice picutre of how this works in Amazon's description of this item. If you do not align the arrows (or have no light to see them ... hmmmm) you probably will have trouble. I bought two of these lanterns to keep me going in two different rooms in the event of another power outage. I am also an outdoorsman and will be taking one of these with me next deer season.

Soooo, if you are an outdoorsman or want to beef up your emergency prepardness kit I thnk you will be very happy with these inexpensive, power sipping illumination wonders!llign the arrows of the bottom of the lantern with the arrow on the inside of the battery lid and give it a 1/8 turn to secure it in place. product_title: Armed Work Wear 12-Ounce Cotton Canvas Work Pants with Built-In Knee Pads, Dark Khaki
review_body: The slot or pocket for the knee pad inserts is set off center to the outside of the legs, therefore the pads do not work 40% of the time; BIG TIME OUCH!!!!!

product_title: F016800183 Bosch ART 26 Accutrim Blades Pack of 24
review_headline: Innovative design makes blade replacement a breeze - effective & durable on grass (even buffalo) - expect wear against concrete
review_body:
UPDATED FEB 13, 2012
Yes this is the \\"whipper-snipper line-reel of the future\\" - in the form of a short red plastic blade.

Love that it is easy to replace - simply loop the bigger hole onto the mounting shaft (tip) and \\"click\\" by pulling the smaller hole onto the mounting shaft to lock on. Bosch innovation comes into the fore again.

SURPRISINGLY EFFICIENT for BOTH EDGING as well as grass trimmings, even though powered by 18V Lithium batteries instead of 36. For effective edging your will need to have brick edging for the blade to give a clean cut.

Blade does not wear on grass, but does melt away some against concrete. If you treat it as a consumable then this shouldn't worry you. Cheaply replaceable in packs of 24 circa $15-$18. Goodbye to troublesome line-reel replacements in the more traditional trimmers or messy adjustments.

KUDOS to the design team at BOSCH!

product_title: Delta Industrial 46-460 12-1/2-Inch Variable-Speed Midi Lathe
review_body: Do not buy this item from Amazon unless you want to take a chance on wasting a lot of time and effort.  The first 46-460 lathe I received had a smashed ON/OFF switch and speed control box.  The replacement I received had a completely broken off mounting flange.  So three possibilities exist - none good.  Damaged equipment was repackaged and sent to me or the shipping was so rough two separate times (a drop ?) it twice damaged the equipment but left the boxes OK or the equipment is so fragile that normal shipping destroys it.  So I have returned it and the assembled stand that never saw a lathe mounted on it to Amazon for a full refund and will look elsewhere.

product_title: FastCap Chopshop Saw Hood
review_body: We are remodeling and had to set up the saw upstairs on our deck. It was so great when I didn't have to clean up all the dust after the job was done. And the Saw Hood also protected the saw from the rain. Super simple to set up and take down and it collapses flat for easy storage. Now we keep it on the saw in the garage for other smaller improvements on the house. It is nice that there isn't a layer of dust on everything when I'm finished. Keeps the gargage clean and the wife happy. I recommend this to anyone!

product_title: Allied International 89086 Mechanics 32 piece Combination Wrench Set SAE/Metric
review_body: An otherwise good set of wrenches at a low price, got it at just over $25 and was about $27 just a week before my order. Guessing this might go up again before going down.  I would have given these 5 stars due to both price and reasonable quality if the stubby 3/8 inch wrench hadn't been missing with a second stubby 10mm in its place. I won't complain (much) since there's only a 13/1000 inch difference, meaning it'll do okay most of the time. 10mm is slightly larger than 3/8 inch so no problem putting the wrench onto nuts and bolts, it just doesn't fit tight.  Plastic case appears flimsy and crude (in hand, not from picture) yet seems to hold the wrenches firmly and easily enough. But I sure wouldn't throw it into the back of my truck and expect it to stay together every time!  Mainly telling this so other buyers reading reviews will be sure to check the sizes immediately. I'm not going to return for exchange risking yet another problem, can't beat the low price anyway because a couple large wrenches at Sears cost the same as this whole set (with free shipping).  So considering all this I would say take a chance on it as long as you think over my review here and can deal with the possibility of a return/exchange.

product_title: Mainstay Emergency Food Rations - 3600 Calorie Bars
review_body: In my opinion, the best tasting and most nutritionally complete ration as compared to Datrex, ER Bars & Mayday. Has the texture of a shortbread cookie & flavor of a vanilla-ish sugar cookie. Comes vacuum packed as one large bar scored into 9 smaller bars (very easy to break apart) so carry a Ziploc bag with you to store the uneaten bars. That the bars are not individually wrapped is pretty irrelevant when you consider that if the situation at hand dictates you must subsist on this product for a day or three you will likely end up having to consume the entire package anyway.

product_title: CH Hanson 15217 21-Inch Marking Flags
review_body: I was looking for something to mark our dogs messes with in the backyard since my son was having problems finding them. I had seen the flags outside our house marking the gas line and it dawned on me why not use flags. I got the hot pink ones so they cannot be confused with the water, gas, and other \\"official\\" flags.  They work great! When there is a sea of pink flags in the backyard it's time for my son to go clean 'em up. It goes so much faster & he doesn't complain as much. My neighbor even likes them because she can see where the messes are and knows not to park the car to close to them so her kids won't step in them. I am hoping they will make cleanup in the winter snow easier & faster too.  Only problems I have had are they rusted with all the rain and are easy to bend if the ground is too hard. But for the price, amount of flags, & not having to hear my son complain it's to hard & takes to long they are worth the money & I will most likely buy more in the spring.

product_title: Nite Ize SpotLit Clip-On LED Light with Carabiner, Weather Resistant

product_title: Delta Industrial 46-462 Midi-Lathe Stand with Straight legs
review_body:
The stand no longer has splayed legs. The legs are straight. Having said that, the stand is still VERY sturdy. It was a great improvement over the wood workbench I had previously been using. I was able to mount a 12x3\\" blank on the lathe and could run up to 1500 rpm with no vibrations, even at that size.

I do have a couple complaints: There is no place to store the knockout bar except in the tool holder. Also, the tool holders could be a little lower. I had a long tool handle get wedged under the motor and I burned my hand on the hot motor when reaching down to free it.

product_title: DELTA 20-950 20-Inch Variable Speed Drill Press
review_body:
I have had several e-mails back and forth with both Delta and a vendor I was able to find that still has a few 20-950s for sale, still packed in original packing. Here are quotes from e-mails I have.

Delta says: \\"Unfortunately, since the product you are looking to buy has be [been] discontinued some time ago, the warranty would no longer be in effect.\\" And, \\"The reason why the model 20-950 was discontinued was related to the variable speed control mechanism and that service parts are not available for this particular model. We are working on improving the quality of this machine for when we do re-introduce this machine. As soon as we can improve the quality to a level that our customers expect from the DELTA brand we will re-introduce.\\" And, \\"It is in our plans to discuss bringing back the 20-950 Drill Press, but that will most likely not happen for at least a year. We are not sure exactly when it will be available.\\"

Vendor says: \\"When Delta decided to discontinue this machine we purchased all the inventory that was left in stock as this was and still is a very popular machine. We have less than 5 left.\\" And, \\"We do have a few unit[s] left in stock, that are still in the original boxes from Delta. When Delta decided to discontinue this machine we purchased all the inventory that was left in stock as this was and still is a very popular machine.\\" And, regarding Delta's written assertion that it will NOT honor the warrantee, \\"... Delta should be honoring it. It should not matter [whether] it would be purchased through a[n] authorized dealer that still has inventory. Warranty starts from date of purchase to customer.\\" And, regarding parts, \\"The new Delta company does not offer parts for older machines [;] they are offered from Dewalt the original company that owned them before the take over.\\"

In summary, the vendor has a few original machines. They are for sale at full price, despite being discontinued several years ago, and despite Delta saying the warrantee is void. I have not checked whether Dewalt has a good inventory or parts. I am not an attorney; I do not know whether Delta should be honoring the warrantee; I only know that it says it is not doing so.

The stats on the machine are wonderful, as we all know. Am wondering how folks have been doing with the ones they have been using the past few years. And, given what they know and have now read (above), were they in the market for a drill press right now, would they buy one of these last few remaining available machines??

product_title: Ingersoll-Rand 7802RAKC Heavy Duty 3/8-Inch Reversible Pnuematic Drill With Keyless Chuck
review_body: By far the most heavy duty air-drill I've ever had! I use this every single day, and it never fails to perform! Packed with power, and very comfortable to use! Worth every penny!

product_title: Makita HP1640 5/8-Inch Hammer Drill
review_body: Have the same problem a lot of people do with it stuck in hammer drill mode.  took it apart and still can't see what the issue is.  Its like the plastic selector bit swelled up somehow and doesn't fit right.  for a hammer drill only, it does its job.

product_title: Leatherman - Style PS Multitool, Black
review_headline: This is my EDC Multi-tool.  It's exactly what I wanted.
review_body: This is a really high quality tool.  I have only owned one other Leatherman tool before this and now I know why people love this brand.  It's really great quality for such a small tool.  It is precision made and feels like it was hand built.  The belt clip on my Style PS works great when I hook it on my jeans.  If anyone has belt loops that don't fit in the 'biner clip then they must have some pretty hefty belt loops.  Also, I considered the Squirt but I think the build quality on The Style PS is superior, and while the Squirt may offer more tools at a slightly heavier weight, I don't need those tools.  I purposely chose this because it didn't have a knife.  Honestly, I'm amazed at how well this is made.  My old Leatherman Wave (1st gen) isn't as good as this and it is a full sized tool.  Of course it also weighs over half a pound, has three different knife blades (!?!) and I'm getting tired of lugging it around when I go hiking and having to check it when I travel.  The Style PS is a great multi-tool that can go anywhere with me.  I love it.

product_title: SOG Salute Folding Knife FF11-CP - Hardcased Black 3.625" Blade, G10 Handle, Stainless Steel Liners
review_body: I work in heavy construction, and am pretty hard on my knives-- for the price, this SOG knife is the best I've had to date-- easy opening, good feel to the hand, and best of all, a STURDY clip-- haven broken three clips on knives this year to date, I really appreciate when a manufacturer designs it right. What makes this clip unique is one large countersunk screw, vs two tiny ones-- I doubt this thing is gonna move for years-- and if it does, it's easy to get to for quick tightening.  Delivery was super fast as well.  Top notch, all around.

product_title: DEWALT DC9320BP 7.2-to-18-Volt NiCd/NiMH/Li-Ion 1-Hour Dual Port Charger and XRP 18-Volt Battery Combo Pack
review_body: Using multiple voltage tools, as well as migrating to Li Ion batteries made this charger a must. The smart charging circuits 'should' make all the batteries I use last longer. We'll see.

product_title: Dewalt Safety Glasses - Contractor Pro Safety Glasses
review_headline: So cool I feel hot in them...
review_body: I did not buy these glasses for the protective feature, although it's reassuring to know they would protect my eyes should the need arise. I actually purchased them because blue's my favorite color and I like the rather unusual style on the sides. I hoped they would fit over my regular glasses and they do. That's a big plus for me.  Another plus is that they're lightweight and the rubber tips at the temples and rubber nose piece make them very comfortable.  My eyes are light sensitive and these aren't dark enough for bright sun, but they're perfect for reading on the patio...or when outdoors on shady days, working with my plants.  I highly recommend these Dewalts! The price is right because I've seen similar for double and triple this price.  Review by Betty Dravis, November 19, 2011  Author of \\"Star Struck: Interviews With Dirty Harry and Other Hollywood Icons\\"

product_title: Jet JJP-10BTOS 10-Inch Bench-Top Jointer/Planer
review_body: This tool is very lightweight so moves easily when wood is moved through/across it, which makes accuracy challenging, but also felt unsafe to me. The adjustment knobs are weak and adjustments were awkward. Changing between planer and jointer functions is tedious.  Not impressed.

product_title: Loupe - Doublet, Chrome Plated, Round Body
review_headline: Excellent Value For A Excellent Quality Loupe
review_body: I purchased this because I like to collect coins and needed something with a lot more power than a magnifying glass, yet is much smaller. This jewelers loupe is exactly what fit that bill. When I first saw it's price I figured it was going to be all plastic, but the magnification would be strong enough to see very fine details in coins; I was very pleased to see that the casing is made out of very heavy and sturdy polished steel. The lenses are in fact glass, and the magnification is awesome. Some say that it is more like 10 or 15 power, but mine sure magnifies those small details at 30 power! It focuses perfectly on whatever you are looking at up close through the loupe, be it coins, stamps, bugs, microprinting, etc... A case is also included to store the loupe in. Cleaning the lenses of the loupe is quite easy, merely use a damp q-tip and gently stroke the lenses free of any smudges. Other than that this little guy is well worth the money for the quality and magnification. These are priced just right to give as novelty gifts to friends and family, which I am going to do around the holiday season as stocking stuffers.

product_title: Screwdriver Set 6-in-1 Multi Bit Phillips and Flathead
review_body: It's nice to have any screwdriver you need all in one tool. Works well, and is a good buy for the money.

product_title: Hobart Airforce 500534 250ci Light Weight Plasma Cutter with Air Compressor
review_headline: Ready to use right out of the box
review_body: Great product in a small package. Ready to use right out of the box. I purchased this model because it had a built-in air compressor, so I didn't have to run an external one at the same time. Makes the machine extremely portable and able to use in any standard 110v outlet. I've cut up to 3/16\\" tubing so far with no worries. Definitely worth the money compared to burning through cut-off discs on the angle grinder. I added 2-day shipping and it arrived exactly as detailed.

product_title: Greenlee CrimpALL Crimper Frame Only, Series PA8000
review_body: Got the crimper right on time, and both die sets, feels like a solid tool. The min I walked in my door and saw the box I tore into it like a fat kid around cake! Tried it out immediately works like a charm, and its gonna get daily use and cut my time on site and hand fatigue down big time. Cant wait to try out more paladin tools!

product_title: United Cutlery UC1183 Knife Roll
review_body: This knife roll i ordered from this exact add. It is a great thing to have for any knife collector as my self. I have read other reviews saying there knifes don't fit. Well the slots are a little small but they will fit mostly every knife and if the knife is to big all you have to do is clip it to the strap with the clip that's already on most knifes to clip to your pants. I give this a 5 out of 5 and would recamend to anyone!

product_title: Rayovac Lantern
review_body: I was very surprised by the high quality and high light output of this light.  This light is VERY bright and very sturdy.  I have MANY camp lights to compare it to and this is my favorite.  It's almost as bright as a propane light.  The light is also very even.  Many lights like these are too bright to the eyes directly but are still uneven. This light has a ribbed or corrugated plastic globe that evens out the light.  it also has a very convenient hook on the bottom to hang it in a tent.  I really love this light!  Very highly recommended!

product_title: Great Neck 35C Midget Hacksaw Frame

The only way i could get even halfway successful passes was if i only tried to take off about 1/64\\" every pass, so you do the math!!! that took forever!!! The manual says adjust roller tension, roller heights etc and i adjusted it from one extreme to the next and every setting in between and this thing will NOT work as a reliable planer!!!! the only good thing is, when it does actually feed the wood through it comes out REALLY SMOOTH and its easy to almost have no snipe.  I don't know why this machine wont work properly, i think dust collects under the out-feed roller and causes it to bind but i have a 1 1/2 hp JET vacuum attached to it with about 10' of hose and yes some sawdust and chips do build up under the hood, but why??? I have used other planers,,, even much smaller ones that didn't have this problem.  I am sooo furious , after about 30 calls to customer service,, they basically quote verbatim whats in the manual,,, then finally during the last call the guy in tech support flat out said '' ya just got to keep on trying and eventually you'll get it,, just keep adjusting'' WTF????? Everyone complains about the made in china stuff but as soon as i sell this i am going to buy a shop fox!!! DO NOT BUY THIS AS A STAND ALONE PLANER!!!

product_title: MagLite XL50 LED 3-Cell AAA Flashlight, Blue
review_headline: Mag XL50 is Okay, Not Great.
review_body:
Essentially, the XL50 is a simpler, slightly cheaper version of the XL100 and XL200. Like the others, while of solid construction with 2 different, bright, usable settings (104 or 26 lumens), Mag Instruments could have done much better with the design of the entire XL-series (especially for the higher price they want over other, cheaper, equivalent LED flashlights). As most others have pointed out:

1. No lanyard hole or pocket clip. I'm not personally crazy about lanyards but can understand those that like the feature, especially on a small flashlight. Supposedly, Mag has a holster and is coming up with a solution but it should have been there in the first place.
2. Rolls easily when horizontal. A problem that Mag could have corrected during the design phase.
3. No tail cap switch lockout (to prevent turning accidentally \\"on\\" in coat or bag). This has actually been addressed with the switch on the much more complicated XL200. The price of the XL200 is not much more than the XL50 so, if you really want this feature and don't mind fiddling with the other, myriad switch options, get the XL200, instead.
4. The electronic tail cap switch consumes a very small but constant amount of current even when the light is off. This is a relatively minor irritant that may actually apply to any LED flashlight.
5. It has a plastic lens that is not removable. Glass would be preferable. Even if it wasn't there in the first place, why did Mag make it so hard to change out the plastic lens? I've read where it's possible to change the plastic lens but the probability is high that the process will damage the plastic reflector.

What hasn't been mentioned:

6. No ability to focus the beam, other than removing the whole lens assembly. I've never personally much cared about this aspect of the Mag flashlights but I suppose someone might.

Something I really hate about the 3-AAA battery holders in all of these LED flashlights is how close they are to the size of a single C-cell battery, yet they're just slightly smaller so one C-cell battery won't work. I mean, c'mon, how hard would it be to make the 3-AAA battery holder (and flashlight) just 1 mm (or whatever) wider in diameter to allow the option of using a C-cell? I can understand it in the cheap, Chinese flashlights, but this is a Maglite!

Likewise, the designers of the entire Mag XL series just didn't do such a great job. It's almost like they looked at the cheap, Chinese, multiple LED, 3-AAA flashlights that are everywhere and simply copied the whole, basic design with little thought of improving it. One of the few improvements that they 'did' do is recess the 'clicky' tail switch which allows the flashlight to stand on either end (which is good since it rolls when laid down lengthwise).

In summation, if you want a simpler version of one of the slightly more expensive Mag XL flashlights, the XL50 is okay. But if you don't mind the overly complicated switch on the other XL flashlights, they have more features and are probably worth the few extra dollars over the XL50.

review_headline: Not comparable to leather (in terms of puncture resistance)
review_body:
I purchased this product because of its claim that it was \\"4 times stronger than leather.\\" However, this lead me to believe that, being four times stronger than leather, it would make a perfect makeshift gauntlet for this troubled parrot we have at the vet clinic. The parrot did not like males and kept biting the nutritionist as well as myself around the forearm unexpectedly. Now what I had in mind was wrapping my arm around a layer or two of thick cowhide leather. But because I could find no such product online I settled for this Scabboard.

Well, in **terms of cut & slash resistance** this is four times stronger than leather. I took my USMC Kabaar Knife to it and didn't even change the fiber pattern of the scabboard Just don't take an industrial tool with a serrated edge to it and you'll be fine!

But the failure was paritally my own fault. Becuase the parrot I mentioned relied on the tip of her beak and therefore the feature I should have looked at was \\"Puncture resistence\\" which this does not have. So I received two 1/2\\" deep punctures in my arm again with this product on. So even though it says \\"4x stronger than leather\\", apply it only to cut & slash resistence terms. Do not think this will protect against an accidental nail gun misfire or animal with claws/fangs/beaks. All in all, nice product, protects against what it says. Don't assume the same thing I assumed.

If you never measure anything metric, you might be ok, but even if you argue that the mm scale is provided as a convenience this level of accuracy falls short of any reasonable expectation.

product_title: DEWALT DWD520K 1/2-Inch VSR Pistol Grip Hammerdrill Kit
review_headline: DeWalt DWD520K 1/2-Inch VSR Pistol Grip Hammerdrill
review_body: Great drill - 1200 watts thats power to spare and results in effortless drilling.  Variable speed, 2 gears, Hammer Drill function.  I did read somewhere that some people had problems with the drill bit slipping because the chuck becomes loose when using the hammer drill function.  My response to that is to tighten the chuck with chuck key in each of the 3 holes. I drilled 3 seperate holes each 20mm hole through approx 7 inches of granite using the hammer drill and an irwin joran drill bit, no problems not once did it loosen up.  I bought it for use in Australia so being that it's a 110v drill I hooked it up to my 2000w 240V > 110v step down transformer. Australia runs at 50 cycles while the US runs at 60 cycles doing the math I dropped about 60w of power not much of a price to pay with that much raw grunt.  Some may find it a bit on the weighty side, but I don't think it is.  It's a quality bit of kit, and I'm already looking at a DeWalt cordless for those lighter jobs when I need a cordless screwdriver.  Great purchase at half the price I pay in Aus for the same item.

product_title: SOG PowerLock EOD Multi-Tool B61N-CP - 18 Tools, Black Oxide, Nylon Sheath, Compound Leverage
review_headline: Need improvement on some of the tools
review_body:
I purchased this multi-tool about 1 month ago. In my search for the perfect multi-tool I thought I might have found it.

I thoroughly enjoy the \\"force multiplier\\" pliers but the main area of weakness of this particular multi-tool is the tools themselves. I use the Phillips bit the most and the design is mediocre at best. The thin bit is very brittle and breaks easily. The SOG Company was quick to send me replacement bits but I have already gone through all 4 of them. Also, the 1/4\\" bit driver is a real nice feature but the small retainer clip fell off - without me knowing - not too long ago. I will be e-mailing the company yet again for a Phillips bit and 1/4\\" bit driver replacement.

The locking design of this particular model is so so; there are other multi-tools such as Leatherman and Gerber that have better tool locking designs than this SOG. You cannot pull each individual bit out by themselves; when trying to access one, the other tool tend to come out with it. Somewhat annoying but I can live with that.

I gave it 3 stars due to the fact of the expensive price vs the poor quality of the tools. SOG makes good knives but I think they need to improve on the quality of their multi-tools.

I guess I may have to continue looking for the perfect multi-tool.

product_title: Incra MITER1000SE Miter Gauge Special Edition With Telescoping Fence and Dual Flip Shop Stop
review_headline: Good guage, a few problems with build quality
review_body:
I haven't had a chance to use this much, but I'm knocking off a couple of stars due to some initial problems that I encountered with it.

As a few others have mentioned, the bent \\"right-angle\\" piece that connects the fence to the guage is not even close to 90 degrees. This means that the face of the fence is not perpendicular to the surface of the table. The instructions suggest using pieces of paper to shim this angle-bracket to make the fence square to the table, but this really should not be necessary. I work with metal fabrication equipment, and I know that it shouldn't be all that difficult to make and ship these brackets with a true 90-degree angle.

The other initial problem that I found is with the Flip Stop assembly. The assembly includes two white plastic thumb-screws (probably Nylon or UHMW) that are used to secure the Flip Stop in position along the fence. One of the two thumb-screws was much too tight in the threaded hole, and I had to use a pair of pliers just to turn it. I backed it out with the pliers and then used a 3/8-16 tap to clean up the threaded hole in the aluminum. It was a pretty easy fix, only because I happened to have the appropriate tap on hand. The fact is, the unit should have never been shipped in this condition.

These problems are easy to address, but first you have to care. Incra has some good designs, but they're not helping their reputation by shipping products with these quality-control issues.

product_title: Smith and Wesson TXRBB Texas Rangers Big Bowie Knife
review_headline: Still not as awesome as Walker!
review_body: When I saw this knife I felt an instant rush of awesomeness.  For a few bucks I could be like a Texas Ranger.  You know who's a Texas Ranger?  Cordell Walker and that's Chuck freaking Norris.  I once saw him survive 12 explosions in one hour.  He beat up a bear and rescued his girlfriend from certain death 1,893 times.  So, I thought if I could get some of that mojo from this knife, why not?  I tried karate lessons but that didn't work.  I was still getting picked on.  I guess I never perfected that super sweet spinning crescent kick as well as I could.  I even tried Native American mysticism.  Nothing worked.  No matter how hard I tried to be like Walker I was still getting picked on.  With all the money and time I put into it, could the solution be this 10.2\\" blade of manhood?  I impatiently waited for it's arrival day after day.  When it finally arrived I ripped the package open pulled it out, raised it to the sky, and yelled \\"I am Walker?.  So I put on my long sleeve shirt in the plus 100 degree weather, my cowboy hat, jumped in my truck and drove to the local 7/11 to show those little pipsqueks who was in charge.  I jumped out with my Texas Ranger knife in hand and asked them to please leave me alone.  It's important in Walker's world to act humble and like you don't want to fight.  Of course, in actuality you are ready to wipe the floor with them.  They just laughed at me and stood up and surrounded me.  I peed my pants, jumped in my truck, drove home, and cried with my teddy bear all night.   Muttering \\"damn you Walker, damn you Walker, why will I always be in you shadow?\\"

product_title: Gerber Epic Knife, Serrated Edge, Drop Point [30-000176]
review_headline: Very Nice Design, but Mine Came with a Defect :/
review_body: I ordered my Epic about a week ago and it arrived in a day due to one day shipping (only $4 with Prime). To my surprise the knife is very good looking, it has a stylish design and a bottle opener on the end that will definitely make you look cooler at parties than the other guys using keychain openers, that is if you go to parties with a fixed blade knife... So yeah, the knife is nicely designed and all, but the blade itself is about the length you'd see on a pocketknife. The blade is wider and thicker which is nice again, but as stated earlier its short (personally I love the size, it makes me not have to carry around a silly pocket knife when I don't feel like lugging around my USMC Ka-Bar). The major flaw on mine that can be fixed in an hour was blade's edge. My knife came extremely dull to the point where I couldn't (and still can't) cut paper. I contacted Gerber because I would rather get it switched out than have to go through a whole sharpening process on a brand new knife. So yeah, the knife is dull but that is only an isolated incident and will probably be resolved in a few weeks -__-. The sheath on the knife is very nice in my opinion, so many other reviews hit mainly the sheath negatively but I've found it to be better than many other sheaths I've used. Instead of having to unbutton or unvelcro a strap on top and sometimes still have to push down a locking device, this sheath is just the single lock and I really really like it. Unlike the other reviews state, I have absolutely no problem quickly unsheathing the knife when in a hurry or putting the knife back in the sheath and the fact that its not super bulky with 500 different pouches all over the place to hold completely random 'survival' equipment, which is nice not to have. I know you are probably reading my wall of text and are getting filled with rage about now, but its not all wasted. The knife and sheath are very nice and I would recommend getting one if you want a compact knife and don't like silly pocket knives (like me), if you do end up with a defected knife just contact Gerber and they will ensure that you get a replacement or repair. so there, buy one already.

product_title: (Double Pack) Emergency Power Outage Light - Flashlight - Night Light
review_body: I bought a couple pairs of these handy lights for emergency use in the event of a power outage. They stay charged by leaving them plugged into a power outlet. They use only 1.5 watts when charging, a small trickle of electrical power at best. They are designed to not block the second plug in a standard electrical outlet. The power plug's prongs are designed to rotate 90 degrees into the body for lantern use. There is a sensor that turns both the night light and the flash light on and off only when it's dark. The switch in front let you set it to on which turns the tiny one LED night light on, to automatic where the night light goes on and off with the sensor and turns on the 21 LED array when the electrical power fails, or off. The construction is pretty good with a quality plastic housing that feels like it can take some use. The included carry cases lend some protection to the lantern and allow you to hang them from something. There are cutouts in all four corners which could be used for attaching alternative lanyards (not included). I have the blue LED night light which works well in the hallways and bathrooms. In use the emergency lantern brightens a entire room for many hours - more than any local power outage is likely to last. Overall a well designed product with quality construction. Every family home or apartment needs a pair.

product_title: RIDGID 31405 Model 342 Internal Wrench, 4-1/2-inch Internal Pipe Wrench
review_headline: The best tub drain removal tool
review_body: The best tub drain installation and removal tool I've used.  Works if the bottom of the drain is broken off or if it's intact.  Works on cross threaded drains that are extremely tight.  Lots of torque with the steel handle, you can even use a cheater bar (piece of steel pipe) for more torque although you run the risk of bending the tool's handle.  The base of the handle is hex shaped so you can use a crescent wrench as an alternative to the handle.  Fits many sizes as the tool can have the jaws flipped around to access the other sizes.  Even if it doesn't fit perfectly (too small) you can manually spread the jaws until it makes contact with the inner surface of the drain.  Once you make contact, it will bite, and the inner shaft will spin and apply pressure to hold the jaws in place.  Sort of like a wedge effect.  The harder you turn the handle, the farther the jaws will spread.  If you are installing a drain, or replacing a drain that is not broken or corroded, the other, cheaper style works great.  Usually has a hole going through it you can insert a screw driver into, to act as a handle.  If it's corroded try jamming a screw driver or two down the drain and try to unscrew it that way.  If it breaks, you have 3 options: use the cheaper \\"Drain Key\\" expanding wrench which  doesn't bite well and is of overall cheaper construction, the Ridgid expanding wrench which in my opinion is the best tub drain tool ever conceived, or a few hundred dollars on a full set of internal pipe wrenches.  If you just need to remove or install one tub drain, maybe have someone with some knowledge in the field help you with one of their tricks.  If you plan to replace tub drains with any sort of frequency, buy this tool.  It will quickly pay for itself in time saved, less busted knuckles, and money not deposited into the swear jar because Joe Shmoe cross threaded the drain when he installed it 5 years ago.  The only flaw I see as using this tool for tub drains is that it might scratch thesurface of the inner drain when installing.  If this is an issue, wrap the jaws in a rag to protect the surface.  Should still bite well enough to install it properly.  This tool used to be sold at home depot for $60 some years ago.  After searching retail stores, and Ridgid's own website for 6 months to find a replacement for the one I had stolen years ago, I found it on Amazon.  I didn't like the new higher price, but seeing as demand is likely low it makes sense.  Also it's the best option.  If you want to cut down a tree, buy an axe.  If you want to cut down a forest, buy a chainsaw.

product_title: IIT 17920 Magnetic Hide A Key - 3 Piece
review_body:
I've had this brand, and one other brand of Mag-lock, and both failed miserably. Why?

Undercoating on vehicles is sprayed at the manufacturer, and prevents solid magnet-to-metal contact. Even if this seems like it grips tight on your refrigerator, for instance, this is not the same as the underside of your car/truck.

The car will get wet, and muddy and soiled, and not only does that further reduce the bond when the magnet gets filmy and the metal gets oxidized on your car, but it will ruin the computer chip key (most modern vehicle keys have a computer chip) as this mag-key holder is not watertight. This can somewhat be allayed by wrapping the key in tin foil, which is recommended and does not disable the chip.

You will, during a lock-out, climb under your vehicle (or under the fender, or wheel well, etc.), and not find this box. And with computer chip keys about $50, you will pull your hair out when you trusted your key to a $2 box.

One solution is the hide hitch combination lock, if you have a vehicle with a trailer hitch; I have one on my Chevy truck and it's superb. People can watch you put the key in (plus spare cash, whatever), and they still can't get it out. Only you have the combination.

[[ASIN:B000I66JEM HitchSafe Key Vault]]

To hide a key on a car, there are plenty of options, but best remains wrapped in tin foil (ziplock baggies do not last), and wired with stiff wire (the cheap coat hangers from the cleaners work well, the cheaper the better, more flexible) through the key itself and then to a high piece of metal (not the frame close to the ground, but get under there near the firewall of your vehicle and find metal you must reach up for), where you wrap and wrap that wire around the metal 4-5 times. It'll be there when you look for it four years later when your purse gets stolen from the restaurant with your car keys in it.

OK yes it is a bit heavy but that is to be expected with a multi-tool, at least in my opinion. Quick access to the blade, serrated blade, file and saw is good. After unfolding it it seems to have a nice balance to it. Now I've read another review that stated the pliers were stiff; well that is because it is fairly new and the pliers need to be broken in. Once that is done then the pliers will be very loose. The locking mechanism on this is better than the Schrade. The Schrade bent the locking mechanism out of place as I was using the large screwdriver.. OK maybe I used the large screwdriver a bit too hard but then again shouldn't these multi-tools take some mild abuse?

Anyway I started carrying it around with me and do not really notice the weight on my pants. I have not had an opportunity to use it yet; however, I will update my review to reflect that. I would say this model is pretty good if you are going to casually use a multi-tool from time to time.

review_body: This bucket is probably most famous for being hawked by the president of the manufacturer on a famous televangelist show...let's called in the \\"Bim Jakker\\" show. Keep in mind a normal healthy adult male should not consume less than 2000 calories per day. If you used this as purported \\"275 meal\\" bucket as a 30-day supply of food for one adult male, you would get just 1200 calories a day while consuming over 4500mg of salt. Ouch! If you actually want to not waste away and instead get at least 2000 calories every day, this bucket barely lasts over two weeks. And at that point, you are now getting nearly 8000mg of sodium each and every day. Double ouch! product_title: Klein Tools 32557 Heavy-Duty Multi-Bit Screwdriver/Nut Driver
review_body: I have been using Klein tools for years and have never been disappointed with their quality.  This tool is no exception; the quality is there, it is the thought behind it that puzzles me.  Most multi-bit drivers are designed with some sort of consistent logic to make their use intuitive.  Typically, you will find double-sided bits with a small flathead and #1 philips on one, large flathead and #2 philips on another, and #1 and #2 square drive on another.  This helps to make finding the correct bit more intuitive in practice.  For some reason though, Klein decided to throw all logic to the wind on this one.  They put the small philips and large flathead on one bit, the small flathead and large square drive on another, and the large philips and the small square drive on the third.  In actual use, this arrangement makes finding the correct bit a frustrating exercise in trial and error - mostly error.  The frustration is compounded by the fact that I have other multi bit drivers, including a Klein 11 in 1 that employ the more intuitive arrangement of bits.  Switching between the different tools involves re-learning the tool's logic each time.  Argh!  I had to return this one; it wasn't worth the frustration.  Not dissing Klein, they make quality tools. product_title: WindFire Super Bright Wf-501b Cree Xm-l T6 LED 1000 Lumens 5 Mode 3.7-18v Flashlight
review_body:
I'm quite happy with my WF-501B flashlight. It is very bright, and I believe it does indeed live p to the claimed light output.

I've examined the parts that other reviewers have found to be defective or deficient. The quality of the screw threads for the battery chamber seem to be good to me, they do not seem to suffer from any obvious quality problem in the unit I purchased. On the other hand, the electrical contacts on both ends are soldered to circuit boards, so I can see how defects could occur at either end, solder could fail, the circuit board could crack, and any of a number of other things *could* happen there. But to include current limiting circuitry, there must be a circuit board of some kind somewhere.

It is easy to change the mode of the flashlight, while on, press the button half-way (don't click it). Each half-press will change the mode.

I only found one thing that I was disappointed with, that being the lack of a focus function. The flashlight this one replaces for me, a $30 Coleman 3AAA LED Flashlight that I really liked, has a nice focusing function. I was hoping that this would be a big step up, and be able to use as a wide-beam work light as well as a spot light... But alas, this one has no focus option. So I dropped it one star for that. To be fair, there is a good reason for the lack of focus option. This is a high-power light that can generate a lot of heat. It would be difficult to get good coupling to dissipate that heat if the LED was on a movable mechanism, that would cause heat build-up and shorten the life of the LED. There ARE some flashlights that do this successfully, but they have more complex mechanical construction, and cost more as a result.

The only other downside is the special battery that is required, but if I want a super-bright flashlight, I need a high current battery. No points off for something required by the specifications.

So in summary, this is a great, very bright, flashlight in a small package. VERY nice for the price!ERY nice for the price!

product_title: DEWALT DW744XRS 10-inch Job Site Table Saw with Rolling Stand
review_headline: The best thing in my garage...which includes my car!
review_body:
I originally received a DW745 portable saw with the same rolling stand but purchased separately as a gift. I opted to get the DW744XRS instead because of the larger table size and rip distance and I'm glad that I did. It takes up about the same amount of space and adds some much-appreciated capacity.

This saw is really well thought-out. Everything is adjustable to make sure you get perfect, straight cuts even with different blade types/widths or after years of use and wear and tear including the blade height, blade alignment, rip gauge, and blade angle gauge. The anti-kickback and blade gaurd assemblies look like they'd be in the way but they're actually very unobtrusive and easy to quickly remove and replace when you need to reconfigure the saw. Every accessory has a place to be stored on the saw itself including the miter gauge and all of the gaurd assemblies so when you decide to fold-and-go with it you'll never leave a crucial piece behind.

My only complaint is that the miter gauge doesn't slide without binding in the slots on the table. I sanded a lot of the gray coating out of the track and applied a light coat of wax but it still sticks a bit.

Overall I am completely pleased with the saw and I have been slowly turning every piece of wood I can get my hands on into sawdust! Highly recommend it!

-- ADDED NOTE --

I have had the saw for 4 months now and I'm still VERY happy with it, but I must add one note for other buyers shopping around for a portable saw like this. The limited depth of the table and the proximity of the blade to the front edge of the table has made it difficult to use the miter gauge with wider boards (4\\"+). At times, you are still holding the board against the miter gauge while holding both of them in thin air off of the table when the workpiece comes in contact with the blade. I realize that this is a small saw on purpose, but similar Bosch, Makita, and Ridgid saws all have very slightlydeeper tables (by about 2-3\\") although I'm not sure how much clearance their blades have from the front edge. Jet is the only portable table saw manufacturer I have found that actually advertises the \\"Table in front of saw blade at max cut depth\\" measurement, claiming 10.5\\". This suggests to me that maybe Jet noticed and corrected the mistake that most other manufacturers did not. I'm certainly not about to run out and return my DeWalt...I love this thing...but if I was shopping for this saw again I would check this measurement to avoid the nuisance I've been having with miter cuts. If the Jet had that much more room in front of the blade I would probably buy it, mount it on the superb DeWalt stand that comes with the 744XRS, and sell that flimsy-looking Jet stand to some poor soul on Craigslist, ha ha.

(the pellet stove was in the house I recently purchased, I had no experience with this prior to moving in). I went with the Dustless Tech Cheetah II Ash Vacuum.  First impressions:  This vacuum is US made, purpose built for vacuuming warm and cold ash. The tank is steel, the hose is metal lined and the vacuum has a double filter system. The motor has replacable brushes  and has a internal \\"jiggle\\" rod designed to clean the filters on the fly without disassembling the unit.   I have used it about 4 times already and noticed that it picks up ash quite well and leaves no exhaust residue. It is loud (what vacuum isn't)but I think I could probably go a full season without having to empty the vacuum. It takes me approx 1 to 3 minutes to fully clean the stove and I tend to clean it every 3 days.   There are some negative reviews regarding this vacuum not cleaning wood fragments(fireplaces). Contact cement doesn't stick to hands, but it sticks to itself.. like cement. You have one chance to lay it down just right. You will need at least one person to help position it right. But if you've priced out laminate rolls and plywood compared to a finished product, you can save $800 easy on an average sized kitchen. You could screw up four times and still come out ahead. product_title: Stanley 10-778 Fatmax Retractable Knife
review_body:
I purchased this at Home Depot because I've had good experiences with Stanley tools in the past. In the past 20+ years, I've owned and used numerous utility knives, so I'm not new at this. But after using the Stanley FatMax for a drywall-cutting project, it's going right back to the store -- with complaints. In short, this is the worst utility knife I've ever had the misfortune to use. From both an ergonomic and safety perspective, it's mind-boggling how this made it through any kind of quality-control process.

What's wrong with this product? Let me list the problems.

The blade jiggles and moves around even after it's \\"locked.\\" When you retract the blade, it fails to go all the way back into the housing, posing a serious danger to anyone walking with this knife or storing it in a tool box.

The blade-storage unit in the handle is a total hazard. It's very difficult to get blades in or out. You have to force the blades, thereby begging for an accident.

The \\"quick-change\\" blade system is frighteningly difficult to use. To install a blade, you must hold a tiny (and I mean tiny) little button down while pushing a razor-sharp blade into the unit. All the while, there is resistance, so you're constantly running the risk slipping and slicing your finger. To remove the blade is equally dangerous. You hold that tiny \\"quick-change\\" button again and hope the blade comes out nicely. It didn't do so for me. Pulling the blade out, I had the same resistance as when installing it.

The only thing they got right here is the rubberized grip. But even that I would only rate as \\"decent.\\"

Overall, this seems like a product created by a company that has excess cash to waste on product-liability lawsuits. I don't feel like playing that game. I'll keep my fingers intact and get a refund instead.

You have been warned!
