It does not fog up, which is good.  The plastic on the facial portion is surprisingly thin and flimsy and the adjusting bracket on the sides is paper thin.  They are so thin that I will never be adjusting them for fear of breaking one.  I guess you are paying all this money for the mask.  But what good is it if you can't get a proper fit?  They should have either made the attachments portion out of thicker plastic or simply charged less for this.

product_title: SAS Safety 5420-50 LED Inspectors Safety Glasses
review_body: These are awesome!!! very bright!! and gives you the option of turning individual lights on/off or both on/off. Very useful item.

product_title: PSI Woodworking Products LCSIDE2 Round Side Scraper Chisels, 2-Piece set
review_body: Good for the cost, worth the money. Affordable useful scrapers. Comes in nylon wrap  making them easy to store or transport.

product_title: Dremel 120-Volt Saw-Max Tool Kit (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: My wife once asked me why I needed so many different saws and I told her that it wasn't that I needed so many different saws, but that they all did a job the others couldn't do either as easily or as efficiently.  At first she didn't believe me and tried to cut wood with my tile saw.  That didn't do anything but burn the wood.  So what did the above story have to do with this saw, well, this one saw has replaced or will replace at least 4 of the saws I have.  It is small enough that my wife can handle it (she is a very small woman) and yet powerful enough to handle pretty much anything I have thrown at it.  Obviously, it will not cut a 2x4 all the way through, but it does a nice job with base boards, chair rail, tile, wood floor, laminate flooring, OSB, plywood, etc.  Overall, this is a great hand tool with all sorts of useful applications.

product_title: SE 7503SD 3-Piece Power Extension Bit Set for Drills
review_body: this is a very poor quality socket adapter set. the first time I used the 3/8 adapter the metal ball flew right out of the adapter. If you want a cheap adapter set I would recommend that you buy it from Harbor Freight.

product_title: Makita BSS501Z 18-Volt LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless 5-3/8-Inch Circular Trim Saw (Tool Only, No Battery)
review_body: Nice saw.  Very strong motor and it cuts about everything.  Got only 4 stars as I am replacing a 9.6v Makita saw and this one is considerable larger.   Size is the only downside so far.

product_title: Maxcraft 60199 1/4-Inch Dual-Drive Mini Ratchet Driver
review_body: I have tried a few of these mini ratchets: The [[ASIN:B001NCEXGG Great Neck 51063 Mini Ratchet and Bit Set, 10-Piece]]; the [[ASIN:B003BXKZZ8 MAXCRAFT 60199 1/4-Inch Dual-Drive Mini Ratchet Driver]]; the [[ASIN:B000XYOUS6 Neiko 03044A Mini Ratcheting Screwdriver and Bit Set, Pocket Size Close-Quarters ,1/4-Inch Drive]]; the [[ASIN:B002Q8CDX6 SE 1/4in Square/Hex Reversible Mini Ratchet]]; and a few more. The Great Neck is my favorite. The Great Neck may not be as sturdy as the Maxcraft, but it seems more comfortable to use. They are both really good. All the others are too cheap, they wobble and are low quality.

product_title: Factory-Reconditioned BOSTITCH U/CPACK300 3-Tool and Compressor Combo Kit
review_body: I was a little worried after reading some of the poor reviews of this product, but I must say, I am very well pleased. I am not sure what others may expect from a product at a reduced price that is reconditioned. My compressor and guns arrived in better than expected condition, as good as new and work as the seller and manufacturer described. All of the guns look to be never used or in new condition. The compressor tank has some minor scratches, could possibly be from shipping without any wrap inside the box, but absolutley no damage. Works excellent. My biggest disappointment was the canvas bag for the 3 guns has a long tear in it. Also most likely caused from being loose inside the shipping box. Overall, an excellent product, exactly as described. Can't wait for my first project.

product_title: Makita MAC700 Big Bore 2.0 HP Air Compressor
review_body: The MAC 700 is quiet, it quickly charges the air storage tank and it retains stored pressure in between uses.  It is superior to the non-lubricated compressors having similar CFMs in the less-than-$200 price range.

product_title: Howard Leight Impact Sport OD Electric
review_body: These are by far the best earmuffs I have ever used while at the shooting range.  The noise level is quite bearable and I could also hear my sons talking to me.  These were so good, I bought my wife and grandson a set as well.

product_title: MSA Safety Works 817663 Multi-Purpose Respirator
review_body: Do not skimp on a good respirator by buying disposables ones. Yes, the strap on this model can be prone to breaking as claimed by previous buyers. However, it is much stronger than the disposable ones which will break after several uses. Loosening the strap before removal will prolong it's longevity. For the price point and quality of the respirator, it's hands down 5 stars. I wish I bought this a couple weeks earlier when I was stripping out old paint. Currently, I am sanding down the ceiling and having a good respirator makes a world of a difference. The rubber nozzle contorts to your face and gives you a nice snug feeling. It is lightweight and comfortable. Works well with the Dewalt anti-fog protective glasses.  Edit - After using this for a couple years, the head strap broke due to the stitching. I was able to salvage the respirator by using a staple gun. Downgrading the respirator from 5 stars to 3 stars.

product_title: Fastback Flip Utility Knife
review_body: It's built very well, I've dropped it a few times on a hard floor and it's fine. The clip is very tight and it doesn't fall out of my pocket. The blade release is easy and secure; the razor has never came out on accident.

product_title: TR Industrial TR89100 Electric Demolition Jackhammer with Point, Flat and Spade Scoop Shovel Chisels Bits, 4-Piece Set
review_body: So I bought this with the purpose of installing a sump pump pit in my basement. In order to avoid \\"rental return anxiety,\\" I figured I'd just buy my own. Then I could get it done at my own pace. The price was certainly reasonable enough, even with shipping. I could also loan it out to my pals.  In short enough time, I received the hammer. It comes in an OK metal case. Not great, but sufficient. It had three bits in the package I purchased, a point, a chisel and a spade. There were instructions and some accessories. It's pretty heavy (which is a plus for hammering). There were a few wrenches and an more-or-less empty oil container.  The instructions were fairly typical for a China made product. Here's an example:  \\"5. Feeding oil (refer to the paragraph on oil feeding). Prior to using the power tool, remove the oil gauge and do not fail the oil tank with the provided oil. (Although the oil tank is built in, it contains only a small volume of oil when shipped from the works.)\\" Soooo, I'm not supposed to \\"fail\\" the oil tank with the supplied oil?? Well, OK, then. It continues later: \\"Since  , oil chamber is built in this  Electric Hammer, it can be used for approximately 20 days without supplying lubricating oil, assuming that the Hammer is used continuously 3~4 hours daily.\\" So am I supposed to fill it or not????? (remember that SNL skit, \\"Son, you can never put too much water in a nuclear reactor.\\")  What kind of oil does it use? \\"Shell Oil Co. Rotella #40 (engine oil) can also be used. This oil is sold as Shell filling stations most anywhere.\\" Hmmmm. I don't think I can find one of those. On a local's advice, I'm probably going to use Air Compressor Oil or maybe an SAE 40.  Anyway, that said, I did figure out how to insert the bits properly, and the oil level seemed OK to me. So, it was \\"go\\" time.  I chose the point chisel, set it on the concrete and pulled the trigger. Brap, brap, brap, brap. I let the weight of the hammer drive the point into the concrete. Occasionally, it would hit a rock or something that would slow it, but I would either just move it or wait. It would get through. It took a few minutes to get the hang of, but after that this hammer made quick work of my slab (about 4-5\\"?). Frankly I was amazed at how quickly it worked. Perhaps disappointed because I found myself thinking of other things I might jackhammer.  That said, I like the hammer. It feels solid. It got me through my project and, for this price, if I can use it a couple more times or loan it out, it'll be well worth it.  One other thing, regarding replacement/other bits. I couldn't find any. That's not saying that there aren't any. But in the time I looked, I couldn't find any.

product_title: Chicago Pneumatic CP715K Heavy Duty Zip Gun Hammer with 4 Chisels
review_body: I've had this air hammer for about 2 years now. This model was recommended to me by some seasoned auto mechanics as a great tool for the price.  I have not been disapointed by its performance.  It hits hard and has held up to some serious use.  Be sure to wear safety glasses when using because something is going to coming loose very soon when you put this beast to work.  Just a note: Looks like price has gone up about $20 for this kit since when I purchased it 2 years ago.

product_title: Kreg R3 Jr. Pocket Hole Jig System
review_body: I am a beginning woodworker.  I was trying to figure out how to put two boards together without using biscuits or dowels to come together with a strong very tight join.  I came across an article on the internet on how to use pocket screws.  I never heard of this method before.  (Remember, I am a beginner.)  I read it and the article mentioned Kreg jigs for pocket screws.  I read countless articles and reviews on the Kreg jig so ordered the Kreg R3 jig kit from Amazon, received it before the expected delivery date, went out to my workshop, tested it, and within 5 minutes, I had my 3 boards that I needed to join perpendicular to another board, drilled and joined.  Tight perfect joins.  It was perfect for my needs and I am sure I will use this for years to come.  It was easy to setup the jig to the proper depth of my board using the gauge on the jig itself and then set the drill stop using the gauge in case.  I couldn't be happier with this jig.    The jig itself is made of plastic, very tough plastic with stainless steel inserts for the drill bit.  I was concerned about the strength of the plastic but that only lasted during my first 2 pocket screw joins.  After that, I knew it would be tough and last.  I had the same concern about the clamping pad of the jig.  But after I clamped it down I knew that was just as tough.

product_title: Zircon MultiScanner Center-Finding Stud Finder with Metal and AC Electrical Scanning
review_body: I've used this stud finder trying locate wood studs behind 1/2\\" drywall as well as behind old fashioned plaster and lath walls.  I believe the i520 works a bit better than Zircon's $20 model, but it is only adequate. I would gladly give up the metal finding and deep scan capabilities for better stud finding ability.  If you buy one of these for stud finding plan on spending lots of time going over areas again and again and carefully marking your results on the wall with a pencil.  Scanning results are inconsistent so your best bet is to take many 'readings' and then make a judgement on which readings make the most sense. In my work I found it best to 'scan' and locate one stud, then measure off 16\\" to estimate location of the rest.

product_title: Smith & Wesson SWMP5LS M&P Linerlock Knife with 2nd Generation MAGIC Assisted Open and 40% Serrated Drop Point Blade
review_body: I havent written a review on Amazon before, but this knife made me want to do it for the first time. For around $40, this knife is one of the sturdiest and best I've owned. I know it's hard to determine the quality of a knife over the internet, but this arrived a few days ago for me, and it is very sturdy, fits my hand perfectly, and is very high quaslity. The assisted open is smooth, effortless, and quick. It has a separate side-lock for additional safety when putting pressure on the blade, and it arrived razor sharp. Buy it. It's worth it. I'm going to buy a few of these.

product_title: 8 Piece Set of Dry Diamond Polishing Pads
review_body: great products, cheap price.  i ordered a dry polishing pad set bundled with the rubber velcro holder and the pads and holder both performed very well.  polished 125 linear feet of granite edge and still life on the pads and the rubber velcro holder is like new.  pads stick well but not so much removing them is a pain. dont skip steps and take your time and these pads work well.  initally I thought they were not working so well but I went back and spent a bit more time on each set of pads and viola! it looks good.

product_title: DMT W6XP 6-Inch Diamond Whetstone Sharpener
review_body: It's called a whetstone but really it's a hollow plastic box with a perforated metal plate on top and a seperate plastic baseplate with rubber feet. Sounds cheap, but works really well. I don't know how long it would last as it's not like a thick stone that is gradually ground down - it's just the single diamond-encrusted plate. That said, it is diamond and did a great job of sharpening my santoku ... will be working through the rest of my kitchen knives and then when I get the Fine and Coarse versions of this stone in a few weeks will work on my KA-BAR, SOG tomahawk and other utility knives. Would be nice if the stone or holder said \\"Extra Fine\\" on it in case I can't remember the colour-coding once I have the set of stones, but rectified with a Sharpie. Now I can get rid of that damn useless honing rod!

product_title: PEC Tools 262-006 6" Inch/MM USA Rigid Steel Rule, reads 32nds, 64ths, 1mm, 1/2mm.
review_body: I've been looking for a 6\\"rule that does metric too, since the rest of the world uses metric & we don't. (What's easier? Adding 16ths & 32nd's or ones? Get with it America  This rule is well made and easy to read. Good finish.

product_title: Milwaukee 7110-20 2- to 3-1/2-Inch Clipped Head Framing Nailer
review_body: Just bought this nailer to build 2 x 4 shelving units for the basement. Shot approximately 200 3\\" ring shank nails through it with no issues.  1.) This gun is the lightest framer I've used and well balanced.  2.) The shorter magazine makes this gun less clumsy and able to fit in tighter spots. Though it may not hold 2 sticks of Paslode nails as other reviewers commented, I am not doing production framing so it is not an issue.  3.) The trigger lock-out mechanism when you are down to the last few nails is genius. Wish my other guns had this feature.  4.) This framer drives and feeds consistently. For my application I ran at 100 psi.  5.) Instead of 3/8 fittings and hose I reduced the inlet down to 1/4 with a swivel fitting. Gun performed flawless (although I am not using rapid bump fire). This allows me to use the 1/4 quick connects and hoses all my other air guns use.  6.) Of course Milwaukee recommends Milwaukee nails, which I am unable to find. I shot Paslode \\"round drive\\" nails from Home Depot. As others have mentioned, these nails fit into this clipped head nailer but have a full round head... it is just offset from the nail shank. This way you satisfy code requirements for full rounds plus keep the benefit of paper collation and tight nail spacing.  The only two cons I see are:  First, there is no case. However, many people who buy air nailers will not mind building their own cases I'd wager.  Second, gun is made in Taiwan. I would prefer and would pay for good ol' Made in the USA but alas, it is hard to find these days.  In short, another great Milwaukee product. Not sure why I never see these in the big home improvement stores. Also, Amazon price was great at $179.99

product_title: Shop-Vac 90503-00 2-1/2 Inch x 8-Ft. Hose
review_body: I purchased one of these hoses to replace one that had worn out with age on an older model Shop-Vac. I am very pleased with this hose and would recommend it to everyone. I like it even better than the old original Shop-Vac hose because its longer and makes it easer to use when cleaning out the inside of a car or truck.

product_title: Elenco TL-12  Banana to Mingrabber Set
review_body: The mini grabbers do not extend from the plastic sleeve very far, Makes it difficult to connect to a wire or terminal. Impossible to connect to some larger test points. Requires a lot of pressure to extend the tip so disconnecting creates too much pressure at the connection point. Very limited in usefulness. Would prefer the mini be a bigger mini.

product_title: Bosch 4100-09 10-Inch Worksite Table Saw with Gravity-Rise Stand
review_body: Saw is terriffic, not real impressed with Amazon/Warehouse Sales. Purchased as an open box item from Warehouse Sales. Did not ship for 4 or 5 days so had to have the item delayed at UPS center due to being out of town, cost $5. Saw did not have the bolts and nuts package to put together the easy rise table so had to call Bosch. They sent the bolts/nuts package to me free of charge but the package did not contain some of the correct bolts so had to purchase $10 of bolts/nuts at local hardware store.

product_title: Gerber Profile Fixed Blade Knife, Drop Point [22-41795]
review_body:
I purchased this knife with a competitor, and I must say, this is the best knife I own from Gerber.

I own Ka-Bar, Ontario, Bear, and several Gerber multi-tools, but this is the first fixed blade knife I now own from Gerber.

The reason I bought this on top of what I already have is because I wanted a fixed blade knife that I could strap on my belt which would be easily at the ready. My Ka-Bars, and Ontarios are too large to simply strap on without bringing attention to myself, and pocket knives/multitools are convenient for their size, but not practical if you have to fight with them.

This knife serves as both a utilitarian cutting/slicing tool, but also a tool I can use to immediately defend myself with.

It has a thick full tang, and I wasn't too sure about how the handle would feel, but it is a nonslip handle and fits in my hand effortlessly.

For the price, if you are looking for a fixed blade for practical reasons as well as tactical reasons, this is an excellent knife to bring on board.

product_title: DEWALT DW744XRS 10-inch Job Site Table Saw with Rolling Stand
review_body: Both me and my girl friend enjoy working with this tool. Its precise, easely portable, easy to set up. Shop around, there is some good price for this product.

product_title: Stanley QB2 Banded Reusable Ear Pads (RST-63004)
review_headline: Great to wear with a hat
review_body: I like them because they are always there.  I don't notice them one bit around my neck and instead of having to stop to go get ear protection, or more likely go without, I now always have them and thus I protect my ears more.  I still like the big comfy over the ear type for when I know I'll be using them a lot but for infrequent use or especially when I'm wearing a hat, these are great.

product_title: Grip 3 pc Socket Tray Set
review_headline: So much better than the old traditional metal holders
review_body: We are so happy with this set of socket holders.  They are so much easier to use than the old fashioned standard metal strips for sockets.  My spouse threw all those metal ones away and use these exclusively.

product_title: Nite Ize LRB2-07-PRHP High Power LED Upgrade Bulb C/D Cell
review_body: I have been favorably impressed with the new LED flashlights I have bought recently (bright light, longer battery life) but I had two older incandescent type flashlights.... One dating from my days at summer camp in the '60s and the other a newer MagLight. I was sentimentally attached to the summer camp flashlight and the MagLight had been rather expensive back in the day.    So I decided to replace their incandescent bulbs with these LED replacements.    Bottom Line... The replacement LED \\"bulbs\\" worked as indicated with a brighter light and, I presume at this point, longer battery life.

product_title: Bondhus 12632 GorillaGrip, Set of 8 Star Fold-up Keys, sizes T6-T25
review_body: The product is overall pretty good. The Green handle/grip seems impossible to twist or break. But for the smaller bits, they seem a little too flexible but that's probably just because the metal is thinner to allow the smaller Torx size. Overall I love the product, it will make easy for opening my 360 and fixing it, or various other electronics.

product_title: Auto Darkening Solar Powered Welding Helmet - ANSI Approved, Red Flame Design with Polished Black Finish
review_headline: I'm hooked, - - that's about all there is to say
review_body: I've been welding for a long time, but this was my first experience with an \\"auto darkening\\" hood..  It worked even better than described.  I wish we had these years ago.  I'm hooked, - - that's about all there is to say

product_title: Bucket Boss 55010 Electricians Pouch
review_body: Pros:  Well put together, it even has some padding.  Cons:  Stitched on rubber logo cheapens the look, and the hammer holder is WAY too big, it looks like they had to stitch on extra fabric in order to attach it to the pouch.

product_title: Trademark Black Firm 4.5" Tactical Pocket Knife
review_headline: My favorite knife even after 9 months of use
review_body:
I appreciate the speed of this knife, and for so cheap it isn't bad. I found that it does not lock when manually opened. I would recommend looking up your state laws on knives before buying this, as it is spring loaded and may be illegal to carry. Seems pretty solid for now, has some weight to it. I am a female with fairly small hands and I can grip it with no problem. There is a lanyard hole on the bottom of the knife, as well as a belt clip. Came sharp right out of the box and did not need sharpening. Overall, I'm satisfied but I'm not sure if this knife will last too long. We'll see in a couple months I suppose!

UPDATE: 9 Months later and it's still my go to knife. I've only had to sharpen it once, though it doesn't get heavy, gritty, use. The spring mechanism is still just as strong as it was 9 months ago. Whenever I take it out around friends they always ask to play with it and are pretty impressed with it. This is a knife I carry everyday on my pocket. I've changed my rating to a 5. If this ever breaks I'll be buying a new one.

Again, be sure to check your state laws, mine seems to be legal in Washington State.

product_title: Columbia River Knife And Tool 7120 Assisted Opening Folding Knife with 2.85-inch Blade, Drop Point Razor Edge, 6.75-inch Total Length.
review_body: This knife is a good buy, especially online.  In stores it is very expensive. I picked it up for under $20, when in stores they're charging $60-$80, which is quite ridiculous. The opening mechanism takes a little while to get used to, it does open very quick, so be careful, and can be shocking at first, but you get used to it pretty quick.  It is very easy to use also. If you have it in your pocket though, then I hope you don't put your hands in your pocket a lot while it's in there because there is a tiny little sharp piece that tends to scratch me if I reach in my pocket. Other than that I think it's awesome, It is definitely an EDC knife. It is pretty small, and is a great knife for my little female hands...so if you have pretty big hands, it might not be as comfortable.  I love this knife...

product_title: Aranyik 7.5" Box Cutter - Thai Utility Knife
review_body: I was not expecting much when I ordered this and I didn't get much.  These are crude beyond belief.  The handle on the one I have is split and glued back together,  The grinds are terrible.  The handle attachment is atrocious.  The pins do not fit in the holes and it is a short tang. It will cut paper and is very flexible.  For the quality it should be priced less than $2.00

product_title: Tooluxe 40420L Cordless Soldering Iron, 1050° F (565° C) | AA Battery Powered | LED Spotlight
review_headline: This device is great if you use COMMON SENSE with it's use
review_body: Just like tons of impatient people, I tried getting this thing to work without even reading the back of the container that it came in. It lacked complete detail, but if I'd read it, I wouldn't have made some of the mistakes I made. First of all, I put the batteries in wrong, and of course, it didn't work. If you look carefully, when you take off the battery compartment cover, you find that there are engraved illustrations of which position the batteries go in. I put the batteries in correctly, and it still didn't come on. The batteries I were using were 1600mah NiMH. Turns out they weren't strong enough to power up the device. I put in some 2700mah NiMH batteries, and this time it came on. I then noticed that when I pushed the black power switch to the \\"on\\" position, nothing happened. I knew the device was working because whenever I pushed the little red button that's surrounded by the power switch, the led would come on, but the tip still was not getting hot. If I had paid more attention to the reviews on this site, I would have seen that you have to CONTINUOUSLY HOLD THE RED BUTTON DOWN WHILE THE BLACK SWITCH IS IN THE \\"ON\\" POSITION IN ORDER FOR THE TIP TO REMAIN HOT. Once you let go of the little red button, the tip shuts off. I thought the tip was solely for the light control. No, it is also to start, and sustain the tip in a heated state. Once I figured all that out, I was up and running with it.     There are a lot of negative reviews for this product, but it indeed works if you do everything right, plus it's not designed for whopper soldering jobs. I've seen reviews where people state that they've tried to use it to solder wires in car engines together. This device is not powerful enough for that. It's designed for light jobs. The reason I got it is because I fly remote control helicopters. One thing that happens a LOT is that you CRASH the things. The parts that break on most of them are various tiny plastic parts. Sometimes, glue (even STRONG glue) will notsuccessfully rebond the parts. One thing that WILL rebond them is melting the broken areas back together. Previous to writing this review, I've successfully used it to remelt two plastic pieces together on 2 of my helis that Gorillla Glue was not able to accomplish. Remelting the pieces gave them a much stronger rebonding than any glue could have done. Simply applying heat to the broken areas was enough to give them a strong rebonding. The device also works well for light soldering. I have a wireless doorbell that works on AA batteries. One of the metal pieces that creates a contact between the positive battery end and the circuit board inside the doorbell had snapped. I used the soldering iron and some rosin core solder to re solder the connection, and it held great, and now the doorbell works fine again. I'm sorry for those of you that are having a hard time with this product, but for ME, it was just what I needed. I only have one negative comment.  I think the fact that there is no replacement tip is psychotic, but at the same time, a shrewd business move. Why make a replacement tip when they can just make the customers buy a whole new unit? I'm going to search the net to see if things have changed and if there is now a replacement tip for this thing. Maybe there's a web site in China that sells them. If I DO find one, I will come back on here and edit my review, with information on where you can order a replacement tip for the unit.

product_title: Akuzuki Top Quality 2-in-1 Pneumatic Hardwood Floor Flooring Air Cleat Nailers and Stapler
review_body: Worked right out of the box.  Other reviewers wrote about problems with this tool, but not me.  Two nails needed to be fixed but it was my fault, not the tool.  I would strongly recommend using hearing protection with this tool.  I also used Bostich nails as suggested by other reviewers.

product_title: Bosch CLPK27-120 12-Volt Max Lithium-Ion 2-Tool Combo Kit (Drill/Driver and Impact Driver) with 2 Batteries, Charger and Case
review_body: I've been eyeing this Impact for some time now, and the only regret I have is not buying it sooner. As soon as you feel this Lil guy you can feel the quality. I work with Locomotives and my tools take a beating, this one stands up to the test. Traction Motors  don't stand a chance, and since it weighs about 2 pounds, work has never been easier. I love this Impact Driver..

product_title: Multi-Pack Thin Clear Flexible Plastic Cutting Board Mat 12" x 15"
review_body: No problem with these mats until I accidentally cracked one. When transferring some chopped vegetables to a pan on the stove, I bent the mat into a cylinder to keep my onions from flying around. When I whacked the cylindrical mat to release the onions that remained clinging to the surface, the mat cracked, creating a 2 inch gash. Now that I know this, I'll be more careful using the my second mat.

product_title: DEWALT DC390K 18-Volt Ni-Cad 6-1/2-Inch Cordless Circular Saw Kit
review_body: As soon as I charged this up the first time I used it to build a workbench.  It is as powerful as a corded one and only slowed down at the very end after what seemed like a great deal of use.  Easily cut through 3/4\\" plywood (about 40' worth) plus more 2X4 cuts than I can remember.  Very comfortable and easy to use too.  Has a safety lock that you can easily push for either a left or right handed grip.  Blade and angle adjustments worked very well and seem solid.  I need a new project!  By the way, I love Amazon Prime.  I ordered this at 4:00PM one day and had it on my porch by noon the next day, not to Houston but to a very rural location in Virginia, for only $3.99.

product_title: SE FS374 All-Weather Emergency 2-IN-1 Fire Starter & Magnesium Fuel Bar (Everything you need to start a fire!)
review_body: The magnesium fire starter was just what I was looking for. Pocket sized and easy to use.   I will be able to embrace firestarting in a new way.

product_title: Milescraft 1206 SignCrafter Signmaking template kit with TurnLock
review_body: This has made routing signs and much more so much more easy. It was well worth the money.!!! I suggest this for anyone from hobbiest to professional.

product_title: Stabila 37524 Promo Level Pack, (Includes 37424 - 24-Inch and 37459 - 59-Inch)
review_headline: The only choice for a pro
review_body: The price might be a little hard to swallow next to box store specials, but these levels are amazing: straightforward, clear, and STRONG. The lifetime warranty (except in the case of a bent frame) makes the price a little easier to take, too.  As far as length, the 59\\" is the perfect length not only for jambing, but as an IDEAL compromise between 4' and 6', which is cumbersome to carry in a vehicle, for example.

product_title: DEWALT DW920K-2 1/4-Inch 7.2-Volt Cordless Two-Position Screwdriver Kit
review_body:
This unit was purchased to replace an identical well-used one that broke after falling from a ladder. The drill head can be angled or set straight like a screwdriver, and when the drill landed in the angled position its cast metal hinge broke cleanly in two.

The drill works well for small jobs and is smaller and more convenient to use than the full-sized larger units. The proprietary quick release chuck accepts only bits designed for it, although these can be used in conventional Jacobs chuck drills as well. The drill is fine for up to 1/4\\" holes and with a #2 Phillips bit it works very well to install drywall and deck screws. Generally there is plenty of torque and the battery capacity is sufficient for most jobs. For example installing paneling or siding with a dozen or so screws per sheet, the battery capacity is good for an hour or so of installation time. Batteries recharge quickly and can be charged and swapped out without significant work delay. The full-size higher voltage DeWalt unit will also charge these smaller 7V batteries.

If this is your only drill/screwdriver then you might want to consider the full-size unit with greater capacity and more torque. If your work is mainly light duty then this drill is convenient to use and perfectly adequate. I like the magnetic bits that will hold screws in place while you are starting them for driving. A selection of bits and drills can be found at home improvement and hardware stores so the use of the quick-release fitting isn't a show-stopper by any means. However if you need drill bits larger than 1/4\\" this drill isn't going to do the job.

review_headline: Technically an 18 volt battery, but great run-time nonetheless. A bit pricey

I've used this battery on pretty much every tool in the kit and am continually impressed. For instance, when in use on the Impact Driver, I was able to drive 100+ screws into hard wood before needing a charge. Using the drill, I was able to drill several holes for 1/2'' x 2-3/4'' Wedge Anchors, then drill 6 holes in a steel car frame and still had battery left over. The saws, while harder on the battery, were still able to be used to cut several pieces of timber for a outside deck.

Dewalt definitely has a winner with the new 20 Volt Max line. I just really don't like the trend all tool manufacturers are taking with the \\"Max\\" ratings. Reminds me too much of car audio. But this doesn't really matter as long as the tools/batteries perform and these definitely do.

I will say, however, these are quite pricey if bought by themselves. But DeWalt isn't alone with it's battery pricing. Most of the \\"contractor-grade\\" tool makers tend to get a bit crazy with battery pricing.

product_title: Campbell Hausfeld TL1004 Dual Action Sander
review_headline: Not a good choice for a DA
review_body:
Out of the box this thing worked great. However, a couple of things to consider before purchasing this particular brand/model sander. It uses around 10SCFM @ 90PSI. This is a high air demand tool and for those of you that don't already have that high of an output air compressor or don't have the extra $$$ to pony up like myself you probably should avoid this sander from the get go. I would recommend having no less than a 6-8 SCFM compressor to even consider this as it made my 4SCFM compressor 26 gallon run CONSTANTLY when sanding a fender for my truck (not good). I now have a craftsman DA sander that cost about 30.00 more but only requires 3.1 SCFM to operate therefor an extremely lower load on my compressor that works just as good.

The really bad: About 2/3rds of the way sanding through my fender this sander got stuck in the what seemed like ON position. The switch or some other component inside failed and would not shut off. I had to use the built in regulator to slow it down enough to stop it and unplug the hose. Could be dangerous or at least scare the crap out of you like it did me. I wound up taking it apart and checking everything out and rebuilding it but I could never figure the darn thing out and wound up trashing it for the less demanding craftsman DA.

I've quickly found out with air tools you get what you pay for. Sometimes it really isn't worth it to try and save yourself 30.00 especially when the tool only lasts all but 1-2 hours of usage. In my opinion/experience with this sander is they might as well label it a D Sander - Disposable Sander instead of a DA.

Also: I did oil this sander prior to first use, I did not drop it, bang it, or place it under any excessive stress during its short time in operation. Don't think it's my error.

review_body:

I really resisted getting a caulk gun because I didn't want to store it in my tool room for what ever reason - it really doesn't take up too much space at all... -The moving mechanism is very smooth with a lot of control over how much caulk you squeeze out. Very even and accurate controllability
-Fits all regular size caulk tubes & easy to load

Cons - none

Tip - When opening the tube tip, be cognizant about how large a diameter you will need for the project. Start with a small tip opening and work on the small areas of your project, and then make it larger as needed.

product_title: Makita BO4900V 2.9 Amp Variable Speed 1/2 Sheet Sander with Paper Dust Bag
review_headline: I agree - the best "Half sheet" sander you can buy
review_body:
I admit I am a tool snob. I really enjoy buying and using the best tools available. This Makita is in a class of its own. I bought both the Makita and Festool FS2 E sander for testing with full intention of keeping the Festool and returning the Makita - but it worked out just the opposite.
Here are my findings after one month of using both.

Festool advantages:
*Longer cord. Festool 11.5 ft Makita 8 ft. Nice for moving around a large table top.
*Better hook-up to Festool vacs, but the Makita works great with the Fein adapter. (921072K13)
*A better and more robust paper hook-up for standard sandpaper, (non hookand loop) which was my favorite thing about the Festool. The Makita's works fine but the Festool's clamp seems stronger and will probably last longer too.
*Comes with a systanier.

Advantages for the Makita:
*MUCH smoother running -BIG surprise to me. I even called Festool and they told me to use the sander for 5-6 hours to break it in and it would smooth out. After 10 hours of use the Makita was still smoother and much more comfortable to use.
*Flatter pad. The Makita came with a flatter sanding pad and that aided in keeping table tops flat. The Festool was not as flat and tended to jump around a lot when it encountered a non-flat surface.
*The Makita was much easier to control.
*The Makita was quieter when running at full speed.
*Better flatter finish when done sanding with the Makita.

For me the Makita did a better job of sanding with less vibration, was quieter and a pleasure to use. It also uses the same paper as the Festool, and was less than half the price. Just a great tool.

product_title: Troy-Bilt (3") 250cc Tow-Behind Chipper Shredder - 24A-424E066
review_headline: A workhorse that's amazing value for the price
review_body:
We've all seen the municipal tree crews - 6 guys picking up a huge branch and tossing it into the maw of a huge chipper where it disappears in seconds. If you're looking for this one to do the same, only in miniature, you're going to be disappointed. Every branch has to be fed in carefully by hand, and pushed through with a push stick. That's a safety feature, to keep you from being sucked into the machine along with the branches!

I have some 90 myoporum trees, each 25'- 35'high, that are diseased and dying. I don't have the time or money to pay someone to take them down, so it's a one at a time deal for me. Drop one, trim off the branches, shred them, cut the main wood for firewood, then on to the next. I run this little workhorse for one hour a week, and it keeps up with the rate at which I generate fodder for it. No problems with jamming, stalling, or anything.

I have only one criticisms, hence the 4/5 rating. The engine exhaust is opposite to the chipper output, right where you rationally want to stand to feed the machine. I'd much rather see it exhausting along the tongue, where you can't possibly stand.

Now a couple of operational warnings.

1. If you run it without the bag (I always do), you'll get shredded debris on the exhaust, where it will start to smoulder. Be careful you don't start any fires!

2. Make sure you don't run out of gas when it's shredding. If the motor stops when there is material in either hopper, you'll have to dismantle it and clear everything out before you can start the machine again.

It takes a bit of time to learn the best way to use this machine for your purposes, but be patient, figure out how best to feed it, and you'll find it's worlds better than paying $180 a day to rent a commercial chipper, and then busting your chops to run it every daylight hour to get your money's worth.

I don't know how I managed so long without it!

Update -May 2014

A few comments based on long term ownership.
1. Keep a careful log of how many hours you run the machine, and follow the service schedule to the letter. Failure to do so will result in premature cylinder head or valve failure - the engine runs hot, and deferred servicing will make this problem much worse.

2. The slots around the recoil starter housing are the air intake for cooling the engine. If you let them get covered with debris, you will shorten the engine life dramatically. Keep clearing them as you work.

3. I found a large sheet of plywood with a slot cut in it, placed over the chute deflector helps to keep the debris separate from the machine and operator.

4. Do not try to feed long thin pliable branches through the chipper chute. They will wrap around the drive shaft between the back of the impeller assembly and the haousing, and stall the engine. Then you will have to dismantle the entire machine to get at what's jammed behind the impeller.

I still love this machine, and I still think it's an incredible bargain for the price.

product_title: King Ice Bear 6000 Grit Waterstone
review_body: These King Stones are legitimate Japanese Water Stones made in, you guessed it, Japan. They are extremely versitile and are the highest quality stones I have used. However, there are a few more good companies out there. Water stones are true to the craft of knife honing and sharpening and is a useful skill to teach yourself. I highly recommend watching virtuovice (YouTube Name) on YouTube for excellent tutorials on how to sharpen with stones.   The lower grit stones like the 250 and 400 are great for taking out chips in the blades or reprofiling the edge to fit your needs or preferences. As a camper who beats on knifes and axes, I really need this benefit to take out those chips and these stones do so beautifully.  A good stone grit to breach the gab between the lower grits and the finishing stone is the 1000 grit. This will help smooth out the edge and give it some great sharpness. It also makes finishing the edge with a 3000 or 4000 grit stone an easier and less time-consuming step in the process. Finally, you should use a leather strop with a green and black compound to really get a good edge.  Bottom Line and Reccommending Sharpening System:  1.) 250/1000 grit King Water Stone   2.) 3000 or 4000 grit King Stone   3.) Leather strop with compound  You only really need the 250, 1000, and 3000 (or 4000) grit stones with the strop. I have seen the strop put a better edge than 8000 grit stones. Keep in mind a strop is only 30 bucks or so, and you could almost spend $100 on an 8000 grit stone. This reccommended sytem will make a butter knife scary sharp if you wanted it too. However, the stones are expensive and will loose shape over time depending on how much you use them. But the time you use them will definitely yield better results than a spyderco Sharpmaker (I have one). I also reccommend some sort of a stone holder like the Steelex Sharpening Stone Holder (If needed). This works well and makes it easier to work with.

product_title: DEWALT DW7352-2 13-Inch Heat Treated Double Sided Replacment Planer Knives, 2-Pack
review_body: The DeWalt DW735X is at the top of my list for a planer for use in a very tiny workshop that I have at my Florida home.  The reviews of the unit itself are quite good where several reviewers have indicated it is the best portable planer on the market.  I have no reason to doubt that.  However, I am used to running a 15\\" Bridgewood planer wherein the longevity of the blades is an issue for me.  I am seriously thinking about installing the new spiral cutter head in my Bridgewood planer.  The cost is around $800 for the spiral cutterhead.  The advantage is that it runs much quieter, uses less Hp and each 1/2\\" x 1/2\\" blade has four cutting edges and is MUCH easier to change that the standard planer blades.  I've tried the disposable blades and find that they only last about half as long as the regular blades.    Now, looking at the blades used by the DeWalt DW735X, I see that they are made of the same cheesy grade of steel as the dispos-a-blade system which only lasts half as long as regular planer blades.  The difference is M2 HSS in the Dewalt and Dispos-a-blade system vs T1 HSS used in the regular blades.  The latter are much harder and last twice as long.    In addition, It appears that with the DeWalt DW735X you are locked into a custom type of blade -in effect- limiting you to the performance of the cheesy M2 steel performance.  (The blades aren't going to last very long.)    I've looked and have not found the higher quality steel blades that would fit a DeWalt DW735x planer.  THIS could be a knockout factor for purchasing what is reportedly the best portable planer on the market.  I mostly plane extremely hard kiln dried red oak.  Note that after only a few hundred bdft, the disposablade knives looked like someone ran a course grindstone ON the edge.  This never happens with regular blades.  They eventually wear to the point that they need \\"sharpened\\" but they ALWAYS hold their edge (the edge stays sharp and even but need replaced or sharpened and adjusted because of the wear that changes the cutting angle and depth).  These regular T1 HSS steel blades start making more noise at about 800 bdft, and after about 1,500 bdft, the wear is bad enough that the angle needs to be rehoned and the blade depth re-adjusted.    The dispos-a-blade system knives lost their edge after only 500 bdft and basically stopped cutting shortly after that.  This is the same steel used in the DeWalt blades.  Not good.    Any comments or suggestions are welcome.  Thanks,  Rick G.    April 8, 2012 update: I did purchase the Dewalt DW735X planer system and have been using it for four months now.  As expected the M2 HSS blades are a problem due to chipping of the cutting edge.  However, (See Danny's reply to my earlier review) Danny Found a site [...] that sells the T1 HSS 3 blade replacement set for the Dewalt DW735 for $47.95.  That's not a bad price for these higher quality blades. And, as Danny pointed out they also have a set of carbide blades for the Dewalt DW735 planer for $123.00.  This is a game changer for this Dewalt planer.    After four months of use, I've found the Dewalt DW735 (or DW735X for the kit) to be an excellent bench planer.  The blade quality is the ONLY issue.  Having found a source for better quality blades I can recommend this planer to anyone.  I am very impressed with the performance and quality of the machine itself.  It is very well designed has minimum skype as well as many features that make using this planer enjoyable.  Most of my planing is on very hard red oak.  It doesn't get much tougher than that.  I've been surprised at the power of a planer only running on 110v.  Other than the blade quality, I have absolutely no complaints and now that Danny found a source for the better quality blades...this planer is fabulous.

product_title: Power 140C 120V MIG Welder 140A
review_body: The 140c model is NOT the standard \\"Lowe's\\" or \\"Home Depot\\" store model Lincoln.  Those are the \\"140T\\" models and they are NOT AS GOOD AS THE 140c.  My review will discuss the 140c model.  The difference between the two is that the 140c model is a bit more expensive, but has a \\"continuous\\" rheostat voltage control knob.  This allows one to find the \\"sweet spot\\" for welding certain thicknesses of metal.  The 140T model has a \\"tapped\\" voltage controller which is inferior.    The 140c can weld 1/4\\" steel plate no problem.  If you know what you're doing and have some experience in welding that is, it is not hard to \\"tweak\\" the machine into doing what you want it to do.  In fact, I regularly use it to weld 3/8\\" steel handgun targets.  Also, another key point is that one needs a 120v wall outlet that is a minimum of 25amp service.  Using a traditional RV 30A outlet with a simple $8.00 plug adapter would work perfectly!  However, most people do NOT have a 25A or 30A service outlet at their homes.  However, many residential houses all have have 20A service outlets, that will pretty much work for most metal.  Only time even the 20A outlets trip the breaker is when you turn the voltage rheostat up to the high range and then your breaker will trip regularly.  Especially if you're running an extention cord from the outlet to the machine.  I try NOT to using an extension cord.  Longer the cord, the increase in resistance, thus decrease in voltage to the machine.  Now if one only has a regular 15amp 120v outlet at their house, the welder will work, but not on a \\"high\\" setting, therefore it will limit one to welding thinner stuff.  Thinner metals do not require the \\"higher\\" voltage or wire speed settings that the thick stuff needs.  If I recall correctly, Lincoln's owner's manual recommends at least a 25A 110/120v outlet.    Anyway, this Lincoln 140c is THE BEST mig welder on the market for the DIYer at home or on the farm, bar none.  You get what you pay for.  This machine will last a life time with proper care (...or not, it's a LINCOLN!).  If you want a higher duty cycle and be able to weld slightly thicker metal, then you'll need to buy the 180c model which is 240v only.  Now Lincoln makes a dual voltage machine that can run on either 120 or 240v by simply using the proper plug it comes with.  240 volts give you more power for thicker metal.  If you only need a simple great welder and are limited to the standard 110/120v wall plugs, get the 140c.  You will NOT be sorry.

The allow for a more stable elevated base to work on with your router or hand plane. The work piece doesn't slide around the bench (unless it is dirty with saw dust. I also use these when spraying finish on the front of raised Panel doors.  All in all a great product for the assistance it provides.

product_title: Shop-vac 90304 Cartridge Filter
review_body: This is just the same as a product I would have purchased in the store, but for less $$.  It worked well for me

product_title: Dremel 8300-01 12-Volt Cordless Multi-Max Oscillating Kit
review_body:
Dremel has put out another winner in a large group of great tools. I've only done a couple of quick jobs so far but I am a happy camper. The Max is big enough to hold easily but not too big or heavy. product_title: Astro 2181 Double Cut Carbide Rotary Burr Set with 1/4-Inch Shank
review_body: I purchased these with some hesitation because my Snap On Tool guy wanted $55 for just one of these carbides. I've used them several times now and they seem avery bit as good as the Snap on carbide bits that I have purchased. An awesome buy for the money !!!  Really can't go wrong with a set of eight bits!  BUY THESE! They will not disappoint!

product_title: Stanley 91-929 3/8-Inch Drive Pear Head Quick Release Ratchet
review_body: I have many Stanley tools. For the money I have found these tools to hold up and have a lifetime warranty. I wanted another 3/8-inch ratchet and I found this Stanley 91-929 3/8-Inch Drive Pear Head Quick Release Ratchet at amazon.com. This is a very good ratchet.

product_title: Leatherman - Squirt PS4 Multitool
review_body: I have a larger Leatherman, but wanted one that I could easily have with me at all time.    This has already come in handy on numerous occasions.  I would definitely buy this again and again.

product_title: Makita Bare-Tool BTD141Z 18-Volt LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless Impact Driver (Tool only)
review_body: I love my tools, every once in a while somebody makes one perfectly suited to what it is designed to do. I love this tool, it's like an auto-darkening welding hood because once you've used either one, you're ruined, you can never go back to what you used to use.

review_body: I purchased this (Sidekick) at REI today, and I returned just after one day, when I got home and started to use this \\"Leatherman tool\\" I soon became aware of the reason for the great price point! Old saying goes you get what you pay for and I believe leatherman just wanted to make a product that would be more appealing to the ppl with a little less money in there pocket, which don't get me wrong somethings on this multi-tool where good but I think all in all it was built very flimsy ( I included pictures to show)..and as far as the \\"wire cutters\\" this is a joke, if you can imagine pressing 2 nails together and hoping to cut something than you can understand my point, they do not over lap each other, nor is there any kind of edge to the cutters!!!! FAIL... the blade shape and sharpness where fine, the screwdriver and flat head where fine, and I was happy to see there was a pocket clip!! The pliers felt very weak as if you where to put any force to them they would twist sideways as would the handle.. now don't get me wrong I know this is not the top of the line leatherman multi-tool for $40 bucks (REI)..but at least give me a sturdy platform.. review_headline: Perfect for what I got it for.

Did a TON of research before purchasing this. The other choice was the makita TD020DSEW which was just overkill for electronics. much heavier and not nearly as adjustable. review_body: I saw this package at my local electronics store that I frequent often, and it seemed like a good deal but luckily the line was too long for my liking so I decided to skip out. product_title: Streamlight Knucklehead Work Light without Charger
review_body:
This rechargeable LED work light has nice features, and also weak points, including a primitive NiCd battery system.

(I have the nearly identical [[ASIN:B004MOLJI2 Streamlight 90627]].)

PROs:

* Lots of hanging, pointing and mounting options
* 3 brightness levels + Strobe. Nice! (see Note 1)
* Adapter for AA batteries (extended wilderness use)
- Water resistant (IPX4 - can take rain and gentle splashes)
- Nylon housing - 2 meter impact-resistance
- 2-year warranty (Lifetime warranty on non-electrical defects. See Note 2)
- Looks like a high-end flashlight

OKs:

* It's a work light - optimized for close range. It does not throw a concentrated beam. (See Note 3.)
- This model (90627) includes the Steady (slow) 120v AC or 12v DC charger. It does NOT include the 1-hour FAST charger.

CONs:

* NiCd battery - Not Li-Ion (1990's technology, self-discharges or wants 24x7 trickle charge. Other issues -- see Note 4.)
* Dumb charger - wastes energy, no charge status indicator. (See note 5)
* Very expensive for what you get
* Ergonomics - Not great. (see note 6)
- Not very comfortable when hand held
- Super-strong magnet: A pointless design element with multiple hazards (see note 7).
- Owner manual: Some carelessness and missing information. (see note 8)

Note 1: 3 brightness levels + Strobe: From very bright, to \\"moonlight,\\" which lasts 20 days. Nice!

Note 2: Limited Lifetime Warranty: \\"Streamlight warrants this product to be free of defect, including the LED, for a lifetime of use. We will repair, replace or refund the purchase price, at our option, of any Streamlight product that does not work as a result of a manufacturing defect for as long as you own it. This lim­ited lifetime warranty excludes abuse, batteries, chargers, switches, electronics and normal wear and tear. Recharge­able batteries, chargers, switches and electronics have a two (2) year warranty with proof of purchase.\\"

Note 3: It's a work light: It's good for lighting up whatever is 3 to 20 feet away. It does not throw a concentrated beam; it does a poor job lighting up distant objects.

Note 4: NiCd battery: In addition to weight, self-discharge, and memory effect issues, the following applies: a.) \\"Several charge and discharge cycles may be needed to achieve full battery capacity.\\" b.) \\"A small leakage of liquid from the battery cells can occur under extreme usage or temperature conditions. This does not necessarily indicate a failure. [ <--Really, not a failure??!! ] However, if the outer case seal is broken and the chemical leakage gets on your skin...Any liquid chemical must be flushed off the skin with a generous amount of water. Brush any dry or powdered chemicals thoroughly, before flushing the area with profuse amounts of water.\\"

Note 5: The included Steady Charger (works off 12v DC or 120v AC) is not an smart charger. It can't tell you if the battery has reached a full charge, because it has no idea. You're supposed to just trickle charge your Knucklehead 24x7 as a tribute to energy waste. If you remove the Knucklehead from the charger, the red light will stop shining as way of confirming the obvious: The Knucklehead is not in the charger. However, the wall wart (transformer plug) will continue to radiate heat (waste electricity) and the Knucklehead's primitive NiCd battery will self discharge at a rate of maybe 20% per month. This is to be expected from a $30 flashlight sold at Wal-Mart or a state-of-the-art flashlight circa 1990. Not today's $140 flashlight.

Note 6: Not very ergonomic: No show stoppers, just little things. It's not very comfortable when hand held. The battery latch is a pain to open. The AA battery adapter is a slight pain to open. The markings for AA battery direction are hard to see. You can't switch to moonlight withoutenduring the strobe mode for 6 seconds. The charger's bright red pilot light (which tells you nothing) could be an eyesore in a dark room. If you want to take the magnet off, (and you will -- see note 7), get yourself a 9/64\\" Allen wrench. Really? They couldn't have gone with a common 1/8\\"?

Note 7: Super-strong magnet: 135 pound pull strength. Really? To hold up a flashlight? Or is this about affirming my manhood? It's a pinch hazard, a painted surface hazard, a pacemaker hazard...and who knows what it will do to your smartphone or camera?

Note 8: Owner's manual: a.) very small font. b.) Vague about what's included (Fast Charger is not included, but manual describes it as if it is.) c.) Gives very few specifications (but lots of specs are available at Streamline's Web site.) d.) Says it ships with magnet detached, but the opposite is true.

Summary: Nice idea, but they didn't finish the job. Wal-Mart battery technology at a Brookstone price.If you want to take the magnet off, (and you will -- see note 7), get yourself a 9/64\\" Allen wrench. Really? They couldn't have gone with a common 1/8\\"? Note 7: Super-strong magnet: 135 pound pull strength. Really? To hold up a flashlight? Or is this about affirming my manhood? It's a pinch hazard, a painted surface hazard, a pacemaker hazard...and who knows what it will do to your smartphone or camera? Note 8: Owner's manual: a.) very small font. b.) Vague about what's included (Fast Charger is not included, but manual describes it as if it is.) c.) Gives very few specifications (but lots of specs are available at Streamline's Web site.) d.) Says it ships with magnet detached, but the opposite is true. Summary: Nice idea, but they didn't finish the job. Wal-Mart battery technology at a Brookstone price.

review_headline: The Price was correct for the product...
review_body: Exactly as shown in the picture.  My only complaint is that there needs to be a larger screwdriver.  The largest screwdriver was just small enough to strip one of the case screws on my MacBook Pro (aluminum case).  I'm sure that everything else in this package has wonderful uses, but I was pretty bummed that the largest screwdriver was too small.    If all you need is the screw drivers, save yourself a few bucks and just get a mini screwdriver set at the hardware store.

product_title: Campbell Hausfeld 17-Piece Air Tool  and Accessory Kit (MP284701AV)
review_headline: A lot of parts or is it???
review_body: Well to be honest I was like WOW your getting a lot of parts for the price.  But in actuality the \\"excess\\" parts that come with it you need for the \\"tools\\" to connect the tools to an air hose.  So by saying it is a 25 piece kit is not exactly true. Yes it cost a little more, but you do get what you pay for!

product_title: Neewer® LCD Display Digital Wood Moisture Meter to Measure the Percentage of Water in Wood, Sheetrock, Carpets and More with 4 Steel Sensor Pins, a 9V Battery and a Carrying Bag

review_body: Yes, it works well. Next time you buy that 2by4 that looks like laser beem today just to turn into twisty question mark in a week or two - figure out why using this little gizmo. Good tool for a smart person.

product_title: Brinkmann 809-9010-S 6 LED Flashlight with AAA Batteries, 10-Pack
review_headline: Very impressed! Nice lights for the price
review_body: I needed a bunch a flashlights to take to a overnight charity event - something easy to slip into the pocket, enough light to walk along unlit paths, and of course inexpensive enough to not be a budget buster. Batteries included was a real plus.  I bought several packs and was very pleasantly surprised that every single light worked right out of the package.  Oddly, some of flashlights had a small paper tag under the cap that had to be removed before using, some didn't. I've gotten similar style 6 led flashlights with metal cases and found many of those are broken right at the store.  These 100% worked!   The only trick I found is the threading is a little tricky and you have to screw it on just right or the light might not work.  They do make as much light or more as a old style two D battery flashlight, but small and light enough to put in your pocket  The rubberized case makes for a nice grip. If you depend on a flashlight every day as part or your job these obviously can't be expected to replace a Mag-lite, but for keeping around all around the house, garage, car, camping, this are great.  Best part if you lose one it's no big deal, you still got nine more left.

product_title: Smith & Wesson 1st Response SWFRS Liner Lock Folding Knife Partially Serrated Drop Point Blade Steel Handle
review_headline: best folding knife i've ever bought!
review_body: This knife is great! it keeps a nice sharp edge, it's big but not too big and if i'm ever in a car crash i can cut myself out of the seatbelt and break the window!

product_title: Bosch 4100-09 10-Inch Worksite Table Saw with Gravity-Rise Stand
review_body: I was ready to buy this saw until I read in the reviews that there is no blade height locking mechanism.  I couldn't believe that any major company would make a saw without a blade height lock, so I called Bosch technical support and asked about this.  The rep treated me like I didn't know what I was asking about (I own a cabinet shop) and tried to convince me that \\"it just stays in place.\\" He then tried to act like the bevel lock was a blade height lock, which he later admitted it was not.  Even a well tuned stationary cabinet saw with minimal vibration can have the blade height change (gradually drops from minor machine vibration and motor weight) without the lock on.  How on the earth did they overlook this feature?  If the blade height is not lockable then you can't reliably cut dadoes, and if I can't cut dadoes on it, I'm getting a different saw.  This is a major let-down from bosch, who by all accounts makes an otherwise great saw, with the best stand available, what a shame.   From what I gather the ridgid 4510 is the only saw that really gets all the major features right in this category, I would suggest looking into that one, that's where I'm headed.

review_body: This stone is quite large which is definitely a good thing, as it allows for a good stroke along the edge of a 10\\" chef knife. This stone should really be used as part of a set with a 6000 grit or higher if you are shooting for arm hair shaving sharp.

product_title: LSN3 LOTOS 2-in-1 Air Hardwood Flooring Cleat Nailer and Stapler Gun
review_body: I debated between renting or buying, with the price for the Lotos it was a no brainer to buy. I was worried about such a low price, would the tool perform, well it did.  This was my first hardwood floor job, 2 bedrooms about 400 sq ft, 3/4 inch oak. The tool performed flawlessly, not one jam. The only mistake I made, was hitting the tool too lightly, getting staples out is not easy if they don't go all the way down. Once I perfected the hitting stroke, I never had an issue. If I rented, my cost would have been higher than purchasing, and renting does not let you work at your own pace.  Loading staples was easy, one wish would be for the tool to let you know staples are out. All in all this was a great purchase.
