product_title: Makita LXT601 18-Volt LXT 6-Piece Lithium-Ion Cordless Combo Kit
review_headline: TAKE THE IMPACT DRIVER AND DRILL AND LEAVE THE REST
review_body: The impact driver and light hammer drill are great, but the other tools are all sub par.  I had used a coworker's impact driver and drill at work and was impressed with Makita's cordless tools, so I purchased this set (Note: did NOT purchase from Amazon).  The light was great until it stopped working, and the stitching on the bag was poor and the zipper didn't work.  The circular saw is really underpowered, and the only thing it goes through quickly is the battery.  The reciprocating saw is nothing to brag about, and also eats up the battery in short order.  The grinder has an auto shut-off that will disengage the machine at the slightest effort, which deems it pretty useless.    The only thing good about this package is that the charger works quickly and well, and the drill and the driver are still very impressive tools.    If I had to do it over again I would only get the drill/driver combo set, or I would go with a different manufacturer.

product_title: Hitachi DS12DVF3 12-Volt Ni-Cad 3/8-Inch Cordless Drill/Driver Kit  (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: This refurbished set I purchased rocks the house down. The Drill and all the extras work to perfection. I can honestly say this is probably the best purchase I have made on Amazon since I started making purchases on here. I am very pleased and will return here when future cordless power tool needs arrive.

product_title: Festool 583492 CT 26 E HEPA Dust Extractor
review_body:
I just purchased the CT26 Dust Extractor. It arrived w/ problems. The top hose caddy, the saddle the hose rest in, to be wound was cracked through. Also the addition of a Systainer 1, compact cleaning kit, did not seat correctly into the top mount in the hose caddy.

I immediately called the place where I purchased the CT 26. They, w/ some reluctance agreed to send me a new hose caddy rather than sending the whole unit back for exchange. One reason they were willing to do so, this was not their 1st incident of a cracked through saddle in the top compartment.

With Festool's reputation for German engineering, and the premium price you are paying for this \\"Exceptional Tool\\", you would think that their quality control would be better.

The function of the tool is good. The machine is very quiet, and has a suction control, depending on your task. Since I have only had the machine for several day, I am limited in performance statements.

The one thing I am not happy w/ besides quality control is the diameter of the hose connections. They are unique to Festool. I guess they prefer you buy all of their high $$ accessories. If like myself you already have a large selection of tools you will need hose adapters to convert to your shops tools.

product_title: Rayovac SELUX2AA3W-B Sportsman Xtreme 3-Watt Luxeon LED Flashlight With Batteries
review_body: 1.Is it a small aluminum LED flashlight: Check.    2.Does it work when the batteries are installed: Check.    3.Is it really bright for it's size: Check.    4.Did it spontaneously combust and/or explode when I turned it on: No.    5.Could you use it to disarm a bank robber: Depends on your ninja skills/ knife throwing skills.    In conclusion, it's bright, it didn't explode, and it's durable. Will it be able to replace the sun one day if it burns out.. probably not.      I would buy another one if it was still on the lightning deals.

product_title: MAGLITE XL100 LED Flashlight
review_body: Maglite used to be known for making a rock solid product; like their lines of flashlights that they ran over with transport trucks to demonstrate the point.  The XL100 is not as solid as one might expect from such a lineage.    The form factor is nice.  The shape is pleasing to look at, compact and simple and the button has a nice texture to it.  It lacks any sort of attachment (ie. belt clip or included holster) but ordering a lanyard ring like a previous reviewer mentioned solved that.  The lens focus is a bit loose, 1 wrap with some teflon tape made it feel more secure.  The plastic battery holder could be sturdier and the insertion direction could be more clearly indicated.      Functionally, the modes are clearly indicated on the tail and holding the light horizontally with the desired mode at the top is simple enough and explained in the manual.  The light is bright and produces a nice beam profile.  I did not get a chance to try the lockout mode before it died.  It died within a week of use, the batteries were not at fault as a fresh set did not fix the issue.      Unfortunately if a light doesn't work, what's the point of keeping it?  The shape does not lend itself to being a very good paperweight.

product_title: DEWALT DWP611PK 1.25 HP Max Torque Variable Speed Compact Router Combo Kit with LED's
review_body: Awesome router... ideal for detail routing and trim work and has the power to handle most router functions. Led lights up work for accurate detail routing such as inlaying.Plunge router base operates smoothly and accurately.

product_title: Genius Tools 32Pc 3/8" Dr. Metric Deep Impact Socket Set TF-332M
review_body: This set is perfect for when I work on vehicles, I can switch from air ratchet to ratchet to impact. It has about every size you need in 3/8ths drive. Now I need to get some socket rails to hold them.

product_title: Shop Fox D2058 Adjustable Extra Heavy-duty Mobile Base
review_body: I put a 20\\" harbor freight drill press (about 275#) on this base with an additional 150 # of tooling stored on the bottom. Base works great; no deflection; very solid; easy to move on a smooth concrete floor.  A couple of the reviews for this unit speak of plastic wheels breaking up and caster interference, but they must have this model confused with some other unit.  My D2058A base came with very heavy machined cast iron wheels and the two casters can be rotated a full 360 degrees with absolutely no interference to anything.  Assembly was easy for something this heavy and so completely size adjustable but I will agree that the screws that come with the unit are terrible!  They are very, very, soft and will twist off with the slightest over torque.  The poor quality fasteners is my only complaint about an otherwise great mobile base. I plan on buying another one, and would highly recommend it to anyone.

product_title: Dorcy Lumen High Flux LED Cyber Light Flashlight with Alkaline Batteries
review_body: Unbelievable - amazing - I was looking at spotlights from $50-$150 and came across this flashlight.  With all of the great reviews, I decided to try it since it was a lot less expensive and weighs a lot less.  I use it to check cows at least twice a night every night and the first set of batteries lasted a month! Good reach - super bright - lightweight - small enough to fit in my coat pocket - dropped it in a mud puddle and it still works.  Must have - you will not be disappointed!!!

These batteries showed up in excellent condition. Batteries were placed on the charger and immediately charged. I have been using this drill now. It hasn't been used for about two years because of the original batteries. The price for these replacements were about half the price Sears wants for the replacement. I will definitelt conduct business with this company oin the future.

product_title: Columbia River Knife and Tool 2020 AG Russell Sting Razor Sharp Edge Knife
review_body: nice knife. Fine steel, well made,fits hand nice. Very good sheath and velcro straps. Straps nice to end table leg,easy access for me. For price should be sharp and of finer finish. GOOD BUY.

product_title: Johnson Level & Tool 916 16-Foot Big Johnson Power Tape
review_body: I love my Big Johnson.  I have two of these.  I particularly like the quick release that makes it easy to reholster without trying to get it on you pants pocket each time, and it doesn't wear out your pants in the process. My oldest one doesn't hang level when holstered due to the plastic wearing but it still functions flawlessly.  I wish they made them in a longer version but for light construction they are great.

product_title: Smith & Wesson SWEX4 Extreme Ops. Knife with Fixed Tanto Blade
review_body: Bought this knife for general use.  Solid hefty feel to the knife.  It feels as though it would be good for light prying and hacking as well as beating things.  I really like the looks of the knife and the sheath.  I Love the scales and this one has a fish scale look to it. Have only had it for several days attached it to load bearing equipment for hiking.  Very satisfied with product and value thus far. Only fear is scratching or wearing the finish off the blade, its so scary pretty.

product_title: MagLite XL50 LED 3-Cell AAA Flashlight, Blue
review_body: This flashlight is nearly perfect.  It has 3 settings the first two are brightness, the third is a strobe.  I like the fact that you don't have to run through each setting to turn it off.  This light has a retina burning LED that will have you seeing sun spots for a long time if you look into it.  It also has great distance (not really for corn fields but good for most anything else).  I usually use the lower setting due to that even being too bright for most situations.  This is my carry flashlight.  Before the XL 50 I never carried a flashlight before.  But this is the right size and shape.  It fits well in the hand (length and diameter just right)and the rear button is sub-flush so you really don't have to worry about accidentally turning on.  It also tolerates moderate abuse.  I can not at this time comment on heavy abuse (but I'm sure it will hold it's own).    Also, I love the fact this runs on AAA batteries rather than needing some odd ball expensive hard to find fancy batteries.    My only complaint is the knurling.  It is along the length of the body.  So if you are not gripping tight enough or your hands are wet it will slip before actuating the button.  I would rather the knurling be cross.  I would also like to see a lanyard hole but not necessary.    All in all this is a most excellent flashlight.  I would recommend this as a safety light for ladies.  This would fit in a purse and since it has a cornea blistering light it may give you that 1 second advantage you might need.  And since it has an aluminum body it would serve as a kubotan substitute.  At 30 toad skins each if you break it on a bad guy's head you can buy another one with no guilt.

product_title: Neiko 10224A Extra Long Security Power Bit Set, 32 Piece | 1/4" Shank | 6" Length
review_headline: Neiko 32-Piece 6-Inch Extra Long Security Bit Set
review_body: The set appears to be as advertised. I was looking for smaller size bits. I kept them even thought, they didn't work for what I bought them for

product_title: MAGLITE XL100 LED Flashlight
review_headline: I have something which will last longer & remain !
review_body: I have liked it. i ordered two one for my wife and one for me. i do not live in USA but  far ina country where we do not have electricity  more than 12 hours a day. So, we find this very useful. Battery last longer.

product_title: LED Gloves Green LEDs
review_body: These gloves are very bright and functional.  However the wires on the inside cracked and broke apart leaving half of the lights powerless.  If your planning on getting these gloves prepare to be dissapointed.

product_title: Dico 527-BSC2-6 Hard Metal 6-Inch Buffing Kit
review_body: Until we became more vigilant, our new kitchen sink disposal seemed to enjoy trying to eat our expensive Mikasa stainless steel spoons.  Before long, we had gone from 6 shiny and bright eating utensils, to two.  The 4 that had been chewed had dents, cuts, grooves and sharp pieces of steel sticking out at odd angles and were too scary to use.  The word from the chief cook and bottle washer was out to the kitchen help (me) that a fix was in order. I considered having someone else do it but the section under \\"spoon polishing\\" in the Yellow Pages was underwhelming at best.  I tried using a file and sandpaper but I found that I couldn't easily work on the concave surfaces and it left a very dull and unattractive surface. Of course, I turned to Home Depot for a solution and brought home a 6\\" Ryobi grinder but HD had no polishing or buffing wheels to sell.  My next stop was Amazon and there I located the Dico 6\\" hard metal buffing kit.  It seemed to meet my criteria, (I'm a cheapskate!), and a few days later it was mounted on my new Ryobi and I was grinding and polishing away.    I will tell you that the Ryobi grinder and fine abrasive wheels plus the Dico kit gave me the results I wanted......safe, shiny spoons!  They likely wouldn't have passed factory inspection but the grinding marks were gone (mostly) and they shone like new.  I was a hero again!    What I wasn't prepared for was the cotton fuzz and dust that was everywhere in my garage, including my hair and clothes, on our car and every flat surface.  This appears to be the price you'll pay for polished steel, the gradual breakdown of the buffing pads to fine cotton thread.  It's like they're returning to their roots.  What a mess!  Thankfully I was able to clean it up quickly but I think that next time I'll look for a product less likely to self destruct so quickly.  The pads likely lost about a half inch of diameter and I'm unsure how much longer they'll last if they continue to obliterate themselves at that rate.Also, I consumed about 50% of both compounds polishing 4 spoons.    Don't get me wrong, the Dico buffing kit works well but expect to have a major cleanup when its all over.

product_title: Milwaukee 49-56-9105 Big Hawg Arbor
review_headline: works well but not sure about O-ring life
review_body: There are lots of arbors that have the 2-pin piece slide into the hole saw and then a second ring to tighten it into place. The Milwaukee is supposed to not loosen with vibration as it has a rubber O-ring in between the two pieces. It works well but rubber O-rings deteriorate quickly from sun and smog and this O-ring is not replaceable when it goes. Good but not great as arbors go.    It comes with a spade bit for wood which is what the Big Hawg are meant to cut. Reduced shank of this type of pilot bit makes it easy to get the cut piece of wood out and works much better than a regular twist bit that is meant for use on metal.

product_title: Ulzio T-1 Ultrabright CREE LED Flashlight Kit - Weapon Mountable
review_body: I very much enjoyed opening up this product and immediately feeling a flashlight of higher quality than anticipated. The metal that the flashlight is made out of is indeed descent and well made. The LED is capable of very bright output and with a little trail and error is easy to manipulate through the other different light modes. I wasn't expecting much for the price I paid for this item, but was very happy when I mounted it on my Ar15 and felt it out for myself. The ONLY issues I had/am having with this flashlight kit is that A: The mount that is included is complete crap, made out of a much lower grade aluminum than the flashlight and was SOOOOO TIGHT around the light that it scratched the crap out of the inside of the mount/slightly scratched the outside of the flashlight. B: The corded tailcap switch that was included was defective and I am in the process of trying to have it replaced....I mounted the light originally for use with the pressure switch, and it shorted out within about 25 on/off cycles. I wasn't very happy with this, but for the time being since I use a forward grip on my setup it i moved it around to work well with using my thumb!!     I'll be stoked once I get another working pressure switch, but am still happy with the important part of this kit....the flashlight itself!!

product_title: DEWALT Bare-Tool DCD950B 1/2-Inch 18-Volt XRPHammerdrill/Drill/Driver
review_body: I bought this drill recently after mine had some unfortunate \\"incidents\\" with coworkers. I didn't want to spend all the money that the stores were asking to get a whole new kit and so I did some searching and found this one.  I was a bit nervous at first because it was so cheap and thought maybe I was getting ripped off, but it is legit and works fantastic.

product_title: Stanley 85-610 10-Inch Long MaxGrip Locking Adjustable Wrench
review_headline: this is my go to adjustable
review_body: Nothing replaces box wrenches, but in a pinch adjustables will work. The biggest problem I have always had with the plain adjustable is releasing the tool after closing the jaws on the bolt/nut; perhaps, it is because I do not use the most expensive tools out there, (& thus the best???). The Stanley maxgrip solves the mentioned delemma, and goes one step further. Locking onto the bolt, I do not need to grow a third hand to keep the wrench in place- it stays. This is my go to tool when adjusting sailboat rigging over salt water. Releasing the tool is just a squeeze of the finger. As for using an expensive adjustable in my work environment, I've found once they've fallen into the water they all sink at about the same pace.

product_title: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools F06TN-CP Fasthawk Tactical Tomahawk with 2-Inch Steel Axe Blade and Black Ballistic Nylon Sheath, Black Finish
review_headline: Higher quality than you would think
review_body: At this price this is a well built combat tool. Feels natural in my hands, well balanced, parts don't wiggle, not easy to break and very solid. Also not as handy as the larger one for wood work, I would only use this smaller one for tossing into hay bales at the farm and for pulling out if someone threatens me. It might be good at hacking small limbs or a survival tool and maybe for working on a deer but not an everyday wood cutter. Bought this with a Buck 650 Nighthawk knife, very good combo.    Update: Got a second one and been throwing them for a few weeks. Handed one to my bud and he tossed it into first one on accident, handle is missing a chunk at very bottom where the one he threw landed with the flat part of the head onto the handle of the first then deflected. The steel for the head is very hard and still just as sharp as it was from the factory, the handles just seem a tad too brittle for me to consider buying any more. I will try find some black epoxy and see if I can repair it.     These tomahawks are not expensive like the Lagana's but they are expensive enough to prohibit easy replacement. I might look at local flea markets for more axes to throw, these tomahawks work well but you are always bound to have accidental \\"bumps\\" when you throw a few at the same area and that exposes the achilles heel of these otherwise fine tools.

product_title: Ingersoll Rand 231P32 Protective Tool Boot
review_headline: Fits Tighter Than Lady Gaga's Meat Dress
review_body: Yes, it takes a fair amount of sweat to get this cover on (picture Red Skelton putting on his \\"invisible\\" girdle). But, unless you like to throw your expensive air tools around like you're a NASCAR pit crew, this thin red \\"girdle\\" will protect your shiny new impact wrench from getting trashed. It works. Simple as that.

product_title: Bosch GMS120 Digital Multi-Scanner
review_body: The Bosch Digital Multi-Scanner generally works as described with the use of a 9V 'rechargeable' battery.  The Scanner also impressively worked as a metal detector to locate screw holders that were dropped/lost in the thick grass outdoor our workshop.     However, in a repeated case of using the Multi-mode detection feature, the device found steel pipes, but could not detect the live wiring on one side, which were encased behind a solid wall.  We tried testing it again from a different angle on another side, and it finally located the wires.      So, it seems the three sensor technology may have a 91% reliability, but we'll see how it fairs on other projects, as it does work well in detecting metals.

product_title: Hobart 195186 Protective Weather Resistant Cover for Welder Handler Models 135/140/175/180
review_body: This cover fit the welder without issue and the pocket on the side is awesome for keeping the gun and clamp stored securely out of the way.  I was pleasantly surprised to find that there was even a nicely finished, veclro slit on the back of the cover so that it can be installed around the power cord and gas line--when you want to weld, just unhook the velcro and it pulls off and over the machine.    I think the material will also do well to keep the welder clean and safe from all othe other things happening in my garage.  I bought it for that reason--I also do some woodworking and was concerned about the amount of stuff that would get thrown into the welder from saws, routers, sanders, etc.  I think this bit of kit will do well to protect the welder from all of that.    Bottom line: it protects your welder, seems well made, and makes it easy to cover/uncover your equipment.

product_title: Irwin Industrial Tools 2078601 8-Inch SAE Quick Adjusting Wrench
review_body: I would love to say how good it is but several letters and 5 weeks and I still have not received it

product_title: Senco 1R0004N DS200-AC Duraspin 3,300 RPM Collated Screwdriver
review_body: I was looking forward to putting in ~ 2000 cement board screws and another 2000 screws to hold down underlayment.  I decided to purchase this Senco gun.     The good: (and it's mostly all good): Man does this gun lay the screws in fast. I pay a guy $25 / hour to help me and the money I spent on the gun and collated screws paid for itself in both time and aggravation. Zip - pop - bam, the screw is in and waiting for you to tell it where the next one goes. It made what would have been a miserable job fun.  My gun came with a Philips bit and two square head bits. It is easily adjustable for depth and even has an adjustment  so you can countersink the screws a bit. Very cool.     The bad: The only niggle I would have with this gun is the logistics. I tore the grooves off the end of the Philips bit that came with it in short order and then went on a merry tour to many local home improvement stores and then even a Senco dealer. None of them had bits ( or collated screws) to fit. I ended up placing an order back with Amazon to get the bit. I found that Milwaukee brand collated screws fit just as well. I ordered all these, round 2, from  Amazon.     Bottom line: When you use this gun, be sure to plan in advance and get the screws and extra bits you might need from Amazon. Be sure to use the square headed screws and bits, the Philips bits don't last long.

product_title: G & F 8126S Cowhide Leather Thumb Guard, Thumb Protection, Small, Finger Guard Sold Separately
review_body: Love these little finger and thumb guards - kept me from many trips to the E.R.!!!  Maybe I'm lucky or just a little cautious, but they've prevented me from being cut even once since I started using them years ago.  Would definitely recommend them to any and all.  Safe carving to you!

product_title: SE FS374 All-Weather Emergency 2-IN-1 Fire Starter & Magnesium Fuel Bar (Everything you need to start a fire!)
review_body: Threw it in my 72 hour kit.  Hope i never have to use it, but i tested it, and it works great.

product_title: Brown Bag Company 30299 ToolRider GSR
review_body: For the most part I really like this tool belt.  Very well built, quality material and workmanship, pouches are rugged, the shoulder pads are comfortable and the   belt and buckle is pretty tough.  The only drawback is the strap adjustment.  I'm 5'7\\" and I have the straps adjusted as short as they can go. I like  the shoulder pads to be  centered on my shoulder. Minor issue and if you are taller, it won't be.  All in all, for the price it is a very nice rig.

product_title: Damascus Nexstar III Medium Weight All Duty Military Gloves with Multi-Cam Camo, Multi-Cam
review_headline: Great but still a little long in the fit.
review_body: I bought a pair of these in medium size back earlier in the year and liked them very much.  I like the fit of the palm very much. They easily grasp anything from a triggerguard to a page in a book.  I would have given them five stars but the fingers are too long with excess fabric which limits my finger dexterity.  I would reccomend them for most tasks.  Don't reccomend them for hard \\"tactical\\" use as they dont have the durability to withstand that.  Spend more money if you want excellent gloves and you wont go wrong.  Just don't spend too much especially if the product is made overseas.  For the price they great. I personally think they could have been sewn better but these were made in Pakistan so go figure.  Try to get your quality control better Damascus and you will have a winner glove.

product_title: Milwaukee 2310 12-Volt Lithium-Ion M-Spector Digital Inspection Camera and 2401 M12 Compact Screwdriver Combo Kit
review_headline: Great little driver, pretty good camera...
review_body: I got these for one sixty during the recent deal of the day. The driver does not disappoint. Great battery life (used ALOT and have recharged 3x so far) and torque for it's size. Clutch is dead on. Get a 1/4\\" hex to 3/8\\" chuck adapter and you have a good little drill, but it's not very precise (minor wobble) or a speed demon. The handle is a little bulky so I use my middle finger on the trigger and point my index at the tip and it feels like that is the way it was intended to be used. The battery life indicator is a big plus and the led light actually helps, but it could be aimed a few degrees higher (I've used it a flashlight a couple of times!). The camera is okay for certain applications. I'm in the a/c and heating business so I'm using it to examine a/c evaporator coils for dirt and gas furnace heat exchangers for rust. It can also help read motor info off hidden data plates. It really is a time/labor saver and at the price I paid it was a steal. I haven't used it to see inside a wall but others have mentioned the limitations there. I do wish the monitor or flex line could swivel to correct sideways or upside down views. It's reassuring to know it's waterproof in case I need to into a sewer line or something. At the current price I may hold off, but if the price drops again I would not hesitate to buy this combo.

product_title: PacTool International SS404 SteelHead Fiber Cement Cutting Shear
review_headline: An absolute must have for hardie board siding
review_body: I really like this tool, I did have to get use to cutting straight with it at first but you get use to it and I always cover up my cut ends anyway so it wasn't too bad. There is no dust when you use it, it zips right through with hardly any effort at all. The manual says not to use it on 1/2\\" hardie board, but it does still cut through it quite well (I don't know if it will affect the longevity of the tool or not though). It was well worth the price, it paid for itself within 2 weeks or less.

product_title: SE MW10087L Mini 16x Microscope with Illuminator
review_body: I read all the reviews before purchasing this 'toy'.  It is indeed a tiny little microscope, but I was very pleasantly surprised at how well it worked.  As others have said, it is definitley not a 45X, but it does the job.  The little LED lights are very bright and perfectly illuminate my object.  I bought a jeweler's loupe and this little gem, and this baby wins.

product_title: MAGLITE XL100 LED Flashlight
review_body: Two things I noticed right away. The bottom of the flashlight has print on it to indicate which function you are using. It would be very nice if it was fluorescent / glowed in the dark. Also there is no place to put any kind of attachment cord through. Lastly to call the light be adjustable is slightly ridiculous.      Besides these over sites the light is great for the money. I am looking forward to the next revision.

product_title: Oshlun Stack Dado Set with 5/8-Inch Arbor
review_headline: Dado stack set, Oshlun, 6-in, 30-tooth carbide, 5/8" arbor
review_body: Very well machined, carbide teeth nicely finished, 5/8 inch arbor hole is slightly tight on my Craftsman table saw (as other reviewers have commented).  Well-balanced & quiet, finish of the dado cut is smooth.  Have used this only for a few cuts so far.  Very satisfied.

product_title: SHOP FOX W1690 556/702/1044 CFM Deluxe Ceiling Mounted 3 Speed Air Filter
review_body: I was glad it did not take 5-7 weeks for delivery.  i looking forward to how great it realy is, i will be doing lathe work in the spring.  So time will tell.

product_title: Milwaukee 48-00-1303 Sawzall Blade Wood 5 Teeth per Inch 12-Inch Length, 5 Pieces in 1 Pack
review_body: I purchased a package of these blades to cut down a 6\\" Oak Tree that was covered with English Ivy.  the Ivy had grown around the tree for at least 10 years and had died this last winter.  It would be impossible to remove the ivy from the tree since it had become imbedded into the trunk.  I needed the 12\\" length of the blade and it proved to be all I had hoped for a more.  I cut the tree down to the ground in two foot sections.  The tree was over twenty feet tall.  The whole job was done with one blade.  I recommend these blades highly!!!

product_title: Campbell Hausfeld 17-Piece Air Tool  and Accessory Kit (MP284701AV)
review_body: This assortment of pneumatic connectors contains most of the common fixtures that you would likely need.  The quality is uneven and the tire pressure gauge is junk (all plastic).

product_title: Apex Tool Group D550PK Soldering Gun Kit, 260/200-Watt
review_body:
If you buy this gun, take it outside the first time you use it!
Plugged it in, hit the trigger and my garage was filled with a horrible smell. Afterwards the gun will not heat up at all. You can hear it humming, but the barrels and tip produce no heat at all.
Weller was once top shelf U.S.A. made product, now it's south of the border crap.
A day later, the stink still lingers!

product_title: SE 7519SD 33-Piece Security Bit Set with Magnetic Extension Bit Holder
review_body: In this case, you get what you pay for.    Is this product very inexpensive? Yes. But that still doesn't mean that it shouldn't be lacking this much quality...    Pros:  -It seems to fit everything I've used it for, with one exception (Xbox 360 controller), but that was my fault, not the fault of the product.  -Very inexpensive    Cons:  -Some of the portions that were drilled out (so that the bits are compatible with security-type screws) are off-center, one of the holes was off-center by .52mm, according to my digital caliper. I have not had any use for that particular bit, so I cannot tell if their lack of quality control will affect the tool's ability to do their intended job.    I'm not unhappy with the product (yet), but I'm also not pleased about it either.

product_title: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools FSA8-CP Flash II Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 3.5-Inch Steel Drop Point Blade and GRN Handle, Satin Finish
review_body: This is a nice everyday knife that gives you a big 3.5\\" blade and decent-sized handle at a very light 3.1oz.  The pocket clip is a unique design that allows it to stay in your pocket inconspicuously, yet still allowing it to be removed easily.  The blade comes sharp out of the box, and has a nice full flat-ground shape.  It is also a good width and I prefer the smooth edge over a serrated combo-edge version.  SOG needs to make the black TiNi version with a straight blade, I would prefer that version.    The handle is a bit strange-looking to me, but it allows people with bigger hands to get a full grip, although it is a bit too smooth IMO.  I like the ease of the assisted-opening mechanism, but it is hard to close the knife with one hand.  The lack of a steel liner keeps the weight down and is not needed as the handle material is durable enough.    The lock is a feature I won't usually need, and I don't like that it can be accidentally activated when carried.  It would be  a useful feature if you are afraid children might get their hands on this knife somehow.    Overall, for under $50 this knife is a good choice, it isn't too bulky and is light enough to carry frequently.  This would make a good knife for outdoor use camping or backpacking, and could also be carried as a threat deterrent if needed.

product_title: Dorcy Lumen High Flux LED Cyber Light Flashlight with Alkaline Batteries
review_body: All the positive reviews are true. This flashlight is superbright. It lit the whole room during blackout and now I can see everything in my attic. Great product for the money.

product_title: Racor Pro Folding Bike Rack
review_headline: well made and easily worth the money
review_body:
I only have one bike but like the option of adding another. This is a nice unit that is easy to install and works great. Love that you can tuck it flat if not in use (like winter time).

Man! i just saw this rack which may be even better because of the bsket.
[...]

product_title: Fastback Flip Utility Knife
review_body: What a handy household tool.  I use it around the house -- not in a professional capacity -- and have found it very convenient and useful.  It does flip open quickly as advertised, although that feature is not really all that important to me.  It's bigger than I thought it would be and a good thing about that is that it's less likely to get lost in the \\"junk drawer\\" or elsewhere.  My favorite use for this utility knife is opening boxes -- this tool works a lot better than regular box cutters.

product_title: DREMEL 7134 5/64" Diamond Whl Pt.,
review_body: Ordered five of these to bore some holes in some rocks.  I wanted the holes to be just about the size of the diamond tip on these bits, but they just couldn't cut the stone.  Might work better on other materials, but on rock I had two of them break off in the hole while I was drill, and the little pieces of bit got so wedged into the rock I had to grind them out too.  At least they were only a buck each.  I've found the 1/8 inch ace brand hammer masonry drill bits to be more effective, but not fun to use.

product_title: Stanley Consumer Tools 15-579 15-Inch Plastic-Handle Hand Saw

review_body: I bought this sander to replace my old orbital sander.  The vibration was so great that I had difficulty keeping it on the wood.  Returned it after only my second time trying to use it.

product_title: 25pc Plastic Razor Blades Non-Scratch Scraping Sticker Label Removal
review_headline: Good as you can get for plastic
review_body: Our business has been using plastic scrapers (for kitchen stoneware) to remove stickers from used laptops/electronics for over 6 years.  Some of the stickers are designed to break apart when being removed (for security).  With these new sticker issues we decided to try out some actual razors. review_body: This riser kit is something I have wanted for a long time, but I was not sure it would be simple to install. Had my wife help with removing the top part of the saw.  While adding the riser block I saw that it attached with 4 roll pins which really helped to keep it level.  It took about 1/2 hour to change out the bolts, but about  1 hour to make everything was lined up and level.  Very easy to install and very stable, but make sure you take the time to tweek everything on the saw or the blade will bind.

product_title: Streamlight 88032 ProTac 1AA High Performance Alkaline Flashlight with White LED, Black
review_body: So far I've purchased two of these flashlights.  They work as advertised.  The features that stand out from the rest is the light throw in a pitch black room from a 1 AA battery operated light. It's amazing how much light comes from one AA, which are pretty cheap to replace.  It comes with a Velcro flapped holster that can sit on a belt or you can carry in the same pocket as a cell phone without worrying about scratches from it's aluminum build.  Overall it's compact and powerful.  If you are looking for something light and easy to carry daily get this light.  I switched from a Surefire 6P Defender LED to this.  I have yet to take it to the range to see how it withstands 9mm, .40 S&W, or .45 ACP recoil. Considering it's LED there should be no issues with the bulb, just have to do a range test on the electronics and housing.

product_title: Johnson Level & Tool and Tool 700 Magnetic Angle Locator
review_body: I've had magnetic levels before, but they always broke.  I'll be more careful of this one, although it seems much better built.  These are almost indispensable, allways the right tool for those special jobs.  I use mine to make sure my satellite dish is set up perfectly level.  I take my tv with me when I go camping and this makes setup a breeze.

product_title: Hitachi Framing Nailer and Brad Nailer Combo Kit
review_body: If you've ever pulled your baseboards off, you know what a joy it can be to tac nail them back into place without marring the surface.  This inexpensive little gadget really cuts down on the time, frustration, and cost of repairing or replacing damaged baseboards (when installing them.)    The Hitachi is a 5/8\\" to 2\\" pneumatic (compressed air) powered nailer.  It will require a small air compressor of some kind, but just about any light duty pancake compressor should be more than enough to power it.  It takes readily available strait-collated brad nails.  It's simple side load design.  The trigger is simple and has a short enough stroke to be practical.  I have not had a jam yet but clearing it seems simple enough.  There is a pressure activated safety just like on the large commercial roofing and framing nailers that prevent firing unless the head makes contact with a surface.  It's small and light enough to be a terrific project or furniture nailer.  Small boxes are a breeze to assemble.  I'm VERY impressed with this little nailer!    Out of the box it comes with an attached standard size M-type / industrial style quick-disconnect male air coupler.  You will need some pneumatic tool oil.  The instructions say add 5 to 10 drops thru the hole in the coupler before each days use.  (Twice a day if it's heavy usage.)    Update: 9-20-2011  I had an issue with a leaking back porch roof.  I was able to use this nailer as well as some cheap furring strips to temporarly tac a tarp over the roof until I get it repaired.  It's worked well.  The burst (AKA bump fire) mode worked flawlessly...  Everytime I touch this nailer I find another use.  I couldn't be happier with this purchase!

product_title: Mechanix Wear CG Leather Impact Pro
review_body: I bought these for my wife as I have a pair and they are the best protection glove I have found. My wife loves them. We have been clearing some trees and brush around our place. She stated that out of all the gloves she used  these worked the best.  We highly recommend them.

product_title: Leatherman 70202003K Juice S2 Pocket Multi-Tool, Flame Orange
review_body: I love this leatherman!  I lost my first one, after several years, and promptly bought the exact same one again. Other than that minor irritation, the meter functionality is awesome.

product_title: GearWrench 85051 3/8-Inch Drive Micrometer Torque Wrench 25-250 in lb
review_headline: Well-made (in the USA!), well-designed torque wrench
review_body: I've always favored Precision Instruments for torque wrenches; unfortunately in this torque range their only offering is 1/4\\" drive which is useless for my application (I own 3/8\\" and 1/2\\" drive sockets only).  Previously used the Craftsman offering in this range which eventually failed, much as I suspected it would, at the plastic locking ring.  Rather than throw good money after bad, I thought I'd try my luck with GearWrench, since I am extremely happy with their ratchet sets.  My concerns - it's not easy to figure out where the wrench is made (in the USA), or what the locking ring is made of (metal).  Having received and used the wrench, my concerns were laid to rest - the wrench is well made, with a sturdy metal locking ring and the micrometer adjuster has a nice detent.  The low-profile head in particular is extremely nice; there were places in my Subaru engine bay where I had to go through all sorts of theatrics to get the Craftsman wrench to fit - easy in-and-out with this wrench.  Of course, calibration is spot on.  Extremely happy with this purchase!

product_title: Howard Leight MAX-1 Foam Ear Plugs Uncorded, 20 Piece
review_body: These plugs are AMAZING!  I have used them for riding, shooting, loud auto work, and they drown out the sound for EVERYTHING!  I read reviews on other sites about people complaining how they are uncomfortable for people with smaller ear canals, but they seem to work fine for me.  They are made of a really soft compound, so when they do expand to fill the ear canal, it fills everything and does not over-expand.  I suggest going on Howard Leight's website and watching the video on how to insert them.  I actually learned a thing or two.  Overall, GREAT product.

product_title: Dorcy Lumen High Flux LED Cyber Light Flashlight with Alkaline Batteries
review_body: After dealing with a mediocre Maglite for the past few years, I wanted something *brighter*...  My dad has a small LED flashlight that I found to be superior, as far as brightness goes, so I jumped on Amazon and started checking reviews of LED flashlights.    The Dorcy 41-4750 was ranked #1, so I started reading the reviews...so far, so good... I compared it to several other flashlights in the same category and after seeing how expensive they were, I figured that I would go with the Dorcy, despite never having heard the brand name before. (Spare me, flashlight enthusiasts!)    Once I received my flashlight in the mail, I had mixed feelings.  Overall, I was excited to be holding a flashlight with such high regard; however, I was a bit disappointed with how dinky it felt in my hand.  I suppose I was used to my \\"nine pound\\" 4D Maglite ([[ASIN:B00002N6SI MAGLITE S4D016 Heavy-Duty 4-D Cell Flashlight, Black]]), but this Dorcy felt somewhat delicate, like I might break it somehow.  My worries were soon laid to rest as I inserted the 4 AA batteries and turned this sucker on for the first time.    OMG.    While I'm sure there are brighter flashlights out there, I was blown away.  This thing puts out an incredible amount of clean light!  I was head over heels in love.      Now, it seems as if I have two issues: 1) I want to order a second one to keep in my truck (in case my headlights go out, of course) and 2) it has a knack for pointing out how much dust I have coating my house when I shine into nooks and crannies.    All in all, the Dorcy 41-4750 was a fantastic purchase and I have been showing it off to all of my friends and family (all the while blinding them for fun).  While I may not be able to knock anyone out with this flashlight, it is a wonderful product and I would highly recommend it for anyone!

product_title: JET 708620B AFS-1000B 550/702/1044 CFM 3-Speed Air Filtration System with Remote and Electrostatic Pre-Filter
review_body: I'm thoroughly satisfied with this Jet Air Filter.  My shop is 30 by 40 feet with open ceiling joists, so there is a large volume of air for this unit to handle.  Hanging it was simple - my joists are 4 ft. on center so I just nailed up 4 joist hangers,cut two 2X4s to fit, bolted the unit to the 2X4s with lag screws, and dropped it in place. I was pleasantly surprised at how complete the package is. All kinds of hardware for installing the unit are included, even batteries for the remote.  There's also a Velcro sticky pad setup for mounting the remote.  My filter is relatively quiet, certainly no louder than a hand sander, and exhibits no vibration at any speed.  Other reviewers expressed problems with interference from fluorescent lamps but my filter is unaffected by these fixtures.  I like being able to set the timer and leave the shop.  And yes, the air stays much cleaner.  As others have said, I should have gotten one of these years ago.  It rates a solid 5 stars in my book.  I shopped around and couldn't find as good a deal as Amazon anywhere.

review_body: These are a great buy, and serve the purpose well. Maybe it's meant to be this way, but there's not much volume range for an aux device. (Obviously you can use the volume on the aux device, but it doesn't seem to allow much increase.)  However, these are priced great and do serve well on the range. Props to the Nutnfancy Project (TNP) on YouTube for the excellent review of these, that's why I made this purchase.

review_body: The screwdriver worked perfect for my pentalobe screws on the Verizon iphone 4. You will need to buy a flat head and phillips screwdriver also; they are available at Walmart for $1.50 at the optical place. Hope this helps!! Shipping was also very fast!!

product_title: Freud LU96R006M20 160mm Thin Kerf Rip Saw Blade for Ultimate Performance on All Track Saws
review_body: If anyone out there is looking for a blade to cut melamine laminate, this one is the way to go. I used this blade to make several   base cabinets for two bathroom projects using double sided melamine laminated chip board. The performance was excellent as advertised.   Absolutely zero chipping on either the top or bottom surface. I did make and use a new zero clearance insert for my table saw, which  I think is the only way to get maximum performance from this blade. The blade did show some signs of slowing down after cutting up (10)  2' x 8' sheets, but still performed flawlessly. As for dados, I cut right & left sides of the slot to depth with this blade and then   used my stacked dado set to finish them up. Again, no chipping whatsoever. Incredible blade for a specific purpose. I will save this   blade to cut laminates only and nothing else. It can also be used to cut plywood with great results ( I tried several test cuts just  to check performance ). A little pricey, but worth it if you need chipp free cutting of laminated chip board or plywood.

product_title: Maglite Mini Maglite AA LED Flashlight
review_headline: Best American Flashlight I have found.
review_body: If you ever laughed when you heard \\"vote early, vote often\\" then you haven't figured out that the most important vote you cast is with your dollars. Personally I'd be embarrassed to tell you I knew how Chinese or foreign crap performed. I do know I use this light to inspect welds inside of pipe before the root is finished.  We have to be able to identify anomolies and fix em before the X-ray sees em and sends a welder home.  I need the brightest most focused beam I can find. I need it to stand up to a terrific beating in terrible conditions too. I must have got all the good ones because these, with their 3 Watts of lumens, have become my favorite.  I've spent the last couple hours stocking up and sending them out as gifts. A US made Leatherman, Kershaw Leek, and Buck 120 are the only knives I've ever felt good enough about to give regularly as gifts. Now I am busy handing out Maglite flashlights. Kershaw in my pocket, a Buck on my hip in the field, a Randall next to my Ruger on the night stand, a Remington with Leupold and Burris glass, Maglite to shine light on the subject, Redwings or New Balance on my feet, Filson everywhere else anda Union built Ford to carry my carcass around in. review_headline: User for twenty years; it's great...
review_body: Whoever puts this tool down doesn't know what they're talking about. It's not a sexy piece of equipment, but as an old work electrician, I use this tool on at least 50% of the jobs I go to. On old wood lath, The thin kerf blades have the ability to cut quickly and precisely without shaking everything apart. I can cut drywall in such a way that the cut out part makes a tight patch which is easy to spackle back in. With a little patience this rugged little tool can do quite a bit of magic. I like this tool so much I bought a back-up about ten years ago, but it's so rugged I still haven't had to retrieve it from storage. Care does have to be used with the metal blades since they are quite hard and brittle and will snap rather easily, but cutting bolts, conduit and such is really facilitated by this tool.

review_body:
I purchased this box and it took 5 weeks to ship. Finally when it did ship, the only information I saw was that it came from Phoenix Arizona. I was excited to finally receive it. But when it was delivered, the box was damaged. Total waste of money and time. Thanks for nothing, lame shipping company. Although after seeing the box in person, I admit it is nice. The top mat was foam not rubber. The drawers and finish looked really great and the trim was stunning. Not a bad box. Just a huge disappointment.
I received my second box in black instead of blue. Regret that decision already. I prefer blue it looks nicer. The box feels decent as far as structure and strength. The castors feel like plastic and the stops are rather flimsy. The sides appear single walled and the box does have trim. The trim is silver and contrasts nicely with the black but it's also just a thin 90 degree piece of metal along the front corners of the box. The drawers feel wobbly when loaded. The detents on the drawers are nice. Hold really well. The drawer liners are just thin foam sheets. I replaced it with premium liners. The handle just bolts to the wall, no threads or bolt hole supports. The same with the castor bolt holes. I expected the holes for the castors to be stronger.
The top wide width drawer has a support that goes horizontal the full width of the drawer. Instead of a support that divides the drawer vertically, it's like a bump in the drawer at least 3 inch strip of metal in the middle of the drawer. Kind of a bad design. But the drawer holds all my sockets, sledges, long prybars,and breaker bars. So I made it work well for me. The drawer trim does not have any securements like griplatch or other systems.
At least it's a bigger box for me, holds all my tools with minor room for expansion and cost less than $1000! All other boxes this size sell for much more. If I keep the box stationary as much as possible, it should last long. I question the longevity if it will be moved around a shop often. I have my Matco MSC12 for that so I'm good.a shop often. I have my Matco MSC12 for that so I'm good.

review_body: I've had this for 2-1/2 years. At first it seemed to compare well to two other humidity sensors I had. Over time the humidity reading has drifted downward, and it now reads about 15% low compared to the other sensors. product_title: Shop-Vac 5840500 5-Gallon 2.0-Peak HP Wet/Dry Vacuum
review_body: Bought this vac at Walmart 6 years ago for use in my garage. I had some concerns over durability when I purchased it. I kept thinking there was no way it would last but I have definitely got return on investment with it.     I have done major home revisions and in all of them this vac was used for cleaning up excessive amounts of dry wall, tile and wood dust. I rebuilt 15 X 12 X 10 foot wall in my living room, put down 700 feet of wood flooring, building a custom queen size Murphy bed frame, routered trim out of oak planks for a 10 X 10 room, cut tile for 100 sq feet of floor and countertop. Most recently I sucked three or four cups of dirt out of the under ground piping connected to my down spout and vacuumed drywall dust left during construction of a 15 x 15 room.     Two problems with this product....   1) The filter it comes with is crap. If you intend to push its limits you will need to buy one or two of the high quality washable cartridge filters and throw out the crappy filter it is packaged with.   2) Its suction is not that strong so you could never use it as a replacement to your standard in-home vacuum. Consider what your expectation for the product are before you buy it. If you use it like I have used it, you are sucking up huge chunks of dirt and if using it in your house you will run the in home vac after the 'big' dirt piles have been removed by this vac. If I was using a standard in home vac for projects mentioed above I would be dealing with clogged filters, dumping the dirt reservoir or replacing bags constantly.    I noticed multiple reviews state they had problems within a month or two.  This makes me think I was incrediably  lucky with my purchase. If you don't get a lemon when you buy this vac, it will work and if your experience is anything like mine it will exceed your expectations.

product_title: DEWALT DC822KL 18-Volt 1/2-inch Lithium Ion Cordless Impact Wrench with NANO Technology
review_body: Just added the impact driver to my stable of DeWalt cordless tools.    I'm glad they've finally got their Lithium line in production.    I was afraid I would have to switch brands to get the better batteries.    They have designed their products to use the same battery in the older as   well as the new tools which means you won't have to carry two types of   chargers and two types of batteries when the older NiMH batteries die.    Just update your batteries to the Lithium and use the older tools.

review_body: Plenty of light in the single LED mode and even brighter than I expected as you go up. Great for nights outdoors or working on repairs and hobby items on the workbench.

product_title: Dustless Technologies 16006 HEPA Wet/Dry Vacuum
review_body:
This 16-gallon wet/dry vac is a powerhouse with a 5 horsepower, 10.6 amp motor that can vacuum a sizable area without having to lug or drag the thing around. The 12 foot hose's thickness of 1 1/2 inches means this thing can suck up some pretty big items, including a few you might not want to vacuum (make sure your watch is firmly attached to your wrist, lest it get sucked into the hose). Of course, if it does get sucked in, you could just root around inside the canister for it, though I would recommend wearing a mask while doing that.

It contains a HEPA filter designed to capture particles as big as .3 microns. A micron, or micrometer is 1/1000 of a millimeter. In more standard terms, that's 0.0003 millimeters. In other words, very, very tiny, an item that most likely cannot be seen with the naked eye.

That's all well and good, as most people tend to aim the hose at items they can see such as dirt or sawdust, so it's good to find a workshop vacuum cleaner that can suck up things you can't see, but could still be breathed in and possibly cause lung problems later in life.

This is a \\"wet/dry\\" vacuum, meaning that it can vacuum things that are wet or dry, and can switch between the two without stopping. That's where I draw the line. I don't have anything wet I need to vacuum, and I wouldn't want to mix sawdust with something wet (I can't think of anything other than wet leaves, but why you'd want to vacuum those is beyond me). The other thing I don't like about that is I'd be afraid of not knowing the power cord has a small fray in it and getting it in water.

At the very least, the vacuum might be toast or the fuse box might get burned, but at the very worst, I'd be a crispy critter.

Of course, my personal fears are no fault of this vacuum cleaner's.

Above all though, this vacuum cleaner is quiet and can vacuum 40 pounds of dust and debris in its sixteen gallon canister. However, I never let it get thatfull before disposing it of its contents. The power cord itself is 15 feet long, add to that the 12 feet of its hose and it has an effective range of 27 feet and that's not even adding the extended range an extension cord would yield.

product_title: Milwaukee 2615-21 M18 Cordless Right Angle Drill Kit, 1xC Battery
review_body: M 18 Cordless 3/8 right angle  drill     I never owned or used a right angle drill until this month. I probably though I would use it once or twice therefore it wasn't worth the money.     After using the M18 drill I found out that I was wrong on a my prior assumptions.  I had to drill some holes in the cross? beams in my home so I could run coax for the tv  in my basement. Using a conventional electric drill to make straight holes in a tight space is difficult at best.  With the M-18 right angle drill  I merely charged up the battery and started drilling holes. The drill made short work of it.      The drill weighs 2.75 lbs and  feels top heavy but that is the nature of a right angle drill. The gearing and head are only 2 inches apart unlike a conventional drill. I look forward to using this drill in many other ways. I  can attach an  adapter and a socket and then be able to get hard to reach nuts unscrewed.   Other non right angle  cordless tools can't do this because of their design     If you have no preference concerning the manufacturer  of  a right angle drill, this might be the drill for you to purchase. Milwaukee Electric tool Corporation  has come up with a rechargeable battery called the M18. The  M18 is a 18 volt battery which is used in Milwaukee cordless tool line.  The M18  is a Lithium-ion which will last a long time in use. There is a fuel gauge on the charger that l tells you how much power you have left. The battery will work at temperatures of 14 degrees Fahrenheit which  is pretty cold.     The drill retails for $ 368.00  with battery and charger.

product_title: Bradford White MI5036FBN-337 50 Gallon Natural Gas Water Heater
review_body: As a licensed master plumber and mechanical contractor , I can attest to Bradford White's dependability and quality.  Out of 274 Hot water heater service calls for 2010 only 2 were bradford white, and the one that needed replacing was over 20 years old. I work with A.O. smith,American, State ,Bradford White, Rheem, Mor-flo, G-E, Ruud, Lochinvar ( made by Bradford white) and maytag. After 20 years in the business, I recommend Bradford White . If you have bad water conditions(i.e. well water with high mineral content-dissolved solids), its important to maintain the sacrificial anode rod on any heater or they will see a short life. I've never replaced a well maintained heater before it was due. Made in Michigan and the only heater made in the USA, not just assembled here.

product_title: Mirka Bulldog Gold 5-Inch 8-Hole 60 Grit Grip Vacuum Discs
review_body: I recently refinished my dining room floor.  The floor had a dark stain and finish over oak.  I wanted to see the wood and grain so I decided to sand and refinish with polyurethane.  I used a large orbital sander on a floor in my last house and I wrecked my floor so I decided to use my hand belt sander and hand orbital sander and refinish this floor the hard way. review_body: I use my Dremel Multi-Max quite often.  It has never failed me and I have used it for home maintenance, craft and art work and even for some minor auto body work.

product_title: Atlas Nitrile Tough Assembly Grip 370 Work Gloves
review_headline: A Very Good General Purpose Work Glove...
review_body:
I've been buying these from my local ACE Hardware for the past couple of years, after seeing one of my contractors wearing something similar.

These are great all-around gloves -- sufficiently warm on cold days, but not uncomfortable on cool days. Durable enough for most tasks such as electrical work, yard work, framing, painting, tiling, plumbing. In fact, the only tasks I purposely don't use them for are soldering copper pipe with an open flame, and heavy lifting abrasive items such as paving stones and cinder blocks. I've even used worn out Atlas gloves for hand-digging in the dirt, though beware that this quickly eats away at the fingertips.

The back is a medium weight mesh that is clingy and breathable. The palm is a medium weight plastic nitrile coating that is very durable. The cuff is heavier than the fabric at the back of the hand, and heavily elasticized. Mine typically fail at the upper knuckle, but usually only after lots of use and some abuse.

I typically bounce between large and extra large gloves, and the Atlas XLs are my preferred choice, though I have fit comfortably into their Larges previously (large fits me, but the fingers are a bit too short). There's a bit of room for error here because the gloves are so elastic.

In a nutshell, these are good to have in all temps and for most work conditions, much more comfortable but not as durable as leather, though a good bargain (especially in bulk here on Amazon).

product_title: Bosch 1617EVSPK 2.25 Horse Power Plunge & Fixed-Base Electronic Router Pack,
review_headline: Great tool for me the Beginner Woodworker
review_body:
This is my first router I have ever owned so I have no frame of reference. However, this router so far has been great. I used it to make round edge spindels for my daughters bunk bed. It felt very balanced in my hands and comfortable for the 6+ hours of routing I needed to do. The speed settings go up to 6 but I only needed it at 3 to make my cuts. It has plenty of power.

The directions are great and easy to understand for a complete beginner like myself. Pictures and text really help out.

The look and feel of this router is very good. It looks very well made and not some piece of plastic garbage that is going to fall apart at any moment.

I highly recommend the edge guide that can be purchsed for this unit. It was very helpful.

So far no downsides from the times I have used it. Routing makes a TON of sawdust. Dont use this inside without some sort of dust management system.

product_title: Apprentice ACS10L 7-1/4-Inch Circular Saw with Laser Guide
review_body: I purchased this product from Kent Building supplies last summer. I am a woman in my late-30's and am always doing odd jobs around the house.  Little things such as cutting 2x4's, or light-weight panel board that neighbours have passed on to use as firewood when we go camping.  The weight f the saw seemed right for me; it was comfortable compared to some of the others, and it was reasonably priced (I believe it was around $49).      Two weeks ago while using the saw to cut 2x4's, it broke into two pieces- luckily all pieces remained attached at either side of the blade area rather than fly into someone's face who was working around the yard. I didn't even realize what had happened at first until I pressed the button again and nothing happened.       When relaying this story to my father, a seasoned woodworker and carpenter, he thought I was joking.  In fact, a Fisher Price saw would be hard-pressed to break in two!  The saw has been used very lightly used; in fact, it still has the sticker on it, although now sliced in two.      When I went to Kent to see about replacing it, they no longer carry this brand. Now, there is something else in its' place, which, if I had to guess after this experience, has probably taken the Apprentice's place as a rookie on the shelf!!!  I am going to talk to Kent again because no one else carries this product either, that I am aware of, and my receipt is dated for over a year ago. I was unable to pursue many projects last summer due to a serious neck injury at the time.    I am trying to find out the name of the actual manufacturer.  If I had it to do all over again, I would likely spend the additional $50 and buy a brand that is well-known such as the Black & Decker saw.

product_title: Wiha 26199 Slotted and Phillips Screwdriver Set in Rugged Canvas Pouch, 8 Piece
review_body: I have been repairing computers for some time and I have found no drivers more comfortable than these. Some days I will do a good 2 hours of screw turning total and I will use only Wiha drivers when I can. I have never had any wiha screwdriver break on me except for the 1mm slotted, those can be fragile depending on your application.     BUY THIS KIT WITH CONFIDENCE, you will not regret investing in these screwdrivers, they will probably be the last you ever need to buy.     The canvas pouch is a nice touch, keeps them safe in the tool box, this feature is not pictured, but the pouch has an internal flap that protects the heads of the drivers.

review_body: Great kit it's easy to use I would recomend this product to any one interested in doing inlays or designs.

review_body: This compass is \\"Just Adequate\\" for use.  It's a Plastic Compass, but what can you expect for the price. All of the Lensatic Compasses I've seen, owned and used are much sturdier and housed in metal.  I'll be using this ONLY in my Emergency Kit.

product_title: Brinkmann 800-2250-0 MaxFire Marine Dual Xenon Spotlight
review_headline: Charge lasts about 30 minutes!  Arghhh! -- UPDATE Dec 16 2010

product_title: Niji Roll Multi-purpose Pouch
review_body: Somewhat disappointing. Strap is vinyl rather than leather and has a single snap fastener so no adjustment to cinch up the roll. product_title: P3 International P4480 Kill A Watt Electricity Usage Monitor with Electronic Graphic Timer
review_headline: Quality Control could use some work
review_body: Purchased this from Amazon when it was a gold box special.  Works well, does what it says.  If it wasn't on sale, you'd probably be better off with the base model as this units only adds a highly programmable on/off timer.    Knocked off a star for what I imagine is a quality control issue.  Item came in Amazon's \\"frustration free\\" packaging, so just the unit and the instructions, no packaging.  I can't tell if this was a refurb or not, but the item description did not indicate that.  The unit was missing one of the four case screws, and there was something rattling inside.  After taking it apart, I found it was a large piece of solder floating around in the unit.  Glad I decided to investigate before plugging it in and risking a short.  As i said, i have no idea if this was a refurbished unit, but with the missing screw and loose solder piece, I imagine it is.

product_title: Dremel 100-N/7 Single Speed Rotary Tool Kit with 7 Accessories
review_body: It wasn't a Dremel 300(commonly used in computer modding) but this tool can get the job done! =) It didn't have too many accessories(cutting disks,sander, etc) to actually perfectly mold my computer case, but luckily, I bought those re-enforced cutting disks and everything worked out fine.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE C2002 Oil-Free UMC Pancake Compressor
review_body:
Bought this compressor for use with my water well. It uses the compressor activated by a water level switch to force air out of the ground and into a settling tank.

I have had it almost a year now and it has worked well. Since it is out of sight I like that I don't have to remember to check the oil. I also like having the two couplers so that I can connect another hose to it without disconnecting it from the well.

I probably should have bought one with a little larger tank but this one has performed very well.

product_title: Nite Ize Clip-On Flashlight Holster with Stretch Capability and 8-Position Rotating Clip - Durable Nylon Flashlight Holster for Belt Attachment with Full 360 Degree Rotation
review_body: Yes it is very tight at 1st. I am using this for a small 1\\" diameter flashlight and after a couple days the holster conformed to the flashlight and now fits in good yet still holds. Yes its an open top design but the before mentioned dust and rain shouldnt matter if your using a decent quality flashlight. I wear this 5-6 days a week and have had no real issues. product_title: Everlast MT1280D 12" Miter Saw Blade
review_body: This is an excellent blade with a great price tag.  I have put it through its paces on my miter saw and it cuts hard and soft woods cleanly and cuts prefinished mouldings with no tear out front or back.  The large industrial style carbide will allow for many sharpenings unlike the teeth on most comparably priced blades.  I will be purchasing a couple more to add to the blade rotation.     Update. I still think this is a good blade after a few years of use but have found that it can deflect pretty badly on more demanding cuts. product_title: DEWALT DCD710S2 12-Volt Max 3/8-Inch Drill Driver Kit
review_headline: The 18v line gives a much better value and is a higher quality tool
review_body:
I use a lot of power tools, and own a bunch of the Dewalt 18v tools. This is a drill/driver from their 12v line. It is a lightweight version of their 18v tools. All said, I would stick with the 18v tools unless there were a very good deal on these 12v tools. I compared this with the [[ASIN:B00008WFT3 DEWALT DC759KA Heavy-Duty 18-Volt Ni-Cad 1/2-Inch Cordless Drill/Driver Kit]] I own. (Please be sure to see the photo comparison I also loaded onto this product.)

The only advantages of the 12v over the 18v are: (1) the 12v includes a light at the end, (2) it is much lighter and smaller (which could be good when doing a lot of work overhead); and (3) the 12v has a better rubber grip.

The 18v version is superior in every other aspect. The 12v has a plastic chuck where the 18v is metal. With a full charge they both seem to have about the same power, but after a few minutes of use the 12v gets noticeably weaker. The 18v version has a little clip holder for your driver bits on the base of the grip - this is noticeably absent from the 12v version (and will be sorely missed).

I did notice that the 12v uses a li-ion battery (instead of the ni-cad used in my 18v tools). (and it comes with two of them.) However, I have never really noticed any problem with the 18v batteries, and they now sell [[ASIN:B000YIDD1Q DeWalt DC9180-2-C (2) 18V NANO Lithium-Ion Batteries w/ DC9310 7.2V - 18V Ni-Cd / Ni-MH / NANO Lithium-Ion 1-Hour Battery Charger]]that are interchangeable if you need to replace.

I don't really mean to knock this tool. It is probably fine for most light use do it yourself-ers, but I think the 18v line represents a higher quality tool, for a comparable price. (The 18v tools also can be found in many combo packs that end up being an unbelievable deal - if you actually need everything in the package.) You are buying into a system, and the 18v tools are a well-developed line that are favored by most professionals.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE PCL120CRC-2 12-Volt MAX ClampSaw
review_headline: Possibly limited usefulness, but dang handy in a pinch!
review_body:
I bought this saw on a whim the day after discovering it online, while trying to find a way to hack out a section of 1½ inch copper pipe. I needed to add a Tee fitting to this existing copper vent line, right below the top plate of the wall and in a space cramped with plywood sheeting, a nearby stud, and a 4\\" cast iron drain line. There was no way I was going to get a standard pipe cutter or a full sized saw in there.

As it was, this clamp saw barely made it. The saw body is over 2\\" wide at the \\"grip\\" portion just behind the blade. And although the clamp portion is adjustable, the shoe (the piece that sits between the blade and the saw body), is NOT adjustable like it is on a conventional reciprocating saw. This means that the blade extends beyond the clamp (or outer shoe), the distance being variable on how close in I have the clamp set to the body (i.e. adjusted for smaller pipes means a greater amount of blade extension).

No matter, thanks to the 3-position rotating handle (straight like the Amazon photo shows, or at 90° like a drill) I was able to get into the workspace and make very clean cuts, with only minor interference with the plywood sheeting. The variable speed trigger is sensitive enough to stroke the blade and set it in a fully-extended position before beginning, just for my own reference with respect to the other materials that were at risk of interfering with my cut; however, it also serves as an indicator as to how strong the motor is (or isn't) when starting with the blade already in a partial cut, starting slowly with a soft squeeze, and noticing how little resistance it takes to bog this saw down to a halt.

The Clamp Saw comes with two very tiny 12v batteries and a charger, plus a soft carrying bag, and two blades. The blades lock in and lock out with a half twist of a toolless spring-loaded collet, and will install either blade up or blade down. The Lithium Ion batteries must leave the factory charged, because both of mine completed charging within minutes of plugging them into the charger, and even the full charging time is claimed to be only 30 minutes. I'm stoked these are Li-Ion, because they ought to have awesome shelf-life, unlike my army of 18v Ryobi NiCads that become \\"stale\\" within a day or two of charging.

Despite this saw's size, it's deceivingly hefty, and not exactly \\"balanced\\" like you might be accustom to with a similarly sized cordless drill -- mainly (I think) because the super-light battery in the grip means all the weight is concentrated in the body. No matter, as it is designed to allow two-handed operation, similar to a full sized recip saw.

The small batteries are also small in capacity. Cutting a little bit of copper, but mostly 1-1/2\\" ABS pipe, gets me maybe a dozen cuts. As the battery depletes, the saw's speed slows noticeably, until it finally gives a few strokes then stops with each trigger squeeze. I can't really find a fault with this, since the trade-off is the small size and light weight of the battery packs. Plus with two batteries included, and the quick 30 minute charging time, it hasn't really slowed me down.

A couple of nits to pick:
- The trigger lock is an on or off affair, just like the door lock in your car. So I can unlock it and it'll stay in that position. Now far be it from me to complain about something like this that many users would probably look at as a blessing after dealing with so called \\"idiot proof\\" trigger locks on other power tools, but the problem is the \\"button\\" (switch?) that releases the pivoting handle: it's in a position that I accidentally squeeze the trigger when reseting the handle position, and I certainly don't want the saw sawing while I'm holding it sideways futzing with it.
- The LED light only comes on when the trigger is squeezed, and goes off as soon as it is released. And that's unfortunate, because it's a very bright and useful light. But I think you'llagree with me that most of the time we want to see our workpiece and line our blade up on our cut mark *before* we squeeze the trigger, yes? Some sort of time-delay off feature would make this light more useful.
- The clamp requires the use of an allen wrench to adjust. The allen wrench has a holder built into the body of the saw, so presumably it'll always be right where you need it when the time comes (yeah, right!!) but honestly, looking at this setup, a thumb screw would have been really easy to implement here.
- The trigger pinches and holds my nitrile-coated gloves when I release. These are the common tight-fitting, rubberized palm work gloves, not ones that are loose fitting.

All in all, I'm pleased enough with this tool that I'm looking at other 12v Porter Cable tools I can share these batteries with. So far, it appears only a compact drill and impact driver are offered, either individually or as a [[ASIN:B0045JK3GI 2-Tool Kit]]. This might be a worthwhile backup to my full-sized, 18v Ryobi gear just due to size and the long shelf-life Li-Ion batteries. However, as convenient as this clamp saw is, it's no replacement for a full sized recip saw, and certainly will have limited usefulness due in part to battery capacity, motor strength, blade size, and stroke.orkpiece and line our blade up on our cut mark *before* we squeeze the trigger, yes? product_title: Makita 193379-7 Router Dust Nozzle (RD/RF/RP 1100/1101 Series)
review_headline: A costly attachment for what is (not) included, but effective
review_body: I have a makeshift woodworking shop in my basement and sawdust - especially MDF dust - must be kept to a minimum. After a job in which I had to cut dados on a piece of MDF, the router kicked the dust all over the room, traveled even further into the next room and I spent the better portion of the afternoon vacuuming everything once, then twice (for further settling dust).    So I decided to buy this dust attachment to see if it would improve things. First off the bat, I think this item is overpriced at [...] (Amazon), let alone the [...] list price. It's a simple piece of plastic with no box (other than the shipping one) and like the previous reviewer said, no mounting screw is attached. I had to find something at the hardware store and cut it down to length appropriately with a Dremel.    In addition, the dust nozzle on this attachment was too small for my Shopvac. Fortunately I had a universal adapter sitting around which fit fine, except it still was too loose in the slot. Some painter's tape around the adapter hose solved this problem. For the price, I feel some attachments should be included.    But all that aside, does the dust attachment do it's job? Quite well, actually. The piece fits onto the router easily and provided you can find a compatible mounting screw, you'll be good to go. The dust collection is a little less effective when routing the side of a piece with an open air exposed end (such as flushing edges) but still manages to grab at least half of the created dust.    When it comes to routing things like dados and mortises, the dust attachment really does it's job. I replaced the standard subbase with a square piece of acrylic plastic (for support), and this is also effective at holding the dust down, giving it little else to go than right up into the vacuum. Other than the bit of dust that escaped when routing through the ends, hardly any MDF dust got past my workpiece and my basement remained clean, little vacumming or cleanup required.    So inthat regard, the price is worth it. However, I feel this attachment should be no more than [...], and I'd go so far to say that I think it should have been included with the router in the first place. One star down for lack of mounting screw and another for being mispriced, but I still do recommend this for any Makita router owner.

product_title: Bosch 1587AVSP-1 5 Amp Top-Handle Jig Saw Kit with Bonus Blades
review_body:
Don't buy this out-dated discontinued jigsaw.

Someone must of bought out the entire stock of Bosch discontinued jigsaw at a bargain and now wish to unload them on the unsuspecting consumer. The new ones have a large lever located at the front of the jigsaw for quick release. The older model requires you to squeeze your finger into the tool's housing to flip a tiny lever to release the blade. The obvious inconvenience and awkwardness of the older blade-change system gave way to the ergonomic one found in the newer models. Apparently, almost all jigsaw makers are adopting the front-lever blade release design with a big lever. Porter Cable has a jigsaw with a large bright red lever that releases the blade when you pull up on the lever. Bosch, and others employ the horizontal sliding lever mechanism.

Scam artists often give rosy tool reports in order induce sales. They are shills.
