The CK1 kit which includes 4 large nuts without the locking pins comes with no washers at all. Someone didn't think those kits through properly. I would have included small washers with the small nuts and large washers with the large nuts and added more threads to the nuts to compensate for the thickness of the washer.

If you don't have a set of hole saws with these adapters I'd recommend buying a complete Bosch set that does rather than select a favorite brand of hole saws and try to adapt them to this quick change system.

product_title: Trend CE/127635 Router Collet Extension, 1/4-Inch Shank
review_body: specs are misleading.    Says 1/4 in. shank, but picture shows 1/2 in. shank.  Better said, it is an estension for a 1/2 in.collet that receives 1/4 in. bits whose shank is 1/4 in.

product_title: HERCULES HOOK WALL HANGER
review_body: A friend introduced me to this product. I absolutely love it. It is so economical and easy to use. I can hang all of my pctures, plaques, wall hangings easily and effortly. I have all size and wieghts of items, and none have fallen, nor have any large holes been made into my walls.

product_title: Fluke Electrical Tester with a NIST-Traceable Calibration Certificate with Data
review_body: This is an excellent tester, particularly the phase rotation feature.    However, it can be improved by installing a magnetic strip on the back of the unit so that it can be attached to metal surfaces.    Finally, I do find it a bit unforgiveable that the tester doesn't come with a (well fitting)storage pouch or case.  You either have to buy the over-sized Fluke case, or go with something aftermarket.    User background: IBEW Industrial Electrician for over 20 years.

product_title: Black & Decker FSMVC 9.6-Volt to 18-Volt Slide Style Battery Charger
review_body: This charger works great - charges within an hour - it does detect bad batteries with a rapid light flashing.  Should have come with two color lights (red/green) because when put in a battery to charge it does flash and if you had not seen the rapid flash you might think your battery is bad. B&D should have included this as its charger since its batteries last 20 - 60 minutes and it takes 60 minutes to recharge and with two batteries at least you can finish a project at one time - the charger included takes 8 hours and I'm sure this effects sales and when I tell others of this quick charger they are much happier but some do return their machine because they feel taken.

product_title: Garrity Industries E300G Power Failure Rechargeable Flashlight
review_body: Truly a piece of junk, lasted less than a year & was built like crap to begin with!

product_title: Zircon MultiScanner Center-Finding Stud Finder with Metal and AC Electrical Scanning
review_body: I'm not as enthusiastic about this product as some of the other reviewers.  I previously used a Zircon PRO SL before it broke and I was hoping for better performance.  First, I was annoyed by the large size of the device.  This made it difficult to get into smaller spaces and was hard to hold with the spring loaded on/off switch.  I then found that the LCD screen was very difficult to read at awkward angles.  Yes, it looks great and bright straight on but when working on baseboards, the display faded to near invisibility.  Finally, the calibration process now takes an extra second, which turns out to be annoying and slows you down.     For stud finding, it was no better than the very old PRO SL.  There was still plenty of ambiguity with some walls (no, it's not a shear wall) but not others.  The suggestion to use a piece of smooth cardboard on \\"rough\\" walls did not help to resolve the ambiguity.  Sometimes just knocking on the wall and listening to the sound proved more definitive.    Detecting AC was reasonably useful as it did always indicate when a hot wire was near.  However, trying to trace electrical wiring without opening the drywall has proved elusive.  Wires seem to vanish mid-wall with no detectable resume point on the wall.  On well, the product never claimed this as a feature.    I have not tried the metal detection feature.  The deep scan worked no better at finding studs through 5/8\\" drywall or on my shear wall which has an additional 3/8\\" ply.  I think I'll just go back to the cheap $10 version since I'm now convinced that technology is the same and only the display is different (but not better).

product_title: Factory-Reconditioned Dremel 6300-DR-RT 120-Volt Multi-Max Oscillating Kit
review_body: I purchased this tool as I needed it to cut some square holes out of a TV cabinet.  I was installing some fans I bought from Cooler Guys as the components were getting too hot.  I try to stay away from refurbished products because I don't seem to have any luck with them.  This tool however was not the case as it performed the job perfectly.  I was cutting through about a half inch of wood and even though it might have taken longer than expected, it did get the job done better than expected.  I'd suggest buying this if you're just going to use it for a few projects.  If you're thinking about using it more than that then you should look into a more heavy duty tool.

product_title: Hitachi Single Bevel Compound Miter Saw with Laser Marker
review_body: Very happy with this saw , it has a very solid build, exact cuts, comes with a pretty good blade stock.

product_title: SE - Watch Repair Tool Kit, 16 Pc - JT6227
review_body: I purchased this watch repair kit to have the ability to remove links in bracelet type watch bands and do other minor repairs to my watch collection.  The individual tools work great and the case is sturdy and keeps all the tools together in one place for easy use.  I would definitely recommend this kit if your watch bands are too big and you want to create a more custom fit and/or you want to change watch batteries and do other minor repirs.  The transaction with the seller was first rate and the case was shipped very quickly.  Over all I'd give the seller and merchandise an A+ rating.

product_title: Malco AV3 Forged Steel Combination Aviation Snips,
review_body: great product great price, I am a woman with small hands and found these easy to use unlike my husbands shears which cost more and are more difficult to use

product_title: CLOSEOUT Leatherman 830684 Charge TTi Multi-Tool with LeatherNylon Combination Sheath and Gift Tin OPEN BOX PRISTINE CONDITION
review_body: I already have a Victorinox Spirit but felt the Charge TTi had enough unique features to warrant another multitool purchase. Both are great and extremely rugged tools. I would give the edge to the Spirit for build quality (although the Charge TTi comes very close). For example the flathead/pry bar on the Spirit is much thicker. Fit and finish is also another plus for the Spirit. However because of the (slippery) polished finish, I prefer the Charge because I can get a better grip on it. Pros of the Charge of course is the one handed blade opening. I love the shape of the regular and serrated blade, especially the cutting hook on the serrated blade which is very useful. Best features to me though are the changeable bit drivers and mini eyeglass screwdriver. I was skeptical on how well flat headed bits would work but after trying it out I immediately bought the 40 bit accessory kit. The Spirit also have a few good things going for it, like a chisel and awl which the Charge does not have. Both tools have scissors, file and of course pliers but I prefer the ones on the Charge. The scissors are about even and really just a preference, the diamond file seems finer and the pliers are slightly more narrow than the Spirit so you can use it for more precise work. I find myself grabbing the Charge more often for work because its my beat it up tool. But the Spirit works just as good and quality wise it is classic Victorinox, so well made and high quality I like too keep it in good condition. If you are looking for just one multitool you should decide whether the chisel on the Spirit is more important or the changeable bit drivers on the Charge. Overall both are great tools, if you are a geek for hardware like I am I would highly recommend getting both.

product_title: 3M AO Safety/3M Tekk 90534 WorkTunes AM/FM Hearing Protector
review_body: great

product_title: All Power America APT2007 7.5 Amp 1/2-inch Corded Impact Wrench With 4 Impact Sockets And Case
review_body: This impact wrench is not exactly as advertised. The cord is less than 8 feet and it doesn't seem to provide 240 foot pounds. It won't loosen lug nuts on its own. I had to use a breaker bar to loosen all the lugs on my car. I then used the impact wrench to take off and put back on the lug nuts. I used a torque wrench to finish tightening them to 110 pounds. The impact wrench hadn't gotten them there. For the price, it's okay. It's not an industrial grade tool.

product_title: TerraLUX TLE-ST1 LED Upgrade Kit for Streamlight, Stinger, Stinger XT Flashlight
review_headline: Update... Product Redesigned. Problem Is Fixed.
review_body: UPDATE: The ST/XT Stinger upgrade has been redesigned. The focal dome separation and poor focus issues have been resolved. I received the warranty replacement about two months ago. It works awesome. It is bright, clearly focused and has good battery life. The bulbs have a lifetime guarantee they won't burn out and are covered by a 1 year manufacturer's warranty for defects. I don't think my original bulb had a manufacturer's defect, I feel the design was defective.    The representative at TerraLUX was pleasant and helpful. No hassle at all. I would recommend calling the company directly instead of trying to address the issue with the supplying vendor.    Here is my original review:    Everything described by A. Prado happened to me too. The focus on the included lens was never quite perfect. The beam was poorly focused when tightened all the way; Causing me to leave it a bit loose to allow for adjusting.  For the one week it worked, it was great. First to go were the soldered circuit board prongs... a quick and easy fix for anyone with a soldering iron. Just one day after I did the self repair, the glass dome over the LED came off... So, I put the old bulb back in and am happy with my yellow tinted, not as bright but operational flashlight. Just $50 poorer...     I also purchased the TerraLUX TLE-300 for the Magcharger at the same time. That thing is FREAKING AWESOME! Seems like a quick lens change and it would burn holes on the moon! lol! That bulb is built how this one should have been.

product_title: Stanley Bostitch RH-MC14815G-S 1000CT 1-1/2" MCN Nail
review_headline: If you are nailing metal connectors, use the right nails
review_body:
Metal connectors are quite useful when doing framing. Pounding in all the nails is a pain. So using a pnuematic nailer is really helpful.

If your nailer will do this, then you'd be hard pressed to find better nails than these. They are specially hardened, so that if you miss the hole a bit, they will still go through. And they are available in thicker sizes than regular nails of this length (which is perfect for nailing a bracket to a 2\\" board without protruding from the back). They are heavily galvanized, so you would be hard pressed to find anything more rust resistant. Really, they have no down side.

product_title: Bench Dog Tools 40-188 ProCaster Set
review_body: Not much to say here.  The casters are trivial to install if you do so when you first build the table.  They are solid and work well.

product_title: 3/4" Outside Bullnose Trowel
review_headline: Does what it is supposed to..
review_body: I purchased this item to use for installing plastic bullnose corners. (something not available in my area and had to be specially ordered). If I were to purchased again, I would look for a wider outside trowel as the corner seemed slightly larger than the trowel purchased and we had to wipe mud with a rag. No big deal because this tool was a huge help and I don't see how this job could be done without one.

product_title: Stanley 83-069M Maxsteel Multi-Angle Base Vise
review_body: I use my Stanley as a PC board vice while drilling holes using the Milescraft rotary tool drill press and the Black and Decker RTX.  Couldn't be happier.  The total work station on my desk takes up about as much room as a mousepad.  You can rotate your work HOWEVER you want it.  It has a sturdy grip and jaw covers so you wont mar delicate surfaces. And the Stanley is light and strong.  As a hobbists vice I very highly recommended it. If you wanted a shop vice to shape steel, I would find a another vice.  for accurate solid work with huge amounts of mobility, this is a gem.

product_title: Streamlight 69110 TLR-1 C4 LED Rail Mounted Weapon Flashlight, Black
review_body:
I bought this light about a year ago from another site (and paid way more!), and was going to put it on my CX4 carbine, but it found its way onto my Beretta 96D pistol instead. My pistol is my primary home defense weapon, and with this light on it, I'll get the drop on any goblins who venture in late at night. The switch on it works well, and has a very positive lock to the full on position. Extremely bright, I saw it advertised as high as 135 lumens, and as low as 80. I would say it's closer to 135, because it drowns out the light on my other gun which is advertised as 95 lumens. All I know is that it is blinding, and lights up the interior of my house like daylight. It's also pretty durable, I've done regular shooting with it on my carbine, pistol and my M&P 15 and after over 500rds it still works like the day I got it. Overall, great value for the money, and a great product.

For even more fun, pick up the newer version ([[ASIN:B0037CJCMK Streamlight 69210 TLR-1s Weapon C4 LED Light with Strobe]]). Same quality light, but with a strobe!

product_title: Rayovac Highbeam Flashlight K2 Luxeon LED Headlight
review_body:
this was delivered on time
ps note that it is not the brightest led headlight around
i have another cree 3w led which appears to be more brighter than
but then i have to give points to be more sturdier and compact
'the headband elastic is also of good build
final verdict is
if u r not particular about brightness then its good buy
but if need a decent sturdy headlight. this is it

product_title: Wixey WR300 Digital Angle Gauge
review_body: I bought this WR300 because I need to check the cut angles on a number of power tools that I have. It works quite well, easy and fast to use. I compared it to a Bosch digital angle gauge and it measured the same.   It only has 2 drawbacks, it only measures Relative angles (between say the saw table and the blade) not Absolute and for me it is too small.   If you need to check the cut angle on a table saw, this device will work quite well.

product_title: Youngstown Glove Women's Garden Glove, Performance Glove, Pink
review_body: I bought a pair for my mom and my wife.  Both have raved about these gloves.  They are NOT hot in the summer.  They fit very comfortably.  When they are dirty if you let the dirt dry, it just falls off.  My wife worked with rose bushes and torn trees; she was completely protected.  When my wife lost her pair, she would not buy a different kind; but insisted that we spend an immense amount of time looking for them.  The gloves were cheap enough that I just bought her a new pair.  In short, they are great gloves and my mom and wife really like them.

product_title: Hitachi 315129 EB14B 14.4-Volt 2.0 Amp Hour NiCad Pod Style Battery
review_body: A good battery was delivered on time, and at half the price.  My drill now works perfectly.

product_title: Stanley 94-248 65-Piece Homeowner's Tool Kit
review_body: This is a great standard toolkit. I work on the go and bought this kit for the convenience of the carrier. It's not too heavy and practically anything I need is included. It's also convenient to store behind a car seat, under a bed, practically anywhere out of sight as it doesn't take up very much room.

product_title: Grizzly G5113 64-1/2-Inch x 1/2-Inch x .025-Inch Bi-Metal Band Saw Blade
review_body:
I have a Jet brand bandsaw and had a hard time finding a replacement blade until I located this one from Grizzly. I did not realize that 64-1/2\\" x 1/2\\" is an industry standard and that anyone's bandsaw blade would work.

I paid double the normal price for a standard bandsaw blade to get this Grizzly branded one which is no better, just twice as expensive. Next time I will know better.

product_title: Klein Tools 32477 10-in-1 Screwdriver/Nut Driver
review_body: Buy a Lennox 9 in 1 (or whatever it's called) instead.  These things strip out on you.  The shaft on my first one cracked when I was using the screwdriver part, so I returned it and got a new one.  Same thing happened again.  An old electrician told me they always do that.  Now it's in my kid's toy toolbox.

product_title: Devonshire Flasks 8 oz. Flask, Brushed Stainless
review_body: This flask came quickly and as advertised.  It is a decent flask and did not leak.  The metal is a little thin on the body so expect dents.  But at the price when it gets bad just repace it.  Finish is okay.  The crudest part is the cap system which appears to be chromed steel rather thn stainless like the rest of the flask.  It is made in china.

product_title: Stanley FatMax Xtreme AntiVibe Curve Claw Nailing Hammer
review_body: I've moved further away from mechanical work to doing more carpentry work.  So looking for different types of tools than I'm used to but not settling for cheap.  Have been looking at and trying different hammers and I'm sold on the Stanley FatMax Xtreme AntiVibe Rip Claw Nailing Hammers.  A good, balanced feel, comfortable grip and, being an uncoordinated left-handed klutz, I seem to get away with more off-center strikes compared to other hammers and I'll take any breaks I can get.  The price at Amazon couldn't be beat anywhere, received quickly and without any problems.  I would definitely recommend the hammer and Amazon to family and friends.

product_title: Milwaukee 6148-30 4-1/2-Inch Small Angle Grinder
review_body: Works great so far.  It is loud as is any grinder but it's got plenty of power, the controls are great (get this model or one of the others than also has the ability to lock it on).  It would be nice if Milwaukee included a rubber strap for the tool that would attach it to the power cord.  I just zip tied it on there.

product_title: BOSTITCH SX1838K 18-Gauge Narrow-Crown Stapler
review_body: This is a versatile tool that can be used for many tasks. Smooth operation and quality construction. I love it.

product_title: Leatherman 81080003K Squirt S4 Storm Gray Multitool with Small Scissors
review_headline: Nice build quality, but not without its flaws
review_body: At first sight it seemed like a very good pocket tool. Very small and handy and can fit in virtually any size pocket. The blade knife that it comes with is very VERY sharp and i can cut thru almost anything. The scissors are also good as i can cut fishing line and even braided lines with ease as compared to other pocket tools with scissors as a sub tool.     There are however, flaws that i've noticed that makes me regret my purchase. First thing i notice after a couple of usages is that the scissors tend to \\"stick\\". The scissors are spring-loaded and therefore retract to original position after u clamp it down. Mine however, tends to stick together in which that i have to unstick them before i can continue cutting. Its a big nuisance because i've tried WD-40 in all the moving parts but it did not seem to help it at all. This is a major downfall to a tool which scissors are its primary function. I cant recommend this tool because this is my second S4 which also sticks just like the first 1 i had received.     Another thing that is a deal breaker is that the bottle opener is junk. I bought this tool mainly for the scissors, but the blade and bottle opener were also taken into consideration as those were the other tools that i was gonna use frequently. The only thing the bottle opener tends to do is shred the bottle cap in half but not actually opening the bottle in the first place. You can actually get cut if u were not paying attention. The bottle cap will split in half,the part u are trying to open, creating a sharp edge which the bottle opener tool will slip off and u can cut ur fingers. I got a lil scratch not too deep but the bottle did not open. Out of the 4 bottles i tried to open, only the 1st one was the easiet, took two tries in two different areas to get it to open. I got a cheapo 5 dollar china made pocket knife with bottle opener that can bust open the caps in 1 try.     The only thing that i find that works and that works well is the blade, however, im not gonna be dropping 23 bucks on just a tiny 1.5 inch blade so im afraid this has to go back. Great idea but poorly executed, but maybe thats the reason why the S4 was discontinued.

product_title: KR Tools Five-Piece Multi Tool Set-VARIATION
review_headline: Unique, basic tool set. Great as a backup or for a second home
review_body: I've got the set with the racing Flame design and I think it looks much better than the camouflage design. At least there's some reason for having a flame design and it alludes to some racing heritage or something....    Anyway... this is a pretty basic set. The rubberized grips are nice but I do find them to be a little thicker than expected and this is somewhat problematic for my (average) hands. This is most noticeable on the wrench and the pliers.    The tough thing with tools is that, well, you can't tell how tough they are until you've used them for many years and I don't want to wait that long to write this review. These seem like they'll hold up overtime. All the basics are their: Phillips head screw driver, flat head, hammer, pliers, adjustable wrench. I think they make a great set to keep in the car or in some alternate location. Saves me from having to grab the big toolbox everytime I need someting.

product_title: The Original Pink Box PB2BELT Tool Belt
review_body: Purchased for a women remodeling her house. Has nice pockets and sleeves for items like pencils, screwdriver ect. This type of belt is nice because the pouches slide along the belt, you can put it on and adjust as required. One problem from reading other reviews is the pink dye on the leather ones bleeds off onto clothing, not a good thing, this one is made of nylon and that should not be an issue.  Also the color of pink is very nice. The only problem someone may have if you have a small waist, the belt is a little long. It has 10 rows of holes for the buckle, and if it is still too big you could double the belt back and sew it making it shorter.  Can not comment on durability, but so far so good.

product_title: Bosch T4B Gravity-Rise Miter Saw Stand
review_body: Easy to raise and lower.  Large wheels make it easy to move around.  The stands size makes it quite stable, yet it still fits through most home doors.  My older (non-Bosch) miter saw installed with no problems.  The side extensions are helpful when dealing with lighter pieces of wood, but nothing beats a pair of saw horses for 2x8 or larger.

product_title: Irwin Industrial Tools Professional's Industrial Extractor Set
review_body: A 12mm bolt that holds the oil filter cover on my old 750 Honda was completely rounded off.  There was no hope of loosening it with Vice Grips or such.  I inserted this socket over the bolt and lightly tapped it with a hammer.  It turned maybe a fourth of a turn before it gripped but then it held fast. It must have taken 30 ft-lbs to break it loose but the socket worked perfectly.

product_title: Bosch RA1190 Stationary Stand for RA1180 Router Table
review_body: I put a Bosch router bench table on it and am very happy with the stability.

product_title: Factory-Reconditioned Ryobi ZRCSB123 12 Amp 7-1/4-in Circular Saw
review_body: I bought this saw about 1 month ago. It prooved quite useful soon after as we were replacing kitchen cabinets.   The person doing the cabinet work is an experienced guy, and he didn't even know that the saw was reconditioned!   He actually thought it was brand new!     The appearance and performance was first  class.     Ordering was very quick and easy, and it was delivered maybe 3 days earlier than promised.   I'd recommend it to anyone interested in a 7 1/4 Circular saw.   In hindsight, I should have bought one or two more, they would make ideal gifts.

product_title: Brush Research (BRMGB4-1/8) 4-1/8in. 180 Grit Flex Engine Cylinder Hone
review_body: works great, some of the balls started falling off, but to it's defense I was a little aggressive honing my cylinders.

product_title: Surebonder DT-280F Dual Temperature 60 Watt Full Size Standard Glue Gun
review_body: I bought this to make hair bows for my little baby girl. I was shocked to see the package contains a warning stating the power cord contains lead. It suggests hand washing after an usage. I will return it immediately and try to locate a glue gun without a \\"lead\\" power cord.

product_title: Gerber Diesel Multi-Plier
review_body:
Excellent tool. I use it all the time. I'm not sure how I functioned without it. The tool is very sturdy and built well. It took about a week to break it in... Being new, the tool was stiff and had a slight coating of oil. After about a week, it is very easy to get to all the accessories with little effort. Also, I understand it has a lifetime warranty.

Excellent tool!

product_title: Makita LS1013F 10-inch Dual Slide Compound Miter saw with Light
review_body:
I am a Finish Carpenter and bought this saw 6 or so years ago. I have used it almost every work week for 8hrs a day. Right away the lock down bolt broke from bouncing in my trailer not a big deal but had me worried. Then for about 5 years NOTHING went wrong. Now after bout 12,000 Hrs of use I dug a grave for it. A screw loosened up and when i went to make cut the blade guard exploded. And it doesn't like to lock in 1/4 degree increments anymore. So 12,000 hrs and 500 bucks is about 4 cents an hr to rent this. I am very very impressed with it and how accurate and durable it really has been, and now i bought the ls1016 and too early to review it.

Ok here is why Makita > Dewalt. I had 2 employees working for me and i bought them the 10in chopsaw. First one lasted 6months before it went to hell. So I thought it was a lemon and tried another one..That one lasted 6 months too.Then I tried their belt drive 12in I went through 3 of them in the 60 day home depot warranty. Then i bought their 8\\" sliding compound that broke after 3 months and had to have it completely rebuilt. The cuts are no straight even with a FORREST blade and it doesn't like to cut all the way through. Nice lockdown feature but DEWALT SUCKS! NONE of their tools have lasted me over a year. But what do you expect its black and decker haha. WIth that said I will never ever buy another dewalt saw. 1 makita has outlasted 6 dewalt saws and it still is cutting just without a guard :D

product_title: OLFA 45mm Rotary Blades, 10-pack
review_body: Because I go through rotary blades quite frequently in my hobbies, I was pleased to see I could purchase the blades much cheaper in bulk instead of one at a time at Joanns Fabric.  Thank you rottenrotts.

product_title: Zibra ZPCOPEN-OR Open It Universal Package Opener
review_body: I got this for my husband this Christmas and I'll admit, I've used it more than he has! It works so quick and easy and it's comfortable to hold. So glad I picked this and so is he. No more struggling for twenty minutes trying to open those funny plastic containers. Sweet!

product_title: Ironclad HUG Heavy Utility Gloves
review_body: I have had these for a while now and they have held up beautifully.By this time my other gloves had torn out at the fingertips but the ironclads carry on.

product_title: Weller 7874B ESD Safe Manual Desoldering Tool
review_headline: Spend the money & buy the Edsyn Soldapullt
review_body: I ignored the other reviews and picked this desoldering tool because of the lower price and free supersaver shipping.  Most of my electronics work is rebuilding vacuum tube amps and radios, which often have multiple leads twisted together in a single large solder joint, and have to be thoroughly desoldered to be taken apart.  This Weller unit doesn't have the suction to get more than 60% of the solder out of a joint.  I have to take it apart after every \\"suck\\" and use pliers to pull out the \\"tube\\" of solder that jams the tip.  Depending on the way I hold it, the plunger will bind on my hand and not generate any suction, and it \\"jumps\\", making delicate work very difficult.  My dad had Edsyn Soldapullt units when I was a kid that worked great, and I should have bought that.  This Weller unit would probably work OK for PC board disassembly.

product_title: Gerber LMF II Survival Knife
review_body: Ive been in scouts my whole life so ive owned many difrent knives, this I have to say has been the best one yet, Ive cut wood, rope, cardboard, cloth and some copper wire with it and it takes it all. The shieth is a litle hard to deal with since its designed for a military type uniform not jeans and a leather belt, so I took all the velkro of and just tuck it under my belt with a cord around it. Great product!!

product_title: Boss Black Over-the-Sock Boot - Men's Size 11, Model# 2PK200111
review_body: Very fast service. These boots are great, they are comfortable, and they keep your feet dry. I can't say enough about them. I am glad I made this buy.

product_title: Xcelite Screwdriver - Allen Hex Tip - 3/32 in Tip Size - 25/32 in 3 1/2 in Length - P3321 [PRICE is per EACH]
review_body: Perfect little screwdriver especially for professional audio equipment such as mic cables and microphone reparations.

product_title: Kenmore Single Undersink Drinking Water System
review_body: While the object sold was OK, it was not a \\"system\\". Despite the sellers contention it could not treat water. It was missing the filter!  It was shipped as if it came from Sears. I had an unpleasant experience as I was charged a 15% re-shelving fee (Find that in the ad.)

product_title: Rockwell RW9121.3 Sonicrafter 1-3/8-Inch Standard End Cut Blade, 3-Piece
review_body: The blades work well when new, but wear down very quickly. The commercial stated that you could cut at least 100 nails, but I had to replace the blade after 4 nails due to the teeth were ground down to nothing. The price would be good if the blades were a better quality.

product_title: Racor PHL-1R Pro HeavyLift 4-by-4-Foot Cable-Lifted Storage Rack
review_headline: Cheaply made and wrong/missing parts included
review_body:
I was expecting a well built product from the Racor PHL-1R Pro HeavyLift model since it was supposed to be the heavier duty version of the lighter weight model Pro+. I bought two of these at once and was dissapointed at the cheap materials and construction when I opened the package. The wire grid sections were bent and fit terribly on the support beams. The J-hooks and nuts were of inferior quality with three of them having stripped out threads. The included lag screws for mounting the support rails to the ceiling rafters were cheap grade and I twisted off two of them upon installation into the joists after following the directions and pre-drilling 1/8\\" pilot holes for the lag screws. Do yourself a BIG favor and make a trip to the local hardware store and pick up some quality hardened lag screws and extra J-hooks to avoid the frustration I had trying to install this product.

Worst thing of all is that both of these units were shipped with the WRONG gear box assembly for the hoisting mechanism. They were packaged with the lightweight PRO+ gearbox which apparently has a much smaller drive shaft than what ships with the HeavyLift model. review_body:
***Product Description
5HP, 26 Gallon Vertical Compressor, Direct Drive Oilless Pump, Attached Wheels, Delivers 6.9
CFM @ 40 PSI & 5.5 CFM @ 90 PSI, Made In USA, UL Listed, Carries Standard Duty One
Year Warranty. ***

The above product description is misleading at best. Google \\"CFM\\" and \\"SCFM\\" and you'll find CFM is a static number where SCFM can be measure at pressure (typically @ 40 & 90 psi). I took the chance that the copy meant SCFM given the numbers provided were at pressure and rated at the standard 40 & 90psi. Not the case and I'm a little frustrated by the copyright's or seller's lack of knowledge. Upon product arrival the 5hp motor is really a 2hp motor (5 peak) and the SCFM is about half of the incorrectly used \\"cfm\\" above (~ 4.8 @ 40 & 2.? @ 90). A disappointing transaction in that I had to return the product and look for something that truely produced in the range of 6.9 SCFM@ 40psi.

The plastic housing/tool storage area actually looked to be very useful when viewing in person. If you want to run a brad nailer or pump up a few tires or basketballs once in a while, the product would work great. If you want to run any cutters, die grinders, or anything that would require even moderate air flow I'd move on.

product_title: DEWALT DWD115K 8 Amp 3/8-Inch VSR Mid-Handle Grip Drill Kit with Keyless Chuck
review_body:
I purchased this drill before a mostly DIY kitchen renovation where we figured we'd need the power of a corded drill. I'm really glad we got this drill as it is solidly built, well-balanced, and has a ton of power. I've used it to drill holes, from tiny ones to large Forstner-mades, drive all sorts of screws into studs and hardwoods, and mix thin-set.

The chuck spins easily when changing bits, so it's fast to switch the chuck from a thin to a thick bit (or vice versa). I've never had a bit slip in the chuck - those teeth clamp down securely.

The variable speed trigger is quite sensitive and there have been times when I've given it a little more power than I was wanting to and stripped a screw head or over-driven a screw deeper than I wanted to. In those situations, I might have opted for a cordless drill/driver since they're not as powerful or aggressive. It's taken me some time to get used to the sensitivity of the trigger and now I'm much better at squeezing gently and gradually. I didn't have all of this extra power in my previous drill and I was accustomed to giving the trigger a full squeeze all the time.

But those cordless power tools will never be able to mix thinset (and if they can it won't be for very long!). If you do use this drill to mix thinset (with the appropriate mixing wheel, of course), take it slow and rest the drill plenty. It will overheat and smoke if you push it too hard.

Another note - it's a fairly loud drill, especially compared to the wimpier cordless drills. And if you are doing finer work with it and like to have your face closer to your workpiece to the right of your drill (remember your safety glasses!), you'll get blast of air in the face from the side vent.

Overall, this is a great alternative to the 18V cordless drills out there, especially if you don't want to drop $150-200 right now for a decent model + battery. I've found most of the time I'm close enough to an outlet where the corded aspect of the drill doesn't bother me.

product_title: Dremel 7300-PT 4.8-Volt Pet Grooming Kit
review_headline: Good product makes for a happy owner and a happy dog
review_body:
I purchased the short-lived previous version of this product, [[ASIN:B001L4GH1A Dremel 765-01 Pet Nail Grooming Kit]], and liked it so much that I bought the Dremel 7300-PT for friends. There are two differences between the 765 and the 7300- the casing of the 73000 is gray, and Amazon charges $29, rather than $32.

The newest version of Dremel's Pet Nail sander is well worth the money. It has changed what was previously a tortuous experience into something quick and easy.

I did some research before buying the 765 and 7300, and ended up choosing these over other products for several reasons.
PediPaws Pet Nail Trimmer- Several friends had bad experiences with it, generally finding it to be of poor quality.

Dremel 7700-02 MultiPro 7.2-Volt 20,000 RPM Two-Speed Rotary Tool with 50 Accessories- Although this is more powerful, it is also more expensive, heavier, larger, and louder, which would make it difficult to use on my nervous pet.

Dremel 761-03 Cordless Pet Nail Grooming Rotary Tool- This is the older version of the 765; the primary difference is that this required AA batteries. Because several people complained about having battery problems I decided to go with the updated version.

I made the right choice! I have a large pitbull who has dark nails, hates having anything done to her feet, has very long quicks that are fast to bleed and slow to stop, and wiggles and refuses to stay still when she is nervous. I have tried clipping her nails, filing her nails, and even taking her on long runs on rough ground to wear them down. This is by far the best solution.

I began by letting her see and smell the sander, and then running it over her body and feet with the power off. I then turned it on and held it away from her, again letting her hear, see, and smell it. I had treats at the ready, but she was fine. I held it near her for several minutes while on, and then touched the non-sanding end to her body so that she could feel the vibration. No problems. In fact she bent down to smell it, and pinned the sanding band between her face and my hand. We both jumped, but no pain or damage to either of us. Although I was prepared to stop if she got tired or nervous, she was so good that I was able to do all four paws. It took about 15 minutes, but with lots of \\"good girl\\" and belly rubs interspersed she was fine.

The sander itself is relatively small and light, making it easy to hold even for long periods. It is easy to put together; it comes with a small wrench to put new sanding bands on. Unlike its predecessor it comes with a rechargeable battery and charger. When sanding, even on high, it is fairly quiet and vibrations are minimal. The body of the sander was warming a bit after 15 minutes, but I noticed no heat in either my dog's nails or the sanding band. In addition the battery was still going strong. My sole complaint about this product is minor; the LED light on the charger lights up to indicate a connection between the battery and the charger, but doesn't change color or go off to indicate when charging is complete. The instruction book indicates that a full charge should take approximately 3 hours, so that's what I've gone with. I had to recharge it after about the fourth or fifth use.

I gave the Dremel 7300 to a friend, and she's used it on her two German Sherpherds and her cat, with similar success

This is a great product for nervous animals and/or owners, as it's almost impossible to do damage with, and allows easy care for an oft-neglected aspect of your pet's health.

**Update 10/19/11:
After about a year of ownership the Dremel is still my go-to tool for trimming my dog's nails. My only complaint is that the battery is not holding its charge nearly as well as it originally did. With one full charge I can usually get through a full sanding on all four feet, however by the end the power is running low, and I don't doubt that soon I won't be able to do all four feet at once. Despite this drawback I still highly recommend the dremel for those who want an alternative to clipping their pet's nails, and when the battery on mine dies for good I will definitely be investing in a new one.

product_title: Magnesium Fire Starter Flint Stone
review_headline: Good sparks for a cheap firesteel
review_body:
Not a premium firesteel, but for the price it works well. The included striker is a bonus: You don't have to mess up a good knife blade. I haven't used it much, but it makes adequate sparks with sufficient pressure. Durability is unknown, but I'll carry this as a backup firestarter.

At first use, it will take some scraping to clear the black oxidation. Once you're through the oxide layer, firm pressure and a quick wrist will generate lots of very bright sparks.

Dryer lint is an excellent firestarter, and takes a spark well. For emergency fire kit, knead some vaseline (petroleum jelly) into some cotton balls. Penny sized pieces of this gooey mess burns quite well and for a while.

The instructions say to scrape a pile of metal off the firesteel. With dryer lint, cotton balls or other good tinder, this is a waste of time.

UPDATE: June 2013: Since the review was posted, I have used it occasionally and have lit many fires with it. Bottom line: it's light, it throws good sparks, and lights fires. Now the rod is getting a little thin from use, but it lights fires just as well as an expensive one that has a much larger diameter rod, at 1/4th the weight. Bumped my review to 5 stars.
Oh: the description is way off: this is not a magnesium bar, it's a standard ferro-rod, just like the other thousand or so products that are just like it.

The only improvement I made was to take the loop of line holding it together, and get rid of the loop... a longer lanyard on the striker makes this easier to operate... Just untie the knot, and use a double overhand knot on each end to keep the firesteel and striker from being separated.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE PN650 Palm Nailer Kit
review_body: The nailer works well, When I got it i tested a bunch of nails through some 2x4's.  It easily sank the largest nail had in the basement which was a 16 penny nail.  The 16 penny nail just fit in the tip, a 16 penny galvanized nail's head is to large to fit in the standard tip.    I then went to change tips to drive finish nails and i could not get the tip off.      I could not get much leverage holding the thing in my hand so i built a wooden box only slightly wider than the nailer and put it in there to get some good leverage.  It sill would not budge,  I even hit the wrench with a hammer, nothing.  I called porter cable and they said i could return it or bring it to their factory store and they could fix it.  I chose the latter (the store is 15 minutes away and my wife able to go there during their poor hours).  In order to fix it they needed to 'torch' it.  They had the tip off in a couple minutes.    When i got it home i found the torching demagnetized the tip so went back to the porter cable store and asked the to order me a new magnet (the magnet is size of small pill held in by clip on the end of the tip).  They did, couple days later went to pick it up and they had ordered a whole new tip, which fine.  It was free of charge of course, i peaked at the invoice and saw it would have cost me 25 dollars if i had to pay for it.  Now have an extra tip.      Since then it has worked fine, I have used it for mostly finish nails, some 2.5 inches (60 psi) and even some tiny 7/8th inch ones (use 30 psi).  I like to stop before the nail goes all the way in and finish with a nail punch.  The nailer does not come with enough spacing washers to keep the nail proud of the surface.  I ordered some more spacing washers, they are not here yet, 5 dollars each for washers (sigh).      I have used the hammer attachment to fix my snow thrower.  The cowling was bent and making it hard to use.  I have tried hitting it with a 3 pound hammer in the past but only bent it back half way orso,  I was able to use the hammer on the bend and push on the leading edge and it flattened it nicely.  I was then able to finish with the 3 pound hammer to make it look like new again.     I have also used to as a hammer to chisel wood.  Set to 30 psi.  I plan to try it as hammer to split wood when it gets warmer outside.    I like the size of the thing.  I like that you can change the pressure to the job at hand.  I dont like that you cant adjust to leave the nail proud with out buying some extra super expensive washers.  Also dont like that it came with the tip siezed on.  But it has been a very useful tool so far.

review_body:
I was hesitant to buy this at first, but its cheap and it comes with plenty of fabric.

I sew on quite a few pieces to my leather vest without actually testing it first, and when I went out at night it turned out to be too much... The reflection is like nothing you have seen before. I ended up only using a couple of stripes in the back, similar to the picture, and a few in the front at chest level. The best feature of this is that its black during the day, so it blends in with the black leather just fine during the day to be almost unnoticeable and then at night its like you had a reflection vest. Great product highly recommended.

product_title: Freud D0620X Diablo 6-Inch 20 Tooth ATB Trim Saw Blade with 1/2-Inch Arbor
review_body: I replaced the original blade that came on my porter cable 6\\" trim saw with this one form Freud. the freud blade is much smoother, cuts a thinner kerf and is a joy to use. great blade at a great price

product_title: Columbia River Knife and Tool 5160 Hole in One
review_body: Yet another fine knife from CRKT. Love the way it clips to my belt loops leaving pockets free. Also like the fact it has a bottle opener built in as well.

product_title: Extech Brix Refractometer
review_body: I'm using this unit to measure the salinity in my fish tank and for the first time I really know the real value of this important parameter. At first I was using a regular plastic hydrometer and was trusting the results I was getting, but then I bought a second hydrometer and the readings were totally different from the first one. That's when I realized that I needed more precision, and this unit is of course more expensive, but the accuracy you get is worth the extra money. It turned out that the salinity in my tank was way too high and was the reason for several problems I was having with the aquarium. The unit it's extremely easy to calibrate , all you need is destilled water and 10 seconds of your time, and is also very easy to use.

product_title: MARSHALLTOWN The Premier Line 6D 14-Inch by 14-Inch Aluminum Hawk with DuraSoft Handle

product_title: KR Tools 93351 Pro Series 3-Tine Cultivator
review_headline: Well-Made, High Quality, Strong and Useful Garden Tool
review_body:

product_title: The 'Green' Flashlight - 5 Bright LED SOLAR-Charged!
review_body: Sufficiently bright to poke around in a car engine after dark, those little LEDs definitely generate a decent light.  I bought this specifically to leave in my car so I'd always have a charged flashlight when needed, and so far I'm quite happy with it.  The only poor design issue is the side panels made of rubber seem to shrink over time (due to age and being in a hot car, no doubt) so they are now loose and can fall off. However, it doesn't affect the functionality at all and the flashlight does everything I wanted it for (ie, stays charged and gives off light).

product_title: Capri Tools Magnetic Bar Holder Tool
review_body: I have ordered this product before.  I use one in my kitchen for my knives and keep them near the stove and counter top.  There's one in the barn for my tools there and the new ones are in the garage for additional tools I use in the house frequently.  The magnet is strong and will even hold a hammer or pipe wrench yet it is easy to remove the tool.    Great device!  Recommend it highly!  Will eventually have the need for another.

product_title: Panasonic EY6432GQKW 15.6-Volt 3.3Ah NiMH 1/2-Inch Cordless Drill/Driver Kit
review_headline: Excellent for the Average Home User, and Small Contractor
review_body: I have used this drill for everything from very small to medium size home \\"DIY\\" projects & repairs.  Each time, it has performed above & beyond the call of duty.  I have no gripes whatsoever, and highly recommend it.  It is relatively compact, charges quickly, and is well-balanced in my hands.    If you make a living doing things with drills (ie, contractor, etc.), then I don't know how it will hold up under constant heavy use.  But, for general home user use, including building several large wooden structures on my property (for example a large wooden playset, a workbench, etc.), it has been excellent.

product_title: Makita DA3010F 4 Amp 3/8-Inch Right Angle Drill with LED Light
review_headline: Great angle drill:   LED light   /   Fan blows dust out of the way
review_body: This is the best drill I have ever owned..  The angle head is the smallest I have seen, so there is even more room in tight places..  It feels very well made (sound and feel)..  The cooling nan ports air to where you  are drilling, which blows stuff out of the way so you can see what you are doing..  The only bad thing is when you are drilling stuff you shouldnt really be drilling (you get more stuff airborne)..  A speed chuck would be nice too, but apparently they take up more room (and it looks like they designed it to be small).. Also, a speed cuck on an angle drill might be more of a hazard (I am surprised we dont hear of more eyes being put out by speed chucks)..     LED LIGHT:  The LED light is fantastic (I wish all my tools had it)..  Could use it a tad bit brighter..   You have to actually press the trigger to turn on the light..  I washed there was an alternative, but after thinking about it I came to the conclusion this is the best solution..   If it were designed to stay on all the time, it would be a pain to unplug when done..  If it had a switch, or some kind of smart electronlcs it would increase the chances something would break..  Still, twist the led itself would make a good switch..      CONS:  I gave it 5 stars, so these cons are just being picky..     (1)  There is virtually no \\"feel\\" to how tight a screw is (compared to 18V drill)..  Still the moror is probably much more powerful..  There is no cluth, but I havent found a cluth to be useful anyway (I use a touch on the trigger and go slow, and it bogs down the motor when the screw gets tight).. This doest work with the makita well, because even at slow speeds there is a lot more torque than I am used to..     (2)   The dang cord wants to coil up like a phone cord (so there is a fair amount of cord management; rather than drilling mgmt).. The twisted wires inside must be doing it..  Possibly a fluke.. But the cord likes to walk into the way.. The cord is prettty long, but could have used even longer..     (3)  I wish there was some kind of switch or lock to use when changing bits..  It is cumbersome to keep unplugging the thing to change bits..  The trigger is very easy to turn on by accident (as are all drills of this type I believe)..  But one more switch means one more thing to break..      bobbler

product_title: Rayovac Lantern
review_headline: Great Price Idiot Instructions Luckily Amazon Notes Showed Me How
review_body: Excellent product for the money but their instructions were written by someone with an IQ under 2020! Luckily Amazon Notes show you how to put the batteries in. product_title: Northern Industrial Service Cart - 600-Lb. Capacity, Steel
review_body: I bought this cart to use for a table top bbq grill.  works great, was easy to assemble.  would recommend.

product_title: BLACK+DECKER LI4000 4-Volt Lithium-Ion SmartSelect Screwdriver with Magnetic Screw Holder
review_body: This would have been be the last cordless screwdriver I would ever buy if it wasn't for one tiny detail; battery life is horrible. I was very disappointed when I ran out of battery after drilling 8 (eight) 1.5\\" screws into drywall. Excellent torque on the first four screws though. product_title: Milwaukee 49-22-4185 28-Piece All Purpose Professional Ice Hardened Hole Saw Kit
review_body: I purchased this set for my husband for Christmas and he was thrilled. Not long after Christmas my husband needed to drill a hole in some heavy metal. Before it would have taken him forever, but he came and told me how fast he drilled the hole with one of these hole saw bits. He couldn't believe it and is thoroughly impressed. We are sold on Milwaukee products anyway, and this is just one more example of a great product. I also feel I got a good deal on Amazon. That is where I have purchased all of my Milwaukee gifts for him. Hard to beat Amazon's price and free shipping, I have tried.

product_title: 8 - ton Vertical Log Splitter
review_headline: Worked OK for a few months, jack quit working
review_body:
The heart of this splitter is a cheap hydraulic bottle jack modified with two foot pedals - one for pumping and one for releasing. When the jack fails the splitter is finished. Mine lasted just a few months; probably less than a cord of firewood. It did OK on ponderosa and juniper but when I started splitting oak and pinyon it bit the dust.
When it worked it was slower than splitting with a maul but much easier on the joints and was pleasant to use. It often required turning the wood over and splitting from the other side because of it's short stroke. It was an OK splitter while it lasted.

review_body: I bought this pencil torch with the greatest expectations to get the job done... I may have gotten an messed up pencil torch but it didnt even light for me and I used RONSON MULTI-FILL ULTRA BUTANE FUEL. review_body: This lamp is not quite one would want on the desk. The reason I bought this lamp was because I was looking for two things.    1.  Obviously good light on my desk    2.  I like scratch-boarding. For those who don't know what this is, it is a form of art where you scratch fine lines into a board of clay or foil, coated with a black ink. The concept is nice but several others have implemented it.    Cons:    1.  The lens does not really perform to expectation. In fact, one has to squint into it and move one's head to focus. product_title: Wiha 36238 TorxPlus Screwdriver with SoftFinish Handle, IP15 x 80mm
review_body:
Wiha tools are Germany's gift to those of us who appreciate quality and craftsmanship in their tools.

If you've ever bought cheap tools and been forced to use them, you've paid the price. Cheap tools work cheaply and wear early. If you tinker often, you're probably on your second or third generation of cheap, worthless tool sets.

The problem is that it's increasingly difficult to find decent tools. Stanley and the like are certainly passable, but they're not remarkable. And screwdrivers, in particular, reveal limitations of their manufacture by wearing with use. Phillips are notorious for wear.

These screwdrivers, however, are simply gorgeous. Nearly sexually alluring. They enlarge the handle for larger tips to provide proportional torque. The material itself is marvelous, feeling simultaneously firm and soft. Even after extended work, your hands will not fatigue as they do with poorer drivers. They feel as balanced as well-made kitchen knives. You'll be tempted to do circus tricks with them.

Their tips are precision machined to perfectly fit the screws they're intended for. The screwdrivers feel almost magnetic, locking into place in the screw, and releasing only when held perfectly perpendicular to the screw. Even better, this model's hex bolster permits the use of a wrench or pliers when extra torque is needed.

The particular line pictured here includes steel end caps on each driver. Although you certainly won't want to use your tool to chisel anything, it would permit you to use a mallet, if, for example, you needed to clear some paint from a screw before removing it. Also, the shaft itself is hexagonal.

I also own the lighter duty version of these, which dispense with the metal caps, the hex bolsters, and have round shafts. Frankly, unless your drivers are going to see serious duty, you could do perfectly well with these. They're also lighter. Common to both versions is flattened part of the handle, so that they won't roll away.

Wiha provides a \\"100% satisfaction guarantee,\\" which provides protection against defects in manufacture. Despite the title, I somehow doubt that you could return them with the complaint that you're only 98% satisfied. But regardless, you'll be plenty satisfied.

You can find some Wiha tools in better hardware stores. It's fairly common to find their precision drivers (i.e., jeweler's screwdrivers--I have many of their precision drivers, and a precision micro bit set--they're as good) in hobby and electronics stores, but tracking down their full size drivers is trickier. The easiest place is their US distribution site: [...]

Wiha tools are pricey relative to other tools, but they are actually economical if you consider how many cheaper drivers you'd go through to match their lifetime. I'm all for paying more upfront to support a company that clearly cares about what it produces. We have a local Ace Hardware, which I frequent and support, and their brand of tools come with a similar 100% guarantee. I recently bought a set of hobby pliers and cutters, and one of the springs popped out after several uses. Sure, I can, and will, bring it back to Ace, but they offer the guarantee not because their tools are well made (it's the same Chinese tools that have flooded the market everywhere), but because they're inexpensive to replace, and most customers will never bother to take advantage. Frankly, instead of feeling grateful for the guarantee, it frustrates me that I end up wasting my time exchanging poorly-made tools. I have nothing against Chinese-made products--what would Walmart do without China--but it's a waste and an environmental abuse to produce, buy, and discard short-lived products.

Check out Wiha's line of other tools when you visit their site. They have an entire line of drivers for high-voltage work, a driver with adjustable torque settings, and unusual ratcheting, palm-drivers for extra power (yet with less stress on the wrist). They also have beautiful pliers and wire cutters.a power (yet with less stress on the wrist). They also have beautiful pliers and wire cutters.

product_title: Youngstown Glove Tradesman Plus Performance Glove, Brown
review_body: I bought these gloves about 1 month and 1 week ago, and they have saved my hands from a great deal of cuts, bruises, and impact/shock.     I use these everyday I work, lifting cases of drinks and snacks, and then restocking vending machines.     The first gloves I tried were about $10 from WalMart, and were labeled as being 'light-duty work gloves', for construction and general labor use. They lasted less than 1 day. (There were holes in them after a few hours actually). These Youngstown work gloves have held up Remarkably better than the other gloves. The stitching for the fingers and thumbs started to go first, and then the thumb stitching came undone, and now both thumbs are 'in the open' but the fingers still have one layer covering them out of two total.     Overall, I am quite happy with the performance level of these gloves, and am especially happy with the amount of dexterity I have...I can write with a pen and pad easily with both on, and handle medium-small objects. The only downside is that they lasted only about 1 month. Other than that - They're great!

review_body: Bought this to cut metal downspouting to install a rain diverter.  Worked great and  left a relatively smooth edge.  I recommend it for light metal cutting applications.

product_title: SE BT20 Battery Tester
review_body: I got this to weed out brand new batteries that I know got thrown into the recyling battery bin.  This tester read that almost all of the batteries in my bin were either \\"good\\" or \\"low\\" when I know most of them are all used up and junk.  It seems that unless the battery was completely dead and drained, it had a reading of \\"good\\". It was cheap and worth a shot, but it's not accurate and I can't trust the reading.

product_title: Powermatic PM1300 1791077CK 1-3/4 HP Dust Collector with Canister Kit
review_body:
- After lots of research, I ordered the Powermatic 1300 w/ canister based on it's ability to capture low micron dust (1 micron) and large filtering surface area afforded by canister system (compared to bag systems). I think it's a false sense of security to buy many of the less expensive \\"bag\\" units, many of which will only capture down to 30 micron dust and coat over quickly thus reducing available dust collecting capacity of the system. My long termed health is worth the greater investment to me.
- Order was easy to place and was received in a timely fashion (4 days after order placement)
- Delivery driver was courteous and helpful - took packages right into my garage for me; this is important because this machine is heavy
- Assembly directions were fine and assembly went very well with no specialized tools required. All parts went together great, hole alignment was right on! Finished product is a very solid build - no squeeks or rattles
- Vacuum is extremely powerful from the unit. I have not yet had occasion to try it under heavy loading, but feel confident it will handle anything my one man shop can throw at it
- Machine runs fine on a dedicated 20 amp 110 volt circuit. Clear instructions provided for future conversion to 220 volt power if desired.
- The remote and timed operating options are useful; should assure consistent use of device as intended
- Although packaging seemed adequate, the metal discharge chute was received dented. This was a cosmetic issue, did not impact unit's functionality. However, at cost of this machine, I wanted it to look pretty which lead to perhaps the most pleasant surprise of the transaction. I called listed problem resolution number and actually promptly got an American agent to assist me! I briefly explained the issue and gave her parts numbers for chute and gaskets on each end of chute and she assured me parts would be ordered promptly. I received email verification of parts order shortly thereafter and replacement parts were received in only 3 days... amazing service and concern for customer satisfaction compared to other experiences I have had!
- this is my first Powermatic purchase but I will not hesitate to purchase their products again as my shop grows; based on my limited experience with them I would highly recommend the PM 1300 dust collector to a friend.ts were received in only 3 days... amazing service and concern for customer satisfaction compared to other experiences I have had! - this is my first Powermatic purchase but I will not hesitate to purchase their products again as my shop grows; based on my limited experience with them I would highly recommend the PM 1300 dust collector to a friend.

product_title: DELTA 50-760 1.5HP 1,200 CFM Vertical Bag Dust Collector
review_body: THE BEST !!! GREAT PRICE, GREAT PERFORMANCE. INSTALLED MINE WITH 6\\" GALVANIZED DUCT WORK. THE FINAL RESULT WAS WORTH THE EFFORT. CONNECTED MY PLANNER TO A 30 GALLON DUST SEPARATER. MADE THE MISTAKE OF LEAVING THE BLAST GATE FULL OPEN. SO MUCH AIR WENT THRU THE SEPARATER THAT ABOUT TWO INCHES OF SAWDUST ALREADY IN THE BOTTOM OF THE UNIT WERE SUCKED OUT INTO THE DELTA BAG. SOLVED THIS PROBLEM BY INSTALLING TWO PLASTIC ELBOWS ON THE BOTTOM SIDE OF THE SEPARATOR LID WITH THEM FACING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. FOUND THAT CLOSING THE BLAST GATE TO HALF OPEN PRODUCED THE RIGHT FLOW TO REMOVE THE SAWDUST FROM THE PLANNER AND CARRY ONLY THE FINES TO THE DELTA BAG. HAVE USED IT THE SAME WAY WITH MY GRIZZLY TABLE SAW AND THE RESULTS ARE BETTER THAN EXPECTED. NEXT PROJECT IS TO BUILD A \\"SANDING HOOD\\" & CONNECT IT TO THE DELTA SO I CAN ELIMINATE THAT SOURCE OF DUST IN MY BASEMENT SHOP. GREAT UNIT. SORRY I WAITED SO LONG TO BE SERIOUS ABOUT DUST COLLECTION. ALL THE LITERATURE INDICATES THAT DUST IN THE 2 TO 10 MICRON SIZE IS THE WORST FOR OUR LUNGS. DELTA TOP VENT BAG FILTERS DOWN TO 1 MICRON !!! IS YOUR HEALTH WORTH IT ??? ALSO RUNS PRETTY QUIETLY FOR A LARGE VACUUM UNIT.

review_body: I bought these and have tried 3 separate times, following the instructions, to remove screws with stripped out threads.  on all occasions, i spent over 10 minutes trying to \\"burnish\\" the ends and then backing out the screws.  in all cases, the tool did absolutely nothing except drain my drill battery.  Save your money and buy a dremel, that way you can just grind out the screw, or grind a groove in the screw and back it out with a flathead screwdriver, which is what I ended up having to do.

product_title: Hitachi C10FSH 10-Inch Sliding Compound Miter Saw with Laser  (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: HItachi C10FSH 10-inch Miter Saw with Laser
review_body: After a lot of research when it came to purchasing a miter saw I came up with two conclusions.  1) The Hitachi I am reviewing by far was the best bang for your buck at 420 dollars and free shipping (arrived in 2 days), (same saw at Lowes is 580) and 2) I figured there was a high risk of receiving damaged goods after reading hundreds of reviews of various items similar in size from Amazon.  After I was done putting the saw together and making the necessary adjustments I thought I lucked out and got a mint saw with no damage.  When I hooked the saw up and went for the first rip I noticed the plastic housing to the safety switch was cracked and the black button which goes into the housing to release the safety was missing.  I went back to the box and noticed the black safety release button was at the bottom of the box along with one piece of the green plastic housing.  Also worth mentioning that the box it came in is the same box you would see in Lowes.  There was nothing else for added protection.  I figured with something of this size I would get a box inside a box.  Back to the set up.  Keep in mind there is a small clear plastic pin in the plastic housing which is exposed and seemed to work properly.  The black safety release button presses against the clear plastic pin which releases the safety.  At this point I was presented with 2 options. 1) Send this 45 plus pound saw back and take the risk of getting a more damaged saw in return, or 2) make good with what I had which would include some super glue and McGiver like adjustments.  I went with option two, and although it's far from perfect appearance, the safety release now functions appropriately.      Now for the the review of the functionality of the saw.  The laser was right on, both 45 degree cuts using the left and right bevel along with 45 degree miter cuts were perfect out of the box.  I put up window trim in my house along with baseboard trim and the angled cuts were dead on.  The stocked blade cut through window trim and baseboard like butter leaving no cut marks what so ever. I will be installing a new deck this summer but I can not comment on larger cuts with different wood as I have not done any jobs of that nature yet.  Overall the functionality of this saw is amazing and I strongly recommend this saw to anyone whether it be a starter or experienced carpenter.  This saw can do it all.      If you don't mind taking a risk of getting damaged goods, you may make out all right.  If you don't want to the risk, you can always go to Lowes and pay [...] more.  Either way if you get an undamaged saw, you will not be disappointed.  I hope this review helps.  Good luck to all.

product_title: Mr. Nozzle M-115-DB Vac Tool Kit
review_headline: Great hose, OK tools; fits Fein vacuums
review_body:
I have a Fein vacuum in my workshop. It's expensive but quiet and powerful. It comes with a 16' hose but no tools. The hose doesn't have a standard-sized end, so it's not easy to find a substitute for the hundred-plus dollar accessory set Fein wants to sell you. The Mr. Nozzle set has an excellent 16' hose and it comes with three plastic wands and a set of floor and carpet tools. It's not inexpensive but it's more reasonably priced than the Fein tools and just as functional.

The plastic wands aren't as elegant as the stainless steel ones you get with the \\"genuine\\" brand but they feel tough enough and they have tapered ends for a secure fit. The plastic floor tools are OK -- functional and replaceable at the local home center if they wear out. If you have a European cannister shop vacuum/dust extractor (Fein or Festool) and you're looking for an alternative to the manufacturer's accessory set, this is a \\"good enough\\" choice.

product_title: Crescent 170-Piece Mechanics Tool Set
review_body:
I received this as a Christmas gift and at the time I was working at a machine shop. The open-ended wrenches in it are decent and have a nice finish. Many of them were smaller than I could use at my job at the time. The screw drivers and pliers that came with the set were also decent and served well. Where the set shines is the ratchets and sockets. I used and abused them on the job and they've held up very well. There is a good selection of sockets and the ratchets are beefy and easy to use. I am a full time electrician now and don't really have much of a need for this set on the job but I have used it many times to perform minor maintenance on our cars and at that it has also proved it's worth.
This set is also nice for a shop environment because tools tend to walk away in a shop so for the cost they are a good alternative to having more expensive tools disappear. If you are a serious or pro mechanic with a nice locking tool chest I would probably recommend Snap-on or even Craftsman wrenches which are both very good. As I said before the ratchets that are included in this set worked just as well for me than a more expensive model. For the home mechanic this is closer to a 5 star kit. For a pro or serious level it's about a 4 star set.

product_title: HyLoft Adjustable Ceiling Rack
review_body:
I bought 4 of these (2 sets) to store my obnoxiously large stock of scrap trim lumber.

Pros
Very sturdy design. Will easily support any amount of lumber I shove up there. Not as much wiggle, side to side\front to back as I've seen in similar products.
value - Good price for as stout as these are.

Cons
The only place I would ding this product is the install guide. It tells you to attach the end pieces to the joists first and then assemble by connecting the remaining four pieces. Unless you are very precise with your meansurements, you'll be out or square (requiring you to twist the final assembly to join the pieces) and while the width is adjustable, the holes are 1\\" apart meaning you'll likely have to bend the unit a little to align the holes. Instead, I recommend attaching one end leaving the lag screws loose (about 1\\" protruding from the joist), assemble the unit, put the other end up to the joist, mark the holes, pre-drill and screw in.

product_title: Shop-Vac 9520262 5-Gallon 4.5-Peak HP Hang Up Wall Mounted Wet/Dry  Vacuum
review_body: This shop-vac is second to none.  Works excellent!!  There's nothing it can't pick-up.  In fact, if your not careful it will pick up items you didn't mean to vacuum.  The wall mounting was very easy and it's great for holding all of the vacuums accessories.

product_title: PORTER-CABLE FR350A Round Head 2-Inch to 3-1/2-Inch Framing Nailer
review_headline: Good Gun but jams are hard to fix
review_body: Porter cable makes great tools (Lefty saw, routers, sanders ect) and this is no exception. I have a framing company and own 6 hitachi NR83's and am pretty much dedicated to them. However I ended up with one of these PC's and much to my suprise i was impressed.     The gun can take a beating and still keep nailing which is very important, uses plastic collated nails which work with my other guns and are easily found anywhere, depth adjustments can be made on the tool saving trips to the compressor, well balanced, and easy to use.    Downsides; clearing jams. I have found that most backloading guns are a real pain in @$$, and not firing the last 3 nails. I have never liked or understood the reason for this feature on any nail gun but it is what it is.     As you can see only 2 real issues that are bad and everything else is just great. I highly recomend this gun to homeowners, DIY guys, and framers looking to buy their own gun and cant afford the Hitachi NR83. Porter Cable makes good tools for evryone from rookies to the pros and you will be satisfied with your purchase for many years to come.    Rick \\"Main Frame\\" Payne

review_body: Very simple design, middle button switches between centigrade and fahrenheit trigger button takes reading.  It is limited to about 81 inches any more and you the sensor is looking at too large of an area to take accurate readings.  It appears to be accurate, I had planned to use it during the summer monthes and/or winter monthes to spot air leaks in my home.  It is currently too mild to do this now, but it performs well when I was trying to ascertain which of my pipes were cold and hot to prioritize insulating them.  Not a lot of bells and whistles but a good buy.

review_body: This light is super bright, small & compact, and appears to be of good quality.  The box states the light wave is 380-385nm. I was even able to see prior spots I thought I had cleaned well.

product_title: Rayovac Lantern
review_headline: First electric camp light that made me forget propane ...
review_body:
Before buying this light, I was a bit skeptical of battery operated camp lanterns. I'd had one with a halogen bulb that went through batteries and was dim to boot. I guess I was spoiled by gas/propane mantle lanterns from years ago.

This light made me a believer. I took it on a week-long camping trip and couldn't have been happier. Well made, really bright, and when I took the diffuser off and hung it upside down in my tent, my wife and I could both read effortlessly. A friend spent twice as much for a small light with a cool little three legged wire stand. Less light, less battery life, and no way to remove the diffuser.

No issues with the battery cover; I'm happy it is a positive lock. It isn't like you need to change batteries very often!

Highly recommended.

product_title: Arrow Fastener 8000 PowerShot Pro Forward-Action Staple Gun
review_body: I purchased this item, and used it successfully to drive about 20 or 30 nails, after which the stapler gun broke. When I press on the handle, I can feel the normal spring resistance, but it no longer \\"releases\\" that energy to drive a nail or staple into the work piece.  I have checked thoroughly, and the unit is not dirty or jammed.    This is the second arrow stapler gun that I have owned... the first one was a light duty version, and the second one that broke within the first 1/2 hr of use.      I hope that Arrow tests their products and works in improving the quality of them.

product_title: Black & Decker HPB14 14.4-Volt Battery Pack
review_headline: 3 to 4 years of life, used 4 times, battery and charger dead!
review_body:
I used this battery with the drill about 4 times max in a span of about 3.5 years. Then both batteries and the charger were dead. I took it to a DeWalt / B&D service center and the technician confirmed they were both dead. Another reviewer said the same thing; that they both die. You lose both batteries and charger. Since these are Ni-Cad I used to drain the batteries to avoid memory but another user said one should not drain completely with the charger they recommend, maybe that is the trick. I don't know.

Now I have a B&D drill in mint condition but it's a better investment for me to buy another drill that comes with a better battery life. I found a Lithium powered drill for a good price during Black Friday deals.

product_title: 7-1/4" Circular Saw
review_body: Light and easy to handle. Lower power than some, but the thin-kerf blade cuts through all wood I have tried without problems. I would be leery about using a regular kerf blade on it (I haven't tried). I have used it infrequently and for fairly light jobs.    The saw wanders when trying to cut following a guide. It took me a while until I discovered the reason. The base plate is grossly misaligned. The distance from the front of the blade to the edge of the plate is about 1/8 inch greater than the same distance from the back of the blade. As a result you cannot get an accurate cut by running the saw along a straightedge. There is no alignment adjustment for this condition.
